reason: With only 30 patients per arm, this pilot study is severely underpowered to detect realistic accelerations in re-epithelialization over silver sulfadiazine.
rationale: Silver sulfadiazine 1% cream modestly slows re-epithelialization in partial-thickness burns (typical median healing 14-15 days), giving topical comparators room to improve healing speed. However, this is an exploratory N=60 Phase 2 pilot by a small biotech with unstated drug concentration, where 80% power requires a hazard ratio near 2.0. Still recruiting in late October 2026 with a December 2026 target completion after 4.5 years of enrollment across 6 sites, the trial is likely to slip past Q1 2027 and faces substantial sample-size limitations if it reports.

reason: Three years of weekly intravenous infusions carry notable patient attrition that could dilute treatment differences or increase missing CT densitometry data.
rationale: In the 2-year RAPID trial, standard 60 mg/kg weekly alpha-1 augmentation slowed annual CT lung density decline at TLC by 0.74 g/L/year (p=0.03). SPARTA extends follow-up to 3 years (156 weeks) and tests double-dose 120 mg/kg alongside 60 mg/kg across 345 patients, substantially increasing cumulative PD15 separation (~2.3 g/L expected for 120 mg/kg) and statistical power, with either dose sufficient under round rules. Severe exacerbations rarely respond to augmentation. Having completed in July 2026, topline results and subsequent regulatory filing by Grifols in 2027 are highly likely.

assumptions.claim: In the 2-year RAPID trial, weekly intravenous alpha-1 proteinase inhibitor 60 mg/kg slowed annual CT lung density loss at total lung capacity versus placebo (-1.45 vs -2.19 g/L per year, p=0.03).

reason: Over nearly a decade of follow-up in older localized prostate cancer patients, competing non-cancer deaths can substantially dilute the metastasis-free survival hazard ratio.
rationale: Adding potent androgen signaling inhibition to radiotherapy and ADT improved MFS strongly in very-high-risk STAMPEDE (abiraterone HR 0.53), though ENZARAD showed how lower metastatic event rates and competing non-prostate-cancer mortality over 8-10 years attenuate MFS hazard ratios in broader high-risk cohorts receiving active antiandrogen/ADT + RT. With N=1503 enrolled since 2015 and central BICR conventional imaging, apalutamide should meaningfully reduce distant metastases, yielding an overall MFS HR around 0.76 and ~62% probability of statistical significance, with strong concordance on EFS if primary MFS succeeds.

assumptions.claim: In STAMPEDE, adding abiraterone to androgen deprivation therapy and radiotherapy in high-risk non-metastatic prostate cancer significantly improved metastasis-free survival (hazard ratio 0.53).

reason: This completed pediatric Phase 2 GERD study by Takeda has passed its July 2026 completion date and is very likely to post summary results on ClinicalTrials.gov within roughly one year.
rationale: The trial is already marked completed as of its registered primary and study completion date of July 21, 2026, making post-completion termination or withdrawal nearly impossible and substantive primary outcome amendments unlikely. Because Takeda is a large pharmaceutical sponsor with high FDAAA compliance and the statutory 1-year results submission deadline falls in July 2027—prior to the August 31, 2027 assessment date—results have a high probability of being posted on ClinicalTrials.gov in time.

reason: Meeting both registered primary endpoints requires statistically significant Week-24 symptom reduction alongside spleen volume response despite high early dropout and open-label control reporting.
rationale: In PERSIST-2, pacritinib 200 mg BID outperformed best available therapy on both Week-24 SVR35 and TSS50 in thrombocytopenic myelofibrosis, particularly at platelets <50,000/uL where physician's-choice options (steroids, danazol, hydroxyurea, very-low-dose ruxolitinib) rarely shrink spleens (~3-4% SVR35 vs ~22-25% for pacritinib). With N=407 randomized 2:1, SVR35 power exceeds 95%; the main hurdle is achieving co-primary modified TSS50 amidst disease-related early discontinuations. With October 2026 primary completion, H1 2027 readout and regulatory submissions for full US/EU approval are likely.

assumptions.claim: In PERSIST-2, pacritinib 200 mg twice daily achieved significantly higher Week-24 >=35% spleen volume reduction and >=50% total symptom score reduction rates than best available therapy.

reason: The secondary BPD signal from the prior Phase 2a ROP trial may regress substantially toward the null in a larger multicenter extremely preterm cohort.
rationale: OHB-607 (rhIGF-1/rhIGFBP-3) missed its primary ROP endpoint in Phase 2a (NCT01096784) but showed a secondary reduction in severe BPD, motivating this N=295 Phase 2b study in 23-27 week GA infants. Severe BPD or death by 36 weeks PMA occurs in ~45-50% of standard-care infants, requiring an ~11-12 percentage point reduction for p<0.05. Post-hoc/secondary neonatal signals frequently shrink in confirmatory testing across 62 international NICUs, yielding a ~34% probability of success, with topline results expected by mid-2027 following July 2026 primary completion.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 trial NCT01096784, rhIGF-1/rhIGFBP-3 did not reduce severe retinopathy of prematurity (the primary endpoint) compared with standard neonatal care.

reason: Large placebo responses in pediatric functional gastrointestinal trials combined with small per-dose sample sizes make statistical separation on stool consistency difficult.
rationale: In adult Phase 3 IBS-D trials, eluxadoline produced modest stool-consistency improvements over placebo (~0.3-0.5 BSFS points) across >2,400 patients and minimal standalone abdominal pain benefit. Splitting 272 pediatric participants across multiple dose/age strata leaves small arms facing large eDiary placebo improvements (~1.0 p-BSFS point) and the possibility that this pediatric PK/dose-ranging study reports descriptive statistics without formal superiority p-values. Completed in August 2026, AbbVie will likely post results on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 and may still advance to a PREA-mandated Phase 3.

assumptions.claim: In the adult Phase 3 trials NCT01553591 and NCT01553747, eluxadoline significantly improved the composite responder rate of decreased abdominal pain and improved stool consistency versus placebo.

reason: Adding HDAC inhibition with abexinostat to pazopanib increases hematologic and gastrointestinal toxicity, forcing dose interruptions and discontinuations that undermine combination efficacy.
rationale: HDAC inhibitor plus VEGF-TKI combinations in RCC and solid tumors have consistently struggled in randomized trials, as overlapping cytopenias, diarrhea, and hepatotoxicity compromise TKI dose intensity against an active pazopanib control (~8.4-9 months IRC PFS). Moreover, RENAVIV has been recruiting since July 2018 under a financially constrained sponsor while immunotherapy combinations displaced 1L TKI monotherapy. Still listed as recruiting two months before its December 2026 primary completion date, further delays or termination are likely, and success if reported is low.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 COMPARZ trial, first-line pazopanib achieved a median progression-free survival of 8.4 months by independent review in metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma.

reason: Substantial placebo improvement on the PANSS scale across multinational adolescent psychiatry sites frequently narrows drug-placebo separation below statistical significance.
rationale: Dopamine D2/D3 partial agonists including cariprazine have established efficacy in adult acute schizophrenia (-6 to -10 PANSS points vs placebo), and most atypical antipsychotics have succeeded in 6-week adolescent schizophrenia trials. However, multinational pediatric psychiatry trials exhibit high placebo responses (~14-point PANSS drop) and N=330 is likely split across multiple cariprazine dose arms (~110/arm), yielding moderate (~52%) power for an expected ~5-point difference. Because it remained recruiting 6.5 weeks before its December 15, 2026 completion date, minor slippage into 2027 is plausible.

assumptions.claim: In the adult Phase 3 trial NCT01104766, cariprazine significantly improved Week-6 PANSS total score compared with placebo in acute exacerbation of schizophrenia.

reason: With N=437 and two listed primary endpoints (PFS and ORR), modest sample size and potential co-primary multiplicity hurdles could prevent both from reaching formal significance.
rationale: CheckMate 8Y8 isolates ipilimumab's contribution to nivolumab in 1L IMDC intermediate/poor-risk ccRCC. Across CheckMate 214 (Nivo+Ipi ORR 42%, BICR median PFS 11.6 months) and 1L nivolumab monotherapy cohorts (HCRN GU16-260, OMNIVORE: int/poor-risk ORR ~28-30%, median PFS ~5.6-7.4 months), adding ipilimumab meaningfully increases response depth and durable PFS without the early curve crossover seen against VEGF TKIs. However, N=437 provides only ~65-75% power for HR ~0.75 and ~12% ORR difference, especially if both co-primaries are required.

assumptions.claim: In CheckMate 214, nivolumab plus ipilimumab achieved a 42% objective response rate and 11.6-month median progression-free survival in previously untreated IMDC intermediate- or poor-risk advanced renal cell carcinoma.

reason: As an active, non-recruiting industry Phase 3 study reaching its registered October 2026 completion date, the trial is very likely to finish without termination or outcome amendments and moderately likely to post results by August 2027.
rationale: MIS51ON is active, not recruiting, with registered primary and study completion on 2026-10-31 right at the snapshot date. Late termination or substantive primary endpoint amendments after completion are rare for large Sarepta Phase 3 DMD trials, and FDAAA reporting timelines give roughly a 40-45% chance of ClinicalTrials.gov results posting within 10 months.

reason: Although osmotic matching and titration above Kt/V 1.7 strongly favor non-inferior dialysis adequacy, unexpected residual renal function loss or inter-patient variance in N=170 could widen the confidence interval past a tight margin.
rationale: Both arms maintain icodextrin long dwells and tailor short-dwell prescriptions to keep weekly Kt/V urea above 1.7, and earlier xylitol/L-carnitine peritoneal dialysis trials demonstrated equivalent small-solute clearance (~2.0-2.1 weekly Kt/V) versus standard glucose solutions. Consequently, non-inferiority on 24-week Kt/V is highly probable (~78%), whereas still recruiting in late October 2026 makes >90-day completion delay likely given the 24-week follow-up.

assumptions.claim: Glucose-sparing L-carnitine/xylitol peritoneal dialysis regimens maintain weekly total Kt/V urea comparable to standard glucose solutions (~2.0) in CAPD patients.

reason: Eli Lilly's pediatric sJIA study is active, not recruiting, at its registered October 2026 completion date and has low termination or amendment risk alongside high sponsor compliance with ClinicalTrials.gov results posting.
rationale: The trial reached its registered October 2026 completion window while active and not recruiting across 55 global sites. Major pharmaceutical sponsors like Eli Lilly rarely amend primary endpoints after completion and routinely post pediatric Phase 3 results on ClinicalTrials.gov within 10-12 months.

reason: The 9vHPV vaccine induces potent neutralizing antibodies in saliva that prevent persistent oral HPV infection, leaving lower-than-projected event accrual or prevalent baseline latent infections as the only plausible risks.
rationale: VLP HPV vaccines consistently show 85-95% efficacy against persistent type-specific HPV infection across mucosal sites, including ~88-93% protection against oral HPV 16/18 infection in the Costa Rica Vaccine Trial and observational male cohorts. With 6,033 men followed over ~5-6 years, ~60-80 persistent 7-high-risk oral infections provide robust power for superiority, supporting Merck's confirmatory sBLA conversion.

assumptions.claim: Bivalent HPV VLP vaccination demonstrated approximately 93% vaccine efficacy against prevalent oral HPV 16/18 infection four years post-vaccination.
Quadrivalent HPV vaccination showed ~86-90% per-protocol efficacy against persistent external genital HPV infection in young men.

reason: Adding PD-1/PD-L1 blockade concurrently to definitive chemoradiotherapy failed to improve bladder-intact event-free survival in SWOG/NRG S1806, indicating modest incremental activity over effective trimodality therapy.
rationale: Although pembrolizumab is active across urothelial cancer settings, the closely analogous Phase 3 SWOG/NRG S1806 trial of concurrent atezolizumab plus chemoradiotherapy in 475 MIBC patients failed to improve bladder-intact EFS, mirroring mixed outcomes of concurrent PD-(L)1 plus chemoradiotherapy in solid tumors. Double-blind central review and PD-1 vs PD-L1 differences preserve a ~38% chance of success.

assumptions.claim: Modern chemoradiotherapy regimens in muscle-invasive bladder cancer achieve roughly 65-70% two-year locoregional/bladder-intact control.
SWOG/NRG S1806 evaluated concurrent PD-L1 blockade (atezolizumab) with chemoradiotherapy for bladder-intact EFS in MIBC.

reason: Diacerein has weak disease-modifying activity in knee osteoarthritis, high GI dropout rates, and N=128 with four registered structural primary outcomes makes meeting strict primary criteria unlikely.
rationale: Systemic IL-1 inhibition (including prior diacerein knee JSW studies and anti-IL-1 biologics like lutikizumab) has repeatedly failed to arrest MRI cartilage loss or synovitis in knee osteoarthritis. Combined with ~15-20% diarrhea-driven discontinuations, N=64/arm, and four co-registered primary imaging outcomes, the probability of meeting all primary objectives is low.

assumptions.claim: Diacerein failed to show statistically significant structural joint space narrowing reduction over 1 year in knee osteoarthritis.
IL-1alpha/beta dual blockade with lutikizumab did not improve MRI synovitis or cartilage loss in knee osteoarthritis.

reason: Field combined symptom and medication scores over 12 months exhibit substantial patient-level variability, so 50 patients per arm carries meaningful false-negative risk despite active mannan-allergoid immunotherapy.
rationale: Inmunotek's polymerized house dust mite allergoid-mannan conjugate previously demonstrated robust dose-dependent nasal provocation and clinical improvements in Phase 2 (Nieto 2022), and testing two active doses (10,000 and 30,000 MM09) increases the chance one dose beats placebo. However, N=50/arm limits power on noisy 12-month field CSMS, and still recruiting in October 2026 implies probable completion delay.

assumptions.claim: Subcutaneous polymerized D. pteronyssinus/D. farinae allergoid conjugated to mannan met its primary efficacy endpoint in a randomized Phase 2 mite allergy trial.

reason: Molecular heterogeneity within non-GCB DLBCL and potential toxicity-related R-CHOP dose reductions among patients aged 60 to 75 could dilute BTK-sensitive MCD/N1 subgroup benefit.
rationale: In PHOENIX, adding ibrutinib to R-CHOP missed overall EFS due to excess toxicity compromising R-CHOP intensity in patients >=60, whereas patients <60 had substantial EFS/PFS/OS improvements (HR ~0.58). ESCALADE selects GEP-confirmed non-GCB DLBCL capped at <=75 years and uses more selective acalabrutinib, mitigating off-target toxicity while retaining risk from 60-75-year-olds and BTKi-insensitive non-GCB subsets.

assumptions.claim: In PHOENIX, ibrutinib plus R-CHOP failed in the overall non-GCB DLBCL population due to toxicity in patients >=60 years but improved EFS, PFS, and OS in patients <60 years.

reason: Actual enrollment of 69 including the PK cohort leaves roughly 54 randomized patients, giving modest statistical power at alpha=0.05 even with SOLAR-1's true PFS hazard ratio near 0.60.
rationale: Alpelisib plus fulvestrant has well-established efficacy in PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer (SOLAR-1 PFS HR=0.65, median 11.0 vs 5.7 months; confirmed post-CDK4/6i in BYLieve). However, enrollment reached 69 instead of ~135 planned (~54 randomized across two arms), leaving ~42 PFS events where sampling variance creates nearly coin-flip power for formal statistical significance.

assumptions.claim: In SOLAR-1, alpelisib plus fulvestrant reduced the risk of progression or death versus placebo plus fulvestrant with HR 0.65 (median PFS 11.0 vs 5.7 months) in PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer.
In SOLAR-1, 25.0% of patients in the alpelisib-fulvestrant group versus 4.2% in the placebo-fulvestrant group discontinued treatment due to adverse events.

reason: Unselected newly diagnosed glioblastoma has low overall ASS1 auxotrophy, poor blood-brain barrier macromolecule penetration, and a small N=100 Phase 1-2 sample size for overall survival.
rationale: Although pegargiminase (ADI-PEG 20) improved survival in ASS1-deficient sarcomatoid mesothelioma (ATOMIC-Meso) and showed encouraging preliminary activity with radiotherapy/temozolomide in ASS1-negative GBM, this trial enrolls biomarker-unselected newly diagnosed GBM where ASS1 silencing occurs in only ~30-40% of tumors and neutralizing anti-ADI antibodies emerge. With <=100 patients across Phase 1-2, hitting overall OS significance is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Standard concurrent and adjuvant radiotherapy plus temozolomide yields median overall survival of roughly 14.6 to 17 months in newly diagnosed glioblastoma.
ADI-PEG 20 plus chemotherapy improved overall survival in arginine-auxotrophic non-epithelioid pleural mesothelioma in ATOMIC-Meso.

reason: Restricting the primary PFS analysis to patients with baseline CNS metastases within a 217-patient trial leaves a modest event count that increases sampling variability.
rationale: Entrectinib crosses the blood-brain barrier effectively, whereas crizotinib has poor CNS penetration and high intracranial progression rates. Pooled STARTRK-1/2 and ALKA data showed durable intracranial activity and median PFS around 13.6 months in ROS1-positive NSCLC with baseline CNS metastases, while crizotinib typically achieves roughly 7 to 10 months in CNS-metastatic disease. Analogous CNS-penetrant TKIs in ALK-positive NSCLC strongly outperformed crizotinib in baseline CNS subgroups. The main risk is limited statistical power because only a subset of the 217 randomized patients has baseline CNS metastases.

assumptions.claim: In pooled ALKA-372-001, STARTRK-1, and STARTRK-2 analyses, entrectinib showed substantial intracranial response and durable PFS in ROS1-positive NSCLC with baseline CNS metastases.
Crizotinib has limited blood-brain barrier penetration, leading to shorter PFS in patients with baseline CNS metastases compared with patients without CNS metastases.

reason: Delayed recurrences after stopping fixed-duration adjuvant anti-PD-1 plus anti-angiogenic therapy may erode an early recurrence-free survival separation at longer follow-up, as seen in IMbrave050.
rationale: Camrelizumab plus rivoceranib demonstrated strong efficacy in advanced HBV-predominant HCC in CARES-310 (PFS HR 0.52), and PD-1 blockade showed encouraging RFS reduction in high-risk resected Chinese HCC cohorts. With 687 patients, the trial is well powered to detect an HR around 0.75. However, IMbrave050 showed that initial adjuvant IO-anti-VEGF RFS gains (HR 0.72) attenuated to non-significance (HR 0.90) with longer follow-up, and combination toxicity in the curative setting drives notable treatment discontinuation.

assumptions.claim: Camrelizumab plus rivoceranib significantly improved PFS and OS over sorafenib in first-line unresectable HCC in CARES-310.
In IMbrave050, adjuvant atezolizumab plus bevacizumab met RFS at the interim analysis but lost RFS statistical significance on updated follow-up.

reason: Enrollment is complete with 451 participants and a fixed 72-week primary assessment, so this Roche global Phase 3b trial should finish close to its February 2027 target date.
rationale: Velodrome is already active, not recruiting, with 451 enrolled participants and a registered primary completion date of February 4, 2027. Because the primary outcome is assessed at a fixed 72-week visit rather than an event-driven milestone, primary completion slip beyond May 5, 2027 is relatively unlikely unless prior PDS device-refill holds caused unreflected schedule shifts. Posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 31, 2027 is only ~7 months after completion, making results posting before the 12-month statutory deadline modest in probability.

reason: SV2A ligands have historically shown much weaker anti-absence efficacy than T-type calcium channel blockers, as seen in the borderline placebo-controlled trial of levetiracetam.
rationale: The trial completed in July 2026 at N=153 under a two-stage adaptive design, suggesting it passed Stage 1 dose selection without futility termination. Because inclusion requires baseline electrographic seizures on hyperventilation EEG and frequent clinical episodes, spontaneous 24-hour EEG seizure freedom at Day 14 on placebo is very low (~5-7%). Thus even moderate brivaracetam responder rates (~22-25%, similar to levetiracetam's 24% in Fattore 2011) can achieve statistical significance with 153 patients, though SV2A modulation remains pharmacologically modest in generalized spike-wave epilepsy.
evidence: Fattore et al. levetiracetam CAE/JAE trial (2011)

assumptions.claim: In a 2-week randomized placebo-controlled trial of levetiracetam in childhood and juvenile absence epilepsy, responder rates on EEG were modest (~24% vs ~5% on placebo).

reason: This 43-patient Phase 2 PD study in France has passed its registered September 2026 primary completion date and is scheduled for full study completion in April 2027 with low termination risk.
rationale: Enrollment is closed at 43 participants and the registered primary completion date (September 2026) has already passed, with study completion set for April 2027. Termination risk at this late follow-up stage is low. Because Il-Yang Pharm is a small Korean sponsor running a European-only trial (France, no US sites or FDA IND apparent for PD), timely results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov within four months of April 2027 study completion is relatively unlikely.

reason: Microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer with liver metastases is profoundly resistant to PD-1 checkpoint blockade, and local embolization has repeatedly failed to sensitize systemic or intrahepatic disease enough to improve overall survival.
rationale: Liver-metastatic MSS-mCRC carries an immunosuppressive hepatic microenvironment where pembrolizumab combinations and locoregional-immunotherapy strategies have consistently failed to improve OS over TAS-102 or regorafenib (median OS ~6.5-7.1 months). Furthermore, ~37 patients per arm provides adequate power only for an implausibly large OS hazard ratio (~0.50), and if both registered co-primary endpoints must be met, hurdles increase further. With only 3 sites and recruiting status after 5.4 years, completion will likely slip past June 2027.

assumptions.claim: In RECOURSE and CORRECT, median overall survival with TAS-102 or regorafenib in refractory mCRC was approximately 6.4 to 7.1 months.
Pembrolizumab-based combinations failed to demonstrate statistically significant overall survival superiority over TAS-102 or regorafenib in MSS mCRC with liver metastases in LEAP-017.

reason: Frequent ranibizumab maintains visual acuity reliably in anti-VEGF-responsive eyes, whereas subretinal vitrectomy delivery can induce subtle retinal or pigmentary changes that narrow the non-inferiority margin cushion.
rationale: Phase 1/2a subretinal ABBV-RGX-314 cohorts showed stable-to-improved BCVA (+0 to +2 letters) and large reductions in anti-VEGF burden at 1 year. Requiring pseudophakic eyes at entry eliminates post-vitrectomy cataract confounding that hurt earlier surgical nAMD trials (such as Archway), and testing two doses under a ~4 to 4.5-letter non-inferiority margin with 210 patients per arm gives solid power. However, subretinal bleb placement near the fovea still risks slight BCVA loss relative to ranibizumab, making non-inferiority plausible (~62%) but superiority on secondary endpoints unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In Phase 1/2a NCT03066258 higher-dose cohorts, subretinal RGX-314 maintained or slightly improved mean BCVA through 1 year while markedly reducing anti-VEGF injection frequency.
In Archway (NCT03677934), anti-VEGF-pretreated nAMD patients in the control ranibizumab arm had a mean BCVA change near +0.5 ETDRS letters at ~1 year.

reason: Large, variable placebo improvements on the CDRS-R across 81 pediatric psychiatric sites frequently dilute drug-placebo separation at 6 weeks, as occurred in pediatric quetiapine trials.
rationale: Cariprazine has proven efficacy in adult bipolar I depression across three positive trials, and atypical antipsychotics have succeeded in pediatric bipolar I depression (lurasidone diff -5.7, OFC diff -5.0 on CDRS-R). With N=380 and 6-week follow-up, the study can detect a ~3.5 to 4-point CDRS-R difference. However, pediatric mood trials suffer from large placebo responses (-15 to -29 points on CDRS-R; quetiapine failed twice), and cariprazine's adult effect size is somewhat smaller than lurasidone's, making success roughly a coin toss.

assumptions.claim: Lurasidone significantly improved Week-6 CDRS-R score versus placebo (-21.0 vs -15.3) in youths aged 10 to 17 with bipolar I depression.
Quetiapine failed to separate from placebo on CDRS-R change in pediatric bipolar depression due to large placebo response.

reason: With only 40 patients per arm, background 6-month patency around 70-80% on modern anticoagulation, and multiple registered primary outcomes, the trial lacks statistical power for realistic treatment effects.
rationale: Perivenous dexamethasone via the Bullfrog catheter showed anti-inflammatory vascular remodeling signals in arterial PAD (DANCE) and small DVT feasibility cohorts. However, with modern thrombectomy plus mandatory LMWH and 12-month oral anticoagulation, 6-month symptomatic patency in sham patients is already ~70-80%. At N=80 (40 per arm), superiority requires a ~18-20 percentage point gain, and meeting the co-primary Villalta PTS endpoint as well makes formal success unlikely. Still recruiting in late October 2026 with a 6-month endpoint strongly implies primary completion past March 2027.

assumptions.claim: After acute femoropopliteal DVT recanalization and therapeutic anticoagulation, 6-month venous patency rates typically exceed 70%.

reason: Adding atezolizumab to HER2-directed therapy previously failed in early HER2-positive breast cancer (IMpassion050) and unselected metastatic disease (KATE2), and capped enrollment at 1,188 reduces power for modest effects.
rationale: In KATHERINE, adjuvant T-DM1 yielded an 88.3% 3-year IDFS (11.7% event rate, ~14-16% in higher-risk dual-HER2-pretreated cohorts). However, adding atezolizumab to HER2 blockade failed to improve pCR or EFS in neoadjuvant IMpassion050 and missed ITT PFS in metastatic KATE2 (HR 0.82, with benefit confined to PD-L1+ tumors and higher toxicity). Screening closed in June 2024 at 1,188 patients (below initial ~1,700 targets amid T-DXd competition), limiting power to detect small IDFS gains in an unselected population.

assumptions.claim: In KATHERINE, adjuvant T-DM1 achieved a 3-year invasive disease-free survival of 88.3% with an 18% adverse-event treatment discontinuation rate.
In KATE2, adding atezolizumab to T-DM1 did not significantly improve progression-free survival in the overall HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer population.
In IMpassion050, adding atezolizumab to neoadjuvant HER2-targeted chemotherapy failed to improve pathologic complete response in high-risk HER2-positive early breast cancer.

reason: High and variable placebo SRI-4 response rates on background standard-of-care therapies routinely dilute treatment differences in global Phase 3 SLE trials.
rationale: Litifilimab (anti-BDCA2) inhibits pDC type I IFN production, a validated pathway in SLE (anifrolumab). In Phase 2 LILAC (NCT02847598), litifilimab met its week-24 joint count primary endpoint and showed encouraging SRI-4 separation (~56% vs ~29% in a small cohort), though Phase 3 SLE trials using week-52 SRI-4 frequently suffer from high placebo response (40-52%, as in TULIP-1 where anifrolumab missed SRI-4 despite hitting BICLA). With ~183 patients per arm and two active doses, TOPAZ-1 has moderate power (~42% PoS) if true SRI-4 benefit is ~9-11 percentage points.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 LILAC SLE part (NCT02847598), litifilimab 450 mg significantly reduced total active joint count at week 24 compared with placebo.
In Phase 3 TULIP-1 (NCT02446912), anifrolumab failed to meet the primary endpoint of SRI-4 response at week 52 despite targeting the type I interferon pathway.

reason: Active, not recruiting 100-subject DoD/SIGA Phase 2 interaction study with January 2027 completion should finish roughly on schedule with moderate timely registry posting.
rationale: The trial is already active, not recruiting with 100 healthy volunteers across 2 US sites and a short 59-day follow-up window, making primary completion on or near 2027-01-01 likely (low risk of >90-day delay past 2027-04-01). Termination risk is very low once enrollment is finished. Results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by 2027-08-31 (~8 months post-completion) is below 50% since sponsors typically post near the 12-month FDAAA statutory deadline.

reason: Although JAK1 inhibition is highly validated in psoriatic arthritis, sub-optimal dosing or unexpectedly high placebo ACR20 response could narrow the margin.
rationale: SHR0302 (ivarmacitinib) is a selective JAK1 inhibitor developed by Hengrui that has already succeeded in Phase 3 trials for ankylosing spondylitis, rheumatoid arthritis, atopic dermatitis, and ulcerative colitis. JAK1 inhibition in active PsA is strongly validated by upadacitinib (SELECT-PsA 1: week-12/24 ACR20 ~71-78% vs ~36% placebo) and filgotinib. With ~139 patients per arm across two active doses in a mostly biologic-naive Chinese PsA population, statistical power to detect a ~25-30% ACR20 advantage at week 24 is very high (>85%). Hengrui routinely announces NMPA sNDA acceptance within months of readout.

assumptions.claim: In SELECT-PsA 1 (NCT03104400), the selective JAK1 inhibitor upadacitinib achieved significantly higher ACR20 response rates than placebo in active psoriatic arthritis.
In OPAL Broaden (NCT01877668), the JAK inhibitor tofacitinib significantly improved ACR20 response vs placebo in active psoriatic arthritis.

reason: Substantial placebo SRI-4 responses on background immunosuppressants and steroids frequently mask moderate biologic efficacy in 52-week global SLE trials.
rationale: TOPAZ-2 is the replicate Phase 3 trial to TOPAZ-1 evaluating litifilimab (anti-BDCA2) vs placebo on Week-52 SRI-4 in active SLE (N=562 across 3 arms, ~187/arm). Type I IFN suppression via pDC inhibition showed positive Phase 2 joint and global SLE signals in LILAC (NCT02847598) and target validation from anifrolumab. However, replicate SLE Phase 3 trials historically exhibit ~40-50% individual trial success even for active drugs (e.g., anifrolumab missed SRI-4 in TULIP-1; baricitinib succeeded in BRAVE-I and failed BRAVE-II) due to noisy composite endpoints and high background SOC response.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 LILAC SLE study (NCT02847598), litifilimab met its primary endpoint of reducing active joint count at week 24 versus placebo.
Replicate Phase 3 SLE trials using SRI-4 at week 52 can yield discordant outcomes due to placebo variability, as seen across TULIP-1 and TULIP-2.

reason: Pediatric and adolescent migraine trials notoriously exhibit large placebo responses, compounded here by an intravenous infusion placebo and modest 95-per-arm sample size.
rationale: Eptinezumab (anti-CGRP IV mAb) is strongly effective in adult chronic migraine (PROMISE-2: 300 mg reduced MMDs by -8.2 vs -5.6 placebo, delta -2.6 days), and CGRP mAbs have recently shown positive efficacy in pediatric/adolescent migraine (e.g., fremanezumab SPACE trial). However, adolescent migraine trials face pronounced placebo responses (CHAMP trial), especially with IV infusion administration, and 95 patients per arm gives tight power if the placebo effect shrinks the delta toward -1.5 to -1.8 MMDs with SD ~6.2. Still recruiting in Oct 2026 with March 2027 PCD implies moderate delay risk.

assumptions.claim: In adult chronic migraine (PROMISE-2, NCT02974153), eptinezumab 300 mg IV reduced monthly migraine days over weeks 1-12 by 8.2 days versus 5.6 days for placebo.
Pediatric and adolescent migraine prevention trials display high placebo response rates, as demonstrated in the CHAMP study (NCT01581281).

reason: Adoptive CIK cell immunotherapy has limited systemic activity against micrometastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, where nearly all Phase 3 adjuvant add-on trials have failed.
rationale: Immuncell-LC (autologous cytokine-induced killer cells) improved RFS in resected HCC (Lee 2015), but resected PDAC is far more aggressive and immunosuppressive. Virtually all non-chemotherapy adjuvant add-ons to gemcitabine in PDAC (algenpantucel-L, erlotinib in CONKO-005, sorafenib, nab-paclitaxel on independent DFS in APACT) failed to significantly extend BICR RFS/DFS over gemcitabine monotherapy (median RFS ~11-14 months). Furthermore, the record still lists status as recruiting in late October 2026 despite a December 2026 registered completion and a 36-month post-LPI design, signaling a high likelihood of late registry completion.

assumptions.claim: Adjuvant gemcitabine monotherapy after resection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma yields a median disease-free survival of roughly 11 to 14 months by independent review (e.g., 13.7 months in APACT, NCT01964430).
Adjuvant Immuncell-LC previously prolonged recurrence-free survival in curatively treated hepatocellular carcinoma in a Korean Phase 3 trial.

reason: Multi-cohort Merck oncology Phase 2 basket trials frequently extend primary completion dates to allow mature BICR response duration follow-up across cohorts.
rationale: MK-6482-016 is active, not recruiting with 730 patients across multiple solid tumor cohorts and a registered primary completion date of 2027-03-22. Merck routinely updates multi-cohort oncology Phase 2 PCDs by several months based on BICR scan cutoffs, giving a ~45% chance of shifting past 2027-06-20 (>90 days late). Full termination is unlikely since enrollment is complete (even after closing the ESCC cohort). Merck consistently posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov near the 12-month mark after primary completion, making posting by 2027-08-31 unlikely (~12%).

reason: BET inhibitors have shown modest clinical efficacy and dose-limiting hematologic/GI toxicities in mCRPC, while Cohort A alone provides a small sample size.
rationale: ZEN003694 is an oral BET bromodomain inhibitor combined with enzalutamide in post-abiraterone mCRPC, targeting Cohort A (poor abiraterone responders) for primary BICR rPFS. Enzalutamide after abiraterone yields short median rPFS (~4-5.5 months, e.g., CARD/PLATO controls, shorter in primary refractory patients). While Phase 1b/2a single-arm data (Aggarwal 2020) suggested activity in poor abiraterone responders, epigenetic/BET inhibitors in randomized solid tumor trials have repeatedly disappointed, additive thrombocytopenia/fatigue increases discontinuations, and Cohort A comprises only part of the 200 total patients. Recruiting status in Oct 2026 implies likely delay past March 2027.

assumptions.claim: Second-line AR pathway inhibitor switch (enzalutamide after abiraterone or vice versa) in mCRPC yields short median rPFS of roughly 3.7 to 5.5 months.
ZEN-3694 plus enzalutamide showed preliminary clinical activity and acceptable tolerability in a single-arm Phase 1b/2a mCRPC study (Aggarwal 2020).

reason: Demonstrating PFS superiority of high-exposure octreotide depot over active somatostatin analogues is challenging because somatostatin receptors saturate and high-dose SSAs have rarely beaten standard doses.
rationale: CAM2029 delivers ~5-fold higher octreotide bioavailability than octreotide LAR. However, SORENTO tests superiority against active standard-of-care SSAs (octreotide LAR or lanreotide ATG) rather than placebo. Standard SSAs already achieve durable disease control in well-differentiated GEP-NET (CLARINET lanreotide median PFS ~32.8 months in indolent G1/G2; NETTER-2 control high-dose octreotide in higher-grade G2/G3 ~8.5 months; mixed first-line GEP-NET ~22-28 months). Whether higher plasma octreotide exposure translates into a ~30% PFS hazard reduction over receptor-saturating standard SSA doses is biologically uncertain, giving ~42% PoS. OS will be immature at primary readout.

assumptions.claim: CAM2029 provides approximately 5-fold higher octreotide plasma exposure/bioavailability than standard octreotide LAR.
Lanreotide autogel significantly prolonged progression-free survival in well-differentiated enteropancreatic NETs in CLARINET (NCT00353496), with median PFS not reached during the 96-week core study.

reason: Lennox-Gastaut syndrome has heterogeneous etiologies where serotonergic modulation shows much smaller seizure reductions than in SCN1A-driven Dravet syndrome, as seen when fenfluramine barely cleared Phase 3 and soticlestat failed.
rationale: Clemizole HCl (EPX-100) is a repurposed antihistamine with 5-HT2 receptor agonist activity identified in zebrafish Dravet models. Serotonergic activity has partial validation in LGS via fenfluramine (NCT03355209: 0.7 mg/kg reduced drop seizures by median -26.5% vs -7.6% placebo, p=0.001, while 0.2 mg/kg missed at p=0.09), whereas soticlestat recently failed Phase 3 LGS (SKYLINE/SKYWAY) and carisbamate/ganaxolone also struggled. Without robust randomized Phase 2 LGS data and given higher placebo responses (-15% to -22%) in modern countable motor seizure trials, PoS is ~38%. Recruiting status in Oct 2026 implies readout likely slips into mid/late 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 LGS trial of serotonergic agent fenfluramine (NCT03355209), the 0.7 mg/kg/day arm achieved a 26.5% median reduction in drop seizures versus 7.6% on placebo, while the 0.2 mg/kg/day arm was not statistically significant.
Placebo median percent reductions in drop or major motor seizures in Phase 3 LGS trials typically range from roughly 8% to 22% (e.g., 17.2% in GWPCARE3, NCT02224560).

reason: Caregiver-observed seizure termination within 90 seconds in an outpatient setting is vulnerable to administration delays and subjective timing errors compared with inpatient video-EEG monitoring.
rationale: Staccato thermally generated alprazolam aerosol delivers systemic benzodiazepine levels almost immediately via inhalation. In the inpatient Phase 2b study (NCT02351115), Staccato alprazolam 2 mg achieved rapid responder rates (~66% vs ~43% placebo within 2 minutes without recurrence up to 2 hours) with median cessation around 38 seconds. With N=350, the trial is well powered for a ~20-25 percentage point advantage on both co-primaries, though outpatient caregiver inhalation coordination and judging seizure end within 90 seconds introduce higher measurement noise and placebo resolution variability.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2b inpatient study NCT02351115, Staccato alprazolam 2 mg showed a significantly higher responder rate of seizure cessation within 2 minutes without recurrence for 2 hours than placebo (approximately 65.8% vs 42.5%).

reason: As an active, non-recruiting GSK vaccine schedule trial with fixed 24- and 48-month dosing intervals started in late 2021, completion near March 2027 aligns closely with protocol follow-up.
rationale: Enrollment is complete (active, not recruiting) and the March 2027 primary completion date matches Day 1471 follow-up (roughly 49 months) after enrollment began in November 2021, making a >90-day slip unlikely. Termination risk is minimal for a completed-enrollment adolescent immunogenicity study by GlaxoSmithKline. Results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 is modest because only five months elapse after primary completion, whereas sponsors typically post near the 12-month statutory deadline.

reason: Because both stage III EFS and overall ITT EFS are registered as co-primary outcomes, an early readout reporting only stage III while ITT EFS remains immature would not satisfy both co-primaries by the deadline.
rationale: Perioperative anti-PD-1 therapy added to platinum doublet chemotherapy in resectable stage II-IIIB NSCLC has consistently demonstrated large EFS improvements across KEYNOTE-671, CheckMate 77T, RATIONALE-315, and Neotorch, particularly in Chinese cohorts enriched for squamous histology and male smokers (stage III HR ~0.40-0.56). Sintilimab is a validated PD-1 inhibitor in NSCLC (ORIENT-11, ORIENT-12). Biological efficacy risk is low; the primary scoring risk is staggered maturation between the stage III and 3-year ITT EFS co-primary endpoints.

assumptions.claim: Perioperative toripalimab plus chemotherapy in Neotorch (NCT04158440) significantly improved event-free survival in stage III resectable NSCLC with a hazard ratio around 0.40.
Perioperative tislelizumab plus chemotherapy in RATIONALE-315 (NCT04379635) significantly improved event-free survival in resectable stage II-IIIA NSCLC with a hazard ratio around 0.56.

reason: The small Phase 2a trial is active and no longer recruiting with its September 2026 primary completion date already passed, pointing to routine closeout with modest near-term ClinicalTrials.gov posting.
rationale: With 60 patients and status active, not recruiting past the September 2026 registered primary completion date, Day 60 follow-up should already be complete or finishing shortly, making late termination unlikely. Because this is a US-site interventional Phase 2 trial subject to FDAAA reporting, there is a moderate probability that results are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 (~11 months after registered completion), while substantive post-completion primary safety outcome changes are rare.

reason: DHODH inhibitors generally produce modest ~30% reductions in clinical relapse rates, and low placebo relapse rates in contemporary MS cohorts could leave the hazard ratio short of significance.
rationale: IMU-838 (vidofludimus calcium) is a selective DHODH inhibitor, a clinically validated mechanism in RMS via teriflunomide (TEMSO/TOWER ~31-36% ARR reduction, time-to-relapse HR ~0.72). In Phase 2 EMPhASIS (NCT03846219), IMU-838 reduced combined unique active MRI lesions by ~62-70% vs placebo with placebo-like tolerability. Enrolling 1,121 active RMS patients against placebo provides strong power (~80-85%) for an expected HR around 0.68, though declining background relapse rates in modern MS trials remain the principal risk.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 EMPhASIS trial (NCT03846219), IMU-838 30 mg and 45 mg reduced combined unique active MRI lesions by over 60% compared with placebo over 24 weeks.
In the Phase 3 TEMSO trial (NCT00134563), the DHODH inhibitor teriflunomide reduced the risk of sustained relapse (time to first relapse) versus placebo with a hazard ratio around 0.72.

reason: Proteinuria-driven monoclonal antibody clearance and a responsive mycophenolate-plus-glucocorticoid background arm could compress the Week 52 complete renal response delta below ~10 percentage points.
rationale: In Phase 2 TULIP-LN (NCT02547922), standard-dose anifrolumab suffered enhanced renal clearance, whereas the intensified regimen (900 mg x3 then 300 mg Q4W) achieved numerically higher Week 52 CRR (45.5% vs 31.1%, +14.4 pp) and sustained steroid tapering (55.6% vs 33.3%). Type I IFN signaling is prominent in proliferative LN, and N=363 gives ~80% power for a 14-15 pp improvement, though strict UPCR <=0.5 mg/mg criteria and heterogeneous background MMF response leave moderate failure risk.
evidence: Jayne et al. Ann Rheum Dis 2022

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 TULIP-LN trial (NCT02547922), the anifrolumab intensified regimen achieved a Week 52 complete renal response rate of 45.5% versus 31.1% with placebo.

reason: With roughly 37 patients per arm and typical 24-week FVC change standard deviation near 200 mL, only an unusually large >90 mL treatment difference reaches two-sided 0.05 significance.
rationale: HEC585 (yifenidone) is a pirfenidone-derivative antifibrotic tested in PF-ILD over 24 weeks. Even established antifibrotics (nintedanib in INBUILD, pirfenidone in RELIEF) typically slow 24-week FVC decline by ~50-65 mL against a ~90 mL placebo loss with inter-patient SD around 180-220 mL. Splitting 110 patients across three arms (~37/arm) leaves ~30-40% power even allowing two active doses. Still recruiting in late October 2026 against a December 2026 completion date also signals substantial delay.

assumptions.claim: In the INBUILD trial of progressive fibrosing ILD (NCT02999178), placebo FVC declined by approximately 188 mL over 52 weeks (roughly 85-95 mL by 24 weeks).

reason: Allowing baseline leptin up to 20 ng/mL and entry via either elevated HbA1c or triglycerides dilutes metreleptin's metabolic effect while requiring both co-primaries to win in 69 patients.
rationale: Unlike generalized lipodystrophy, familial partial lipodystrophy shows attenuated, heterogeneous responses to metreleptin, especially when endogenous leptin exceeds 4 ng/mL (here allowed up to 20 ng/mL). Moreover, participants can enroll with HbA1c >=7% or TGs >=500 mg/dL, diluting baseline abnormality on whichever co-primary was non-qualifying. With only 69 patients randomized and both Month 6 HbA1c and fasting TG co-primaries required for success, statistical power for meeting both simultaneously is below 50%.

assumptions.claim: In open-label NIH partial lipodystrophy studies, metreleptin produced substantially larger HbA1c and triglyceride reductions in severely hypoleptinemic or poorly controlled subgroups than in broader partial lipodystrophy patients.

reason: Splitting 84 total participants across two sequential anatomical stages and multiple light-fluence cohorts leaves small per-arm sample sizes in Stage Two.
rationale: Hemoporfin 5 mg/kg plus 532 nm green-light PDT is already approved in China based on a 440-patient Phase 3 RCT showing ~90% port-wine stain blanching response versus ~25% for vehicle plus green light (p<0.0001). Green light without photosensitizer produces little vascular clearance, creating a large standardized effect size even in small sequential cohorts where one fluence arm winning suffices. However, still recruiting in late October 2026 with ~44-week assessments makes substantial completion delay likely.

assumptions.claim: In the Chinese Phase 3 randomized controlled trial of Hemoporfin photodynamic therapy for port-wine stains, Hemoporfin 5 mg/kg plus green light achieved markedly higher response rates (~89.7% vs ~24.5%) than placebo plus green light.

reason: Because enrollment is already complete (active, not recruiting) and the primary safety endpoint is assessed within 24 hours of dosing, completion on or shortly after December 2026 is highly likely.
rationale: The trial is active, not recruiting as of late October 2026 with a December 31, 2026 primary completion date and a 24-hour symptomatic ICH primary endpoint (with standard 90-day stroke follow-up). With recruitment finished, slipping past March 31, 2027 (>90 days late) or early termination is unlikely. ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 31, 2027 (~8 months post-completion) has a modest ~18% probability given typical 10-12 month sponsor reporting timelines.

reason: Contemporary relapsing MS populations frequently exhibit lower-than-planned on-study clinical relapse rates, reducing statistical power for time to first relapse within a 72-week window.
rationale: Vidofludimus calcium (IMU-838) is an oral DHODH inhibitor, a clinically validated class in relapsing MS via teriflunomide (TEMSO and TOWER showed ~31-36% ARR reductions and time-to-relapse HR ~0.72). In Phase 2 EMPhASIS, IMU-838 reduced combined unique active MRI lesions by 62-70% versus placebo with placebo-like tolerability and low discontinuation. With 1,100 active RMS patients vs placebo, expected HR (~0.73) yields moderate-to-good power, tempered by historically declining relapse rates in modern MS cohorts that can lower total relapse events.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 EMPhASIS trial, daily IMU-838 30 mg and 45 mg reduced cumulative combined unique active MRI lesions by 70% and 62% versus placebo over 24 weeks.
In the Phase 3 TEMSO trial of the DHODH inhibitor teriflunomide 14 mg vs placebo in RMS, the hazard ratio for sustained relapse reduction / annualized relapse reduction was approximately 31%.

reason: Carisbamate previously showed modest and inconsistent seizure-reduction efficacy in focal epilepsy Phase 3 studies, and refractory LGS drop seizures often exhibit high variability and notable placebo responses.
rationale: Carisbamate is a broad-spectrum neuromodulator evaluated in 252 LGS patients. Earlier Phase 3 focal-onset seizure trials showed modest efficacy, failing primary endpoints in two of three pivotal studies. Recent LGS Phase 3 trials illustrate substantial placebo drop-seizure reductions (~15-22% in GWPCARE3/4 and soticlestat's negative LGS study) and require ~12-15% median separation for significance at N=252. Because the study remained recruiting in late October 2026 ahead of a February 2027 target date, primary completion will likely slip into mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: In pivotal Phase 3 trials of adjunctive therapies for Lennox-Gastaut syndrome such as cannabidiol (GWPCARE3) and fenfluramine, placebo median drop-seizure reductions ranged roughly from 10% to 22%.
Carisbamate previously failed to achieve statistically significant primary seizure reduction at 300 mg/day in one of two parallel Phase 3 focal epilepsy trials (Sperling et al. 2010).

reason: Phase 2 COAST benefits were amplified by an unusually weak durvalumab control arm (median PFS ~6-7 months), whereas Phase 3 EGFR/ALK wild-type post-cCRT durvalumab control arms typically achieve ~17 months median PFS.
rationale: PACIFIC-9 tests two combinations (durvalumab+oleclumab and durvalumab+monalizumab) against durvalumab+placebo in EGFR/ALK wild-type Stage III unresectable NSCLC post-cCRT, giving two shots at meeting a primary PFS comparison. While Phase 2 COAST showed promising PFS HRs (0.44 and 0.42 initially, ~0.65 updated), its open-label durvalumab control markedly underperformed (median PFS ~6.3-7.3 months vs 16.8 months in PACIFIC). Moreover, monalizumab failed Phase 3 INTERLINK-1, and post-cCRT intensification trials (SKYSCRAPER-03, KEYLYNK-012) have repeatedly missed against strong PD-(L)1 control performance.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 PACIFIC trial, consolidation durvalumab after concurrent chemoradiotherapy achieved a median BICR progression-free survival of 16.8 months.
In the Phase 2 COAST trial, the durvalumab monotherapy control arm had a median PFS of 6.3 months at primary analysis (7.3 months with extended follow-up).

reason: Systemic complement Factor B inhibition has modest expected impact on preventing conversion to composite iRORA or late AMD (which includes neovascular AMD in fellow eyes of nAMD patients) in a ~146-168 patient trial.
rationale: This completed Phase 2 proof-of-concept study evaluates oral iptacopan (Factor B inhibitor) in ~146-168 patients with high-risk early/intermediate AMD and fellow-eye neovascular AMD. While intravitreal C3/C5 inhibitors modestly slow established geographic atrophy growth (~14-20%), systemic complement inhibition has yet to prove efficacy in preventing AMD progression, and the composite primary endpoint includes conversion to late AMD—meaning exudative MNV events in fellow-nAMD eyes dilute any anti-atrophic effect. With ~50 expected conversion events, only a large hazard reduction (HR <0.58) reaches significance.

assumptions.claim: Eyes with intermediate AMD and fellow-eye neovascular AMD plus OCT high-risk features experience roughly 25-40% cumulative progression to nascent atrophy/iRORA or late AMD over 24 months.
Intravitreal complement inhibitors (pegcetacoplan in OAKS/DERBY) slowed GA lesion growth by ~17-22% over 24 months without reducing conversion to exudative AMD.

reason: Final enrollment reached only 64 participants across three arms (~21 per arm), severely limiting statistical power to achieve significance simultaneously on both co-primary outcomes (IIEF and EHS).
rationale: This completed single-site Australian nutraceutical trial randomized 64 men across three arms (Testofen 300 mg, Testofen 600 mg, placebo; ~21 per arm) with two registered primary outcomes: IIEF-15 and the 4-point Erection Hardness Score (EHS). Although prior Gencor-sponsored fenugreek extract trials (Steels 2011, Rao 2016) reported significant improvements on subjective sexual-function and AMS questionnaires, meeting both IIEF and coarse EHS superiority in the same dose arm with ~21 subjects per group faces steep statistical hurdles alongside substantial placebo response in mild-to-moderate ED.

assumptions.claim: Earlier randomized trials of Testofen 600 mg/day in aging males (Rao et al. 2016) reported statistically significant improvements in AMS and self-reported sexual function scores vs placebo over 12 weeks.

reason: With ~81 patients per arm, sampling variation in remission rates is the primary residual risk to crossing the non-inferiority margin despite equivalent IL-5 neutralization.
rationale: OCEAN mirrors the Phase 3 MANDARA non-inferiority design (BVAS=0 and OCS <=4 mg/day at weeks 36 and 52) comparing twice-yearly anti-IL-5 depemokimab against monthly anti-IL-5 mepolizumab in 163 EGPA patients. Depemokimab neutralizes the exact same cytokine as mepolizumab with higher affinity and proven Phase 3 efficacy in eosinophilic asthma (SWIFT-1/2) and CRSwNP (ANCHOR-1/2). In MANDARA (N=140), mepolizumab achieved ~56-57% remission and benralizumab easily met the -25% non-inferiority margin; with N=163 and equivalent pathway blockade, statistical power exceeds 80%.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 MANDARA non-inferiority trial in EGPA using the identical primary endpoint (BVAS=0 and OCS <=4 mg/day at weeks 36 and 52), the mepolizumab 300 mg arm achieved approximately 56-57% remission against a -25 percentage point margin.
Depemokimab met primary efficacy endpoints across replicate Phase 3 trials in severe eosinophilic asthma (SWIFT-1 and SWIFT-2).

reason: This FDA-discussed pediatric esomeprazole maintenance study has already completed enrollment and follow-up, making timely ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by AstraZeneca highly likely before August 2027.
rationale: NCT05267613 is an AstraZeneca-sponsored US regulatory pediatric Phase 3 trial already marked completed with primary and study completion in August 2026. Because follow-up is finished, termination is virtually ruled out and substantive post-completion outcome amendments are rare. Under FDAAA 801 timelines (12 months from primary completion, due August 10, 2027) and AstraZeneca's strong compliance track record, results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 31, 2027 is very probable.

reason: Induced sputum absolute neutrophil counts in stable COPD exhibit high within-subject biological and processing variability that can obscure moderate airway PDE3/4 anti-inflammatory effects.
rationale: Ensifentrine is an FDA-approved nebulized dual PDE3/4 inhibitor (ENHANCE-1/2). Earlier human LPS-challenge work (Franciosi et al. 2013) demonstrated significant sputum neutrophil reductions with inhaled ensifentrine, and oral PDE4 inhibition (roflumilast) reduced COPD sputum neutrophils by ~35% in crossover studies. A 56-patient two-period crossover provides solid paired power (~80% for moderate effect sizes), though induced sputum absolute cell counts in chronic COPD remain noisy. Secondary spirometry (FEV1 at 4 weeks) benefits from ensifentrine's well-established ~90-140 mL post-dose bronchodilation.

assumptions.claim: In an earlier human inhaled LPS challenge study (Franciosi et al. 2013), nebulized ensifentrine (RPL554) significantly reduced induced sputum neutrophil counts compared with placebo.
In the Phase 3 ENHANCE-1 and ENHANCE-2 trials, nebulized ensifentrine 3 mg BID produced statistically significant FEV1 improvements with placebo-like adverse event discontinuation rates.

reason: Uncontrolled Phase 2 VIRO-15 PFS gains may reflect patient selection and platinum-doublet rechallenge rather than true viral platinum resensitization, while platinum-refractory tumors often progress rapidly on platinum.
rationale: OnPrime compares intraperitoneal Olvi-Vec followed by platinum-doublet plus bevacizumab against single-agent non-platinum chemotherapy plus bevacizumab in 186 heavily pretreated (>=3 prior lines, prior bevacizumab) PRROC patients. Although oncolytic viruses rarely succeed in randomized Phase 3 oncology trials and Phase 2 VIRO-15 was single-arm (N=27, median PFS 11.0 months), the experimental arm administers doublet platinum chemotherapy against single-agent non-platinum therapy, providing partial cytotoxic activity in patients with longer treatment-free intervals since prior platinum, balanced by poor activity in truly refractory disease.

assumptions.claim: In the single-arm Phase 2 VIRO-15 trial in heavily pretreated PRROC, Olvi-Vec followed by chemotherapy plus/minus bevacizumab reported a median PFS of 11.0 months.
Single-agent non-platinum chemotherapy in >=3rd-line bevacizumab-pretreated platinum-resistant ovarian cancer typically achieves median PFS around 3.5 to 5.5 months.

reason: Because enrollment of implanted cohorts is already complete (active, not recruiting) with fixed 12-to-24-month post-implant follow-up ending late 2026, completion should stay near schedule with moderate results posting by August 2027.
rationale: This NINDS-supported NeuroPace RNS feasibility trial in LGS is already active, not recruiting across six US epilepsy centers with primary completion registered for November 30, 2026 and study completion December 31, 2026. Fixed post-implant evaluation windows make >90-day registry delays past February 2027 relatively unlikely (~25%) and early termination very unlikely. Because FDAAA results posting is due 12 months after primary completion (November 2027), posting roughly three months early by August 31, 2027 has moderate probability.

reason: Serial coronary CT angiography measurements of total atheroma volume carry imaging noise and attrition over 24 months in lower-risk primary prevention patients already on optimized statins.
rationale: Inclisiran reliably lowers LDL-C by roughly 50% on top of maximally tolerated statin therapy with twice-yearly clinic-administered dosing ensuring high adherence over 24 months. Prior PCSK9-targeted imaging trials (GLAGOV, PACMAN-AMI, HUYGENS, ARCHITECT) consistently demonstrated significant coronary atheroma regression proportional to achieved LDL-C lowering. With 610 randomized participants with CT-adapted Leaman score >5 and baseline LDL-C >=55 mg/dL followed for two years, VICTORION-PLAQUE has strong statistical power to detect a 4 to 6 percentage-point difference in percent change in total coronary atheroma volume.

assumptions.claim: Inclisiran 300 mg reduces LDL-C by approximately 50% relative to placebo on top of maximally tolerated statins.
Intensive PCSK9-pathway LDL-C lowering produces statistically significant coronary atheroma regression versus statin monotherapy over 52 to 76 weeks.

reason: Requiring simultaneous fulfillment of all four stringent composite criteria including Breg >=3% and corticosteroid-free reduced immunosuppression at Day 367 creates a high hurdle in a small open-label cohort.
rationale: Donor modified immune cells (MIC) showed promising Breg induction and immunosuppression minimization without de novo DSA in the single-arm Phase 1 TOL-1 study. Because standard-of-care kidney transplant regimens routinely maintain corticosteroids or standard MPA dosing and rarely induce Breg >=3%, the control responder rate on the four-part composite will be near zero, giving leverage to an open-label individualized weaning arm. However, cell therapy translation from Phase 1 to randomized Phase 2 often sees attenuated biomarker and steroid-withdrawal success, and still-recruiting status in late 2026 implies substantial completion delay given the 367-day endpoint.

assumptions.claim: Pre-transplant donor-derived modified immune cell infusion in Phase 1 was safe and associated with increased regulatory B cells and absence of de novo donor-specific antibodies.

reason: Historical randomized trials comparing catheter-directed thrombolysis with surgery in acute limb ischemia show very similar 30-day limb-salvage rates around 85-90%, leaving 170 patients underpowered for superiority unless tested for non-inferiority.
rationale: Catheter-directed thrombolysis and surgical revascularization achieved comparable 30-day amputation-free rates (~85-90%) in classic ALI trials such as TOPAS and STILE. With 170 patients, true superiority on 30-day amputation avoidance is unlikely unless open-label surgical selection favors thrombolysis, whereas a pre-specified non-inferiority hypothesis—matching the sponsor's prior FRIDOM and FRIDA trials of Fortelyzin in STEMI and stroke—would have a high chance of success. Because the registry record leaves superiority versus non-inferiority unspecified, overall probability of meeting the trial's own primary hypothesis is near even.

assumptions.claim: Recombinant non-immunogenic staphylokinase (Fortelyzin) previously met non-inferiority primary hypotheses in Russian multicenter randomized trials in acute ischemic stroke and STEMI.
Catheter-directed thrombolysis and open surgery produce similar 30-day amputation-free survival rates of roughly 85-90% in Rutherford I to IIb acute limb ischemia.

reason: Masupirdine is a 5-HT6 antagonist pivoted to Alzheimer's agitation after failing its Phase 2 cognitive trial on the basis of post-hoc NPI subgroup signals, which rarely replicate against large CMAI placebo responses.
rationale: Masupirdine (SUVN-502), a selective 5-HT6 receptor antagonist, missed its primary cognitive endpoint in a 564-patient Phase 2a Alzheimer's trial (NCT02580305), and this Phase 3 agitation program rests on post-hoc subgroup analyses of NPI agitation/aggression items. Selective 5-HT6 antagonists (idalopirdine, intepirdine, masupirdine) have consistently failed prospective Phase 3 Alzheimer's trials, and Alzheimer's agitation studies using CMAI suffer from large caregiver placebo effects (~9-14 points). Testing two doses across 375 patients (~125 per arm) provides modest power unless true drug efficacy approaches that of brexpiprazole.

assumptions.claim: Masupirdine failed to meet its primary ADAS-Cog11 endpoint in its Phase 2a Alzheimer's disease study, with the agitation hypothesis derived from post-hoc NPI subgroup analyses.
Placebo arms in 12-week randomized trials of Alzheimer's agitation consistently exhibit substantial improvements on CMAI scores.

reason: Subretinal vitrectomy delivery and macular pigmentary or inflammatory changes in a multi-surgeon global trial can cause modest early letter loss relative to nonsurgical intravitreal aflibercept, narrowing the non-inferiority margin.
rationale: ABBV-RGX-314 expresses an anti-VEGF Fab via subretinal AAV8 delivery and demonstrated durable visual acuity maintenance with 60-80% reductions in supplemental anti-VEGF injections in Phase 1/2a nAMD cohorts. Enrolling pseudophakic anti-VEGF-responsive eyes and permitting supplemental anti-VEGF rescue injections protects Week 54 BCVA against severe undertreatment, giving two active dose arms (~245 eyes each) solid power to show non-inferiority (typically -4.5 ETDRS letters) against aflibercept. The main risk is vitrectomy-related surgical variability across 181 global sites slightly depressing mean BCVA versus non-surgical aflibercept; superiority on key secondary BCVA improvement is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Subretinal RGX-314 maintained stable to slightly improved mean BCVA over 1 to 2 years while substantially reducing anti-VEGF injection burden in Phase 1/2a wet AMD cohorts.
Previously treated anti-VEGF-responsive wet AMD eyes maintained on aflibercept typically show near-zero (+0 to +2 ETDRS letters) mean BCVA change over one year.

reason: Splitting 64 patients across ascending TS23 dose cohorts and placebo yields small per-dose sample sizes where lower ascending doses may have submaximal fibrinolytic activity at 48 hours.
rationale: TS23 is a monoclonal antibody that inactivates alpha2-antiplasmin, promoting endogenous plasmin-mediated thrombus dissolution without exogenous plasminogen activators, and showed dose-dependent alpha2-antiplasmin depletion and D-dimer elevation in Phase 1. RV/LV ratio on CTPA at 48 hours is a sensitive continuous imaging biomarker in intermediate-risk PE (baseline >0.9), where heparin alone lowers RV/LV by ~0.12-0.18 while effective thrombolysis lowers it by ~0.30-0.42. Although the mechanism is strong, splitting 64 subjects across ascending doses limits statistical power for individual dose comparisons against placebo.

assumptions.claim: TS23 caused dose-dependent inactivation of alpha2-antiplasmin and endogenous thrombus lysis biomarkers without major bleeding in Phase 1 healthy volunteers.
Standard anticoagulation alone reduces the RV/LV diameter ratio by approximately 0.10 to 0.20 over 24 to 48 hours in intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism.

reason: Detecting statistically significant superiority on both ADAS-Cog and CDR-SB co-primary endpoints at 28 weeks as add-on to cholinesterase inhibitors is severely underpowered with only 120 mild Alzheimer's patients.
rationale: Oral EX039 is an investigational small molecule tested at a single Taiwanese site in 120 mild Alzheimer's patients already receiving background acetylcholinesterase inhibitors. Meeting both registered primary outcomes—ADAS-Cog and CDR-SB change at Week 28—is exceptionally difficult: background AChEI blunts symptomatic separation, 28 weeks allows minimal placebo CDR-SB progression (~0.6-0.9 points), and 60 patients per arm provides minimal statistical power for dual cognitive and functional co-primaries. Furthermore, still recruiting in late October 2026 with a 28-week treatment period makes substantial primary completion delay highly likely.

assumptions.claim: Mild Alzheimer's patients on stable acetylcholinesterase inhibitors typically worsen by roughly 1.5 to 2.5 points on ADAS-Cog over 24 to 28 weeks on placebo.

reason: A 3:1 randomization with only about 211 placebo patients in well-compensated MELD <12 cirrhosis limits statistical efficiency unless resmetirom achieves a large hazard reduction (>30-35%) on hard hepatic decompensation events within 3 years.
rationale: Resmetirom 80 mg is FDA-approved for non-cirrhotic F2-F3 MASH after significantly improving NASH resolution and fibrosis in MAESTRO-NASH, and improved MRE liver stiffness and liver volume in an open-label Child-Pugh A cirrhosis cohort of MAESTRO-NAFLD-1. However, reversing portal hypertension and preventing clinical decompensation in established F4 cirrhosis within ~3 years has defeated multiple MASH agents (selonsertib, simtuzumab, obeticholic acid, belapectin). Moreover, 3:1 randomization (634 vs 211) reduces statistical information per event by 25% compared with 1:1 allocation, requiring a relatively large hazard ratio improvement (~0.60-0.68) across ~120-140 events to achieve p<0.05.

assumptions.claim: Resmetirom 80 mg significantly improved NASH resolution and at least one-stage fibrosis reduction at Week 52 in non-cirrhotic F2-F3 NASH.
Well-compensated Child-Pugh A NASH cirrhosis cohorts with baseline MELD <12 experience cumulative clinical hepatic decompensation/MELD >=15 event rates of roughly 5-7% per year.

reason: Splitting 122 participants across NMDAR and LGI1 cohorts leaves roughly 30 patients per arm per cohort against active background immunotherapies, requiring very large responder differences, especially if both cohort primaries must succeed.
rationale: IL-6 receptor blockade has observational support (tocilizumab in rituximab-refractory autoimmune encephalitis) for curbing plasmablast antibody production and neuroinflammation in NMDAR and LGI1 encephalitis. However, Cielo divides 122 patients across two distinct cohorts (~61 each, ~30 per arm), while standard first- and second-line immunotherapies already produce substantial mRS recovery, creating high variance and requiring ~30 percentage-point responder gains for cohort-level significance. Under the benchmark rule requiring all co-primary Part 1 outcomes (both NMDAR Week 24 and LGI1 Week 52) to be met, joint probability of success is modest.

assumptions.claim: Observational studies of IL-6 receptor blockade with tocilizumab reported improved mRS outcomes in rituximab-refractory autoimmune encephalitis.

reason: With only 20 neonates per arm evaluated on a binary 24-month death or moderate/severe disability outcome, statistical significance requires an implausibly large absolute risk reduction of roughly 35-40 percentage points.
rationale: Sovateltide (endothelin-B receptor agonist) was reported by Pharmazz to improve neurological outcomes in Indian Phase 2 and Phase 3 acute ischemic stroke trials, motivating translational testing in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy. Nevertheless, neonatal HIE neuroprotection trials in low- and middle-income settings (such as HELIX) have shown high ~50% rates of 18-24 month death or disability that resist pharmacologic or cooling interventions, and N=40 (20 per arm) has <25% power unless true absolute risk reduction exceeds 35 percentage points. Still-recruiting registry status in October 2026 alongside a 24-month endpoint also signals likely completion delay.

assumptions.claim: Moderate-to-severe neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy in Indian tertiary neonatal units carries an 18-to-24-month death or moderate/severe disability rate of roughly 45-55%.
Sovateltide reported statistically significant neurological recovery improvements in Indian multicenter acute ischemic stroke trials.

reason: Higher rates of mezigdomide-induced neutropenia and infection could require frequent dose reductions or discontinuations that attenuate the progression-free survival advantage over pomalidomide.
rationale: Mezigdomide is a next-generation cereblon E3 ligase modulator with substantially stronger Ikaros/Aiolos degradation and antimyeloma potency than pomalidomide. In Phase 1/2 cohorts (CC-92480-MM-002), MeziVd produced high response rates (>75%) and deep responses in lenalidomide-exposed 1-3 prior line RRMM. Against a PVd control with expected median PFS around 12-14 months, 810 patients provide high power to detect an HR near 0.65. Because the two-stage study remained recruiting in late 2026, primary completion will likely slip past January 2027, though an event-driven interim PFS readout remains possible in 2027.

assumptions.claim: In OPTIMISMM, the PVd regimen achieved a median progression-free survival of 11.2 months in relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma.
In DREAMM-7, the PVd control arm achieved a median progression-free survival of 13.4 months in patients with at least one prior line of therapy.

reason: Multiparametric MRI quantification of renal sinus fat in CKD patients can exhibit technical measurement variability that narrows signal-to-noise despite robust systemic weight loss.
rationale: Tirzepatide induces substantial weight loss (12-18%) and marked mobilization of visceral and ectopic adipose depots, as demonstrated by large liver and visceral fat reductions in SURPASS-3 MRI. Renal sinus fat tracks closely with visceral adiposity, so 52 weeks of tirzepatide in 134 participants with BMI >=27 and CKD has high statistical power to show a ~14 percentage point relative reduction over placebo, alongside an almost certain win on secondary body weight reduction. Because the trial completed in July 2026, results posting and congress presentation by mid-2027 are highly likely.

assumptions.claim: Tirzepatide produced large, statistically significant reductions in liver fat content and visceral adipose tissue volume at 52 weeks in the SURPASS-3 MRI substudy.
Tirzepatide produced substantial 72-week percent reductions in body weight versus placebo in adults with obesity or overweight in SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-2.

reason: With only 17 enrolled participants split 2:1 (roughly 11 active versus 6 placebo), the study lacks statistical power to achieve two-sided p<0.05 even if true response exceeds placebo by 35 percentage points.
rationale: Topical/mucosal artesunate has shown encouraging ~50-65% histologic regression rates in early-phase HPV-associated cervical and anal intraepithelial neoplasia studies compared with ~15-25% spontaneous regression on placebo. However, enrollment closed at only 17 total participants randomized 2:1 (~11 artesunate, 6 placebo). At two-sided alpha=0.05, even a true 55% versus 20% response rate yields less than 30% statistical power, and a single spontaneous responder in the 6-patient placebo arm requires 8-9 of 11 active responders for significance.

assumptions.claim: Self-administered vaginal artesunate inserts demonstrated histologic regression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2/3 in a first-in-human Phase 1 trial.

reason: With only 12 patients per arm all receiving effective standard IV N-acetylcysteine, extreme right-skewed variability in Day 3 ALT trajectories leaves minimal power to demonstrate superiority.
rationale: This exploratory single-center trial enrolls only 24 acute acetaminophen overdose patients (12 per arm), all treated with standard intravenous N-acetylcysteine while excluding severe organ failure or transplant-criteria cases. Standard NAC already prevents major hepatotoxicity in most early presenters, while occasional late presenters create extreme baseline-to-Day-3 ALT variance (>100% SD). Consequently, demonstrating a statistically significant reduction in Day 3 percent ALT change or clinical hepatic failure with N=24 is unlikely, and ongoing single-site recruitment makes completion delays probable.

assumptions.claim: Intravenous N-acetylcysteine prevents severe hepatotoxicity in the large majority of acute acetaminophen overdose patients when initiated promptly.

reason: Antegrade intracoronary AAV gene delivery historically achieves low cardiomyocyte transduction in humans, making significant clinical or composite improvements over modern heart failure therapy unlikely.
rationale: AB-1002 delivers constitutively active protein phosphatase-1 inhibitor-1 via single antegrade intracoronary AAV2i8 infusion across three arms (n=30-50 each) in stable NYHA Class III non-ischemic HFrEF on contemporary medical therapy. Prior intracoronary AAV trials in HFrEF (such as CUPID 2 with AAV1/SERCA2a) failed to show clinical benefit due to limited myocardial transduction efficiency. Whether analyzed via a hierarchical composite across the four registered primary measures or individually, N<=50 per arm over 52 weeks (~7-8% control CV mortality) provides modest power and faces high biological risk.

assumptions.claim: Intracoronary AAV1/SERCA2a gene therapy did not improve recurrent heart failure events or terminal events compared with placebo in the Phase 2b CUPID 2 trial.

reason: After complete surgical resection removes bulk tumor antigen, adding LAG-3 blockade to PD-1 inhibition may confer limited incremental relapse protection over pembrolizumab while increasing immune-related discontinuations.
rationale: Although fianlimab plus cemiplimab showed high response rates in metastatic melanoma cohorts and anti-LAG-3 plus anti-PD-1 is validated in advanced disease (RELATIVITY-047), dual checkpoint combinations have repeatedly struggled to beat PD-1 monotherapy in the post-resection adjuvant setting (e.g., CheckMate 915, KEYVIBE-010, RELATIVITY-098) where minimal residual tumor limits T-cell reinvigoration and added immune toxicity (~20% vs ~13% AE discontinuations) drives early treatment cessation. Including lower-risk Stage IIB/IIC alongside Stage III/IV further slows event accrual and may dilute relative hazard reduction.

assumptions.claim: Adjuvant pembrolizumab achieved a 12-month recurrence-free survival rate of 75.4% in resected Stage III melanoma in KEYNOTE-054.
Adjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab failed to significantly improve recurrence-free survival over nivolumab monotherapy in resected Stage IIIB-IV melanoma in CheckMate 915.

reason: High and regionally variable Week 52 SRI(4) placebo response rates on background immunosuppressants and corticosteroids in global SLE trials can compress the observed treatment difference below ~8.5 percentage points.
rationale: Deucravacitinib allosterically inhibits TYK2, blocking Type I interferon and IL-12/23 signaling—a pathway clinically validated in SLE by anifrolumab. In the Phase 2 PAISLEY trial (N=363), deucravacitinib 3 mg BID improved SRI(4) by >20 percentage points over placebo at Weeks 32 and 48 and also improved BICLA, CLASI, and LLDAS with good tolerability. Allowing for typical Phase 3 effect shrinkage and ~43% placebo SRI(4) response across 22 countries, N=516 (~258 per arm, needing ~8.5 percentage points for p<0.05) gives roughly 65% probability of success, with topline expected shortly after October 2026 primary completion.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 PAISLEY trial, deucravacitinib 3 mg twice daily met the primary endpoint of SRI(4) response at Week 32 and improved SRI(4) and BICLA responses at Week 48 versus placebo.

reason: Elevated placebo SRI(4) responder rates on background antimalarials, immunosuppressants, and steroids across multinational SLE sites could narrow the treatment delta below statistical significance.
rationale: POETYK SLE-2 is the replicate Phase 3 sister study to POETYK SLE-1 (N=513, ~256 per arm) testing TYK2 inhibition with deucravacitinib in active moderate-to-severe SLE. Strong Phase 2 PAISLEY efficacy on SRI(4) and BICLA and mechanistic inhibition of Type I IFN signaling support a true Week 52 SRI(4) benefit of ~13-14 percentage points after Phase 3 attenuation, versus an ~8.5 percentage point threshold for statistical significance. With both sister trials completing primary follow-up in October 2026, topline results in early 2027 and a supplemental filing in 2027 if positive are plausible.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 PAISLEY trial, deucravacitinib 3 mg twice daily significantly increased SRI(4) and BICLA response rates compared with placebo in active SLE.

reason: Sham intracordal injections and voice care produce substantial subjective VHI-10 placebo improvements while refractory vocal fold sulcus patients may dilute the antifibrotic drug signal in a 62-patient sample.
rationale: KP-100LI (intracordal recombinant human HGF) showed encouraging voice and mucosal wave improvements in a small open-label Japanese Phase 1/2 study, and HGF has plausible antifibrotic activity in vocal fold lamina propria.
