However, moving from uncontrolled early data to a 62-patient (31 per arm) double-blind sham-injected trial using a subjective patient-reported primary outcome (VHI-10 percent improvement) introduces notable sham-response risk and wide inter-patient SD (~34%), compounded by enrolling structurally refractory vocal fold sulcus alongside vocal fold scar. Japanese biotech disclosure norms make a topline release by mid-2027 highly likely.

assumptions.claim: Intracordal administration of recombinant human hepatocyte growth factor was evaluated in an open-label Phase 1/2 clinical trial in patients with vocal fold scar and sulcus in Japan.

reason: Splitting 436 participants across three arms (~145 each for monthly ianalumab and placebo) requires an observed Week 60 SRI-4 difference above ~11.4 percentage points amidst typical SLE placebo variability.
rationale: Ianalumab combines afucosylated ADCC-mediated B-cell depletion with BAFF-receptor blockade, uniting two clinically validated mechanisms in SLE (belimumab BAFF inhibition and obinutuzumab B-cell depletion) after positive Phase 2 results in SLE and Sjögren's disease. A true Week 60 SRI-4 advantage of ~15 percentage points is plausible, aided by mandatory steroid maintenance/reduction windows. The main limitation is sample size per arm (~145 monthly vs ~145 placebo across 3 arms), which raises the significance hurdle to ~11.4 percentage points. With March 2027 primary completion, topline readout is split between Q2 and H2 2027.

assumptions.claim: Belimumab significantly increased Week 52 SRI-4 response rates compared with placebo on top of standard therapy in active SLE in BLISS-52.
Ianalumab met its primary dose-response efficacy endpoint at 24 weeks in a randomized Phase 2b trial in primary Sjögren's syndrome.

reason: Enrolling hospitalized pediatric patients down to 9 months of age with acute serious Gram-negative infections within narrow prior-antibiotic windows frequently causes substantial recruitment delays.
rationale: This Phase 2a pediatric pharmacokinetic and safety trial of aztreonam-avibactam requires 48 hospitalized children across four age cohorts down to 9 months, with strict limits on prior systemic antibiotic exposure (<24 hours unless failing >48 hours). Pediatric hospital-acquired pneumonia, bloodstream, and intra-abdominal infection trials consistently recruit slowly, especially in the youngest sequentially opened cohorts. With status still recruiting in late October 2026 and registered primary completion on 31 March 2027, completion slipping past late June 2027 is likely, while termination is unlikely given regulatory pediatric commitments.

reason: With roughly 60 patients per arm across two active doses and high pediatric IBS-C placebo response rates, achieving statistical significance on the stringent composite responder endpoint is challenging.
rationale: Tenapanor demonstrated clear efficacy in adult IBS-C trials (T3MPO-1 and T3MPO-2), with composite responder advantages of roughly 8 to 13 percentage points over placebo. However, pediatric IBS-C trials characteristically exhibit elevated placebo responder rates (25%-35%), and with 180 total participants split across two active doses and placebo (~60 per arm), an observed improvement of roughly 18 percentage points is needed for significance, especially with multiplicity control across two doses. Because the trial completed in August 2026, public readout and ClinicalTrials.gov posting in 2027 are highly likely.

assumptions.claim: Tenapanor 50 mg BID met the primary 6/12-week combined responder endpoint against placebo in both adult Phase 3 IBS-C trials T3MPO-1 and T3MPO-2.
Diarrhea was the most common adverse event leading to treatment discontinuation with tenapanor 50 mg BID in adult Phase 3 IBS-C studies.

reason: Demonstrating statistically significant PFS superiority over an active same-class PI3K-alpha inhibitor (alpelisib) plus fulvestrant requires substantial potency or dose-intensity advantages.
rationale: INAVO121 compares inavolisib plus fulvestrant directly against active-control alpelisib plus fulvestrant in post-CDK4/6i PIK3CA-mutated HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer. Unlike alpelisib, which suffers ~20%-25% adverse-event discontinuations and frequent dose interruptions that erode real-world PFS (~6-7 months post-CDK4/6i in BYLieve), inavolisib selectively degrades mutant p110-alpha and showed low discontinuation rates in INAVO120. Superior tolerability and sustained target inhibition give inavolisib a credible edge (expected HR ~0.76), though beating an active PI3K-alpha comparator remains non-trivial. Main study enrollment is complete, supporting a 2027 readout, though the open DDI substudy may delay registry completion status.

assumptions.claim: Alpelisib plus fulvestrant showed high rates of adverse-event treatment discontinuation (approximately 21% to 25%) in SOLAR-1 and BYLieve.
Inavolisib demonstrated strong PFS efficacy and low adverse-event discontinuation when combined with palbociclib and fulvestrant in PIK3CA-mutated HR+/HER2- breast cancer in INAVO120.

reason: High and variable 12-month SRI-4 placebo response rates on background immunosuppressants and belimumab frequently obscure modest treatment effects in global Phase 3 lupus trials.
rationale: OPUS-1 evaluates oral S1P1 modulator cenerimod on Month-12 SRI-4 response (using mSLEDAI-2K excluding leukopenia) in 470 patients with moderate-to-severe SLE. In the Phase 2b CARE trial (NCT03742037), cenerimod 4 mg showed encouraging nominal mSLEDAI-2K improvements at Month 6, particularly in high disease-activity/interferon subgroups, but missed multiplicity-adjusted primary significance across doses. Phase 3 SLE trials allowing broad background therapy (including mycophenolate and belimumab) routinely see ~45%-50% placebo SRI-4 response, requiring ~9 percentage points separation for significance at N=235/arm. Being active, not recruiting with fixed 12-month follow-up ending March 2027, on-time completion is likely.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2b CARE study in SLE, cenerimod 4 mg showed nominal reduction in mSLEDAI-2K at Month 6 versus placebo.

reason: Because eligibility selects patients who already responded to initial corticosteroids prior to randomization, higher-than-expected 12-month remission in the control arm could narrow the treatment difference.
rationale: Ianalumab (VAY736) combines enhanced ADCC-mediated B-cell depletion with BAFF-R blockade, directly targeting both autoantibody-producing B-cell lineages and the BAFF surge implicated in relapse after rituximab in ITP. Earlier trials of B-cell depletion plus first-line corticosteroids demonstrated ~20-25 percentage-point gains in sustained 6- to 12-month off-treatment response over steroids alone, and dual BAFF-R inhibition should further improve durability. Testing two doses (~75 patients per arm) provides solid power on the amended SROT-12 endpoint and key secondary time to treatment failure. With primary completion in October 2026, topline disclosure by mid-2027 is very likely.

assumptions.claim: Adding B-cell depletion with rituximab to first-line dexamethasone significantly increased sustained 6- and 12-month platelet response rates compared with dexamethasone monotherapy in randomized primary ITP trials.

reason: Tumor treating fields confer only a modest overall survival benefit on top of gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel in locally advanced pancreatic cancer, leaving moderate risk of missing statistical significance.
rationale: This 512-patient Chinese Phase 3 trial mirrors the global PANOVA-3 study (NCT03377491), which demonstrated a modest but statistically significant overall survival improvement when adding Tumor Treating Fields to gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel in locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma (median OS ~16.2 vs 14.2 months, HR ~0.82), without significant PFS separation. Consequently, conditional on reporting, probability of meeting OS is slightly above even (~58%), with lower probability on key secondary PFS. Operationally, enrolling 512 locally advanced patients across just 5 sites and remaining recruiting in October 2026 points to high likelihood of delayed completion and slow public disclosure.

assumptions.claim: Gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel produces median overall survival of approximately 14 to 19 months in first-line locally advanced pancreatic cancer clinical trials.

reason: Sampling variability in Week-18 radiological response rates could cause the confidence interval to narrowly cross a biosimilar equivalence margin despite analytical similarity.
rationale: Phase 3 clinical equivalence trials of analytically characterized bevacizumab biosimilars combined with carboplatin and paclitaxel in advanced non-squamous NSCLC have an established track record of high success (>85%), and an enrollment of 620 patients provides robust precision around Week-18 independent-review ORR (~42%-48%). With the trial still listed as recruiting across 28 Russian sites in late October 2026 against a December 2026 primary completion date, registry delays beyond March 2027 are moderately likely and ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by Russian domestic sponsors is historically rare.

assumptions.claim: Randomized Phase 3 NSCLC equivalence studies of bevacizumab biosimilars plus paclitaxel and carboplatin with roughly 600 to 700 patients reliably establish equivalence on Week-18 ORR.

reason: Allowing enrollment up to 96 hours after gout flare onset alongside rescue medication access in both arms risks substantial spontaneous and rescue-driven pain resolution on placebo by 72 hours.
rationale: Acute gout flares are driven by monosodium urate crystal activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, and oral dapansutrile showed promising pain reductions in open-label Phase 2a testing. With 200 active versus 100 placebo patients, a ~6-mm difference on 100-mm VAS at 72 hours achieves statistical significance. However, enrolling flares up to 96 hours after onset and providing rescue medication to all participants increases spontaneous/rescue pain improvement in the placebo arm and dampens oral NLRP3 inhibitor impact after extracellular IL-1beta release. Still recruiting after nearly four years, completion is likely to slip past March 2027.

assumptions.claim: Open-label Phase 2a evaluation of oral dapansutrile in acute gout flare showed marked reductions in target joint VAS pain at Day 3 with good tolerability.

reason: Substantial 12-month SRI-4 placebo response rates on concomitant standard-of-care SLE immunosuppressants make reaching the ~9-percentage-point threshold for significance difficult.
rationale: OPUS-2 is the replicate Phase 3 study to OPUS-1 testing single-dose cenerimod versus placebo on Month-12 SRI-4 (mSLEDAI-2K) in 451 moderate-to-severe SLE patients. While Phase 2b CARE data supported biological activity of cenerimod 4 mg, historical SLE Phase 3 programs frequently stumble due to high placebo response (~45%-50%) on background therapy and heterogeneous organ manifestations, leaving single-trial success probability slightly below 50%. Because OPUS-2 is active, not recruiting with registered primary completion on 31 December 2026, on-time completion and public topline reporting by June 2027 (likely alongside or shortly before OPUS-1) are probable.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2b CARE trial in SLE, cenerimod 4 mg showed nominal reduction in mSLEDAI-2K at Month 6 compared with placebo.

reason: With only about 33 placebo patients and three registered primary outcomes (UAS7, ISS7, and HSS7), chance variability in adolescent placebo improvement could leave one component short of p<0.05.
rationale: Oral BTK inhibitor remibrutinib achieved highly robust Week-12 efficacy and placebo-like tolerability in both adult Phase 3 CSU trials REMIX-1 and REMIX-2, improving UAS7 by ~6.2 to 7.7 points over placebo and meeting UAS7, ISS7, and HSS7 endpoints (p<0.001). CSU pathophysiology is identical in adolescents aged 12-17. With 100 patients randomized 2:1 (67 active, 33 placebo) and SD ~11.5 on UAS7, standard error is ~2.45 points, providing ~70% joint power across UAS7 and its ISS7/HSS7 co-primaries. Being active, not recruiting with primary completion in November 2026, timely readout and supplemental filing in 2027 are likely.

assumptions.claim: Remibrutinib significantly improved Week-12 UAS7, ISS7, and HSS7 compared with placebo in both adult Phase 3 CSU trials REMIX-1 and REMIX-2.
Adverse-event treatment discontinuation rates with remibrutinib were low (~3%) and comparable to placebo in REMIX-1 and REMIX-2.

reason: Requiring success across dual primary endpoints or high sunitinib performance in indolent papillary subsets could dilute the observed progression-free survival difference.
rationale: Zanzalintinib (XL092) inhibits MET, VEGFR, and TAM kinases similarly to cabozantinib. In non-clear cell RCC excluding chromophobe histology, VEGFR/MET TKI plus PD-1 combinations (such as cabozantinib plus nivolumab and lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab) achieve 40-49% response rates and 12-18 month median PFS, whereas sunitinib yields ~5.5-6.0 month median PFS and ~10-13% ORR (as in PAPMET). With 317 patients randomized 2:1 and chromophobe excluded, STELLAR-304 is well powered to beat sunitinib on both PFS and ORR.

assumptions.claim: In SWOG 1500 (PAPMET), sunitinib achieved a median progression-free survival of 5.6 months in metastatic papillary renal cell carcinoma.
Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma is excluded from STELLAR-304 enrollment.

reason: With only 94 randomized pediatric patients, moderate chance variation or viral-driven non-eosinophilic exacerbations could prevent statistical significance despite genuine biological activity.
rationale: Benralizumab reliably depletes blood and airway eosinophils via anti-IL-5Ralpha ADCC and reduced exacerbations by roughly 35-50% in SIROCCO and CALIMA among severe eosinophilic asthma patients aged 12 and older. Pediatric severe eosinophilic asthma shares type 2 pathophysiology, though viral triggers in 6-11 year olds can dilute biologic treatment effects (as seen with mepolizumab in MUPPITS-2) and the sample size of 94 limits statistical power if the hazard ratio is closer to 0.65.

assumptions.claim: DOMINICA enrolls 94 pediatric patients aged 6 to under 18 years randomized 1:1 to benralizumab or placebo.
Benralizumab significantly reduced annual asthma exacerbation rates compared with placebo in the Phase 3 SIROCCO trial.

reason: Factor XIa inhibition added to standard antiplatelet therapy may provide only a modest reduction across heterogeneous non-cardioembolic stroke subtypes such as small-vessel lacunar strokes.
rationale: In Phase 2 AXIOMATIC-SSP, milvexian missed the composite primary endpoint including covert MRI infarcts, though doses of 25-100 mg BID showed numerical ~30% reductions in symptomatic ischemic stroke. With 12,523 participants and ~900 clinical stroke events, LIBREXIA-STROKE is well powered to detect a 15-20% hazard reduction. However, non-cardioembolic stroke includes lacunar and cryptogenic mechanisms less responsive to FXIa inhibition, making statistical success nearly a coin toss despite encouraging Phase 2 symptomatic stroke trends.

assumptions.claim: In AXIOMATIC-SSP, milvexian added to dual antiplatelet therapy did not show a significant dose-response on the composite primary endpoint of symptomatic ischemic stroke or covert brain infarction.
LIBREXIA-STROKE randomizes participants within 48 hours of acute ischemic stroke with NIHSS <= 7 or high-risk TIA with ABCD2 >= 6.

reason: Because this rare-biomarker FGFR2-rearranged cholangiocarcinoma dose-optimization trial was still recruiting in October 2026 against a December 2026 target, primary completion will very likely slip past March 2027.
rationale: FOENIX-CCA4 is an FDA post-marketing randomized Phase 2 dose-optimization study comparing futibatinib 16 mg vs 20 mg in FGFR2-rearranged cholangiocarcinoma without prior FGFR inhibitor exposure. Enrolling 120 biomarker-selected patients across 65 sites is slow given commercial availability of futibatinib and pemigatinib, and the trial remained recruiting in late October 2026 with a registered primary completion of December 2026 and a 12-month follow-up window, making a >90-day registry delay highly probable and results posting by August 2027 unlikely.

assumptions.claim: On snapshot 2026-10-29, NCT05727176 was still listed as recruiting with a registered primary completion date of 2026-12.

reason: Apixaban sets a high antithrombotic bar in atrial fibrillation, and even modest excess cardioembolic stroke risk with Factor XIa inhibition could miss the non-inferiority margin.
rationale: Oral FXIa inhibitor asundexian failed dramatically against apixaban in OCEANIC-AF (HR 3.79 for stroke/systemic embolism). However, milvexian in LIBREXIA-AF uses a much higher, twice-daily dose (100 mg BID) producing substantially greater FXIa inhibition, and the 20,284-patient trial remained active without early DMC termination through October 2026 near its December 2026 completion date, ruling out catastrophic inferiority. Still, achieving formal non-inferiority against apixaban requires tightly matching FXa blockade on thromboembolism, leaving success below 50%.

assumptions.claim: In OCEANIC-AF, the oral Factor XIa inhibitor asundexian was inferior to apixaban for preventing stroke or systemic embolism in atrial fibrillation.
In ARISTOTLE, apixaban demonstrated a stroke or systemic embolism rate of 1.27% per year in patients with atrial fibrillation.

reason: Somatostatin receptor 2 antagonism at bedtime may not overcome alpha-cell suppression during real-world nocturnal hyperinsulinemia enough to significantly cut CGM-detected hypoglycemic episodes.
rationale: ZT-01 is a somatostatin receptor 2 antagonist shown in Phase 1b hypoglycemic clamp studies in type 1 diabetes to augment endogenous glucagon secretion. The crossover design and testing three doses (7, 15, and 22 mg, where any single dose winning meets the round objective) help statistical power. Nonetheless, clamp glucagon restoration often translates modestly to ambulatory nocturnal hypoglycemia prevention when exogenous basal/bolus insulin levels are elevated, and ongoing recruitment in October 2026 points to likely timeline slippage.

assumptions.claim: ZONE is a crossover study evaluating three doses of ZT-01 (7 mg, 15 mg, and 22 mg) against placebo across two 28-day treatment periods.
Eligible participants must have at least 1% CGM time below 54 mg/dL over a 4-week screening period.

reason: Demonstrating a statistically significant 12-month overall survival improvement in 387 allogeneic transplant recipients requires a large hazard reduction rarely achieved by supportive microbiome interventions.
rationale: Higher gut microbiota diversity after alloHCT correlates with lower non-relapse mortality, and MaaT Pharma's enema product MaaT013 showed encouraging activity in steroid-refractory GI-aGvHD. However, PHOEBUS uses overall survival at 12 months as its Phase 2b primary endpoint in 387 patients (~95-105 expected deaths), requiring an ambitious HR near 0.65-0.68 for p<0.05 when relapse mortality is unaffected by microbiota restoration. Moreover, because the trial was still recruiting in October 2026 with 12-month follow-up required, readout before mid-2027 is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: The primary endpoint of PHOEBUS is overall survival at 12 months post allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation in 387 planned patients aged 50 years or older.

reason: Sham intrasphincteric injection and diary monitoring in chronic fecal incontinence historically produce large 40-55% placebo episode reductions that obscure modest cell-therapy benefits.
rationale: Iltamiocel (autologous muscle-derived cells) targets external anal sphincter defects in women with obstetric sphincter injury, a biologically enriched subgroup identified from earlier incontinence studies. Nonetheless, randomized trials of injectable bulking and autologous myoblast therapies in fecal and urinary incontinence repeatedly face substantial sham-injection placebo responses (~40-55% reduction in incontinence episodes at 12 months) and high inter-patient diary variability across 200 participants, keeping the probability of meeting 12-month superiority below 40%.

assumptions.claim: DigniFI evaluates a single injection of 300 million autologous muscle-derived cells versus placebo in 200 adult female participants followed for 12 months.

reason: With 1,946 patients rather than the 5,000+ enrolled in global adjuvant CDK4/6 trials, fewer than expected early recurrence events could limit statistical power at the primary analysis.
rationale: Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibition added to endocrine therapy consistently reduces invasive disease recurrence in HR+/HER2- early breast cancer, as demonstrated by abemaciclib in monarchE (HR ~0.68), ribociclib in NATALEE (HR ~0.75), and dalpiciclib in DAWNA-A. Culmerciclib (TQB3616) is a potent continuous-dosing CDK4/6 inhibitor with proven Phase 3 efficacy in metastatic HR+/HER2- breast cancer in China. Enrolling high-risk post-mastectomy patients (2:1, N=1,946) gives strong probability of meeting IDFS, though OS will remain immature.

assumptions.claim: In monarchE, adjuvant abemaciclib plus endocrine therapy significantly improved invasive disease-free survival compared with endocrine therapy alone in high-risk HR+/HER2- early breast cancer.
NCT05780567 randomizes approximately 1,946 subjects in a 2:1 ratio to TQB3616 plus endocrine therapy versus placebo plus endocrine therapy.

reason: High and variable week-52 BICLA placebo response rates on permissive background immunosuppressants frequently erode treatment differences across replicate Phase 3 lupus trials.
rationale: In the Phase 2 SLEek trial (NCT03978520), oral upadacitinib 30 mg daily met its primary SRI-4 endpoint and improved BICLA response and flare rates through week 48, outperforming historical JAK1/2 inhibition with baricitinib (which split Phase 3 SLE-BRAVE-I/II). Using BICLA at week 52—an endpoint less prone to single-organ scoring artifacts, as shown in TULIP-2—and central eligibility review strengthens SELECT-SLE, though high background-therapy placebo responses keep replicate Phase 3 lupus trials risky.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 SLEek trial (NCT03978520), upadacitinib 30 mg once daily met the primary endpoint of SRI-4 and steroid dose <=10 mg/day at week 24 compared with placebo.
In TULIP-2, anifrolumab achieved a significantly higher week-52 BICLA response rate than placebo (47.8% vs 31.5%).

reason: Although enrollment of 49 patients is complete and registered primary completion is December 2026, tracking confirmed PSA nadir responses can slightly delay final primary completion updates.
rationale: PSMACare is an active, not recruiting Novartis Phase 2 trial (N=49) of 177Lu-PSMA-617 with or without ARPI in conventional-imaging-negative, PSMA-PET-positive CRPC, with registered primary and study completion on 2026-12-23. Because recruitment is finished, termination risk is very low. Roughly a third of oncology Phase 2 trials slip primary completion by >90 days for follow-up cleanup. By 2027-08-31 (about 8 months post-completion), ClinicalTrials.gov results posting is modest since large sponsors typically post closer to the 12-month FDAAA deadline.

assumptions.claim: Novartis typically posts ClinicalTrials.gov results close to the 12-month statutory window after primary completion.

reason: Systemic JAK1 inhibition may produce smaller bronchodilator FEV1 gains than biologics like dupilumab or tezepelumab, leaving ~62 patients per arm underpowered for modest effects.
rationale: Povorcitinib is an oral selective JAK1 inhibitor tested across three doses versus placebo (N=247, ~62/arm) on week-24 pre-BD FEV1 in uncontrolled moderate-to-severe asthma. JAK1 mediates IL-4, IL-13, and TSLP signaling, suggesting real anti-inflammatory activity, but systemic JAK exposures are constrained by class safety tolerability. With between-patient FEV1 change SD near 340 mL, ~62 patients/arm requires ~120 mL improvement for p<0.05 (or ~140 mL with multiplicity). Primary completion is November 2026 (active, not recruiting), making a topline readout by mid-2027 likely, though Phase 3 progression faces high regulatory hurdles for systemic JAKs in asthma.

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in moderate-to-severe asthma trials with baseline bronchodilator reversibility requirements commonly show ~90 to 180 mL pre-BD FEV1 improvement from regression to the mean and ICS-LABA adherence.
Potent upstream Type 2 pathway blockade with tezepelumab improved pre-BD FEV1 by about 130 mL over placebo.

reason: Demonstrating statistically significant PFS superiority of PD-1xLAG-3 bispecific tobemstomig over active pembrolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel with only 83 patients requires an unrealistically large hazard ratio reduction.
rationale: This Roche Phase 2 study (N=83) compares tobemstomig (PD-1xLAG-3 bispecific) plus nab-paclitaxel against active standard-of-care pembrolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel in first-line PD-L1-positive, HER2-low metastatic TNBC. Dual PD-1/LAG-3 blockade has shown limited incremental benefit over PD-1 monotherapy in solid tumors outside melanoma, and with ~56 PFS events, achieving statistical significance requires an observed HR near 0.58-0.65. Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy yields ~7.6-9.7 months median PFS in PD-L1-positive TNBC. Primary completion passed in October 2026, so conference presentation or registry posting during 2027 is likely, while Phase 3 advancement in TNBC is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy achieved a median PFS of 9.7 months in PD-L1 CPS >=10 and 7.6 months in CPS >=1 metastatic TNBC.

reason: KRYSTAL-21 is an FDA post-marketing dose-optimization trial that has finished recruitment with registered completion in late 2026, so it should finish cleanly and post results near the 12-month window.
rationale: KRYSTAL-21 (NCT05853575) is a 200-patient randomized FDA post-marketing requirement study comparing adagrasib 600 mg BID fasted/unrestricted versus 400 mg BID with food in previously treated KRAS G12C-mutant NSCLC. On 2026-10-29 it is active, not recruiting, with primary completion on 2026-10-30 and study completion on 2026-11-30. Because enrollment is complete and regulatory commitment drives execution by Mirati/BMS, early termination and substantive primary endpoint amendments are very unlikely. Roughly 40-45% of such industry PMR studies post results on ClinicalTrials.gov within 10 months of primary completion (by 2027-08-31).

assumptions.claim: Adagrasib received accelerated approval with an FDA post-marketing requirement to compare 600 mg BID with a lower food-adjusted regimen in KRAS G12C NSCLC.

reason: Multicenter western pediatric wheezing cohorts with controller use and high vaccination rates may experience a smaller episode reduction from oral bacterial lysates than earlier single-center studies.
rationale: This completed Phase 2 trial (N=296) evaluates 6 months of daily oral OM-85 bacterial lysate versus placebo in children aged 6 months to 5 years with recurrent wheezing. Prior pediatric trials (including Razi 2010) reported ~30-38% reductions in wheezing episodes with intermittent OM-85, and continuous daily dosing during viral season could maintain mucosal innate immune priming. With ~148 children/arm and ~1.5 episodes per placebo child (~400 total events), an observed rate ratio around 0.77 reaches p<0.05. Because the study completed in September 2026 with US sites, public results in 2027 are likely.

assumptions.claim: OM-85 reduced the rate of wheezing attacks by 37.9% versus placebo over 12 months in preschool children with recurrent wheezing.

reason: Continuing CDK4/6 inhibition after progression on prior CDK4/6 therapy has produced mixed results across agents, and dual ORR/PFS primary endpoints raise the bar for success.
rationale: SPH4336 is an oral CDK4/6 inhibitor tested with endocrine therapy versus placebo plus endocrine therapy in 254 Chinese patients with measurable HR+/HER2- ABC post-CDK4/6i. Prior post-CDK4/6i trials diverged: palbociclib failed in PACE/PALMIRA, whereas ribociclib (MAINTAIN) and abemaciclib (postMONARCH: PFS HR 0.73, measurable ORR 17% vs 7%) succeeded, with stronger benefit when prior CDK4/6i lasted >=12 months. Requiring measurable disease boosts ORR power, but meeting co-primary ORR and PFS depends on SPH4336 potency against CDK4. Still listed as recruiting in October 2026 before a December 2026 completion date, registry delay is probable.

assumptions.claim: In postMONARCH, abemaciclib plus fulvestrant achieved a 17% ORR versus 7% with placebo plus fulvestrant among patients with measurable HR+/HER2- ABC post-CDK4/6 inhibitor.
Continued palbociclib plus fulvestrant failed to improve PFS or ORR over fulvestrant alone after prior CDK4/6 inhibitor progression in PACE.

reason: Cardiac surgery-associated AKI involves multifactorial ischemia, hemolysis, and hemodynamic injury where single-pathway DPEP-1 inhibition with LSALT peptide has unproven clinical efficacy.
rationale: Arch Biopartners' Phase 2 trial (N=240, 120/arm) tests 5-day IV LSALT peptide (a DPEP-1 inhibitor) versus saline to prevent 7-day KDIGO AKI (creatinine and urine output criteria) in high-risk on-pump cardiac surgery. Including KDIGO oliguria criteria in CKD stage 2-3 patients with additional risk factors typically yields 40-55% AKI rates. With 120/arm, achieving p<0.05 requires ~13 percentage points absolute reduction, a high hurdle given historical CSA-AKI trial failures and limited prior human efficacy data. Because follow-up is only 28 days, topline press release shortly after March-June 2027 completion is plausible.

assumptions.claim: High-risk on-pump cardiac surgery cohorts assessed by full KDIGO creatinine and urine output criteria exhibit 7-day AKI rates above 40%.

reason: With high 18-month rPFS rates in deep PSA responders and only a subset of enrolled patients randomized at Cycle 7, random variation could breach the non-inferiority margin.
rationale: LIBERTAS randomizes mCSPC patients achieving PSA <0.2 ng/mL after 6 months of apalutamide plus ADT to apalutamide with intermittent versus continuous ADT, testing co-primary 18-month rPFS non-inferiority and hot-flash score reduction. Deep PSA responders continuing potent AR blockade with apalutamide have ~88-90% 18-month rPFS, and EMBARK proved nonsteroidal AR-inhibitor monotherapy causes far fewer hot flashes than GnRH combination (22% vs 69%) once testosterone/estradiol recover. Primary risk is sampling noise on the rPFS non-inferiority margin if ~260-300 of 420 screened patients were randomized. Superiority on secondary PFS2 is virtually impossible for intermittent ADT.

assumptions.claim: In EMBARK, hot flashes occurred in 21.8% of patients on enzalutamide monotherapy versus 68.8% on enzalutamide plus leuprolide.
mCSPC patients treated with apalutamide plus ADT who achieve deep PSA <=0.2 ng/mL within 6 months have >80% 24-month radiographic progression-free survival.

reason: If the trial requires formal non-inferiority against active 2% topical minoxidil under double-dummy clinical supervision, high topical adherence could narrow oral minoxidil's margin.
rationale: This 520-patient European Phase 3 trial (2:2:1 oral minoxidil 1 mg, topical 2% minoxidil BID, double placebo) evaluates 24-week change in non-vellus hair density (TAHC, hairs/cm2). Oral minoxidil 1 mg daily reliably increases female pattern hair density by ~15-20 hairs/cm2 over placebo and matched or numerically outperformed 5% topical minoxidil in Ramos 2020 (+12% vs +7.2%), because hepatic sulfation bypasses low scalp sulfotransferase activity. With 208 oral, 208 active-topical, and 104 placebo patients (SD ~18 hairs/cm2), power for both placebo superiority (alpha=0.01) and active non-inferiority is very high. Completion in November 2026 enables a 2027 European MAA filing.

assumptions.claim: In a 24-week randomized trial in women with female pattern hair loss, oral minoxidil 1 mg daily increased total hair density by 12% compared with 7.2% for topical 5% minoxidil daily.
Topical 2% minoxidil twice daily increases target-area non-vellus hair count by roughly 12-15 hairs/cm2 over vehicle placebo in female androgenetic alopecia.

reason: Induction responders receiving Phesgo plus optional endocrine therapy may achieve longer control PFS than historical CLEOPATRA PIK3CA-mutant estimates, slowing event accrual and attenuating hazard ratios.
rationale: INAVO122 (N=230) tests selective PI3Kalpha inhibitor/degrader inavolisib plus Phesgo versus placebo plus Phesgo as first-line maintenance in PIK3CA-mutated HER2+ advanced breast cancer. Activating PIK3CA mutations confer marked resistance to pertuzumab/trastuzumab (CLEOPATRA median PFS 12.5 vs 21.8 months in wild-type), and inavolisib demonstrated strong efficacy (HR 0.43) and low AE discontinuation (6.8%) in INAVO120. With ~140 PFS events needed, true HR ~0.58 gives >70% probability of success conditional on readout. However, because the trial is still recruiting in late October 2026, primary completion will likely slip past March 2027, delaying readout.

assumptions.claim: In CLEOPATRA, PIK3CA-mutated HER2+ metastatic breast cancer had a median PFS of 12.5 months on pertuzumab, trastuzumab, and docetaxel versus 21.8 months for wild-type.
In INAVO120, inavolisib reduced the risk of progression or death with HR 0.43 and a 6.8% adverse-event discontinuation rate in PIK3CA-mutated HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer.

reason: Near-complete suppression of new T1 Gd-enhancing MRI lesions by anti-CD20 therapy yields very low event counts, creating ratio variability despite comparable PK and B-cell depletion.
rationale: Monoclonal antibody biosimilar Phase 3 equivalence studies from experienced developers like Celltrion succeed over 85% of the time when analytical and PK/PD comparability (CD19+ B-cell depletion) are established. The main statistical risk is sparse new GdE T1 lesions under potent ocrelizumab suppression over 24 weeks in 512 RRMS patients, though equivalence margins accommodate low lesion rates. Because the trial was still recruiting in late October 2026 with a 24-week primary endpoint, completion will likely slip past February 2027 by several months.

assumptions.claim: Ocrelizumab suppressed new T1 gadolinium-enhancing brain MRI lesions by roughly 94-95% relative to interferon beta-1a in pivotal RRMS trials, resulting in very low mean lesion counts per scan.
assumptions.source: OPERA I and II, Hauser et al. 2017 (NCT01247324)

assumptions.claim: Phase 3 confirmatory biosimilar monoclonal antibody trials historically achieve primary equivalence endpoints in over 85% of completed studies.

reason: With enrollment closed at 21 participants and registered completion at year-end 2026, the trial is likely winding down on schedule ahead of Roche's broader Phase 3 afimkibart Crohn's program.
rationale: TAHOE enrolled 21 Crohn's disease participants and is active, not recruiting, with both primary and study completion registered for 2026-12-31 despite an originally described 5-year safety window, indicating the study was capped and shortened following Roche's acquisition of afimkibart (RVT-3101). Consequently, primary completion is unlikely to slip more than 90 days past December 2026, though there is a moderate chance it is formally marked terminated early rather than completed, and Roche routinely posts ClinicalTrials.gov results within 8-12 months of study completion.

reason: While PFS superiority is highly likely, meeting both PFS and OS co-primary endpoints by mid-2027 faces risk from immature OS events and post-progression enfortumab vedotin or checkpoint inhibitor crossover.
rationale: Disitamab vedotin delivers the same MMAE payload as enfortumab vedotin via HER2 targeting and produced >70% response rates with pembrolizumab in Phase 1b/2 HER2-expressing urothelial cancer (RC48-C014). Following EV-302's landmark success over gemcitabine-platinum (PFS HR 0.45, OS HR 0.47, control mPFS 6.3 months), PFS superiority in N=412 IHC >=1+ patients is strongly favored, especially in IHC 2+/3+. The primary risk under ReadoutBench rules is that OS is co-primary and could still be immature at initial PFS readout or attenuated by subsequent ADC/avelumab maintenance therapy in control patients.

assumptions.claim: In EV-302, platinum-gemcitabine control achieved a median BICR progression-free survival of 6.3 months and ORR of 44.2% in untreated locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma.
Disitamab vedotin plus toripalimab achieved an ORR above 70% in HER2-expressing locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma in Phase 1b/2 study RC48-C014.

reason: Large placebo improvements in US multicenter adjunctive MDD trials and modest effect sizes of agomelatine risk overwhelming EEG biomarker enrichment in a reduced subgroup sample.
rationale: ALTO-300 (agomelatine 25 mg) has established monotherapy antidepressant activity in Europe with mild tolerability, but US placebo-controlled trials of agomelatine previously struggled against high placebo response. Although prospectively enriching for an EEG biomarker subgroup aims to amplify separation, Alto Neuroscience's prior biomarker-stratified MDD Phase 2b trial (ALTO-100) failed to replicate earlier enrichment signals across 75 US clinical sites. Restriction of the primary analysis to a biomarker-positive subset of 325 randomized patients also limits statistical power to detect a typical 1.5-2.0 point adjunctive MADRS difference.

assumptions.claim: Alto Neuroscience's Phase 2b biomarker-enriched MDD study of ALTO-100 failed to meet its primary endpoint of MADRS change at week 6 versus placebo.
Agomelatine 25 mg demonstrates modest mean depression rating scale separation of roughly 1.5 to 2 points versus placebo with low adverse-event discontinuation rates similar to placebo.

reason: Permitted background mycophenolate and immunosuppressants stabilize skin and lung disease in placebo patients, historically blunting biologic treatment differences in Phase 3 systemic sclerosis trials.
rationale: Type I interferon pathway activation correlates with skin and lung fibrosis in early systemic sclerosis, and subcutaneous anifrolumab potently neutralizes IFNAR1 signaling with proven efficacy in SLE. Using the revised CRISS-25 responder index over 52 weeks in N=314 anti-centromere-negative patients improves sensitivity compared with mRSS alone. However, Phase 3 systemic sclerosis trials allowing stable background mycophenolate mofetil have repeatedly missed primary endpoints due to substantial spontaneous and background-driven improvement in control arms and lack of prior large randomized Phase 2 SSc efficacy data.

assumptions.claim: Previous Phase 3 biologic trials in systemic sclerosis such as focuSSced (tocilizumab) missed primary skin endpoints despite biologic plausibility, although lung function components showed benefit.
Anifrolumab demonstrated low adverse-event discontinuation rates below 10% over 52 weeks in Phase 3 SLE trials.

reason: Unconjugated EGFRxHER3 bispecific blockade added to docetaxel may modestly improve PFS and ORR without achieving statistically significant overall survival superiority required across co-primary endpoints.
rationale: SI-B001 (unconjugated EGFRxHER3 bispecific antibody) plus docetaxel showed encouraging single-arm Phase 2 activity in post-chemoimmunotherapy wild-type NSCLC, particularly in patients progressing strictly after first-line PD-(L)1 plus platinum. Nonetheless, Phase 3 trials attempting to beat second-line docetaxel on overall survival in unselected post-IO NSCLC have suffered a high failure rate (e.g., TROPION-Lung01, EVOKE-01, CONTACT-01, LEAP-008), as docetaxel performs near 10.5-11.5 months median OS and subsequent therapies dilute survival gains. Meeting both OS and BICR-PFS co-primary endpoints is challenging.
evidence: Zhao et al. SI-B001 Phase 2 NSCLC (2023)

assumptions.claim: Docetaxel control arms in contemporary second-line NSCLC Phase 3 trials after platinum and PD-(L)1 therapy achieve median overall survival of roughly 10 to 11.5 months.
SI-B001 plus docetaxel demonstrated preliminary antitumor activity with manageable rash and hematologic toxicity in Phase 2 second-line wild-type NSCLC.

reason: Large placebo ESSDAI declines over 52 weeks and absence of dedicated Phase 2 Sjögren's efficacy data for deucravacitinib create substantial risk of insufficient separation despite strong IFN biology.
rationale: Anti-Ro-positive Sjögren's syndrome is strongly driven by Type I interferon and IL-12/23 signaling, pathways inhibited allosterically by TYK2 inhibitor deucravacitinib, which succeeded in Phase 2 SLE (PAISLEY). POETYK SjS-1 is well powered (N=774 across two active doses vs placebo, 258/arm) and either dose succeeding satisfies the round's primary rule. However, BMS bypassed a dedicated Phase 2 SjS trial, and SjS trials suffer from 4-5 point placebo ESSDAI improvements and frequent dissociation between systemic ESSDAI improvement and patient-reported ESSPRI symptom scores.

assumptions.claim: Deucravacitinib significantly improved systemic lupus disease activity and suppressed Type I interferon gene signatures in the Phase 2 PAISLEY trial.
Placebo arms in randomized moderate-to-severe Sjögren's syndrome trials routinely exhibit 3.5 to 5.5 point mean reductions from baseline in ESSDAI.

reason: Heterogeneous non-FGFR2 bypass resistance mechanisms (such as RAS/MAPK alterations) after prior FGFR inhibition and modest Part B sample size could dilute tinengotinib's PFS advantage.
rationale: Tinengotinib binds outside the FGFR2 active pocket steric hindrance site to retain potency against acquired gatekeeper and molecular-brake FGFR2 kinase mutations, demonstrating roughly 5-7 month median PFS in Phase 2 FGFRi-refractory FGFR2-fusion cholangiocarcinoma. In contrast, third-line physician's choice chemotherapy after gemcitabine-platinum and an FGFR inhibitor yields dismal median PFS around 2.5-3.0 months. Even with Part B comprising roughly 150-170 of the 200 total patients randomized 2:1, power is good for a ~0.58 PFS hazard ratio, whereas OS will likely be underpowered or confounded.
evidence: Javle et al. tinengotinib Phase 2 CCA (2024)

assumptions.claim: Tinengotinib demonstrated clinical responses and median PFS exceeding 5 months in Phase 2 patients with FGFR2-altered cholangiocarcinoma previously treated with an FGFR inhibitor.
Salvage chemotherapy in previously treated advanced biliary tract cancer achieves median progression-free survival of only 2.5 to 4.0 months.

reason: Because both factorial primary endpoints must succeed, lower-than-expected BARC 2, 3, or 5 bleeding rates or open-label DAPT non-adherence could leave the 1-month vs 12-month bleeding comparison underpowered.
rationale: ANGIODAPT has two factorial primary hypotheses in 2,312 all-comer PCI patients, and both must succeed for p_met. First, thin-strut sirolimus-eluting Angiolite versus everolimus-eluting Xience has ~88% probability of showing 1-year TLF non-inferiority given modern DES parity (~5.5% 1-year TLF) and prior ANGIOLITE randomized angiographic/clinical data. Second, 1-month versus 12-month DAPT reliably lowers 1-year BARC 2, 3, or 5 bleeding by 30-40% (STOPDAPT-2, MASTER DAPT, ULTIMATE-DAPT), giving ~78% power here; combined joint success probability is roughly 0.68.

assumptions.claim: Everolimus-eluting Xience stents consistently record 1-year target lesion failure rates of approximately 5% to 6.5% in European all-comer PCI trials.
Abbreviated 1-month DAPT significantly reduces BARC 2, 3, or 5 clinically relevant bleeding compared with 12-month DAPT in randomized PCI trials.

reason: Repeated intradermal saline injections induce mechanical subcision and dermal remodeling that can elevate bilateral 1-grade ASIS responder rates in the small 39-patient control arm.
rationale: Injectable dermal fillers provide direct physical volume restoration in rolling and boxcar atrophic acne scars, historically outperforming intradermal saline injections by 25-40 percentage points on blinded evaluator scar scales at 6 months (as seen with Bellafill and hyaluronic acid fillers). Requiring >=1-grade bilateral ASIS improvement at Day 181 after three sessions in 157 patients (3:1 allocation, ~118 vs 39) provides high statistical power. The study already completed in July 2026 without termination, making safety derailment unlikely and leaving saline needle-induced remodeling variability in 39 controls as the main risk.
evidence: Karnik et al. Bellafill acne scars pivotal RCT (2014)
V-Volite / HA filler acne scar RCTs (2023)

assumptions.claim: In pivotal randomized saline-controlled trials of injectable dermal fillers for rolling and boxcar atrophic acne scars, active gel arms exceed saline responder rates by roughly 30 percentage points at 6 months.

reason: After NSAID washout, subjective ASAS20 symptom regression to the mean in the placebo arm may narrow the 8-week treatment effect of an oral herbal formulation.
rationale: Jitongning tablets previously showed encouraging ASAS20 improvement in Chinese Phase 2 axial spondyloarthritis studies, and sample size (N=408) provides >85% power to detect a 15-percentage-point difference over an expected ~30-32% placebo ASAS20 rate following NSAID washout. Enriching for HLA-B27 positivity and elevated acute-phase reactants reduces diagnostic noise, though short 8-week patient-reported domains carry notable placebo responsiveness. Because the trial remained recruiting in late October 2026 ahead of a December 2026 registered completion date, enrollment or readout slippage into mid-to-late 2027 is moderately likely.

assumptions.claim: Placebo ASAS20 response at 8 to 12 weeks in active ankylosing spondylitis trials after NSAID washout typically ranges around 25% to 35%.
With 204 patients per arm, a 15-percentage-point improvement over a 31% control rate yields p<0.05 with high power.

reason: With only 103 randomized patients against an active pembrolizumab-chemotherapy standard and multiple registered PFS primary measures, only a large hazard ratio improvement could achieve statistical significance.
rationale: Exploratory POSEIDON subgroup analyses suggested dual CTLA-4/PD-L1 blockade (tremelimumab plus durvalumab) with chemotherapy might mitigate resistance in STK11, KEAP1, or KRAS-mutated non-squamous NSCLC. However, TRITON compares this regimen head-to-head against active pembrolizumab-pemetrexed-platinum (KEYNOTE-189), which retains substantial activity in KRAS-mutated tumors without STK11/KEAP1 co-loss. With N=103 (~78 PFS events), achieving two-sided p<0.05 requires an observed HR near 0.63, and listing 6-month and 12-month PFS rates alongside PFS HR creates co-primary hurdles.

assumptions.claim: POSEIDON exploratory biomarker analyses motivated testing durvalumab plus tremelimumab plus chemotherapy in STK11, KEAP1, and KRAS mutant non-squamous NSCLC.
Pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum achieves median PFS of roughly 6 to 9 months across KRAS-mutant and co-mutated first-line non-squamous NSCLC cohorts.

reason: Promising single-arm FAK inhibitor plus PLD activity in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer often attenuates under blinded central review against a randomized PLD control arm.
rationale: IN10018 (ifebemtinib), an oral FAK inhibitor, showed encouraging response rates (~45-55%) and median PFS (~7-8 months) when combined with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (PLD) in single-arm Chinese Phase 1b/2 platinum-resistant ovarian cancer cohorts. Against expected control PLD median PFS of ~3.8 months by BICR, a 168-patient 2:1 randomized design (~118 events) needs an observed HR around 0.67 for two-sided p<0.05. Uncontrolled single-arm enrichment and FAK pathway heterogeneity temper the probability of reproducing a large PFS benefit.

assumptions.claim: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin monotherapy in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer typically yields a median PFS of 3.5 to 4.0 months by blinded central review.

reason: The stringent CLASI-70 responder threshold at Week 24 may be harder to reach in fibrotic or scarred chronic discoid lupus lesions despite clear biological activity.
rationale: Type I interferon signaling is central to cutaneous lupus erythematosus pathogenesis. In TULIP-1 and TULIP-2 SLE skin subsets (baseline CLASI-A >=10) and dedicated CLE cohorts, IFNAR1 blockade with anifrolumab produced large, rapid skin improvements over placebo, corroborated by Phase 2 CLE data for anti-BDCA2 therapy (litifilimab). With 339 antimalarial-refractory patients and active-not-recruiting status ahead of a November 2026 primary completion, LAVENDER is well powered (>85% for a ~20-25 point CLASI-70 delta) and highly likely to read out and support regulatory filing in 2027.

assumptions.claim: Anifrolumab significantly increased cutaneous lupus skin responses compared with placebo among SLE patients with baseline CLASI-A >=10 in Phase 3 trials.
Targeting the Type I interferon pathway demonstrated superiority over placebo on CLASI-A skin activity at 16 to 24 weeks in isolated CLE.

reason: Oral TPL2 (MAP3K8) inhibition lacks prior clinical proof of efficacy in ulcerative colitis and faces redundant inflammatory pathways in advanced-therapy-experienced patients.
rationale: Tilpisertib fosmecarbil (GS-5290) inhibits TPL2 (MAP3K8), an intracellular kinase regulating ERK-mediated TNF and IL-1beta signaling. While centrally read endoscopic entry criteria curb placebo response (~27% clinical response expected in advanced-therapy-experienced ulcerative colitis) and testing multiple doses helps, novel oral intracellular kinase targets outside JAK1/TYK2 have had low Phase 2 translation rates in refractory IBD. With ~44 patients per arm across a multi-dose N=176 study, moderate efficacy could also miss statistical significance.

assumptions.claim: In moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis patients with prior advanced therapy exposure, Week 12 placebo clinical response per modified Mayo score is approximately 25% to 30%.

reason: Slow donor organ availability in pediatric heart transplantation across three German centers makes enrollment delays beyond the registered January 2027 primary completion date likely.
rationale: This small German Phase 2 safety trial (N=15) requires pediatric first-time heart transplant recipients whose explantation and transplantation teams belong to the same clinic and excludes machine-perfused organs and failing Fontan patients. Because pediatric donor hearts are scarce and the study remained recruiting in late October 2026 shortly before its January 2027 target date, primary completion slippage past May 2027 is likely, and ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

reason: The registry lists feasibility, safety, and appropriateness questionnaires alongside CAPS-5 as primary outcomes in a small dyadic sample compared against an already effective CBCT control.
rationale: Manualized Cognitive-Behavioral Conjoint Therapy (CBCT) alone produces large CAPS-5 PTSD symptom reductions, leaving a narrower incremental margin for MDMA enhancement than placebo-therapy trials, though functional unblinding favours MDMA. Crucially, enrollment of 60 likely represents 30 dyads (15 PTSD patients per arm), and four feasibility/safety measures are co-listed as primary outcomes, making formal superiority across all registered primaries unlikely under round rules. Recruiting status in late 2026 at a single Canadian site also makes delays beyond June 2027 probable.
evidence: Monson et al. CBCT for PTSD JAMA (2012)

assumptions.claim: Cognitive-Behavioral Conjoint Therapy alone produces substantial clinician-rated PTSD symptom improvements in dyadic RCTs.

reason: With only 45 EGPA patients and optional background anti-IL-5 therapy, detecting statistically significant steroid-sparing remission at p<0.05 requires an unusually large effect from JAK1 inhibition.
rationale: NS-229 is an oral selective JAK1 inhibitor suppressing IL-4, IL-5, and IL-13 signaling downstream of common gamma/beta cytokine pathways, offering biological plausibility in EGPA. However, with N=45 (~22 patients per arm), achieving two-sided p<0.05 on Week 28 remission (BVAS=0 and prednisone <=4 mg/day) requires roughly a 32-percentage-point advantage over placebo. Allowing background stable mepolizumab or benralizumab may raise control remission rates above historical MIRRA placebo levels and blunt incremental efficacy.

assumptions.claim: In the MIRRA Phase 3 trial of mepolizumab in relapsing or refractory EGPA, sustained remission with prednisolone <=4 mg/day occurred in 3% of placebo patients versus 32% on mepolizumab.

reason: Limited dermal penetration of topical patidegib 2% gel and inter-patient overdispersion in new BCC lesion counts contributed to an earlier Phase 3 miss in Gorlin syndrome.
rationale: Hedgehog pathway inhibition directly targets PTCH1-mutant Gorlin syndrome, and patidegib 2% topical gel showed promising lesion reductions in Phase 2 without systemic vismodegib toxicities. Although PellePharm's prior Phase 3 trial (NCT03703310) missed statistical significance due to low surgically eligible facial BCC counts in vehicle patients, NCT06050122 improved event capture by requiring >=10 baseline facial BCCs, excluding prior HHI non-responders, and counting all dermoscopically confirmed new facial BCCs centrally. Because the study completed in September 2026, top-line disclosure is imminent.
evidence: Epstein et al. Patidegib Gel Phase 2 Gorlin Syndrome (2021)

assumptions.claim: An earlier Phase 3 vehicle-controlled trial of patidegib 2% topical gel in Gorlin syndrome (NCT03703310) failed to reach statistical significance on new facial surgically eligible BCCs.

reason: High adherence to background inhaled controller therapy could lower severe exacerbation rates or attenuate the relative rescue benefit, while hierarchical gating through the low-dose arm could affect secondary testing.
rationale: Adding an inhaled corticosteroid (fluticasone propionate) to albuterol in a single rescue dry-powder inhaler closely mirrors the proven anti-inflammatory reliever mechanism established by MANDALA (budesonide-albuterol vs albuterol, HR 0.74, p=0.001). Enrolling 2,772 asthma patients (~924 per arm) on stable maintenance controller therapy with a prior-year severe exacerbation in an event-driven design provides >90% statistical power to detect a ~25-27% hazard reduction. With primary completion registered for October 31, 2026, top-line results and NDA filing in 2027 are highly likely.

assumptions.claim: In MANDALA, as-needed high-dose budesonide-albuterol reduced the hazard of first severe asthma exacerbation versus albuterol alone with a hazard ratio of 0.74.
Roughly one quarter of albuterol-control patients experienced at least one severe asthma exacerbation during event-driven follow-up in MANDALA.

reason: With only 18 experimental and 9 placebo patients, two-sided p<0.05 requires an unusually large difference in complete histologic response.
rationale: Topical artesunate has shown biological activity in cervical and vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia in Phase 1 studies (~50% histologic regression vs ~10-15% spontaneous regression in usual-type VIN). However, with N=27 randomized 2:1 (18 vs 9), achieving two-sided p<0.05 requires roughly a 40+ percentage point observed advantage, leaving the trial severely underpowered for realistic true effects (~25-30 percentage points). Additionally, the trial is still recruiting near its December 2026 primary completion date with a small private sponsor, making delays likely.
evidence: Trimble et al. 2020 (topical artesunate in CIN2/3)

assumptions.claim: Spontaneous complete histologic regression of usual-type vulvar HSIL over 4-6 months is approximately 10-15% in placebo arms.
assumptions.source: van Seters et al. 2008 NEJM (imiquimod in VIN)

assumptions.claim: Phase 1 open-label studies of topical artesunate in CIN2/3 and VIN2/3 showed histologic regression in roughly 50-65% of treated patients.

reason: Recruiting ventilated pneumonia patients with rapid-test confirmed Acinetobacter baumannii and strict organ-function exclusions is notoriously slow, making delays past June 2027 highly likely.
rationale: Enrolling 54 HABP/VABP patients specifically caused by Acinetobacter baumannii complex across 15 sites in Greece and Israel within 10 months (May 2026 to March 2027) is very ambitious given strict exclusions for septic shock, ARDS, immunosuppression, and moderate/severe renal dysfunction. Substantial recruitment delays beyond 90 days are likely, while results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 is very unlikely.

reason: Acute hemodynamic eGFR dip from zibotentan may partially offset chronic slope preservation at Month 24 on top of background RAASi and dapagliflozin.
rationale: In Phase 2b ZENITH-CKD, low-dose zibotentan plus dapagliflozin reduced UACR by an additional ~27-34% over dapagliflozin alone while dapagliflozin mitigated ERA fluid retention. Endothelin receptor antagonists (atrasentan in SONAR/ALIGN, sparsentan in PROTECT) consistently slow chronic eGFR decline in high-proteinuria CKD. With N=1835 in severe proteinuria (UACR >700 mg/g), power is high to detect a ~1.5-2.0 mL/min/1.73m2 net total eGFR preservation at 24 months despite an initial ~1-1.5 mL/min acute hemodynamic dip. Trial is active, not recruiting, with primary completion in Feb 2027, supporting a mid-2027 readout.

assumptions.claim: In ZENITH-CKD, zibotentan 0.25 mg plus dapagliflozin 10 mg reduced UACR by approximately 27% more than dapagliflozin alone at 12 weeks.
Patients with CKD and UACR >700 mg/g on RAASi and dapagliflozin still experience chronic eGFR decline of roughly 3 to 4 mL/min/1.73m2 per year.

reason: IL-6 blockade reduces orbital inflammation (CAS) in thyroid eye disease, but its ability to achieve >=2 mm proptosis reduction at Week 20 is much weaker than IGF-1R inhibition.
rationale: TOUR006 (pacibekitug) is an anti-IL-6 monoclonal antibody. While IL-6 pathway inhibition (tocilizumab, satralizumab) improves inflammatory Clinical Activity Score (CAS) in active TED, proptosis >=2 mm responder rates with IL-6R antibodies in randomized trials (e.g., satralizumab Phase 3 SatraGO) have been modest (~25-35% vs ~10-15% placebo), far below IGF-1R inhibitors like teprotumumab (~80%). With ~26 patients per arm (or ~52 pooled active vs 26 placebo), achieving p<0.05 requires roughly a 25-30 percentage point treatment effect. Primary completion passed in Sept 2026, so top-line results are highly likely before March/June 2027.
evidence: Perez-Moreiras et al. 2018 AJO (tocilizumab in TED)

assumptions.claim: Placebo proptosis response rates (>=2 mm reduction) at 20-24 weeks in active moderate-to-severe TED trials are typically 10-15%.
TOUR006 (PF-04236921 / pacibekitug) targets IL-6 rather than IGF-1R.

reason: Active, not recruiting HPTN/Gilead Phase 2 PrEP study whose July 2026 primary completion has passed; ongoing follow-up to January 2028 delays registry results posting.
rationale: PURPOSE 3 (HPTN 102) is active, not recruiting, with primary completion in July 2026 and full study completion in January 2028 (TEAEs assessed through Week 78). Termination risk is minimal given lenacapavir's established safety and approval in PrEP. Because two co-primary safety outcomes run up to 30 days post Week 78, full ClinicalTrials.gov results posting before August 31, 2027 is only moderately likely (~35%).

reason: Active, not recruiting Gilead/HPTN/NIH Phase 2 study with all primary outcomes assessed through Week 52+30 days (completed July 2026), giving a solid chance of timely posting.
rationale: PURPOSE 4 (HPTN 103) is active, not recruiting, and passed its primary completion date in July 2026. Unlike PURPOSE 3, all four registered primary outcomes in PURPOSE 4 complete by Week 52 + 30 days, putting the 1-year FDAAA results-posting deadline around July 2027—before the August 31, 2027 read date. Gilead and NIH/HPTN have good compliance, supporting nearly a 50% probability of posted results.

reason: Patients stable on BTKi monotherapy for >=12 months without overt progression may have low 12-month progression rates, delaying PFS events or narrowing early separation.
rationale: Lisaftoclax (APG-2575) is a potent BCL-2 inhibitor (same class as venetoclax) showing high response and uMRD rates when added to BTK inhibitors in Phase 1b/2 CLL/SLL studies. Adding a BCL-2i to ongoing BTKi therapy (>=12 months prior exposure, suboptimal response or high risk) strongly suppresses progression compared to continuing BTKi alone (expected HR ~0.40-0.50). However, the trial is still recruiting 400-440 patients globally near its Dec 2026 registered primary completion, and patients already on BTKi >=12 months accrue PFS events slowly (~15-20% at 12m in control), risking event-driven readout delays into late 2027.

assumptions.claim: BCL-2 inhibition combined with BTK inhibition achieves deep remissions and high uMRD rates in CLL patients with persistent disease on BTKi monotherapy.
Overall survival differences at 12 months in indolent/chronic CLL patients on active BTKi therapy are minimal (<5% mortality).

reason: S1P receptor modulation (NXC736) lacks clinical proof-of-concept for rapid hair regrowth by Week 12 compared to JAK inhibitors in alopecia areata.
rationale: NXC736 is an oral S1P1/S1P4 receptor modulator tested in moderate-to-severe alopecia areata (N=73 across 2 Korean sites). Unlike JAK inhibitors (baricitinib, ritlecitinib, deuruxolitinib), which rapidly reverse IFN-gamma/IL-15 collapse of hair follicle immune privilege, S1P modulators (etrasimod) have shown slower and much weaker hair regrowth in Phase 2 AA trials, especially at an early 12-week primary endpoint. Placebo SALT percent change at Week 12 is near zero (-2% to -5%), so even modest biological activity gives ~32% PoS, though recruitment status in Oct 2026 suggests possible slight delay.

assumptions.claim: Placebo mean percent change from baseline in SALT score at 12-24 weeks in chronic stable alopecia areata is approximately 0% to -6%.
NXC736 acts as a sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulator rather than a JAK inhibitor.

reason: Intravitreal aflibercept is a highly effective active control (<3% lose >=15 letters), making superiority—or even narrow non-inferiority—extremely hard for topical VEGFR drops.
rationale: KHK4951 (tivozanib eye drops) is compared against intravitreal aflibercept (with secondary outcome counting rescue aflibercept IVT injections) on >=15-letter BCVA loss over 36 weeks in DME (N=185). In DME trials (VISTA/VIVID, Protocol T), <=2-3% of aflibercept-treated eyes lose >=15 letters. Topical VEGFR TKIs struggle to deliver therapeutic posterior-segment concentrations to match intravitreal anti-VEGF, so superiority on vision loss is virtually impossible (<2%) and meeting a formal non-inferiority or rescue-reduction hypothesis if pre-specified in the protocol remains challenging (~8% overall). Active, not recruiting with Oct 2026 primary completion supports a 2027 readout.
evidence: VISTA and VIVID (Korobelnik et al. 2014 Ophthalmology)
DRCR.net Protocol T (Wells et al. 2015 NEJM)

assumptions.claim: In DME trials, the proportion of eyes treated with intravitreal aflibercept losing 15 or more ETDRS letters over 36-52 weeks is approximately 1-3%.
assumptions.source: VISTA and VIVID (Korobelnik et al. 2014 Ophthalmology)

assumptions.claim: KHK4951 is a nanocrystal topical eye drop formulation of the VEGFR inhibitor tivozanib.

reason: Acute post-MI recurrent events include stent thrombosis and non-inflammatory mechanisms, where IL-6 blockade lacks proven MACE reduction despiteCANTOS IL-1beta precedent.
rationale: ARTEMIS tests monthly ziltivekimab (anti-IL-6 mAb) vs placebo initiated within 36-72h of Type 1 MI in 10,000 enriched high-risk patients up to 25 months. IL-6 blockade markedly lowers hsCRP (~80% in RESCUE) and Mendelian randomization links IL-6R signaling to atherothrombosis, supported by CANTOS (canakinumab HR 0.85 in stable post-MI with elevated hsCRP). However, ARTEMIS does not require elevated baseline hsCRP and tests acute post-PCI MI—a setting where colchicine showed mixed results (COLCOT positive, CLEAR SYNERGY neutral at HR 0.99) and early events may be less responsive, yielding ~42% PoS (expected HR ~0.89 over ~850 MACE events).

assumptions.claim: Ziltivekimab reduced median hsCRP by roughly 77-92% in Phase 2 RESCUE patients with elevated inflammatory risk.
Canakinumab 150 mg reduced 3-point MACE with a hazard ratio of 0.85 in patients with prior MI and hsCRP >=2 mg/L in CANTOS.

reason: Enrollment is complete with primary completion registered for December 2026, making timely completion likely with low risk of termination.
rationale: AURORA-HFpEF is a 227-patient Phase 2a safety and pharmacokinetic trial of BMS-986435 (MYK-224, a cardiac myosin inhibitor) sponsored by Bristol-Myers Squibb. Because the trial is already active and not recruiting as of late October 2026 with a 24-week follow-up window and a December 2026 registered completion date, substantial completion delays or protocol amendments to the standard safety primary endpoints are unlikely. BMS routinely posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov within 9 to 12 months of completion, giving a moderate probability of results posting before the August 31, 2027 read date.

reason: Splitting 210 patients across dose-selection arms may leave modest statistical power if FVC variability is high or the selected dose offers less than 90 mL/year slowing.
rationale: Sufenidone (SC1011) is a structurally modified pirfenidone analog tested against pure placebo (concomitant IPF therapies excluded) in Chinese IPF patients. In untreated IPF cohorts such as ASCEND and INPULSIS, placebo FVC declines by roughly 200 to 240 mL/year, and pirfenidone slows decline by ~100 to 120 mL/year. Given shared antifibrotic pharmacology and dose optimization at week 26, SC1011 has a favorable chance of meeting its 52-week FVC endpoint, though multi-dose allocation within 210 patients limits sample size per arm. Because the registry still lists recruiting in October 2026 for a 52-week endpoint, completion delays are likely.

assumptions.claim: Untreated placebo arms in pivotal 52-week IPF trials (INPULSIS-1 and INPULSIS-2) experienced adjusted annual FVC declines of approximately 205 to 240 mL/year.
Pirfenidone significantly slowed 52-week FVC decline compared with placebo in IPF patients in the ASCEND Phase 3 trial.

reason: Large caregiver-mediated placebo improvements on neuropsychiatric scales over 14 weeks and cholinergic/gastrointestinal dropouts in frail elderly patients risk attenuating treatment separation.
rationale: KarXT (xanomeline-trospium) targets M1/M4 muscarinic receptors and succeeded in schizophrenia (EMERGENT trials), while an earlier xanomeline trial in Alzheimer's disease (Bodick 1997) showed dose-dependent reductions in hallucinations and delusions. However, acute parallel-group trials in Alzheimer's disease psychosis suffer from notoriously large placebo responses over 12 to 14 weeks, and elderly dementia patients (ages 55-90) are more vulnerable to cholinergic and anticholinergic tolerability issues leading to early discontinuation or conservative titration. With 500 patients, ADEPT-2 is well powered for a ~2-point NPI-C H+D difference, yielding a moderate 42% success probability.

assumptions.claim: Xanomeline monotherapy reduced vocal outbursts, delusions, and hallucinations in Alzheimer's disease patients in a randomized placebo-controlled trial but had substantial gastrointestinal discontinuation.
KarXT significantly improved psychosis symptoms over placebo in Phase 3 schizophrenia trials with higher gastrointestinal adverse event rates than placebo.

reason: If the trial requires co-primary statistical significance across all three helminth species including Trichuris trichiura, lower benzimidazole cure rates in trichuriasis could prevent full primary success.
rationale: ZP5-9676 (600 mg chewable benzimidazole formulation) is compared against placebo for Day 14 parasitological cure in at least 114 hookworm-infected participants within a 300-patient STH cohort. Spontaneous 14-day placebo cure rates for hookworm and Ascaris are very low (~10-15%), whereas active 600 mg benzimidazole regimens achieve high cure and egg-reduction rates (~70-85% in hookworm, >90% in Ascaris, and ~35-55% in Trichuris vs <10% placebo). Even if all three STH species are tested as co-primaries, superiority over placebo has high statistical power. Main residual risk is Trichuris cure rate or insufficient Trichuris enrollment.

assumptions.claim: Benzimidazole anthelmintics such as single-dose albendazole achieve high cure rates (~75-80%) against hookworm and >90% against Ascaris lumbricoides, with lower cure rates against Trichuris trichiura.

reason: With only 80 patients total, broad symptom-onset eligibility up to 4 weeks, and two co-primary functional scales (BI and mRS), the study is severely underpowered for realistic stem cell effects.
rationale: This single-center 80-patient double-blind trial tests intravenous umbilical cord MSCs (Neuroncell-EX) in moderate-to-severe ischemic stroke within 4 weeks of onset, listing both Barthel Index and modified Rankin Scale as co-primary outcomes. Prior larger double-blind allogeneic cell therapy trials in ischemic stroke (such as MASTERS and TREASURE) failed to meet primary functional endpoints, and the investigators' cited prior Phase 2 MSC study (Law 2021) showed no statistically significant functional score improvement. Requiring statistical significance on both BI and mRS with 40 patients per arm yields low probability of success, and ongoing recruitment in late 2026 implies substantial delay.

assumptions.claim: In the MASTERS randomized double-blind Phase 2 trial of intravenous multipotent adult progenitor cells in acute ischemic stroke, there was no significant difference in global stroke recovery at 90 days.

reason: Crizotinib occasionally achieves nearly 19-20 months median PFS in selected ROS1-positive cohorts, which could delay event accrual or narrow the hazard ratio in a 190-patient trial.
rationale: TRIDENT-3 compares next-generation ROS1/TRK inhibitor repotrectinib against first-generation crizotinib in 190 TKI-naive ROS1-positive NSCLC patients. In TRIDENT-1, repotrectinib achieved a 79% response rate and 35.7-month median PFS in TKI-naive ROS1+ NSCLC with potent intracranial protection and resistance-mutation coverage, whereas crizotinib historically yields ~15 to 19 months median PFS with frequent CNS progression. Analogous to next-generation vs crizotinib trials in ALK+ NSCLC (ALEX, CROWN), an expected PFS hazard ratio near 0.50 provides strong statistical power. Enrollment is already closed with primary completion in February 2027, supporting timely H1 2027 readout.

assumptions.claim: In TRIDENT-1, repotrectinib achieved a 79% response rate and median progression-free survival of 35.7 months in TKI-naive ROS1-fusion-positive NSCLC.
Crizotinib achieved a median progression-free survival of 19.2 months in ROS1-rearranged NSCLC in PROFILE 1001.

reason: First-line platinum-pemetrexed plus pembrolizumab with pemetrexed maintenance can yield 8.5 to 9.5 months median PFS, narrowing separation if first-line zongertinib durability falls short of 13 months.
rationale: Beamion LUNG-2 randomizes 428 first-line HER2 TKD-mutant non-squamous NSCLC patients to selective covalent HER2 TKI zongertinib versus pembrolizumab plus platinum-pemetrexed. In Beamion LUNG-1, zongertinib demonstrated high response rates (~71%), durable disease control, intracranial activity, and low discontinuation (~3-5% due to wild-type EGFR sparing) even in pretreated patients. Conversely, oncogene-driven HER2-mutant NSCLC derives limited immunotherapy benefit, with chemo-immunotherapy median PFS typically ~7 to 8.5 months and ORR ~45%. With enrollment completed and December 2026 registered primary completion, both BICR PFS and key secondary ORR have high probabilities of success.

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed and platinum chemotherapy achieved a median progression-free survival of 8.8 months and ~20% discontinuation of any treatment component due to adverse events in KEYNOTE-189.
Zongertinib showed confirmed objective response rates around 70% with low treatment discontinuation for adverse events in HER2 TKD-mutant NSCLC in Beamion LUNG-1.

reason: With roughly 98 patients per arm against an active cemiplimab-chemotherapy control achieving ~21% pCR, detecting a realistic 6-9 percentage point incremental pCR gain at two-sided alpha 0.05 is underpowered.
rationale: This 195-patient Phase 2 perioperative NSCLC trial evaluates adding anti-LAG-3 fianlimab to cemiplimab plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy on blinded pathological complete response (pCR). Standard neoadjuvant PD-1/PD-L1 blockade plus chemotherapy produces pCR rates of 18% to 25% in stage II-IIIB NSCLC (KEYNOTE-671, CheckMate 816, AEGEAN). While dual LAG-3/PD-1 inhibition shows synergistic activity in melanoma, incremental benefit atop chemo-immunotherapy in unselected NSCLC has been modest so far, and ~98 patients per arm requires roughly a 14 percentage point observed difference to reach two-sided p<0.05. Primary completion passed in August 2026, making public readout by mid-2027 likely.

assumptions.claim: Perioperative pembrolizumab plus cisplatin-based chemotherapy achieved a pathological complete response rate of 18.1% in resectable stage II-IIIB NSCLC in KEYNOTE-671.
Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy achieved a pathological complete response rate of 24.0% in resectable NSCLC in CheckMate 816.

reason: As an active, non-recruiting 52-week rollover extension from a completed parent study, Tranquillo LTE should finish near its March 2027 target without major amendments.
rationale: Tranquillo LTE is Pfizer's 394-patient Phase 3 long-term extension evaluating 52-week safety and randomized withdrawal/up-titration of ritlecitinib in nonsegmental vitiligo participants rolling over directly from parent study B7981040. Because enrollment is closed and all participants have a fixed 52-week treatment duration plus 30-day safety follow-up ending around March 2027, completion >90 days late (past late June 2027) or termination is unlikely. However, August 31, 2027 is only five months after primary completion, well before the standard 12-month FDAAA reporting deadline, keeping ClinicalTrials.gov posting probability low by that date.

reason: Inclusion of lower CLDN18.2 expression cutoffs or higher gastroesophageal junction proportions alongside early on-target gastrointestinal toxicity discontinuations could dilute the PFS benefit.
rationale: This 486-patient double-blind Phase 3 trial in China tests ADCC-enhanced anti-CLDN18.2 antibody M108 plus CAPOX versus placebo plus CAPOX in first-line CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative, PD-L1 CPS<5 gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma. The target and backbone regimen are strongly validated by GLOW (zolbetuximab + CAPOX, PFS HR 0.687, median 8.21 vs 6.80 months, predominantly Asian cohort) and SPOTLIGHT (HR 0.75). With 486 patients and high affinity/ADCC engineering, M108 has good power to demonstrate PFS superiority, though nausea/vomiting discontinuations and potential inclusion of moderate CLDN18.2 expressors pose moderate risk. Recruiting status in late 2026 suggests some completion delay.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 GLOW trial, zolbetuximab plus CAPOX improved median PFS to 8.21 months versus 6.80 months for placebo plus CAPOX (HR 0.687) in CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma.
In SPOTLIGHT, zolbetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 significantly prolonged PFS and OS compared with placebo plus mFOLFOX6 in CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma.

reason: Adding fianlimab to cemiplimab may yield a smaller incremental pCR gain over anti-PD-1 monotherapy than expected in an unselected resectable stage III/IV population of 151 patients.
rationale: Neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 monotherapy in resectable stage III/IV melanoma typically produces pathological complete response rates around 20-25% (e.g., SWOG S1801). Dual LAG-3 plus PD-1 blockade has shown substantially higher pathological response rates (~50-57% with nivolumab/relatlimab) and fianlimab plus cemiplimab demonstrated ~61% ORR in advanced melanoma phase 1 cohorts. With ~75 patients per arm, an ~18 percentage point pCR improvement achieves two-sided p<0.05, giving a solid probability of success, tempered by phase 2 sample variance and recent mixed LAG-3 readouts.

assumptions.claim: Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab monotherapy achieved a 21% pathological complete response rate in resectable stage III/IV melanoma in SWOG S1801.
Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus relatlimab achieved a 57% pathological complete response rate in resectable stage III/IV melanoma.

reason: Active salvage chemotherapy (irinotecan, docetaxel, or S-1) and post-progression crossover therapies may attenuate any overall survival advantage from multi-kinase VEGFR2/AXL inhibition.
rationale: KC1036 is an oral multi-target TKI (VEGFR2, AXL, FLT3) that showed encouraging single-arm phase 2 ORR (~25-30%) and survival in pre-treated ESCC after immunotherapy. However, demonstrating overall survival superiority over active investigator-choice chemotherapy (irinotecan, docetaxel, or S-1, where median OS is ~5.5-6.5 months) is historically challenging for anti-angiogenic TKIs in ESCC (e.g., ALTER-1102 with anlotinib improved PFS over placebo but did not improve OS). With N=490, power is good if true HR<=0.78, yielding near-even odds.

assumptions.claim: In ALTER-1102, anlotinib in previously treated advanced ESCC improved PFS over placebo without demonstrating a statistically significant overall survival benefit.

reason: Sequential dose-cohort escalation across three vaginal AZU-101 doses at a single US site starting July 2026 makes minor enrollment delays past December 2026 likely, though termination risk is low.
rationale: This single-site phase 2A safety/PK study of vaginal lasofoxifene (AZU-101) plans up to 90 postmenopausal women with moderate-to-severe VVA across three sequential cohorts starting July 2026, with registered primary completion only six months later (December 2026). Sequential cohort gating and strict VVA smear/pH screening criteria make slipping more than 90 days past December 2026 moderately likely, while study completion in mid-2027 leaves too little time for ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 2027.

reason: With only 48 patients randomized 2:1 (32 experimental vs 16 placebo) and spontaneous anal HSIL regression around 20-25%, statistical power at two-sided alpha 0.05 is modest.
rationale: Topical/intra-anal artesunate has shown biological activity in HPV-driven cervical and anal intraepithelial neoplasia pilot trials (~50-68% histologic regression). However, biopsy-proven anal HSIL exhibits ~20-28% spontaneous regression over 4-6 months, and a 2:1 allocation of only 48 HIV-negative participants across 2 sites provides limited power (~55%) unless true difference exceeds 35 percentage points. Because the trial remained recruiting in late October 2026 with an 18-week primary endpoint, completion will almost certainly slip past March 2027.

assumptions.claim: Intravaginal artesunate produced histologic regression in roughly two-thirds of HPV-associated CIN2/3 patients in a first-in-human phase 1 study.
