reason: On-target CLDN18.2 gastrointestinal toxicities (nausea, vomiting, hypoalbuminemia) layered onto CAPOX plus tislelizumab could increase early treatment discontinuations and dose reductions, diluting PFS benefit.
rationale: CLDN18.2 is clinically validated in 1L gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma by zolbetuximab phase 3 trials (GLOW PFS HR 0.69; SPOTLIGHT PFS HR 0.75). ASKB589 has enhanced ADCC affinity and showed strong ORR (~75-80%) and durable PFS combined with CAPOX and tislelizumab in Chinese phase 1b/2 cohorts. With 780 patients enrolled (active, not recruiting) and IRC-assessed PFS as sole primary outcome, statistical power is high (>85% for HR 0.75), though background tislelizumab in the control arm (~7 months median PFS) raises the bar modestly.

assumptions.claim: Zolbetuximab plus CAPOX significantly improved progression-free survival with a hazard ratio of 0.687 versus placebo plus CAPOX in GLOW.
Tislelizumab plus chemotherapy achieved a median progression-free survival of approximately 6.9 months in first-line gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma in RATIONALE-305.

reason: Enrolling only 33 low-relapse-risk patients already receiving effective atovaquone-azithromycin leaves severe underpowering to detect faster complete resolution across 11 non-specific symptoms.
rationale: Standard atovaquone plus azithromycin clears acute parasitemia and fever rapidly in immunocompetent, low-relapse-risk babesiosis patients. Requiring 7 consecutive days free of 11 broad self-reported symptoms (including fatigue, headache, cough, and joint aches) introduces substantial noise, while N=33 (~28 resolution events) requires a hazard ratio near 2.1 for 80% power at alpha=0.05. Moreover, tick-borne babesiosis hospitalizations are strictly seasonal in summer, making late recruitment beyond May 2027 likely if target enrollment was not finished during summer 2026.

assumptions.claim: Atovaquone plus azithromycin is effective standard therapy that resolves acute babesiosis in nearly all non-immunocompromised patients.

reason: As an active, non-recruiting fixed-duration 56-week extension of completed STOP-HS phase 3 trials, primary completion should occur near schedule around December 2026 with minimal stopping or amendment risk.
rationale: STOP-HS LTE enrolls roll-over completers from parent phase 3 trials NCT05620823 and NCT05620836 and is already active, not recruiting, with primary and study completion scheduled for late December 2026. Fixed 56-week follow-up makes >90-day slippage unlikely, and Incyte rarely terminates ongoing phase 3 dermatology extensions absent unexpected safety signals. Eight months from December 2026 to August 2027 gives a moderate chance of early ClinicalTrials.gov results posting ahead of the 12-month FDAAA deadline.

reason: Because this GSK vaccine phase 2a trial is already completed as of August 2026, termination is virtually impossible and timely ClinicalTrials.gov results posting within 12 months by August 2027 is highly likely.
rationale: On launch day the trial record already shows status completed with primary and study completion on 2026-08-06. A completed trial almost never transitions to terminated, suspended, or withdrawn. Because 2027-08-31 lies more than 12 months after study completion, GlaxoSmithKline's strong industry-leading compliance with 12-month ClinicalTrials.gov results reporting supports an ~85% probability of posted results, with only minor chance of outcome measure restructuring during results entry.

reason: Meeting both co-primary endpoints requires simultaneous Week 12 superiority on both systolic blood pressure and HbA1c, creating modest compound risk from washout variability or adherence.
rationale: Boryung's phase 3 factorial/add-on combination study tests adding antihypertensive BR1019A (likely fimasartan) on msSBP against an arm lacking antihypertensive therapy, and adding antidiabetic BR1019B on HbA1c against an arm lacking that hypoglycemic agent over 12 weeks (~92 patients/arm). Approved ARB and oral antidiabetic classes reliably lower sitting SBP by ~9-12 mmHg (SD ~13-14 mmHg) and HbA1c by ~0.6-0.8% over component controls, providing >90% power per co-primary and ~82% joint probability of meeting both.

assumptions.claim: Standard-dose ARB monotherapy such as fimasartan reduces sitting systolic blood pressure by roughly 9 to 12 mmHg beyond placebo at 12 weeks.

reason: With only 90 patients registered across three phase II arms and phase III PFS/OS co-primaries also listed, an early phase II readout may be descriptive or underpowered rather than formally meeting all registered primary hypotheses.
rationale: Disitamab vedotin plus PD-1/CTLA-4 blockade (cadonilimab) is biologically active in HER2-expressing (IHC 1+/2+/3+) 2L gastric cancer, likely achieving ~40-45% ORR versus ~16-18% for paclitaxel monotherapy (as seen in RAINBOW control arms). However, only 90 patients (~30/arm) are currently registered for Phase II while Phase III IRC-PFS and OS are also listed as primary outcomes; both small Phase II arm sizes and descriptive Phase II reporting without formal hypothesis testing constrain p_met.

assumptions.claim: Paclitaxel monotherapy achieved an objective response rate of 16% in second-line advanced gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma in the RAINBOW trial.

reason: Allosteric TYK2 inhibition with deucravacitinib previously failed to improve endoscopic or clinical outcomes in Crohn's disease, creating target-validation risk despite TAK-279's higher TYK2 selectivity and coverage.
rationale: TAK-279 (zasocitinib) is a highly selective allosteric TYK2 inhibitor achieving greater IC90 target coverage than deucravacitinib, and testing three active doses (n=67 each vs placebo) gives multiple shots at Week 12 SES-CD endoscopic response where placebo rates average ~14-16%. However, deucravacitinib failed Phase 2 in Crohn's disease (LATTICE-CD), leaving uncertainty whether oral TYK2 blockade sufficiently inhibits mucosal IL-23 signaling compared with anti-IL-23 antibodies or JAK1 inhibitors. Because the study remained recruiting in late October 2026 with a 12-week induction endpoint, primary completion will likely slip past February 2027.

assumptions.claim: Deucravacitinib failed to meet its primary clinical remission and endoscopic response endpoints at Week 12 in the Phase 2 LATTICE-CD trial in Crohn's disease.
Placebo Week 12 endoscopic response rates in modern moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease trials are typically around 12% to 16%.

reason: Although enrollment is already complete, the 24-week safety follow-up in Parts 2 and 3 gives a moderate chance that primary completion extends past February 2027.
rationale: On snapshot date 2026-10-29, this multi-part Phase 1/2 inhaled mRNA trial in healthy volunteers and cystic fibrosis patients is already active, not recruiting, with registered primary and study completion in November 2026. Having completed enrollment sharply reduces termination risk and limits severe delays, though 24-week follow-up in CF cohorts could still push final visits past February 2027. Small private biotechnology sponsors rarely post Phase 1/2 safety results on ClinicalTrials.gov within nine months of completion.

reason: Methotrexate has a gradual onset of clinical action in atopic dermatitis, which could attenuate EASI-75 separation at Week 16 despite well-established longer-term efficacy.
rationale: Methotrexate has well-established clinical activity in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis across active-comparator trials against azathioprine and cyclosporine, and subcutaneous administration improves bioavailability and speed of onset over oral dosing. Against an emollient-only placebo arm where Week 16 EASI-75 is typically ~12-18%, subcutaneous methotrexate (~35-40% EASI-75) with N=277 provides high statistical power for both EASI-75 and EASI-50. Because the trial was still recruiting in late October 2026 with a 16-week primary endpoint, primary completion will very likely occur more than 90 days after November 2026.

assumptions.claim: Methotrexate demonstrated comparable clinical efficacy to azathioprine in adults with severe atopic eczema in a randomized controlled trial.
Placebo EASI-75 response rates at Week 16 in adult moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis monotherapy trials without mandatory topical corticosteroids are typically around 12% to 18%.

reason: With only 83 enrolled patients, manufacturing attrition or an immunotherapy tail without early median PFS separation could leave the trial underpowered.
rationale: Autologous TIL therapy has shown meaningful activity (~31-36% ORR and durable responses) in pretreated recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer, whereas single-agent gemcitabine control performs poorly (~5-8% ORR, median PFS ~2.1-2.8 months). Moreover, this open-label study measures PFS from first study treatment rather than randomization, favoring GT101 by excluding pre-infusion manufacturing dropouts and capturing cytoreduction from lymphodepleting chemotherapy. With ~62 expected events across 83 patients, power is solid for HR ~0.50-0.55, though ongoing recruitment in late October 2026 makes completion delays past May 2027 likely.

assumptions.claim: Autologous TIL therapy lifileucel demonstrated durable objective responses in pretreated recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer in study C-145-04.
Single-agent chemotherapy in second-line or later recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer achieves median progression-free survival of roughly 2 to 3 months.

reason: Large 48-week global Sjögren's trials using subjective symptom endpoints like ESSPRI and DASPRI risk substantial placebo improvement from regression to the mean.
rationale: In Phase 2 (NCT04129164), dazodalibep significantly improved ESSPRI at Week 24 (-1.80 vs -0.53 for placebo; difference -1.27, p=0.0002) specifically in Sjögren's patients with ESSPRI >=5 and ESSDAI <5. With N=434 (SD ~2.0), this Phase 3 trial can detect ~0.40-point differences, providing strong power even if global 194-site placebo responses double and the treatment effect shrinks by half across both correlated co-primary endpoints (ESSPRI and DASPRI) at Week 48. With registered primary completion in October 2026 and study completion in December 2026, top-line results by Q1/Q2 2027 are highly likely.

assumptions.claim: Dazodalibep achieved a statistically significant improvement over placebo in ESSPRI score in Sjögren's syndrome participants with moderate-to-severe symptom burden and low systemic disease activity in Phase 2.

reason: Relatlimab plus nivolumab is an active dual anti-LAG-3/anti-PD-1 comparator, leaving limited room for fianlimab plus cemiplimab to demonstrate statistically significant ORR superiority.
rationale: Fianlimab uses higher anti-LAG-3 dosing than relatlimab to achieve fuller receptor saturation and showed ~61% ORR with cemiplimab in single-arm Phase 1 cohorts. However, Phase 1 melanoma response rates routinely attenuate under randomized Phase 3 BICR assessment, while excluding uveal, acral, and mucosal subtypes should lift Opdualag's ORR slightly above RELATIVITY-047's 43.1% toward ~46-47%. Demonstrating statistical superiority (~11-13 percentage points) over another anti-LAG-3/anti-PD-1 doublet is challenging. Ongoing recruitment in late October 2026 also makes slipping >90 days past March 2027 primary completion likely.

assumptions.claim: Relatlimab plus nivolumab achieved an objective response rate of approximately 43% in previously untreated metastatic or unresectable melanoma in RELATIVITY-047.
Fianlimab plus cemiplimab demonstrated objective response rates around 60% in anti-PD-1-naive advanced melanoma expansion cohorts in Phase 1.

reason: Novel CNS mechanisms tested across 50 US commercial MDD sites face high Week 4 placebo MADRS responses and substantial regression of subgroup signals from earlier trials.
rationale: SP-624 (an oral SIRT6 activator) is evaluated in a 497-patient, 50-site US Phase 2b MDD trial after Phase 2a (NCT04479852) showed sex-divergent exploratory signals rather than robust overall efficacy, yet this study still enrolls both men and women. Large US commercial-site MDD trials experience substantial Week 4 placebo MADRS reductions (~11-12 points, SD ~9) and low success rates for unvalidated mechanisms. Moreover, the trial completed in July 2026 without an immediate positive readout before late October 2026, modestly lowering conditional expectations.

assumptions.claim: SP-624 was previously evaluated in a randomized placebo-controlled Phase 2a trial in adults with major depressive disorder.

reason: Exendin-4 Fc fusion may have slightly lower glycemic efficacy or higher anti-drug antibody attenuation than dulaglutide, risking failure if superiority is required or if efficacy lags.
rationale: Chinese registrational Phase 3 trials of weekly GLP-1 receptor agonists versus dulaglutide with N=200 per arm are standardly powered for a 0.4% HbA1c non-inferiority margin at Week 26, which governs p_met under the round's rules. At 2.4 mg weekly, JY09 (exendin-4 Fc fusion) should achieve roughly -1.4% HbA1c reduction, matching dulaglutide (~-1.4% in Chinese metformin add-on studies) and easily meeting non-inferiority. By contrast, p_key_secondary requires statistical superiority on HbA1c <7%, which is unlikely against dulaglutide. Near-completed follow-up supports a likely 2027 Chinese NDA filing.

assumptions.claim: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg weekly reduces HbA1c by approximately 1.4 to 1.5 percentage points at Week 26 in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on oral antihyperglycemic therapy.

reason: Enrollment is already complete with a fixed 56-week assessment schedule and a major pharma sponsor, making substantial completion delays or termination unlikely.
rationale: As of 2026-10-29, Janssen's pediatric ulcerative colitis Phase 3 trial (QUASAR Jr) is already active, not recruiting, with primary completion set for 2027-02-10 and study completion for 2027-04-28. Because last-patient-in has already occurred and the primary outcome is assessed at a fixed Week 56 visit, Janssen's registered completion date should be accurate within 90 days. Termination risk is minimal given guselkumab's established adult UC approval, while ClinicalTrials.gov results posting typically occurs closer to the 12-month post-completion mark after August 2027.

reason: Extracellular anti-MTBR tau antibodies have limited central nervous system exposure and may not curb intracellular tau tangle amplification enough to significantly reduce global tau PET.
rationale: Unlike N-terminal anti-tau antibodies (semorinemab, tilavonimab) that failed on both tau PET and clinical endpoints, BMS-986446 targets the microtubule-binding region (MTBR) mediating trans-synaptic tau seeding. In Phase 2 TOGETHER, mid-domain/near-MTBR antibody bepranemab significantly slowed tau PET accumulation despite missing overall CDR-SB, giving BMS-986446 a credible ~45% chance on its Week 76 tau PET primary endpoint. However, N=310 is underpowered for small clinical CDR-SB effects (~14% key secondary probability). Being active, not recruiting in October 2026 makes on-time March 2027 completion likely.

assumptions.claim: The N-terminal anti-tau antibody semorinemab failed to slow tau accumulation on tau PET or clinical decline on CDR-SB in prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease.

Bepranemab slowed brain tau accumulation measured by tau PET in the Phase 2 TOGETHER study in prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease while missing the primary CDR-SB endpoint in the overall population.

reason: Intra-articular normal saline injections produce substantial and durable placebo analgesia in osteoarthritis, while extended-release triamcinolone efficacy begins waning around Week 12 in a modest 150-patient sample.
rationale: ZILRETTA (extended-release triamcinolone acetonide) demonstrated significant Week 12 pain reduction over saline placebo in knee osteoarthritis (~0.98 NRS points in NCT02357459). However, glenohumeral osteoarthritis exhibits large intra-articular saline placebo responses, coexisting rotator cuff pathology adds variance, and corticosteroid durability tapers near Week 12. With 100 active and 50 placebo patients and an expected SD near 2.3 NRS points, an observed difference around -0.78 points is needed for p<0.05, yielding roughly coin-flip statistical power. Because enrollment is complete with December 2026 primary completion, topline readout by mid-2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: In the pivotal Phase 3 knee osteoarthritis trial, ZILRETTA 32 mg significantly improved Week 12 average daily pain versus saline placebo.
ZILRETTA is an approved 32 mg extended-release PLGA microsphere formulation of triamcinolone acetonide for intra-articular osteoarthritis pain.

reason: With only 30 patients per arm and an exploratory objective focused on estimating between-group effect size, the study lacks statistical power to show significant superiority over surgical flap coverage plus systemic antibiotics.
rationale: STIMULAN VG (calcium sulfate beads loaded with vancomycin and gentamicin) delivers high local antibiotic levels in dead space after bony debridement, plausibly modestly reducing dehiscence and reinfection following flap closure of Stage IV pressure ulcers with focal osteomyelitis. However, surgical excision, flap coverage, and systemic antibiotics already achieve substantial short-term closure, and 30 patients per arm requires roughly a 25-percentage-point gain to reach p<0.05. Moreover, the registry explicitly frames this Phase 2 trial as estimating effect size rather than testing a formal primary hypothesis, and active recruitment in late October 2026 signals likely delay.

reason: Gastrointestinal intolerability in older insulin-treated patients with moderate-to-severe chronic kidney disease is the main clinical risk, though unlikely to negate retatrutide's large glycemic efficacy.
rationale: Retatrutide (GIP/GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist) produced ~2.0% HbA1c reductions in Phase 2 type 2 diabetes (NCT04867785), and incretin agonists retain full glycemic efficacy across moderate and severe renal impairment because clearance is proteolytic rather than renal. Added to basal insulin in 320 randomized participants over 52 weeks, a placebo-adjusted HbA1c reduction near -1.45 percentage points gives overwhelming statistical power (>99%) for both HbA1c change and <7.0% target attainment. With enrollment complete and registered October 2026 primary completion, topline readout and inclusion in Lilly's 2027 T2D regulatory filing are highly probable.

assumptions.claim: In Phase 2 type 2 diabetes (NCT04867785), retatrutide achieved HbA1c reductions up to approximately 2.0 percentage points versus minimal change on placebo.
Peptide incretin agonists added to basal insulin in phase 3 trials (such as tirzepatide in SURPASS-5) consistently reduce HbA1c by over 1.2 percentage points versus placebo.

reason: Because this Chinese Phase 2 beta-thalassemia trial is still recruiting in late October 2026 with a 24-week primary assessment window, primary completion will very likely slip past March 2027.
rationale: On October 29, 2026, this 64-patient, 5-site Chinese Phase 2 trial of oral AND017 in transfusion-dependent and non-transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia remains listed as recruiting despite a registered December 2026 primary completion date. With a 24-week treatment timeframe plus pre-screening transfusion documentation requirements, completing follow-up within 90 days of December 2026 is unlikely unless registry updates lag substantially. Termination risk is low, and China-only Phase 2 trials rarely post full results tables on ClinicalTrials.gov within months of completion.

reason: Enrolling 63 lower-risk MDS patients with strict pre-study hemoglobin and transfusion history criteria while still recruiting in late October 2026 makes a 25-week primary completion before April 2027 unlikely.
rationale: This open-label Chinese Phase 2 dose-ranging study of AND017 in lower-risk MDS anemia started in March 2025, lists one active site in the snapshot, requires 16 weeks of pre-randomization transfusion history plus up to 25 weeks of post-dose evaluation, and is still recruiting in late October 2026 against a December 2026 target. Consequently, primary completion is highly likely to exceed the 90-day lateness threshold beyond March 31, 2027, with low odds of early ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 2027.

reason: A multi-stage Phase 1/2 oncology escalation-and-expansion study still recruiting in late October 2026 is very likely to extend past March 2027 while awaiting confirmed RECIST responses.
rationale: This open-label multi-stage Phase 1/2 trial evaluating weekly intravenous WGI-0301 plus sorafenib in second-line post-immunotherapy advanced HCC remains in recruiting status in late October 2026 with a December 2026 registered primary completion date. Sequential dose escalation followed by randomized multi-arm dose expansion for confirmed RECIST 1.1 ORR typically experiences enrollment and follow-up extensions beyond 90 days, carries modest early-termination risk in refractory HCC, and rarely posts ClinicalTrials.gov structured results promptly.

reason: Optimizing BHV-7000 to avoid GABAergic sedation could result in submaximal central Kv7.2/7.3 target engagement compared with earlier potassium channel openers against a sizable focal epilepsy placebo response.
rationale: Kv7.2/7.3 potassium channel activation is strongly validated in refractory focal epilepsy by ezogabine/retigabine and azetukalner (XEN1101, NCT03796962, which achieved ~53% median seizure reduction at 25 mg versus ~18% on placebo). BHV-7000 selectively activates Kv7.2/7.3 without GABAA potentiation, allowing 75 mg daily dosing with low CNS adverse-event discontinuation over an 8-week maintenance window without titration. With ~130 patients per arm and completion in October 2026, statistical power is solid, tempered mainly by uncertainty around CNS receptor occupancy and global 150-site placebo variability.

assumptions.claim: In the X-TOLE Phase 2b focal epilepsy trial (NCT03796962), Kv7 potassium channel opener XEN1101 significantly reduced monthly focal seizure frequency versus placebo (-18.2% median change on placebo).

reason: Non-VEGF pathways such as semaphorin 3A inhibition rarely produce rapid two-step vascular lesion regression on Diabetic Retinopathy Severity Scale fundus photographs, especially in small 35-patient arms.
rationale: BI 764524 is an intravitreal anti-Sema3A antibody designed to promote revascularization of ischemic retina (previously studied in diabetic macular ischemia in HORNBILL, NCT04424290). Unlike anti-VEGF therapy (aflibercept in PANORAMA, NCT02718326), non-VEGF ischemia-targeting agents have historically struggled to drive >=2-step DRSS regression on color fundus photography at Week 52, and ~35 patients per arm gives low power unless the effect exceeds 25 percentage points. Furthermore, because the trial is still recruiting in late October 2026 with a 52-week primary endpoint, primary completion will likely slip into late 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the PANORAMA trial of moderate-to-severe NPDR (NCT02718326), approximately 15% of sham-treated eyes achieved a >=2-step DRSS improvement at Week 52.
BI 764524 is a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting semaphorin 3A previously evaluated for safety in diabetic macular ischemia in the HORNBILL trial.

reason: Enrolling only 48 patients in total leaves severe underpowering to achieve statistical significance on paired Week 52 liver biopsy fibrosis and histological NASH co-primary responder endpoints.
rationale: VSA006 (ARO-HSD) is a hepatocyte-targeted siRNA silencing HSD17B13, a genetically validated target whose loss-of-function protects against steatohepatitis and fibrosis progression (Abul-Husn et al. 2018) and lowered transaminases in Phase 1. However, with only 48 randomized patients total and noisy 52-week biopsy histology, statistical power to demonstrate p<0.05 on histological fibrosis improvement AND NASH improvement co-primary endpoints is well below 30%. Additionally, human HSD17B13 loss-of-function does not substantially reduce hepatic steatosis, making significant MRI-PDFF liver fat reduction unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Human loss-of-function variants in HSD17B13 are associated with reduced risk of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis and fibrosis without significantly reducing simple hepatic steatosis.

reason: Lower-than-expected background exacerbation rates during improved controller adherence in placebo recipients represent the main risk, though anti-IL-5 blockade remains robustly powered at 480 patients.
rationale: Drug 610 (SSGJ-610) is a humanized anti-IL-5 monoclonal antibody evaluated in 480 Chinese adults with severe eosinophilic asthma over 52 weeks. IL-5 neutralization is a highly validated mechanism that consistently halves severe asthma exacerbations globally (MENSA mepolizumab rate ratio 0.47, NCT01691521) and in Chinese Phase 3 populations (NCT03562195, rate ratio 0.35). With 480 patients, power exceeds 90% for both annualized exacerbation rate and time to first exacerbation. Recruiting status in October 2026 suggests moderate risk of delayed registry completion past May 2027, though stale Chinese CT.gov updates are common.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 MENSA trial (NCT01691521), subcutaneous anti-IL-5 therapy with mepolizumab reduced the annualized asthma exacerbation rate by 53% versus placebo (rate ratio 0.47).

A Phase 3 trial of anti-IL-5 mepolizumab in Chinese patients with severe eosinophilic asthma (NCT03562195) demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in clinically significant exacerbations over 52 weeks.

reason: With only 100 participants across two arms and roughly 35-40 expected treatment dropouts by 24 weeks, the trial has very low statistical power to demonstrate significant superiority on treatment retention alongside take-home dosing.
rationale: Sonara facilitates remote video-observed methadone take-homes, which may increase take-home dose counts compared with clinic-restricted policies, but usual care already includes take-home methadone under modernized OTP flexibilities. Crucially, with N=100 (about 50 per arm) and ~38% expected 24-week attrition, only ~36 dropout events are expected, requiring an implausibly large hazard ratio (~0.45) to reach p<0.05 on retention, and co-primary rules require meeting both primary endpoints.

assumptions.claim: Six-month retention in US methadone maintenance programs is typically around 55% to 70% (30% to 45% attrition).

reason: Selective IL-13 blockade does not directly inhibit IL-4-mediated IgE class switching and mast-cell sensitization, and adding a biologic onto background intranasal corticosteroids leaves a modest incremental symptom window.
rationale: Type 2 cytokines drive perennial allergic rhinitis mucus hypersecretion and nasal congestion, and dual IL-4/IL-13 blockade (dupilumab) reduced TNSS by roughly 1.0 point in comorbid perennial allergic rhinitis. However, selective IL-13 inhibition with lebrikizumab leaves IL-4 signaling intact, and background standard intranasal corticosteroid therapy produces substantial placebo-arm improvement (~2.8 points on the 0-12 TNSS). With N=450 (225/arm) and SD ~2.6, a ~0.5-point difference achieves p<0.05, giving an approximately even chance of success.

assumptions.claim: Dupilumab improved perennial allergic rhinitis TNSS (0-12 scale) versus placebo in comorbid asthma patients by roughly 0.8 to 1.1 points.

reason: The trial lists start, primary completion, and study completion all in December 2026 while still recruiting for a 6-month dosing and 12-month safety follow-up protocol, making a major completion delay almost certain.
rationale: On snapshot date 2026-10-29, this 40-patient cochlear implant trial has a registered start and completion both set to 2026-12 despite requiring 6 months of treatment and 12 months of TEAE assessment. Consequently, active follow-up will extend well into 2027-2028, driving a high probability of being marked >90 days late on 2027-08-31 and nearly zero chance of results posting by then.

reason: Because both progression-free survival and overall survival are registered as co-primary outcomes, immature survival follow-up or post-progression crossover in China could prevent overall survival from reaching significance simultaneously.
rationale: The control arm is paclitaxel monotherapy rather than ramucirumab plus paclitaxel. Anti-VEGFR2 blockade (pulocimab/AK109) added to paclitaxel already confers proven PFS and OS benefit in second-line gastric cancer (analogous to RAINBOW), and Phase 1b/2 data of cadonilimab plus pulocimab and paclitaxel after first-line PD-1 inhibition showed promising ORR (~48%) and mPFS (~7 months). The main hurdle is meeting both co-primary endpoints (PFS and OS) by the readout.

assumptions.claim: In the RAINBOW Phase 3 trial, paclitaxel monotherapy control achieved median PFS of 2.9 months and anti-VEGFR2 plus paclitaxel improved PFS with HR 0.635.

reason: Anti-TIGIT blockade added to PD-1 plus bevacizumab failed to improve response rates or PFS in larger randomized first-line HCC studies (such as AdvanTIG-206), and N=39 per arm requires an extreme effect size to achieve statistical significance on both ORR and PFS.
rationale: Serplulimab plus HLX04 (bevacizumab biosimilar) is already an active first-line HCC backbone with ~30% RECIST 1.1 ORR (mirroring ORIENT-32 and IMbrave150). While small early tiragolumab data (MORPHEUS-Liver) sparked enthusiasm for anti-TIGIT triplets in HCC, subsequent randomized data (AdvanTIG-206) showed zero incremental ORR or PFS benefit. With only ~39 patients per arm and dual primary endpoints (ORR and PFS), reaching two-sided p<0.05 on both is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Anti-PD-1/PD-L1 plus bevacizumab regimens in first-line unresectable HCC typically achieve RECIST 1.1 objective response rates of 27% to 35%.

reason: Oral O-GlcNAcase inhibition has no clinically validated disease-modifying efficacy in tauopathies, and every prior randomized trial in progressive supranuclear palsy has failed to slow 52-week PSPRS progression.
rationale: FNP-223 (formerly ASN90) inhibits O-GlcNAcase to reduce intracellular tau aggregation. Although oral CNS penetration avoids the extracellular limitation of failed anti-tau antibodies (gosuranemab, tilavonemab), PSP pathology is already widespread at symptom onset and every Phase 2/3 PSP trial to date has shown almost identical ~10-11 point 52-week PSPRS decline across active and placebo arms. Enrollment (N=241) is well powered for a ~3-point slowing, so trial execution is solid, but biological translation risk is very high.

assumptions.claim: Placebo-treated patients with PSP-Richardson syndrome consistently worsen by approximately 10 to 11 points on the 28-item PSPRS over 52 weeks.

reason: In unselected third-line gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma, modest responsiveness in low-TROP2 or topoisomerase-I-refractory tumors could dilute the overall survival hazard ratio above the ~0.81 significance boundary.
rationale: Sacituzumab tirumotecan (MK-2870/SKB264) carries a belotecan-derived topoisomerase I payload at DAR ~7.4 and showed ~22% ORR and ~7.6-9.5 month median OS in heavily pretreated gastric/GEJ Phase 2 cohorts, while winning Phase 3 trials in TNBC and NSCLC. Against 3L+ physician's choice chemotherapy (median OS ~5.7 months in TAGS; irinotecan/taxane similar in 3L+), gastroesophageal tumors are sensitive to topoisomerase I payloads, giving a favorable (>50%) probability of achieving OS superiority with N=473.

assumptions.claim: Third-line or later metastatic gastric/GEJ cancer treated with trifluridine-tipiracil achieved a median overall survival of 5.7 months in the TAGS Phase 3 trial.

reason: Subjective self-reported symptom relief ratings every 15 minutes can occasionally yield high spontaneous 4-hour placebo response rates in milder or resolving hereditary angioedema attacks.
rationale: Direct intravenous replacement of human plasma-derived C1 esterase inhibitor in patients with confirmed congenital C1-INH deficiency (<50% functional activity) directly corrects the underlying bradykinin-mediated vascular permeability defect. Prior placebo-controlled Phase 3 trials of IV C1-INH concentrates (e.g., Berinert I.M.P.A.C.T.1, Cinryze, Ruconest) consistently showed rapid onset of symptom relief (median ~0.5-1.0 hours vs >1.5-4 hours on placebo, HR >2.0). With 124 planned participants, statistical power against placebo is very high.

assumptions.claim: Intravenous plasma-derived C1-INH concentrate significantly shortened time to onset of symptom relief versus placebo in acute HAE attacks in the IMPACT1 Phase 3 trial.

reason: Because the trial is already active and not recruiting as of October 2026 with an 18-week primary assessment window and February 2027 primary completion, it should complete cleanly on schedule.
rationale: Enrollment of 108 patients is already completed ('active, not recruiting' on 2026-10-29) and the primary corneal TEAE assessment spans up to 18 weeks (~4.5 months), matching the registered February 2027 primary completion date closely. AbbVie rarely terminates fully accrued supportive oncology studies early and reliably posts results within 12 months of completion, giving a moderate chance of early posting by August 2027.

reason: Topoisomerase-I antibody-drug conjugates have repeatedly improved PFS without achieving significant overall survival superiority over docetaxel in EGFR wild-type NSCLC, and myelosuppression dose reductions may temper long-term survival gains.
rationale: BL-B01D1 (izalontamab brengitecan), an EGFRxHER3 bispecific topoisomerase-I ADC, demonstrated promising response rates (~30-40%) in Phase 1 EGFR-wild-type NSCLC cohorts, and its large sample size (N=698) provides strong power to detect an OS HR around 0.80-0.83. However, beating docetaxel on overall survival in post-IO, post-platinum EGFR-wt NSCLC has proved notoriously difficult for other topoisomerase-I ADCs (Dato-DXd missed OS in TROPION-Lung01; sacituzumab govitecan missed OS in EVOKE-01), justifying a slightly sub-50% probability.

assumptions.claim: Both datopotamab deruxtecan (TROPION-Lung01) and sacituzumab govitecan (EVOKE-01) failed to achieve statistically significant overall survival superiority over docetaxel in previously treated NSCLC.

reason: Randomizing 120 patients 2:1 yields roughly 80 deaths, requiring a large hazard ratio improvement (~0.62) over an active venetoclax-azacitidine backbone where triplets frequently add myelosuppressive mortality.
rationale: Cusatuzumab (anti-CD70) showed modest activity with azacitidine in CULMINATE and encouraging single-arm remission rates with venetoclax-azacitidine in ELEVATE, leading Janssen to return rights before OncoVerity resumed development. However, randomized triplets in unfit AML have repeatedly struggled to improve overall survival over venetoclax-azacitidine (~14.7 months median OS in VIALE-A) due to cumulative cytopenias and infections. Moreover, 120 randomized patients (80 vs 40) provide low statistical power at two-sided alpha 0.05 unless the true survival hazard ratio is exceptionally strong.

assumptions.claim: In VIALE-A, venetoclax plus azacitidine achieved a median overall survival of 14.7 months in newly diagnosed AML patients ineligible for intensive chemotherapy.
In VIALE-A, 24% of patients in the venetoclax-azacitidine group discontinued treatment due to adverse events.

reason: Gene-agnostic NR2E3 modifier therapy across heterogeneous retinitis pigmentosa genotypes faces substantial biological uncertainty, while subretinal surgery carries early postoperative visual risks.
rationale: OCU400 delivers NR2E3 as a modifier gene therapy across RHO-mutated and gene-agnostic retinitis pigmentosa. Enrollment of all 140 participants is complete with 52-week primary completion due February 2027, making a Q2 2027 topline release highly likely. While gene-agnostic rescue of degenerating photoreceptors is biologically ambitious and prior inherited retinal disease Phase 3 trials (such as XOLARIS and LUMEVOQ) have struggled, comparison against an untreated control on a multi-luminance navigation maze (LDNA) where Phase 1/2 stabilized or improved lux levels gives moderate success odds.

assumptions.claim: Phase 1/2 testing of subretinal OCU400 evaluated multi-luminance mobility/LDNA and low-luminance visual acuity in patients with RHO and NR2E3-related retinal degeneration.

reason: Ruxolitinib-based frontline chronic GVHD therapy achieves high 6-month response rates, leaving limited headroom for a ~130-patient estimation-sized Phase 2 trial to show formal statistical superiority.
rationale: Axatilimab (anti-CSF-1R) proved highly active in refractory chronic GVHD in AGAVE-201, supporting biological synergy with JAK1/2 inhibition by ruxolitinib. However, in newly diagnosed moderate-to-severe cGVHD, ruxolitinib (with or without corticosteroids) already produces high 6-month objective response rates (~60-75%). Furthermore, this open-label Phase 2 study (N=130) is framed to determine preliminary efficacy and contribution of components, so it may either lack power to clear p<0.05 over a strong active control or report descriptive estimation without formal hypothesis testing.

assumptions.claim: Axatilimab demonstrated high overall response rates across three dose cohorts in recurrent or refractory chronic GVHD in the Phase 2 AGAVE-201 study.
Ruxolitinib achieved a 49.7% overall response rate at week 24 in glucocorticoid-refractory chronic GVHD in REACH3.

reason: Only an unexpectedly high delayed EASI 90 rebound on continued dupilumab or protocol deviations could narrow an otherwise overwhelming efficacy gap at week 8.
rationale: SWITCH-UP enrolls moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis patients with persistent active disease (EASI >=12, vIGA-AD >=3, WP-NRS >=4) despite at least 4 months of ongoing dupilumab, then randomizes them to continue failing dupilumab versus switching to upadacitinib 15 mg with week-2 escalation to 30 mg. Even in biologic-naive patients (Heads Up, Level Up), upadacitinib rapidly outperformed dupilumab on EASI 90 and itch relief by week 8. Against continued dupilumab in established dupilumab inadequate responders, ~184 patients provide well over 95% power for both EASI 90 and WP-NRS 0/1.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3b Heads Up trial, upadacitinib 30 mg achieved significantly higher EASI 75, EASI 90, and pruritus improvements than dupilumab 300 mg in adults with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis.
In Level Up, upadacitinib 15 mg escalated to 30 mg based on clinical response was superior to dupilumab on simultaneous EASI 90 and WP-NRS 0/1 at week 16.

reason: Although active and not recruiting with a December 2026 primary completion date for 12-week PSA50 cohorts, multi-part dose-optimization arms and 5-year TEAE co-primary framing create moderate risk of registry date adjustments.
rationale: AlphaBreak is an open-label, multi-part Phase 2 dose-optimization study of 225Ac-PSMA-I&T (FPI-2265) in post-177Lu-PSMA mCRPC that is already active, not recruiting as of October 2026 with registered primary completion in December 2026. Because the PSA50 primary endpoint requires only 12 weeks from first dose, initial primary completion is on track, though sequential Part B cohorts or aligning registry primary completion with the 5-year TEAE co-primary timeframe could push the registered date past March 2027.

reason: As an oral gamma-secretase modulator, RO7269162 suppresses new A-beta42 production rather than actively clearing pre-existing plaques, yielding only a modest Centiloid separation over 72 weeks.
rationale: RO7269162 (RG6289) is Roche's oral gamma-secretase modulator shifting APP processing from fibrillogenic Abeta42/40 toward shorter Abeta37/38 peptides. In amyloid-positive (>=24 CL) preclinical/prodromal AD, placebo typically accumulates ~3-6 Centiloids over 72 weeks, while inhibiting new Abeta42 monomer generation halts accumulation and permits slow endogenous clearance (~4-7 CL net separation, analogous to BACE inhibitors). With 256 participants and low longitudinal PET variance (~10-12 CL SD), even a 5-6 CL difference is detectable, though lack of formal testing on a co-primary biomarker endpoint tempers p_met.

assumptions.claim: Oral amyloid-production inhibitors in prodromal AD produce small net amyloid PET reductions (~4 to 6 Centiloids difference versus placebo over 1.5 to 2 years) compared with plaque-clearing antibodies.

reason: Acute stroke neuroprotectants have repeatedly failed to add measurable 90-day mRS shift benefit on top of modern rapid intravenous thrombolysis and thrombectomy.
rationale: NoNO-42 is a plasmin-resistant PSD-95 inhibitor designed to overcome the thrombolytic cleavage that blunted nerinetide (NA-1) in ESCAPE-NA1. However, nerinetide also missed its primary endpoint without thrombolysis in ESCAPE-NEXT, and demonstrating an mRS shift odds ratio >=1.4 with up to 600 thrombolysis-treated stroke patients remains difficult. Operationally, the trial is still recruiting across 9 Canadian sites in late October 2026 with a 90-day outcome, making a >90-day delay past December 2026 highly likely.

assumptions.claim: In ESCAPE-NA1, nerinetide failed to significantly improve 90-day functional outcome overall due to drug-drug interaction with alteplase.
In ESCAPE-NEXT, nerinetide did not meet its primary 90-day mRS endpoint in endovascular thrombectomy patients not receiving thrombolytics.

reason: Binge eating disorder trials consistently exhibit large 65-75% placebo reductions in weekly binge episodes, which can mask moderate dopaminergic/noradrenergic drug effects.
rationale: Solriamfetol is a dopamine-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor (with TAAR1 agonist activity) tested at 150 and 300 mg daily in 450 adults with BED. Catecholaminergic reuptake/release agents (lisdexamfetamine and high-dose dasotraline) have reliably reduced binge frequency in Phase 3 BED studies, and solriamfetol 300 mg showed central behavioural efficacy in adult ADHD (FOCUS). That strong mechanistic precedent is balanced against notoriously large placebo improvements in 12-week BED trials (~3.5-4.0 fewer episodes/week). Because recruitment is ongoing in late October 2026, completion will likely slip into 2027.

assumptions.claim: Lisdexamfetamine significantly reduced weekly binge eating days versus placebo at week 12 in two pivotal Phase 3 BED trials despite substantial placebo improvements.
Dasotraline (a dopamine and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor) at 6 mg/day significantly reduced binge eating days per week at week 12 in adults with BED.

reason: CDK4/6 inhibition has shown minimal clinical durability across aggressive H3-altered and wildtype high-grade gliomas, and 45 total patients cannot detect modest EFS gains.
rationale: This randomized Phase 2 trial enrolls only 45 children and young adults with newly diagnosed high-grade glioma (including H3 K27-altered non-pontine diffuse midline glioma, H3 G34-mutant, and H3/IDH-wildtype HGG) post-radiotherapy. Despite brain penetration and CDKN2A/B pathway rationale, abemaciclib produced only marginal PFS activity and no OS benefit in adult glioblastoma (INSIGhT), and temozolomide offers limited activity in pediatric HGG. With ~32 expected EFS events across 45 patients, achieving p<0.05 requires an observed hazard ratio near 0.48, making success unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In the adaptive Phase 2 INSIGhT trial in newly diagnosed glioblastoma, abemaciclib did not improve overall survival.

reason: With roughly 21 patients per arm across four groups, inter-patient QMG variability and potential dose-limiting myotonia at the top dose could prevent clear statistical separation at day 21.
rationale: NMD670 is a skeletal muscle-specific ClC-1 chloride channel inhibitor that directly enhances neuromuscular transmission excitability. In a randomized crossover Phase 1/2a study in AChR/MuSK+ myasthenia gravis, single doses of NMD670 produced rapid, clinically meaningful QMG score reductions versus placebo without serious safety issues. Testing three BID doses over 21 days where any single dose meeting QMG superiority counts gives solid proof-of-concept odds, tempered by small per-arm sample size (~21/arm), multi-dose alpha considerations, and risk of tachyphylaxis or mild myotonia.

assumptions.claim: Single oral doses of NMD670 improved Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis (QMG) total scores compared with placebo in a randomized proof-of-mechanism trial in patients with myasthenia gravis.

reason: Heterogeneous post-osimertinib resistance mechanisms and multiplicity split across two experimental Dato-DXd arms could attenuate the PFS benefit over platinum-pemetrexed.
rationale: TROPION-Lung15 tests Dato-DXd with or without continued osimertinib against platinum-pemetrexed in 768 post-osimertinib EGFRm NSCLC patients. Platinum-pemetrexed consistently yields ~4.5-5.5 months median PFS in this setting (MARIPOSA-2, KEYNOTE-789, HERTHENA-Lung02), whereas Dato-DXd showed solid monotherapy activity in TROPION-Lung05 and strong PFS (~9.5-11.7 months) combined with osimertinib in ORCHARD, with continued osimertinib aiding CNS control. Having two experimental arms boosts the chance at least one beats chemotherapy despite alpha splitting.

assumptions.claim: In Phase 3 trials of EGFR-mutated NSCLC after osimertinib progression, platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy achieved median PFS of approximately 4.2 to 5.5 months.
Datopotamab deruxtecan monotherapy demonstrated antitumor activity with median PFS around 5.8 months in previously treated EGFR-mutated NSCLC in TROPION-Lung05.

reason: With only 19 total participants enrolled across two study parts, the trial is severely underpowered to detect a moderate 24-week MRI liver iron concentration reduction.
rationale: REGN7999 inhibits TMPRSS6 to elevate endogenous hepcidin and restrict iron absorption in NTDT. While mechanism validation from TMPRSS6 inhibitors (sapablursen, divesiran) supports rapid serum iron reduction, net liver iron concentration (LIC) decline over just 24 weeks without new chelation is typically modest (~1-2 mg Fe/g DW) relative to between-patient LIC variability (SD ~2.5-3.0 mg Fe/g DW). Furthermore, enrollment closed at just 19 patients across 26 sites with study completion pulled up to December 2026, leaving low statistical power and signaling likely program deprioritization.

assumptions.claim: Placebo-treated patients with non-transfusion-dependent thalassemia showed minimal change in liver iron concentration (+0.38 mg Fe/g dry weight over 52 weeks) in THALASSA.

reason: Early adjuvant treatment discontinuations or missed sampling before weeks 16-19 could reduce evaluable steady-state PK sample size and widen geometric mean ratio confidence intervals.
rationale: Eucalyptus is an Amgen-sponsored double-blind pharmacokinetic similarity trial comparing biosimilar candidate ABP 234 with reference Keytruda in 163 resected non-squamous NSCLC patients. Amgen has an extensive track record of successful oncology mAb biosimilar PK equivalence trials, and N=163 in a homogeneous post-adjuvant-chemotherapy, disease-free population minimizes target-mediated clearance variability from tumor burden while providing high power to keep both first-dose AUC21d and steady-state AUCtau_ss 90% CIs within standard 80-125% bioequivalence margins.

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab is established as adjuvant therapy following complete resection and platinum-based chemotherapy in stage IB-IIIA NSCLC.

reason: A 90-patient randomized Phase 2 trial requires a steep hazard ratio (~0.60 or lower) to achieve two-sided statistical significance on progression-free survival.
rationale: This double-blind Chinese Phase 2 trial randomizes 90 platinum-resistant ovarian cancer patients to B013 plus paclitaxel versus placebo plus paclitaxel. Paclitaxel monotherapy yields ~3.9-4.5 months median PFS in platinum-resistant disease, and with ~60-65 expected events, two-sided p<0.05 requires an observed HR near 0.60, a high bar in an unselected Phase 2 population. Moreover, because the trial was still recruiting after more than two years as of late October 2026 against a December 2026 registered completion date, substantial completion delays and sparse near-term English/ClinicalTrials.gov reporting are likely.

assumptions.claim: Paclitaxel monotherapy achieved a median progression-free survival of approximately 3.9 months in platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer in the AURELIA trial.

reason: High placebo improvements in global generalized myasthenia gravis patient-reported MG-ADL scores could narrow the Week 24 treatment difference compared with earlier Chinese data.
rationale: Telitacicept neutralizes both BLyS and APRIL, suppressing B-cell maturation and autoantibody-producing plasmablasts in AChR+ and MuSK+ gMG. It demonstrated large MG-ADL and QMG improvements in a Chinese Phase 2 study (NCT04302103) and RemeGen's pivotal Chinese Phase 3 gMG study, alongside Phase 3 validation of B-cell/APRIL-BLyS targeting in gMG (MINT). Even accounting for larger placebo MG-ADL responses (~2-3 points) in global trials, N=191 provides >90% power for a ~2-point difference. With enrollment completed and a fixed 24-week endpoint due March 2027, Q2 2027 top-line reporting is highly likely.

assumptions.claim: Telitacicept reduced MG-ADL and QMG scores over 24 weeks in a randomized Phase 2 clinical trial in generalized myasthenia gravis.
Global Phase 3 generalized myasthenia gravis trials show placebo mean MG-ADL reductions of roughly 2 to 3 points at 24 to 26 weeks.

reason: Oral immune modulators effective in ulcerative colitis frequently show attenuated mucosal and clinical efficacy in transmural Crohn's disease, compounded by high CDAI placebo noise.
rationale: Obefazimod (miR-124 upregulator) demonstrated clear efficacy in ulcerative colitis, supporting biological plausibility in IBD, and testing multiple Phase 2b doses helps the chance that one arm beats placebo on Week 12 CDAI change. However, translation from UC to transmural Crohn's disease has failed for several oral small molecules (e.g., S1P modulators), CDAI has substantial placebo response (~50-60 points) and variability (SD ~95), and the registry lists Week 52 endpoints alongside Week 12 under primary outcomes. Still recruiting in late October 2026, primary completion will likely slip into mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Obefazimod demonstrated statistically significant clinical and endoscopic improvements over placebo in Phase 2b moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis.

reason: Systemic oncolytic vaccinia virus has unproved activity in NSCLC, and delaying chemotherapy during viral priming risks early progression despite platinum-doublet rechallenge.
rationale: VIRO-25 compares IV Olvi-Vec followed by platinum-doublet plus ICI rechallenge against docetaxel monotherapy in 142 NSCLC patients at first unconfirmed progression on chemo-ICI or maintenance ICI. Re-administering platinum-doublet plus ICI (especially in maintenance progressors or unconfirmed pseudoprogressors) gives a stronger backbone than docetaxel (~3.9 months mPFS), creating an upside path. Counterbalancing this, systemic oncolytic viruses have poor historical efficacy in lung cancer, the viral lead-in delays cytotoxic chemotherapy, and N=142 requires HR<=0.67. Recruiting at only 15 US sites in late 2026 makes completion delays highly probable.

assumptions.claim: Single-agent docetaxel after platinum chemotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibition in advanced NSCLC yields a median PFS of approximately 3.7 to 4.1 months.

reason: Patients with compensated MASH cirrhosis have lower baseline hepatic steatosis ('burn-out' cirrhosis), compressing absolute MRI-PDFF reductions and increasing GI dropout sensitivity.
rationale: Efinopegdutide (MK-6024) is a potent GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist that directly stimulates hepatic fatty acid oxidation and reduced liver fat by 72.7% relative to baseline at Week 24 in Phase 2a MASLD (NCT04944992), substantially outperforming semaglutide. Even in compensated MASH cirrhosis where baseline MRI-PDFF is lower (~9-11%), a ~50-60% relative reduction translates to ~4.5 percentage points greater absolute PDFF reduction than placebo, providing overwhelming statistical power in 85 patients. Because the study completed in August 2026, Merck is highly likely to post results within the 1-year FDAAA window by August 2027.

assumptions.claim: Efinopegdutide 10 mg weekly achieved a 72.7% mean relative reduction from baseline in MRI-PDFF liver fat content at Week 24 in Phase 2a MASLD.
Semaglutide significantly reduced MRI-PDFF liver fat content compared with placebo in patients with MASH-related compensated cirrhosis despite lower baseline steatosis.

reason: Because this 96-patient multi-basket glomerular disease study was still recruiting in late October 2026 with a 36-week safety follow-up, primary completion will likely slip past June 2027.
rationale: This adaptive Phase 2 basket trial of WAL0921 across diabetic nephropathy and four rare glomerular diseases requires 12 weeks of biweekly infusions plus 24 weeks of post-treatment follow-up (36 weeks total per participant). Because the trial remained in recruiting status on October 29, 2026, newly enrolled patients cannot complete 36-week primary safety follow-up until mid-to-late 2027, making a >90-day delay past the March 2027 registered primary completion date highly probable and ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 2027 very unlikely.

reason: If cyclosporine is maintained continuously through assessment rather than tapered at 12 months, fewer control relapses could narrow the remission rate advantage.
rationale: B007 is a humanized anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody evaluated against oral cyclosporine over ~2 years in 216 biopsy-proven primary membranous nephropathy patients. Anti-CD20 B-cell depletion directly suppresses pathogenic anti-PLA2R autoantibodies and demonstrated marked 2-year superiority over cyclosporine in MENTOR (60% vs 20% overall remission; 35% vs 0% complete remission) and subsequent next-generation anti-CD20 PMN trials due to high post-cyclosporine relapse rates. However, starting in July 2024 with ~2-year follow-up and recruiting status in late 2026 makes delayed completion likely.

assumptions.claim: In the MENTOR trial of primary membranous nephropathy, anti-CD20 therapy with rituximab achieved 60% overall remission at 24 months versus 20% with cyclosporine.

reason: With only about 20 patients per arm against active triple-drug antiviral and steroid therapy that resolves most acute episodes, the trial is underpowered to prove superiority at day 70.
rationale: BD111 delivers CRISPR/SpCas9 lentiviral-like particles intrastromally to cleave HSV-1 DNA and showed biological proof-of-concept in refractory herpetic keratitis. However, standard triple-drug therapy already resolves clinical signs and suppresses tear qPCR shedding by day 70 in roughly two-thirds of acute HSK episodes. With 40 total participants split across two arms and co-listed day 70 and day 112 timepoints, achieving p<0.05 requires an unusually large absolute cure gap. Because the single-center study is still recruiting near its December 2026 registered completion date, timeline slippage beyond March 2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: Intrastromal BD111 gene-editing therapy was previously tested in an investigator-initiated pilot study in refractory herpetic stromal keratitis without dose-limiting ocular toxicity.

reason: Meeting both co-primary endpoints requires statistical significance on TSS50 symptom reduction in addition to SVR35, where gastrointestinal toxicity from MDM2 inhibition can blunt symptom gains.
rationale: Navtemadlin demonstrated meaningful spleen and symptom activity in TP53 wild-type myelofibrosis, both post-JAK inhibitor (BOREAS) and as add-on therapy in suboptimal ruxolitinib responders (KRT-232-109). SVR35 at week 24 has a high likelihood of beating continued ruxolitinib plus placebo (~9% control rate vs ~29% active). However, the round requires both co-primary endpoints (SVR35 and TSS50) to succeed, and MDM2-inhibitor gastrointestinal and hematologic side effects create substantial risk on patient-reported TSS50. Because the trial remains recruiting in late October 2026 with run-in plus 24-week randomized follow-up, completion will likely slip into 2027.

assumptions.claim: Navtemadlin add-on therapy in myelofibrosis patients with suboptimal response to ruxolitinib showed spleen and symptom responses in the Phase 1b/2 study KRT-232-109.
Recent Phase 3 JAK-inhibitor combination trials in myelofibrosis such as MANIFEST-2 met SVR35 but missed statistical significance on the TSS50 symptom endpoint.

reason: Large and variable placebo improvements on clinician-rated HAM-A in multicenter adjunctive GAD trials frequently obscure modest drug-placebo differences at Week 6.
rationale: ITI-1284 is a deuterated sublingual formulation related to lumateperone, which showed strong adjunctive efficacy in major depressive disorder with anxious distress via 5-HT2A antagonism and D2/glutamatergic modulation. Enrolling 705 patients (~235 per arm across two active doses and placebo) provides solid statistical power to detect a ~2.0-point HAM-A separation assuming SD ~8.5. Nonetheless, adjunctive GAD trials historically suffer high placebo responses (-9 to -12 HAM-A points) across US and Eastern European sites and require multiplicity adjustment across two doses, moderating success probability to 36%.

assumptions.claim: Adjunctive lumateperone demonstrated statistically significant 6-week symptom improvements over placebo in Phase 3 trials of major depressive disorder with inadequate antidepressant response.

reason: SGLT1/2 inhibition does not directly relieve dynamic LVOT obstruction or hypercontractility in HCM, so 26-week KCCQ-CSS gains over placebo may fall below the ~2.8-point threshold needed for significance.
rationale: SONATA-HCM is fully enrolled (active, not recruiting) with 500 oHCM and nHCM patients and a January 2027 primary completion date, making a H1 2027 topline readout highly likely. While sotagliflozin improved KCCQ by ~4 points in diabetic worsening heart failure (SOLOIST-WHF), SGLT2-inhibitor KCCQ effects in chronic preserved-EF cohorts are typically smaller (1.5 to 2.5 points), and sotagliflozin does not directly reduce LVOT gradients like myosin inhibitors. With SD ~16 points and 250 patients per arm, ~2.8 points separation is required for p<0.05, yielding a 37% probability of success.

assumptions.claim: Sotagliflozin improved KCCQ scores versus placebo in patients with diabetes and recent worsening heart failure in SOLOIST-WHF.
Placebo arms in symptomatic HCM trials with KCCQ entry thresholds typically improve by roughly 4 to 6 KCCQ-CSS points over 24 to 30 weeks.

reason: Recruiting 90 moderate-to-severe COPD patients across only two sites in Taiwan for an allogeneic mesenchymal stem cell infusion makes enrollment delays past March 2027 likely.
rationale: This Phase 2 cell-therapy trial evaluates safety-only primary outcomes through Day 90 and full-study follow-up across 90 patients at just two hospital sites in Taiwan. Because the study is still recruiting on 2026-10-29 with a registered primary completion date only two months away (2026-12-30) and a 90-day primary safety window, primary completion is likely to slip more than 90 days late. Termination and substantive primary outcome amendments are unlikely, and results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 is uncommon while 12-month follow-up continues.

reason: If sustained axitinib release from the bioresorbable hydrogel implant wanes before scheduled redosing, breakthrough exudation could cause BCVA loss exceeding the non-inferiority margin.
rationale: This Phase 3 repeat-dosing non-inferiority study (SOL-R) of OTX-TKI (axitinib intravitreal hydrogel implant) versus aflibercept is already active, not recruiting, with primary completion set for January 8, 2027, supporting a ~90% chance of topline disclosure by June 2027. Earlier Phase 1b nAMD studies showed OTX-TKI maintained visual acuity comparable to aflibercept while substantially reducing supplemental anti-VEGF burden. With ~275 patients per arm and BCVA SD ~11.5 letters (SE ~1.0 letter), power to exclude a standard -4.5 ETDRS letter non-inferiority margin is high (~72%), likely supporting a 2027 NDA filing.

assumptions.claim: Intravitreal OTX-TKI demonstrated visual acuity maintenance comparable to 2 mg aflibercept over 9 to 12 months in a controlled Phase 1b neovascular AMD trial.

reason: Because baseline blood eosinophil elevation was not required at screening, lower baseline eosinophil counts across ~36-patient arms could increase relative variance.
rationale: Solrikitug (NSI-8226/MK-8226) is an anti-TSLP monoclonal antibody evaluated across three subcutaneous doses versus placebo in 145 uncontrolled asthma patients, and the study is already completed as of October 2026. Anti-TSLP blockade (validated by tezepelumab in PATHWAY and NAVIGATOR) robustly lowers blood eosinophils by ~100-150 cells/uL (~40-50%) within weeks regardless of allergy status. Testing three active doses on a pharmacodynamic biomarker averaged over Weeks 8 and 12 provides high statistical power (~80% probability at least one dose hits p<0.05), with strong odds of public disclosure by mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Blocking thymic stromal lymphopoietin with tezepelumab produced rapid, sustained reductions in blood eosinophil counts of roughly 100 to 150 cells/uL versus placebo in uncontrolled asthma.

reason: If solrikitug has suboptimal pharmacokinetics or neutralising immunogenicity in COPD patients, pharmacodynamic suppression of blood eosinophils through week 12 could be attenuated.
rationale: ZION evaluates two subcutaneous doses of the anti-TSLP antibody solrikitug versus placebo in ~182 symptomatic COPD patients explicitly enriched for elevated blood eosinophils at screening. Primary completion passed in September 2026 and full completion is scheduled for February 2027, pointing to high likelihood of H1 2027 reporting. In eosinophilic COPD (cf. tezepelumab COURSE trial), TSLP inhibition produces large, highly reproducible drops in blood eosinophils (~50-60%), giving ~60 patients per arm >85% chance of meeting the biomarker primary endpoint, whereas Week-12 FEV1 superiority is much harder (~32%) at this sample size.

assumptions.claim: Anti-TSLP therapy with tezepelumab substantially reduced blood eosinophil counts versus placebo in moderate-to-very-severe COPD patients in the Phase 2a COURSE study.

reason: With only 16 patients per arm, achieving two-sided p<0.05 on 6-month progression-free survival against an active bevacizumab control requires an unrealistically large >40 percentage-point gain.
rationale: This open-label Taiwan pivotal device study randomizes only 32 recurrent GBM patients (16 per arm) with low residual tumor burden (<=20 cm3 or >=80% resection) and KPS >=70 to microbubble-focused ultrasound (NaviFUS) plus bevacizumab versus bevacizumab alone. Bevacizumab monotherapy already yields ~35-45% PFS-6 in favorable rGBM via luminal VEGF blockade, where blood-brain barrier opening adds uncertain incremental efficacy. Detecting statistical superiority at alpha=0.05 with 16 patients per arm is severely underpowered. Because the trial is still recruiting in late October 2026 with a 6-month primary endpoint, completion will almost certainly slip past March 2027.

assumptions.claim: Bevacizumab monotherapy achieved a 6-month progression-free survival rate of 42.6% in recurrent glioblastoma in the randomized BRAIN study.

reason: Subsequent systemic therapies after progression in Chinese thoracic oncology centers could prolong control-arm survival and attenuate the overall survival hazard ratio despite superior PFS.
rationale: BL-B01D1 (izalontamab brengitecan), an EGFRxHER3 bispecific ADC carrying a TOP1 inhibitor payload, showed high response rates (~50%) and durable survival in Phase 1/2 pretreated SCLC, substantially outperforming historical topotecan (~15% ORR, ~7-8 months mOS). With 722 patients already enrolled (active, not recruiting) and rapid event accrual in recurrent SCLC, the trial is well powered (~430 expected deaths) to detect an OS hazard ratio around 0.74 against topotecan. Main risks are hematologic/ILD toxicity management and post-progression crossover therapies diluting OS, leaving a 68% probability of meeting primary OS superiority.

assumptions.claim: BL-B01D1 demonstrated encouraging objective response rates in recurrent small cell lung cancer in the Phase 1 trial NCT05194982.
Second-line topotecan-based chemotherapy control arms in recurrent SCLC after chemo-immunotherapy achieve median overall survival of roughly 6 to 9 months.

reason: With roughly 14 patients per arm and high patient-to-patient variability in UPCR, this exploratory 12-week Phase 2a umbrella trial is underpowered for formal statistical significance unless one agent has a dramatic anti-proteinuric effect.
rationale: Enrolling primary MCD and FSGS patients with documented >40% prior proteinuria reduction to immunosuppression enriches for immune-mediated podocytopathy responsive to CD40L blockade (frexalimab), TNF/OX40L inhibition (brivekimig), or BTK inhibition (rilzabrutinib), and having three active drugs raises the odds that at least one arm succeeds. However, ~14 patients per arm yields high sampling noise against a ~40% SD in UPCR change over just 12 weeks, and Phase 2a proof-of-concept readouts often miss p<0.05. Still recruiting across 79 sites in late October 2026 makes completion past March 2027 likely.

assumptions.claim: Frexalimab is an anti-CD40L monoclonal antibody that significantly reduced disease activity at week 12 in a randomized Phase 2 multiple sclerosis trial.

reason: Because enrollment is already complete and the primary endpoint is assessed at a fixed 48-week visit, primary completion should occur near schedule in March 2027, with results posted after full study completion in 2028.
rationale: This exploratory Phase 3b open-label biomarker study of approved bimekizumab in plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis is already active, not recruiting as of late October 2026, with a registered primary completion date of March 9, 2027. Fixed 48-week biopsy follow-up on an enrolled cohort carries low risk of a >90-day delay or early termination, and primary outcome amendments late in follow-up are uncommon. Because overall study completion is March 2028, ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 31, 2027 is unlikely.

reason: Oral TPO-receptor agonists reliably raise platelet counts above 50x10^9/L before procedures against minimal spontaneous placebo responses, leaving mainly operational or reporting risk.
rationale: Herombopag (hetrombopag) is an approved oral TPO-receptor agonist in China with well-established platelet-elevating activity. In Phase 3 trials of peer oral TPO-RAs (avatrombopag, lusutrombopag) in chronic liver disease patients with platelets <50x10^9/L undergoing invasive procedures, responder rates (platelets >=50x10^9/L and >=20x10^9/L increase without rescue) are typically ~65-80% versus ~5-15% on placebo, providing >99% power even with ~50 Part B patients per arm. With trial completion already reached in August 2026, top-line disclosure and a supplemental NMPA filing in 2027 are likely.

assumptions.claim: Oral thrombopoietin receptor agonists lusutrombopag and avatrombopag produced ~50-65 percentage point higher pre-procedure platelet response rates than placebo in Phase 3 chronic liver disease trials.
assumptions.source: ADAPT-1/ADAPT-2 (Terrault et al., Gastroenterology 2018); L-PLUS 2 (Peck-Radosavljevic et al., Hepatology 2019)

reason: Although anti-CD38 therapy added to pomalidomide-dexamethasone is well validated, slower-than-planned accrual or lower event rates in second-line patients could reduce PFS maturity or attenuate hazard ratios.
rationale: SG301 is a recombinant anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody combined with pomalidomide and dexamethasone (Pd) in pomalidomide-naive relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma after lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor, excluding CD38-refractory disease. This mirrors APOLLO (daratumumab-Pd vs Pd, HR 0.63) and ICARIA-MM (isatuximab-Pd vs Pd, HR 0.60), giving strong mechanistic and clinical precedent for both PFS and ORR superiority with ~300+ Stage 2 patients. Because the trial is still recruiting across 12 sites in late October 2026, primary completion will likely slip past March 2027.

assumptions.claim: Adding an anti-CD38 monoclonal antibody to pomalidomide and dexamethasone yielded PFS hazard ratios of 0.60 to 0.63 over pomalidomide and dexamethasone alone in Phase 3 trials.
assumptions.source: ICARIA-MM (Attal et al., Lancet 2019); APOLLO (Dimopoulos et al., Lancet Oncol 2021)

reason: Intensive fluid optimization and weaning protocols in small short bowel syndrome trials can inflate placebo responder rates to 30-40%, narrowing separation with 72 patients.
rationale: PJ009 is a daily subcutaneous GLP-2 analog evaluated using the established STEPS Phase 3 design in teduglutide-naive short bowel syndrome patients dependent on parenteral support. Daily GLP-2 receptor agonism consistently increases intestinal fluid and nutrient absorption, achieving >=20% weekly parenteral volume reduction at weeks 20-24 in ~63-68% of treated patients versus ~20-35% of placebo controls (STEPS, EASE-1). Although N=72 leaves modest vulnerability to high placebo weaning responses, a ~35-40 percentage point treatment effect provides solid power, and September 2026 primary completion supports a 2027 readout and China NDA filing.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 STEPS trial of daily subcutaneous teduglutide in short bowel syndrome, 63% of experimental patients versus 30% of placebo patients achieved >=20% weekly parenteral volume reduction at weeks 20 to 24.

reason: Requiring complete or near-complete nodule clearance (IGA 0/1) alongside itch relief at week 24 is much stricter than itch reduction alone if chronic fibrotic nodules remodel slowly.
rationale: Povorcitinib is a selective oral JAK1 inhibitor that blocks IL-4, IL-13, IL-31, and OSM signaling central to prurigo nodularis (PN) itch and fibrosis, and it previously succeeded in a randomized Phase 2 PN dose-ranging trial (NCT05061693). Extending treatment from 16 to 24 weeks allows greater nodule regression to meet the composite Itch NRS4 plus IGA-CPG-S 0/1 endpoint, where historical 24-week placebo rates are ~9% (PRIME/PRIME2). With N=349 and primary completion in October 2026, top-line Phase 3 readout in early 2027 and regulatory filing by end-2027 are highly likely.

assumptions.claim: Oral povorcitinib met its primary Itch NRS4 endpoint versus placebo in a randomized Phase 2 trial in adults with prurigo nodularis.
Week 24 placebo responder rates for the composite of Itch NRS4 and IGA 0/1 in Phase 3 prurigo nodularis trials were approximately 9%.
assumptions.source: PRIME and PRIME2 (Yosipovitch et al., Nat Med 2023)

reason: Achieving the strict composite of >=4-point itch reduction plus IGA 0/1 lesion clearance by week 24 can lag behind rapid JAK1-mediated antipruritic benefit in patients with dense fibrotic nodules.
rationale: STOP-PN2 is the replicate global Phase 3 trial (N=346) matching STOP-PN1 in design, eligibility, and October 2026 primary completion. Selective JAK1 inhibition with povorcitinib directly suppresses pruritogenic and profibrotic cytokines (IL-31, IL-4/13) and demonstrated strong dose-dependent itch and lesion improvements in Phase 2 PN (NCT05061693). Against a consistently low (~8-12%) 24-week placebo composite response rate seen in global PN studies, ~35% composite response on high-dose povorcitinib yields very high statistical power and supports simultaneous early-2027 readout and NDA submission in 2027.

assumptions.claim: Oral povorcitinib significantly increased Itch NRS4 response rates over placebo in its Phase 2 prurigo nodularis study.
Week 24 placebo rates for concurrent >=4-point WI-NRS improvement and IGA PN-S 0/1 were below 10% in global Phase 3 prurigo nodularis trials.
assumptions.source: PRIME and PRIME2 (Yosipovitch et al., Nat Med 2023)

reason: If the protocol requires both PFS and OS as strict co-primary endpoints rather than split-alpha dual primaries, immature OS or post-progression crossover at initial readout could delay or prevent meeting OS.
rationale: FDA018-ADC is an anti-TROP2 antibody-drug conjugate carrying an SN-38 topoisomerase I inhibitor payload, tested against single-agent chemotherapy in taxane-pretreated locally recurrent or metastatic TNBC (N=350). Peer TROP2 ADCs (sacituzumab govitecan in ASCENT/EVER-132-001; sacituzumab tirumotecan in OptiTROP-Breast01) achieved dramatic PFS hazard ratios of 0.31-0.43, large ORR gains, and significant OS benefits against identical chemotherapy comparators where median PFS is ~2-3 months. Primary risk stems solely from whether OS must also reach significance simultaneously rather than via split-alpha dual-primary testing.

assumptions.claim: TROP2-directed topoisomerase I inhibitor ADCs achieved PFS hazard ratios of 0.31 to 0.43 and OS hazard ratios around 0.48 to 0.53 versus single-agent chemotherapy in pretreated metastatic TNBC.
assumptions.source: ASCENT (Bardia et al., NEJM 2021); OptiTROP-Breast01 (Xu et al., Nat Med 2024)

reason: Intramuscular VLP norovirus vaccines elicit limited gut mucosal immunity in unprimed infants—who form 45% of enrollment and contribute most gastroenteritis cases—and face antigenic drift and possible strict lower-bound VE criteria.
rationale: This 6,600-participant Phase 3 trial tests a 3-dose quadrivalent (GI.1, GII.3, GII.4, GII.17) recombinant VLP norovirus vaccine across infants (n=3,000) and children aged 2-13 years (n=3,600) over two years. Including three doses, four genotypes, all-severity PCR-confirmed cases, and 55% primed older children improves prospects relative to HilleVax's 2-dose bivalent HIL-214, which failed in infants (NEST-IN1). Nevertheless, infants have the highest norovirus incidence and will dominate primary endpoint cases, where parenteral VLP protection and meeting a potential regulatory lower-bound VE margin remain uncertain.

assumptions.claim: The intramuscular bivalent VLP norovirus vaccine HIL-214 failed to demonstrate significant efficacy against moderate-to-severe vaccine-genotype norovirus gastroenteritis in infants in the Phase 2b NEST-IN1 trial.

reason: Beating an active bupivacaine hydrochloride paravertebral block plus multimodal postoperative rescue analgesia on 72-hour pain AUC with roughly 24-32 patients per dose arm is statistically challenging.
rationale: Hengrui's bupivacaine liposome injection is already marketed in China for surgical infiltration and brachial plexus block, and this N=96 Phase 2 dose-finding trial evaluates thoracic paravertebral block against active bupivacaine hydrochloride in uniportal thoracoscopic lobectomy. Across randomized nerve block trials, liposomal bupivacaine often shows modest late analgesia gains (12-48h) that fail to reach p<0.05 on cumulative 0-72h pain AUC against plain bupivacaine when rescue opioids equalize pain scores, especially with small Phase 2 arm sizes (~24-32 patients), though evaluating multiple doses modestly helps.

assumptions.claim: Randomized trials and meta-analyses comparing perineural liposomal bupivacaine against plain bupivacaine hydrochloride frequently find small, non-significant differences in cumulative 72-hour postoperative pain AUC.

reason: Still recruiting 178 lymphoma patients across three sequential/parallel parts two months before its registered December 2026 primary completion makes a substantial timeline delay very likely.
rationale: JASPIS-01 remains in recruiting status in late October 2026 despite a registered primary completion date of December 2026 and 12-month primary outcome assessment windows across 178 planned R/R aggressive B-cell NHL patients. Because Group 1 treatment spans 12 three-week cycles and outcomes are assessed over 12 months, primary completion will almost certainly slip well past March 2027. Early termination risk is modest given multi-part safety and combination cohorts, while ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

reason: Because enrollment of 46 patients is already complete in October 2026 and the primary safety window is 17 weeks, primary completion should occur near schedule.
rationale: MOMENTUM is already active, not recruiting as of late October 2026 with 46 multifocal motor neuropathy participants enrolled across 41 global sites. With a 17-week primary safety and tolerability timeframe from baseline, last-patient Week 17 assessment should occur between December 2026 and March 2027, giving a relatively low probability of exceeding the 90-day lateness threshold. Because overall study completion extends to March 2028, ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 2027 is unlikely.

reason: If amorphous calcium carbonate fails to achieve nearly double fractional absorption in hypoparathyroid patients, a 50% elemental calcium cut will cause hypocalcemia or require calcitriol rescues.
rationale: By design, AMOR-1 replaces baseline supplements at roughly 50% elemental calcium intake whereas the crystalline calcium carbonate control maintains initial elemental calcium intake. Consequently, control patients can rarely meet the composite requirement of at least a 50% reduction in daily oral calcium dose unless down-titrated for hypercalcemia. Prior clinical bioavailability work showed roughly two-fold higher absorption for amorphous versus crystalline calcium carbonate; even moderate normocalcemia maintenance (~55%) in the 41-patient AMOR-1 arm versus ~6% in the 21-patient control arm yields high power for superiority on the composite, though superiority on normocalcemia alone (key secondary) is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Amorphous calcium carbonate demonstrated approximately double the fractional intestinal calcium absorption of crystalline calcium carbonate in postmenopausal women.

reason: Allowing docetaxel chemotherapy in the physician's-choice control arm raises control rPFS relative to the Phase 1/2 enzalutamide-only comparator, attenuating the hazard ratio.
rationale: In randomized Phase 1/2 expansion cohorts (NCT03460977), EZH2 inhibition with mevrometostat plus enzalutamide halved the hazard of radiographic progression or death versus enzalutamide alone in mCRPC. MEVPRO-1 is well powered (N=600) and fully enrolled ahead of its December 2026 primary completion target. However, Phase 3 effect attenuation is expected because physician's choice includes docetaxel—an active comparator post-abiraterone—and mevrometostat GI/hematologic toxicities can limit dose intensity. Overall survival at the primary rPFS readout will likely be immature under stringent interim alpha spending.

assumptions.claim: In randomized Phase 1/2 mCRPC cohorts, mevrometostat combined with enzalutamide improved radiographic progression-free survival compared with enzalutamide monotherapy.
Second-line androgen receptor-targeted switch therapy after prior AR-targeted therapy yields short median radiographic progression-free survival of roughly 4 to 6 months in mCRPC.

reason: Sequential cohorts of only 10 active patients per dose versus 12 pooled placebo patients provide low statistical power to detect a typical 1.2–1.5 weekly SBM difference.
