In early treated PD, motor/total rating scale progression over 6-7 months is modest (~2 points) while between-patient SD is large (~9-10 points), requiring a ~4.8-point separation for p<0.05. Disease-modifying antibodies in PD (e.g., prasinezumab, cinpanemab) have struggled to show 6-month total score benefit even in much larger trials. Enrollment is complete with November 2026 completion, favoring 2027 topline release.

reason: Biweekly GLP-1 receptor agonist GZR18 produces large HbA1c reductions (~1.6-2.0%) versus placebo with near-certain statistical power, leaving non-detailed headline reporting as the main residual risk.
rationale: GZR18 (bofanglutide) is a potent biweekly GLP-1 receptor agonist that demonstrated ~1.8-2.1% HbA1c reductions and substantial weight loss in Chinese Phase 2 T2DM and obesity trials. In 274 diet-and-exercise T2DM patients over 44 weeks against placebo, both the primary HbA1c endpoint and key secondary body-weight endpoint have >99% statistical power. With primary completion passed in August 2026 and full study completion in March 2027 alongside Optimum 2, public topline readout and a China NDA filing in 2027 are highly likely.

reason: Semaglutide achieves robust ~1.7% HbA1c reductions in Chinese T2DM patients, so meeting superiority—if required rather than standard non-inferiority—depends on higher-dose GZR18 maintaining its Phase 2 edge.
rationale: Optimum 2 compares GZR18 against semaglutide in 1,100 Chinese T2DM patients on metformin ± SGLT2i/SU over 44 weeks. Standard Phase 3 active-controlled T2DM trials specify non-inferiority (0.3-0.4% margin) as the primary hypothesis followed by superiority, and GZR18 previously outperformed semaglutide 1.0 mg in Phase 2b (~0.2-0.3% greater HbA1c reduction). With N=1,100 (SE ~0.06-0.07%), non-inferiority is virtually assured and superiority on the highest GZR18 dose is probable. Active-not-recruiting status supports timely December 2026 completion and 2027 NMPA filing.

assumptions.claim: Once-weekly semaglutide 1.0 mg reduced HbA1c by approximately 1.8 percentage points in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin.

reason: Older, frail VEXAS patients have high rates of cytopenias, infections, and gastrointestinal intolerance to pacritinib that could cause early treatment discontinuations and attenuate response rates.
rationale: Pacritinib inhibits JAK2 and IRAK1 while sparing platelets, giving strong mechanistic fit in VEXAS syndrome, where retrospective series show JAK2 inhibition (ruxolitinib) controls flares during steroid tapering far better than placebo taper alone. However, GI toxicity and infections in elderly VEXAS patients pose dropout risks. Operationally, sequential Phase 2a (n=78) and Phase 2b (n=78) enrollment in a rare disease was still recruiting in late October 2026 with a 24-week treatment period, making a >90-day delay beyond 2026-12-30 very likely.

assumptions.claim: Retrospective VEXAS cohorts showed JAK2 inhibition with ruxolitinib achieved higher clinical response durability than other targeted therapies during glucocorticoid tapering.

reason: Anti-ST2/IL-33 biologics yield modest (~10-20%) COPD exacerbation reductions in populations including current smokers, which 256 patients followed for only 24 weeks is underpowered to detect.
rationale: TQC2938 (an anti-ST2 antibody) is evaluated in 256 moderate-to-severe COPD patients (both current and former smokers, without eosinophil enrichment) over a 24-week primary exacerbation window. Prior IL-33/ST2 trials in COPD (astegolimab COPD-ST2OP and Phase 2b/3, itepekimab) demonstrated modest ~13-22% exacerbation reductions and minimal FEV1 gains, especially weak in current smokers. Over 24 weeks (~130 total events), achieving p<0.05 requires ~35% rate reduction, leaving the study underpowered. Active-not-recruiting status supports timely March 2027 primary completion.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2a COPD-ST2OP trial, anti-ST2 antibody astegolimab did not significantly reduce moderate-to-severe COPD exacerbation rates versus placebo (rate ratio 0.78, p=0.19).

reason: A higher-than-expected placebo MG-ADL response rate across 34 international sites alongside typical Phase 3 effect shrinkage could erode power in a 128-patient trial.
rationale: Descartes-08 is an outpatient anti-BCMA mRNA CAR-T therapy administered without lymphodepletion. In the randomized Phase 2b MG-001 study in generalized myasthenia gravis, Descartes-08 achieved a substantially higher MG-ADL responder rate than placebo around Month 3 to 4 (~71% vs ~25% in per-protocol/mITT analyses). Accounting for Phase 2-to-3 attenuation across 34 global sites and ~28% placebo response in AChR+ gMG trials, an expected ~23 percentage-point improvement with 64 patients per arm provides ~68% probability of statistical significance. Enrollment is already complete, supporting timely readout in early 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the randomized placebo-controlled Phase 2b MG-001 trial, Descartes-08 produced a significantly higher MG-ADL responder rate at Month 3 than placebo.
Placebo arms in Phase 3 AChR-antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis trials typically exhibit 25% to 35% MG-ADL responder rates.

reason: Therapeutic-dose aripiprazole oral film (10-20 mg) produces robust 6-week PANSS reductions, leaving virtually no margin if superiority is required or risking a miss if QLM1016 is slightly weaker.
rationale: QLM1016 (3-6 mg) is evaluated head-to-head against active aripiprazole oral film (10-20 mg) in 402 Chinese patients with acute schizophrenia. Under NMPA regulatory standards, two-arm active-controlled Phase 3 antipsychotic trials of ~400 patients without a placebo arm are almost always powered for non-inferiority (typical PANSS margin 6-8 points, SD ~16.5), which `p_met` scores according to the protocol's own primary hypothesis. Assuming comparable antipsychotic efficacy (mean PANSS difference near -0.5 points vs -25.5 on aripiprazole), non-inferiority power exceeds 85%, moderated slightly by the small chance the protocol specified superiority.

assumptions.claim: Aripiprazole 10-20 mg/day typically reduces 6-week PANSS total score by approximately 22 to 28 points in acute exacerbation of schizophrenia trials in Asia.

reason: Splitting 135 patients across multiple Phase 2 dose groups with ~7.5% SD in 52-week TKV growth and elevated aquaretic-type dropouts could limit power.
rationale: Exclusion of impaired thirst, prior tolvaptan, and anticipated diuretic use strongly indicates JMKX003142 acts via vasopressin V2 receptor antagonism or cAMP-driven cyst fluid reduction. In rapidly progressive ADPKD, placebo TKV grows ~5.5-6.5% annually, whereas V2R inhibition causes both acute cyst-volume reduction and slower growth in Year 1 (~4-5 percentage-point separation in TEMPO 3:4). With N=135, primary TKV probability of success is solid (~65%), whereas 1-year eGFR slope is underpowered. Because the trial was still recruiting in October 2026 with a 52-week endpoint, completion will very likely slip past May 2027.

assumptions.claim: In TEMPO 3:4, untreated rapidly progressive ADPKD patients had ~5.5% annual TKV growth and V2R blockade reduced first-year TKV growth by roughly 4 to 5 percentage points.

reason: With only 45 hospitalized patients per arm and large inpatient placebo improvements on CMAI, the Phase 2a trial is underpowered unless ONO-2020 has an unusually large effect.
rationale: NCT06803823 is a 90-patient Phase 2a proof-of-concept study of ONO-2020 in hospitalized Japanese patients with Alzheimer's agitation. Even FDA-approved brexpiprazole achieved only ~3.8 to 5.3 CMAI points over placebo in large Phase 3 studies, and continuous hospitalization from 21 days pre-treatment through Week 12 tends to amplify non-pharmacologic behavioral stabilization (~13-point placebo CMAI drop, SD ~15). With n=45 per arm (SE ~3.2 points, requiring >6.3 points observed separation for p<0.05), two-sided significance is unlikely (~26%). Active recruitment in late October 2026 implies primary completion will slip into mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: Even effective approved therapies such as brexpiprazole reduce 12-week CMAI total score by only about 4 to 5.3 points more than placebo against a ~12-to-15-point placebo improvement.

reason: The only plausible efficacy risk is lower oral peptide exposure in synovial tissue than skin, though massive sample size (N=750) still provides overwhelming statistical power.
rationale: Icotrokinra (JNJ-77242113) is a potent oral IL-23 receptor antagonist peptide that achieved monoclonal-antibody-like skin clearance in Phase 2b FRONTIER 1 and Phase 3 ICONIC psoriasis studies. IL-23 pathway blockade is strongly validated in both biologic-naive and biologic-experienced psoriatic arthritis by guselkumab (DISCOVER-1, COSMOS) and risankizumab (KEEPsAKE-1/2), which yield ~25-32 percentage-point ACR20 gains over ~25-30% placebo response and >50 percentage-point PASI 75 gains. With 750 participants (~375 per arm, SE ~3.4 percentage points), both ACR20 and PASI 75 at Week 16 have >90% probability of success.

assumptions.claim: Oral icotrokinra (JNJ-77242113) demonstrated high-level IL-23 receptor blockade and PASI responses up to 79% PASI 75 in Phase 2b plaque psoriasis.
Selective IL-23 inhibition with guselkumab in mixed biologic-naive and biologic-experienced active PsA improved ACR20 response by roughly 30 percentage points over placebo.

reason: Recruiting 96 patients with rare idiopathic hypersomnia across 29 sites while still open in late October 2026 makes a >90-day slip past November 2026 primary completion likely.
rationale: This adaptive Phase 2 safety and dose-finding study of oral orexin-2 receptor agonist TAK-360 in idiopathic hypersomnia has no efficacy primary endpoint. On 2026-10-29 it remained in recruiting status despite a registered primary completion date of 2026-11-30 and an 8-week treatment follow-up. Enrolling 96 documented IH participants across 6 countries is relatively slow, making primary completion after 2027-02-28 likely (~65%). Early termination risk is modest (~8%, reflecting prior OX2R class hepatic monitoring with TAK-994), and ClinicalTrials.gov results posting before 2027-08-31 is unlikely given expected 2027 completion.

reason: Endothelin A receptor blockade can induce fluid retention or hemodilution, though BNP gating and SC0062's high ETA selectivity make missing 36-week UPCR unlikely.
rationale: SC0062 is a highly selective endothelin-A receptor antagonist that demonstrated clinically meaningful proteinuria reductions with low edema rates in its Chinese Phase 2 IgA nephropathy study (2SMALL). Selective ETA blockade in IgAN on background RAASi/SGLT2i is robustly validated by atrasentan in ALIGN (N=340, -36.1% placebo-adjusted 24h-UPCR reduction at Week 36, p<0.0001) and sparsentan in PROTECT. With 360 randomized patients, 36-week UPCR power exceeds 85%. However, the Week 108 eGFR secondary endpoint matures around late 2028, and ongoing recruitment in October 2026 suggests primary completion will slip into mid-2027.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 ALIGN trial in IgA nephropathy, selective ETA antagonist atrasentan reduced 36-week 24-hour UPCR by 36.1% relative to placebo (-38.1% vs -3.1%).

reason: Gastrointestinal intolerance or heart-rate increases from small-molecule oral GLP-1 receptor agonism in older HFpEF patients could raise treatment discontinuations and attenuate ITT weight loss.
rationale: HRS-7535 is a small-molecule oral GLP-1 receptor agonist that previously demonstrated substantial double-digit weight reductions in Phase 2 obesity trials. Notably, the sole primary endpoint here is percent body weight change at Week 36 rather than heart-failure clinical events, in 225 obese (BMI >=28) HFmrEF/HFpEF patients. Even accounting for smaller weight loss in older heart-failure populations and gastrointestinal discontinuations (as in STEP-HFpEF, where semaglutide reduced weight by -10.7% vs placebo), an expected ~8.5 percentage-point separation (SD ~6.8%) yields >90% power. Active recruitment in October 2026 makes delayed primary completion likely.

assumptions.claim: In STEP-HFpEF, GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in obese HFpEF patients produced double-digit percent body weight loss versus roughly 2.6% in the placebo arm.

reason: Frequent emollient-like vehicle cream application in pediatric moderate atopic dermatitis across 93 sites could inflate vehicle EASI75 response, though expected drug separation remains very large.
rationale: TRuE-AD5 is a confirmatory Phase 3b trial of ruxolitinib cream in 159 children and adolescents (6 to <18 years) with moderate atopic dermatitis (IGA=3) inadequately controlled by TCS/TCI. Across adult/adolescent Phase 3 trials (TRuE-AD1/2) and pediatric Phase 3 (TRuE-AD3, ages 2-11), ruxolitinib 1.5% cream consistently achieved ~56-67% Week 8 EASI75 and ~50-56% IGA-TS versus ~15-25% and ~8-15% on vehicle (~38-45 percentage-point separation). With N=159 (~80 per arm, SE ~7.2 percentage points), statistical power exceeds 95% for both EASI75 and IGA-TS. Primary completion passed in August 2026, supporting near-term disclosure.

assumptions.claim: In TRuE-AD1 and TRuE-AD2, ruxolitinib 1.5% cream achieved approximately 62% Week 8 EASI75 compared with 15% to 25% for vehicle cream.
In the pediatric TRuE-AD3 Phase 3 study in children aged 2 to 11 years, ruxolitinib 1.5% cream met both IGA-TS and EASI75 endpoints at Week 8 by wide margins.

reason: Meeting both co-primary endpoints requires statistically significant WOMAC knee pain improvement at just 26 weeks against large osteoarthritis placebo analgesia across multiple Phase 2 dose arms.
rationale: KBP-336 is a weekly dual amylin and calcitonin receptor agonist (DACRA). Like other amylin/DACRA peptides (e.g., cagrilintide), KBP-336 has a high likelihood (>85%) of producing ~5-8% placebo-adjusted body weight loss at 26 weeks. However, the protocol specifies co-primary endpoints: proportional weight change AND WOMAC pain change at Day 183, both required by the round's rules. Although semaglutide improved WOMAC pain in STEP 9 over 68 weeks (-13.7% weight loss), achieving significant WOMAC pain separation in 26 weeks across split Phase 2 dose arms against ~35-40% OA placebo response cuts overall success to ~48%.
evidence: STEP 9 semaglutide knee OA obesity trial (2024)

assumptions.claim: Weekly amylin-receptor agonism with cagrilintide over 26 weeks produced roughly 6% to 10.8% weight loss versus 3.0% on placebo with diet and exercise.
In STEP 9, substantial weight-loss pharmacotherapy significantly reduced WOMAC knee pain in obese knee osteoarthritis, despite a ~27.5-point placebo reduction on the 0-100 WOMAC scale.

reason: With enrollment already completed across 38 experienced sites and fixed follow-up windows, this Sanofi pediatric catch-up vaccine study is likely to finish close to its December 2026 target without substantive protocol changes.
rationale: On 2026-10-29 the trial is active, not recruiting, with primary and study completion registered for 2026-12-01 across 38 sites in the US, Europe, and Thailand. Because enrollment of 1268 pediatric participants is finished and immunogenicity/safety follow-up durations are fixed, substantial completion delays past March 2027 or early termination are unlikely. Sanofi Pasteur routinely complies with ClinicalTrials.gov reporting timelines (~10-12 months post-completion), giving a moderate chance of results posting before 2027-08-31, while substantive primary outcome amendments late in follow-up are rare.

reason: With only 60 patients per arm against active meropenem, the study cannot realistically show superiority on Day-14 mortality and may report descriptive Phase 2 results without a formal non-inferiority test.
rationale: This completed 120-patient Chinese Phase 2 trial compares HRS-8427 with meropenem in HABP/VABP on Day-14 all-cause mortality. Meropenem is a highly effective comparator with Day-14 mortality around 10-14%, so demonstrating superiority with 60 patients per arm is virtually impossible, and Phase 2 antibiotic trials often report descriptive rates rather than meeting a formal pre-specified non-inferiority margin. Even with comparable clinical activity that supports advancing HRS-8427 into Phase 3 in China, the probability of formally reporting a met primary hypothesis is low.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 REPROVE trial in nosocomial pneumonia, meropenem served as the active comparator with Day-28 all-cause mortality under 15%.

reason: Unexpected immunogenicity, hypersensitivity, or treatment discontinuations are the main residual risks given the thoroughly validated mechanism of plasma kallikrein inhibition in hereditary angioedema.
rationale: Navenibart (STAR-0215) is a long-acting monoclonal antibody inhibiting plasma kallikrein, a clinically validated target in Type 1/2 HAE where lanadelumab reduced monthly attacks by ~87% in HELP and navenibart showed ~90% attack reduction in Phase 1b/2 ALPHA-STAR. With 157 patients requiring at least 2 run-in attacks and enrollment already complete for a December 2026 primary completion, statistical power to detect an ~85% attack-rate reduction over 6 months exceeds 95%. Astria should report topline data in early 2027 and file a BLA later in 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 HELP trial in hereditary angioedema, plasma kallikrein inhibition with lanadelumab 300 mg every 2 weeks reduced the monthly HAE attack rate by approximately 87% versus placebo.
In the Phase 3 HELP trial, the mean monthly HAE attack rate in the placebo arm was approximately 2.0 attacks per month.

reason: Substantial placebo improvement on subjective abdominal pain VAS scores over 4 weeks in functional biliary disorders could narrow between-group separation despite multiple tested doses.
rationale: This 300-patient Russian Phase 2 dose-ranging trial evaluates 4-MUST tablets across multiple doses versus placebo over 29 days in chronic cholecystitis and biliary dyskinesia with baseline VAS pain >=40 mm. Having multiple active dose arms increases the chance that at least one dose achieves nominal significance, and biliary spasmolytic agents conducted in Russian multicenter GI networks frequently demonstrate moderate VAS reductions (-8 to -12 mm over placebo). However, the trial is still recruiting in late October 2026 ahead of a December 2026 completion target, making delays and slow English-language disclosure likely.

reason: Because patients with idiopathic hypersomnia have normal endogenous orexin signaling, wake-promoting effects on 8-week ESS could be smaller than those seen in orexin-deficient narcolepsy type 1.
rationale: ALKS 2680 (alixorexton) is a potent oral orexin-2 receptor agonist that demonstrated robust acute wakefulness improvements in Phase 1b cohorts including idiopathic hypersomnia. With 126 subjects across multiple dose levels (where any one dose beating placebo on Week-8 ESS meets the round objective) and placebo ESS change typically modest (-2 to -3 points), statistical power is strong even with ~30 patients per arm. Enrollment is already finished (active, not recruiting) for a November 2026 completion, pointing to a Q1 2027 topline press release and likely Phase 3 initiation in late 2027.

reason: Large, variable placebo responses across 52 US psychiatric sites commonly obscure modest adjunctive anxiolytic drug effects on 6-week HAM-A scores.
rationale: ABBV-932 is evaluated as a 6-week adjunct to ongoing antidepressants in 315 GAD patients with inadequate prior response across 52 US and Puerto Rico sites. Adjunctive GAD trials historically suffer from high placebo improvements (-8 to -11 HAM-A points) and inter-rater noise across large site networks, leaving modest ~25-30% Phase 2 success odds despite adequate sample size. Because the study remained recruiting on 2026-10-29 with a registered 2026-11 primary completion date, completion is likely to slip into 2027.

reason: Only unexpected renal safety signals or extreme treatment discontinuations could threaten Month-6 serum urate superiority given potent URAT1 inhibition against a near-zero placebo response.
rationale: AR882 is a selective URAT1 inhibitor that produced ~75-89% serum urate responses (<6 mg/dL) at 75 mg in Phase 2b gout trials. Against placebo—where spontaneous achievement of sUA <6 mg/dL is typically <10%—an 866-patient Phase 3 trial (~289 per arm) testing both 50 mg and 75 mg has >99% statistical power on its Month-6 biomarker primary endpoint. Because the trial is already marked completed as of September 2026, topline disclosure and subsequent NDA submission by late 2027 are both highly probable.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 APEX trial in gout, 0% of patients in the placebo arm achieved serum urate below 6.0 mg/dL.

reason: Demonstrating simultaneous pharmacokinetic bioequivalence across two AUC windows against both US- and EU-sourced Ocrevus in 183 MS patients carries modest multiplicity and inter-patient variability risk.
rationale: Sandoz has an exceptional track record in Phase 3 monoclonal antibody biosimilar trials following analytical similarity gating. With 183 relapsing MS patients (~61 per arm across CYB704, Ocrevus-EU, and Ocrevus-US) and typical ocrelizumab inter-subject AUC CV around 25-30%, power to stay within standard 80-125% equivalence margins across both AUC intervals and reference products is roughly 85%. Because the study is already active, not recruiting with primary completion in November 2026 and full completion in May 2027, timely readout and regulatory submission in H2 2027 are likely.

reason: Inclusion of adult EoE participants with prior proton-pump inhibitor non-response could limit histologic remission rates achievable through potassium-competitive acid blockade.
rationale: Placebo histologic remission (<15 eos/hpf on central biopsy read) in adult EoE RCTs is consistently very low (~3-7%), whereas potent acid suppression with vonoprazan 20 mg QD is expected to induce histologic remission in roughly 25-35% of patients, providing good power even with ~48 participants per arm. By contrast, dysphagia-day symptom improvement at Week 12 faces large placebo effects and low power. With primary completion passed in September 2026 and study completion in December 2026, Phathom is very likely to release topline results in early 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 LIBERTY EoE TREET trial in eosinophilic esophagitis, fewer than 10% of placebo patients achieved peak esophageal intraepithelial eosinophil count below 15 eos/hpf.

reason: Enrolling platinum-resistant ovarian cancer patients without prospective B7-H4 expression selection could dilute the progression-free survival benefit of HS-20089 against weekly paclitaxel and other chemotherapies.
rationale: HS-20089 is a B7-H4-directed topoisomerase-1 inhibitor ADC that showed ~30-35% response rates and ~5.5-6.5 month median PFS in early-phase platinum-resistant ovarian cancer studies, whereas single-agent chemotherapy yields ~3.5-4.0 month BIRC median PFS. With 468 TOP1i-naive patients randomized 1:1, the trial is well powered to detect an expected PFS hazard ratio near 0.65, though unselected B7-H4 expression adds dilution risk and OS will likely be immature at initial PFS readout. Because recruitment remained ongoing in late October 2026, event accrual could slip past March 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 MIRASOL trial in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer, single-agent investigator's-choice chemotherapy achieved a median progression-free survival of approximately 4 months.

reason: Intraocular inflammation or delayed transgene expression after single-dose intravitreal AAV.7m8 gene therapy could lower mean BCVA enough to miss the non-inferiority margin against regular aflibercept.
rationale: Ixo-vec (6e10 vg/eye) expresses aflibercept intraocularly and maintained stable BCVA with manageable inflammation under local corticosteroid prophylaxis in the Phase 2 LUNA trial. Because ARTEMIS enriches for anti-VEGF anatomic responders at screening and permits supplemental aflibercept rescue injections, BCVA differences versus scheduled aflibercept should stay small (~-1.2 letters, SE ~1.3 letters with N=311). Against a typical -4.5-letter FDA non-inferiority margin, statistical power is solid, with residual risk from AAV-associated intraocular inflammation or undertreatment before rescue criteria are met.

assumptions.claim: Ixo-vec 6e10 vg/eye maintained visual acuity near baseline while substantially reducing anti-VEGF injection burden in Phase 2 nAMD patients.
Standard FDA Phase 3 non-inferiority trials in wet AMD use a non-inferiority margin of approximately -4.5 ETDRS letters.

reason: Subcutaneous QCZ484 given every 6 months could exhibit weaker or less durable pharmacodynamic knockdown and blood pressure lowering at Month 3 than competing long-acting antihypertensives.
rationale: QCZ484 is a twice-yearly subcutaneous antihypertensive evaluated across multiple doses in 396 washed-out mild-to-moderate hypertension patients using 24-hour ABPM at Month 3. Long-acting RNA-targeted RAAS inhibitors (such as zilebesiran in KARDIA-1) produce 10-15 mmHg placebo-adjusted reductions in 24-hour SBP at Month 3 with between-patient SD near 11-12 mmHg. With ~75-100 patients per arm and only one dose required to meet superiority, statistical power is high if target engagement matches Phase 1 pharmacodynamics.

assumptions.claim: Twice-yearly subcutaneous angiotensinogen-targeting therapy reduced Month 3 24-hour ambulatory SBP by more than 10 mmHg versus placebo in mild-to-moderate hypertension.

reason: High gastrointestinal adverse event rates or an unexpected safety signal could attenuate treatment-regimen weight loss or cause regulatory delay, though missing statistical superiority is extremely unlikely.
rationale: Maridebart cafraglutide (MariTide, a GLP-1R agonist/GIPR antagonist antibody-peptide conjugate) produced up to ~20% body weight reduction at 52 weeks without a weight plateau in Phase 2 adults with obesity without diabetes. With 3,853 participants enrolled, MARITIME-1 has overwhelming statistical power to detect superiority over placebo (~-2.6%) at Week 72 on both body weight and waist circumference. Stepwise dose escalation should keep gastrointestinal discontinuations near 8-12%, positioning Amgen for a marketing submission in late 2027 following April 2027 study completion.

assumptions.claim: Maridebart cafraglutide achieved approximately 20% mean weight loss at Week 52 in Phase 2 participants with obesity without type 2 diabetes.
Placebo arms in 68-to-72-week Phase 3 obesity trials without diabetes typically lose 2% to 3.5% of baseline body weight.

reason: Gastrointestinal tolerability issues during dose escalation could elevate treatment discontinuation, although statistical superiority over placebo in N=1,105 is near-certain.
rationale: In Phase 2 participants with obesity and type 2 diabetes, maridebart cafraglutide produced up to ~17% body weight reduction at 52 weeks. Even accounting for attenuated weight loss in T2DM relative to non-diabetic obesity (as seen in SURMOUNT-2 and STEP 2), a ~13% placebo-adjusted weight reduction at Week 72 across 1,105 randomized patients yields extreme statistical power for both primary weight loss and key secondary waist circumference endpoints. Parallel completion with MARITIME-1 in early 2027 supports inclusion in a 2027 weight-management BLA.

assumptions.claim: Maridebart cafraglutide produced substantial double-digit percent body weight reductions at 52 weeks in Phase 2 participants with type 2 diabetes and obesity.
Dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor therapy in SURMOUNT-2 achieved an 11.6 percentage-point placebo-adjusted weight reduction at Week 72 in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity.

reason: Cross-resistance after prior VEGFR TKI therapy such as anlotinib or lenvatinib could attenuate AL2846's progression-free survival benefit compared with historical cabozantinib benchmarks.
rationale: AL2846 is a multi-targeted c-MET/VEGFR/AXL/RET tyrosine kinase inhibitor sharing cabozantinib's core mechanism for overcoming MET-driven resistance to prior VEGFR TKIs. In the analogous Phase 3 COSMIC-311 trial in VEGFR-TKI-pretreated radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer, placebo median PFS was just 1.9 months and cabozantinib achieved an HR of 0.22. With 144 patients and rapid progression in placebo controls, power for IRC-assessed PFS is strong, though overall survival is unlikely to reach significance early and active recruitment in late 2026 creates moderate delay risk.

assumptions.claim: In COSMIC-311, patients with radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer progressing after prior VEGFR TKI had a placebo median PFS of 1.9 months and a cabozantinib PFS HR of 0.22.

reason: With only about 47 participants per arm and high patient-to-patient variability in KCCQ-CSS scores, a true 7-to-8-point symptom improvement could miss statistical significance alongside the co-primary weight endpoint.
rationale: IBI362 (mazdutide, a GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist) produces ~11-13% placebo-adjusted weight loss at 6 mg in Chinese adults with BMI >=28 kg/m2, making the Week 36 body-weight co-primary virtually certain. However, meeting the trial requires the same dose to also achieve statistical significance on KCCQ-CSS. In STEP-HFpEF and SUMMIT, incretin therapy improved KCCQ-CSS by ~7-8 points over placebo with residual SD ~15-17 points; at n=47 per arm (SE ~3.3 points), power for KCCQ-CSS is roughly 60-65%, making sample size the main constraint.

assumptions.claim: Semaglutide and tirzepatide improved KCCQ-CSS by approximately 6.9 to 7.8 points over placebo in patients with obesity-related HFpEF.
Mazdutide 6 mg achieved roughly 11-12% placebo-adjusted body weight reduction at Week 32-48 in Chinese adults with overweight or obesity in GLORY-1.

reason: Full-dose etoricoxib monotherapy resolves acute gout pain rapidly over 8 days, creating a strong active control and floor effect that makes demonstrating added benefit from betamethasone in 72 patients difficult.
rationale: Etoricoxib monotherapy is a highly potent standard treatment for acute gout flares, producing rapid pain relief over days 2-5 and near-complete resolution by day 8. While adding systemic betamethasone can accelerate early analgesia and edema reduction in the first 48-72 hours, demonstrating statistically significant superiority across an 8-day Likert pain assessment in only 72 patients (36 per arm) faces substantial ceiling/floor effects. In addition, the trial remained recruiting at a single listed Mexican site in late October 2026, raising the likelihood of delayed completion and slow public reporting.

assumptions.claim: Etoricoxib monotherapy produces rapid, substantial reductions in acute gout joint pain across an 8-day treatment course comparable to high-dose indomethacin.

reason: Having already completed enrollment well ahead of its March 2027 53-week primary completion date across 33 US sites, this Phase 2 intra-articular knee osteoarthritis trial is on track to finish on schedule.
rationale: The trial was already active, not recruiting on 2026-10-29 with a registered primary completion date of 2027-03-25 and study completion of 2027-04-15 across 33 US sites. Because follow-up is a fixed 53 weeks from first injection, completion of enrollment by spring 2026 locks in primary completion near March 2027 with low risk of slipping past June 2027 (>90 days late) or early termination. Posting full results on ClinicalTrials.gov by 2027-08-31 (only five months post-completion) is uncommon for a private biotech sponsor.

reason: Routine oncology care across French and German academic centers may already address symptoms proactively, diluting the incremental 3-month quality-of-life gain from app-based ePRO alerts.
rationale: Prior large randomized oncology ePRO trials—including PRO-TECT (N=1,191) and French telemonitoring studies such as CAPRI—consistently demonstrated 2.5-to-5-point improvements in 3-month EORTC QLQ-C30 health-related quality of life over usual care via earlier symptom intervention. With 1,458 planned participants (SE ~1.1 points for SD ~19) and an unblinded pragmatic comparison against usual care, RC-102 is well powered to detect even modest HRQoL gains at 3 months, though overall survival through 2029 will remain immature in 2027 and ongoing recruitment in late 2026 creates moderate delay risk.

assumptions.claim: In the PRO-TECT cluster-randomized trial, electronic symptom monitoring significantly improved 3-month EORTC QLQ-C30 scores by roughly 2.5 to 3 points versus usual care.

reason: A faster-than-expected early UAS7 response in the dupilumab loading-dose arm plus double-dummy placebo response could narrow the Week 4 treatment difference.
rationale: RECLAIM specifically tests Week 4 UAS7 change to capitalize on distinct pharmacodynamic kinetics: oral BTK inhibition with remibrutinib blocks mast-cell and basophil degranulation within days, achieving ~18-19-point UAS7 reductions by Week 4 in REMIX-1 and REMIX-2, whereas dupilumab exhibits gradual IL-4Ralpha-mediated improvement (~10-12-point UAS7 reduction at Week 4 in LIBERTY-CSU CUPID before peaking at Week 24) and weaker activity in anti-IgE-experienced patients. With 409 participants enrolled (SE ~1.15 points), statistical power for both Week 4 UAS7 and HSS7 superiority is very high.

assumptions.claim: Remibrutinib 25 mg twice daily produced rapid UAS7 improvements approaching 18-20 points from baseline within the first 2 to 4 weeks in the Phase 3 REMIX-1 and REMIX-2 CSU trials.
Dupilumab showed a gradual onset of action in LIBERTY-CSU CUPID, with substantially smaller UAS7 reductions at Week 4 than at Week 24.

reason: Repeated sham lumbar puncture procedures and intensive clinical follow-up could inflate sham-arm seizure reductions on caregiver diaries.
rationale: Zorevunersen directly addresses SCN1A haploinsufficiency in Dravet syndrome and demonstrated 70-85% median reductions in convulsive seizure frequency after 70 mg loading doses in Phase 1/2a MONARCH and ADMIRAL studies. With 170 fully enrolled patients randomized against a sham comparator over 28 weeks, statistical power to detect a >=30-45 percentage-point advantage over sham (~15% reduction) is very high. Because enrollment is already complete and primary completion is March 2027, topline results are likely in Q2 2027, supporting a potential NDA filing by late 2027.

assumptions.claim: Zorevunersen (STK-001) produced substantial reductions in convulsive seizure frequency after 70 mg intrathecal doses in the Phase 1/2a MONARCH and ADMIRAL studies in Dravet syndrome.
In the GWPCARE1 randomized trial in Dravet syndrome, placebo-treated patients had an approximately 13% median reduction in convulsive seizure frequency from baseline.

reason: Because the trial is still enrolling by invitation in late October 2026 and requires at least 26 weeks of follow-up plus a planned Phase 3 double-blind portion, registry primary completion is likely to slip past May 2027.
rationale: Although enrollment targets only 24 children from an ongoing observational run-in study, the record remains enrolling by invitation in late October 2026 while primary outcome assessment takes 26 weeks, leaving minimal buffer before the May 2027 90-day late threshold. Furthermore, the title and description specify a subsequent double-blind Phase 3 portion not yet reflected in the arms or outcomes, creating an elevated probability of both primary completion extension and substantive outcome amendment.

reason: Frequent twice-daily application of emollient ointment vehicle in mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis can raise placebo EASI-75 rates and compress the active drug's treatment margin.
rationale: Phase 3 randomized trials of non-steroidal topical ointments in mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis in China have high historical success rates when testing two active concentrations (1.5% and 2%, N=120 per arm) against vehicle over 8 weeks. Vehicle ointment BID typically yields ~20-30% EASI-75 at Week 8, leaving ample statistical power (>90%) for a 25-30 percentage-point gain. Because the trial is still recruiting in late October 2026 and sponsored domestically in China, public English/registry disclosure before mid-2027 is only moderately likely.

assumptions.claim: In Phase 3 vehicle-controlled trials of topical non-steroidal ointments for mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis, vehicle ointment twice daily produces substantial skin-barrier improvements and responder rates.
assumptions.source: AD-301 and AD-302 crisaborole trials (Paller et al., JAAD 2016)

reason: Novel small-molecule epigenetic regulators have low historical probability of demonstrating clinically and statistically significant ADAS-cog 12 improvements over 26 weeks in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease.
rationale: ONO-2020 is an unvalidated oral epigenetic regulator tested in Phase 2 mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease (MMSE 15-24) on background acetylcholinesterase inhibitors or memantine. Historically, novel non-cholinergic oral cognitive therapies in Phase 2 AD fail over 80% of the time on 26-week ADAS-cog 12 (~87 patients/arm requires roughly a 2.2-point separation against SD ~6.5). Because the study completed in September 2026 across US and Japanese sites, topline disclosure via Ono pipeline updates, congresses, or FDAAA 1-year registry posting in 2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: Placebo-treated patients with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease on stable background therapy typically worsen by roughly 1.5 to 3 points on ADAS-cog over 24 to 26 weeks.

reason: Semaglutide 2.4 mg is a potent active comparator, so higher-than-expected weight loss in the control arm or gastrointestinal dose holds on mazdutide 9 mg could narrow the weight-loss difference.
rationale: IBI362 (mazdutide) is a dual GLP-1R/GCGR agonist tested at its high 9 mg weekly dose against semaglutide 2.4 mg in 479 Chinese adults with overweight/obesity and MAFLD. Both co-primary endpoints at Week 48 strongly favor mazdutide: 9 mg mazdutide achieves ~18% weight loss versus ~12-13% for semaglutide 2.4 mg in East Asian cohorts, while hepatic glucagon receptor agonism reduces MRI-PDFF liver fat (~80%) far more than selective GLP-1 agonism (~50%). With enrollment completed and primary completion at end-2026, Innovent is very likely to announce topline results in H1 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the STEP 7 Phase 3 trial in predominantly East Asian adults with overweight or obesity, once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg achieved a mean body weight reduction of 12.1% at Week 44.
assumptions.source: STEP 7 (Mu et al., Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol 2024)

assumptions.claim: Mazdutide demonstrated robust, statistically significant reductions in body weight and hepatic fat content in Chinese adults with overweight or obesity in the GLORY-1 study.

reason: The trial is still recruiting in late October 2026 and requires 52 weeks of post-injection safety follow-up plus Part B manufacturing availability, making primary completion before March 2027 virtually impossible.
rationale: All three primary safety outcomes require 52 weeks of follow-up after intra-articular dosing, and Part B (90 of 135 patients) depends on study drug from a second manufacturing process plus contrast-enhanced MRI screening for active synovitis. Because the trial is still recruiting on 2026-10-29—one month before its registered 2026-11 primary completion date—the final 52-week primary assessment will almost certainly slip well past 2027-02-28.

reason: With only 50 patients across heterogeneous pediatric and adult PMM2-CDG severities, rater variability and developmental or practice improvements on ICARS in the placebo arm may obscure a modest central nervous system effect.
rationale: GLM101 delivers liposomal mannose-1-phosphate to bypass deficient PMM2 enzymatic activity and showed encouraging open-label ICARS improvements in Phase 2. However, translating open-label ataxia gains to a 24-week double-blind trial (N=50) is challenging given blood-brain barrier delivery constraints, structural cerebellar hypoplasia in PMM2-CDG, and rater/practice effects on ICARS (~2-3 points in control, SD ~7). With Part A primary completion registered for August 2026 and enrollment finished, topline Part A disclosure by H1 2027 is highly probable.

assumptions.claim: Patients with PMM2-CDG assessed longitudinally with the International Cooperative Ataxia Rating Scale (ICARS) show short-term score responsiveness as well as substantial inter-patient variability.
assumptions.source: AZATAX trial (Martinez-Monseny et al., Ann Neurol 2019)

reason: Large inpatient placebo responses across 73 US and Japanese sites could replicate the placebo inflation that caused ulotaront to miss its primary endpoint in DIAMOND 1 and DIAMOND 2.
rationale: Ulotaront (SEP-363856) met its primary PANSS endpoint in Phase 2 (NEJM 2020) but failed both Phase 3 DIAMOND 1 and DIAMOND 2 trials due to high placebo improvement (~18-19 points) and modest drug separation. Otsuka tightened eligibility here (requiring an informant, prior antipsychotic responsiveness, and higher doses of 75/100 mg across 538 patients in the US and Japan), giving a meaningful rebound chance (~34%), though 73 sites still carry substantial placebo-response risk. With study completion in October 2026, topline announcement by Q1 2027 is very likely.

assumptions.claim: In its 4-week randomized Phase 2 acute schizophrenia trial, ulotaront (SEP-363856) significantly reduced PANSS total score versus placebo (-17.2 vs -9.7 points).
Ulotaront did not achieve statistically significant superiority over placebo on Week 6 PANSS total change in either the DIAMOND 1 or DIAMOND 2 Phase 3 trials.

reason: As stated in the registry description, enrollment was closed early at 7 randomized patients with study completion set for October 2026, leading to either a Completed or Terminated final registry status and timely safety results posting.
rationale: The registry explicitly notes that the study is being closed out early with safety assessed in the 7 already randomized participants and both primary and study completion set to 2026-10-15. Sponsors closing enrollment early after amending enrollment to actual accrual and outcomes to safety split between marking the final status Completed versus Terminated (~42%). Because this is a small US trial of commercial Pluvicto by Novartis, FDAAA results posting within 10 months is relatively likely, while further outcome amendments are unlikely.

reason: Enrollment of all 411 healthy volunteers is already complete across 9 US sites with fixed vaccination intervals, so primary data collection should conclude close to February 2027.
rationale: This Phase 2 dose-ranging vaccine trial in 411 healthy adults is already active, not recruiting in October 2026 with registered primary completion in February 2027 and study completion in March 2027. Fixed-schedule healthy-volunteer vaccine visits rarely slip by more than 90 days once enrollment closes. Because the 1-year FDAAA posting deadline falls in early 2028, ClinicalTrials.gov results posting prior to August 31, 2027 has a low probability (~12%).

reason: TQB3473 could show lower sustained platelet responses in heavily pretreated chronic ITP than seen with peer SYK inhibitors, though near-zero placebo durable response preserves high statistical power.
rationale: TQB3473 is an oral SYK inhibitor evaluated in 199 Chinese adults with relapsed/refractory chronic ITP and baseline platelets <30x10^9/L. In the comparable Chinese Phase 3 ESLIM-01 trial of SYK inhibitor sovleplenib, durable platelet response (weeks 14-24) reached 48% versus 0% on placebo, and even fostamatinib achieved 18% versus 2% globally. Because spontaneous durable remission on placebo is below 5%, N=199 gives >95% power for any treatment difference above 15 percentage points. However, because the trial remained recruiting in late October 2026 with a 24-week treatment period, primary completion will likely slip past March 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 ESLIM-01 trial of the SYK inhibitor sovleplenib in Chinese adults with chronic ITP, durable response during weeks 14-24 was 48% vs 0% with placebo.
Pooled Phase 3 FIT1/FIT2 trials of SYK inhibitor fostamatinib in persistent/chronic ITP reported stable platelet response in 18% of active patients vs 2% on placebo.

reason: Three-times-weekly vadadustat may achieve slightly lower hemoglobin maintenance than daily dosing or standard ESA, or fail if tested for superiority rather than non-inferiority.
rationale: This completed 353-patient US Phase 3 study compares three-times-weekly (TIW) vadadustat with standard-of-care ESA in maintenance hemodialysis. Active-controlled HIF-PHI trials (such as INNO2VATE) pre-specify non-inferiority on Week 20-24 hemoglobin change using a -0.75 g/dL margin. With SD ~1.1 g/dL and ~176 patients per arm (SE ~0.13 g/dL), TIW vadadustat has high probability of meeting non-inferiority even with a modest -0.15 g/dL difference, though higher open-label GI discontinuations or an unexpected superiority test pose residual risk. Superiority on target-range proportion (key secondary) over titrated ESA is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In the INNO2VATE prevalent hemodialysis trial, vadadustat met non-inferiority to darbepoetin alfa (-0.75 g/dL margin) with a Week 24-36 mean hemoglobin change difference of -0.17 g/dL.

reason: The stringent requirement for Target Not Detected HDV RNA combined with ALT normalization at Week 48 could yield lower response rates in cirrhotic patients, though untreated Week 12 control response is near zero.
rationale: ECLIPSE 1 compares 48 weeks of tobevibart plus elebsiran against 12 weeks of delayed treatment in 124 chronic HDV patients. In Phase 2 SOLSTICE, tobevibart plus elebsiran achieved high rates of undetectable HDV RNA (target not detected) and ALT normalization (~40-60% combined), with low adverse-event discontinuation. Conversely, spontaneous HDV RNA target-not-detected plus ALT normalization over 12 weeks of observation in patients with elevated baseline ALT is ~0-2%, as seen in MYR301. With 124 enrolled patients and completion scheduled for December 2026, statistical power exceeds 99% for both primary and virologic key secondary endpoints.

assumptions.claim: In the MYR301 Phase 3 trial in chronic hepatitis delta, the delayed-treatment control arm had a 2% combined virologic and biochemical response rate at Week 48 and 0% undetectable HDV RNA.
Phase 2 SOLSTICE data for tobevibart plus elebsiran in chronic HDV demonstrated high rates (>40%) of HDV RNA target not detected and ALT normalization.

reason: With only 6 patients per arm and multiple safety and preliminary efficacy primary outcomes, the study is severely underpowered to achieve formal statistical significance.
rationale: CRO-SBS-IF enrolls only 18 patients across three arms (6 per arm) and lists two descriptive safety outcomes alongside two preliminary efficacy primary outcomes (weekly parenteral support volume and stool volume). Antisecretory chloride-channel inhibition by crofelemer produces much smaller fluid-absorption gains than trophic GLP-2 analogs like teduglutide, while between-patient parenteral volume SD is ~3-4 L/week (SE ~2 L/week for n=6 vs 6). Meeting formal superiority across efficacy co-primaries is unlikely. Because recruitment was ongoing in late October 2026 ahead of a 2-12 week stabilization plus 24-week treatment period, substantial delay past March 2027 is expected.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 STEPS trial of teduglutide in SBS-IF, placebo patients experienced a mean parenteral support reduction of approximately 2.3 L/week at Week 24 with substantial inter-patient variability.

reason: Standard skincare and placebo lesion regression could narrow the difference on the strict ISGA 0/1 co-primary endpoint, though antiandrogenic cyproterone plus ethinyl estradiol has robust established efficacy.
rationale: PANDORA tests cyproterone acetate 2 mg combined with low-dose ethinyl estradiol 0.02 mg versus placebo (2:1, N=531) over six 28-day cycles in moderate facial acne. Cyproterone acetate is the most potent antiandrogenic progestin used in acne, and Phase 3 trials of 0.02 mg ethinyl estradiol combined oral contraceptives of similar size (~530 patients) consistently achieved highly significant improvements across all three co-primaries (inflammatory lesions, total lesions, and ISGA 0/1). Starting enrollment in late August 2026 makes completing six menstrual cycles across 531 participants by February 2027 unrealistic, driving high probability of registry delay.

assumptions.claim: Pivotal Phase 3 placebo-controlled trials of low-dose ethinyl estradiol (0.02 mg) plus antiandrogenic progestin in ~530 women with moderate acne met lesion-count and global-assessment co-primary endpoints over 6 cycles.

reason: Faricimab produces ~10-11 ETDRS letters of gain during Week 16 loading in DME, leaving minimal headroom for IBI302 to show superiority or reliably clear a tight non-inferiority margin with 50 patients per arm.
rationale: This 150-patient Phase 2 trial compares two doses of intravitreal IBI302 (anti-VEGF/complement bispecific) with faricimab on Week 16 BCVA in DME. During initial monthly loading, faricimab yields ~10.5-11.5 ETDRS letters of BCVA improvement, and anti-VEGF comparators rarely differ at Week 16 (expected true difference near 0 letters, SD ~8.5, SE ~1.7 for 50/arm). Superiority is very unlikely (<10%); success depends on whether the protocol pre-specified a ~4-letter non-inferiority margin (as in Innovent's nAMD Phase 2 trials) and reports formal testing rather than descriptive equivalence. Regardless, comparable BCVA often supports advancing to Phase 3.

assumptions.claim: In Phase 3 YOSEMITE and RHINE trials in DME, faricimab produced approximately 10-11 ETDRS letters of BCVA improvement during the initial loading phase.
Innovent's Phase 2 randomized studies of IBI302 in neovascular AMD demonstrated visual acuity gains non-inferior to aflibercept rather than superior BCVA gains.

reason: With enrollment already completed for 31 participants and a single-injection 6-month safety follow-up targeting December 2026 completion, the trial is likely to finish on schedule with low attrition.
rationale: This sham-controlled Phase 2 safety trial of a single intravitreal jCell injection in 31 adults with retinitis pigmentosa was already active, not recruiting as of late October 2026 with registered primary and study completion in December 2026. Because the intervention is a one-time procedure with a fixed 6-month safety follow-up, minimal schedule slippage (>90 days) or early termination is expected, and primary safety outcome amendments at this late stage are rare. Results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov before August 31, 2027 (eight months post-completion) has a moderate 25% probability ahead of the 12-month statutory deadline.

reason: Gastrointestinal intolerance, hypoglycemia, or ketosis could increase treatment discontinuations or prompt aggressive insulin down-titration that slightly attenuates HbA1c lowering, though statistical power remains overwhelming.
rationale: SURPASS-T1D-1 evaluates weekly tirzepatide versus placebo over 40 weeks in 905 adults with T1D and BMI >=25 kg/m2 (baseline HbA1c 7.0-10.5%). Earlier incretin trials in T1D (ADJUNCT ONE with liraglutide) and clinical cohorts of tirzepatide in overweight T1D consistently show -0.5% to -0.9% placebo-adjusted HbA1c reductions alongside major improvements in CGM time-in-range and weight. With N=905 (SE ~0.06% for SD ~0.9%), power exceeds 99% even for a -0.3% effect. Being active, not recruiting in October 2026 with November 2026 primary completion ensures timely early-2027 readout and likely 2027 regulatory filing.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 ADJUNCT ONE trial in Type 1 diabetes, adjunct GLP-1 receptor agonist liraglutide significantly reduced HbA1c compared with placebo despite background insulin titration.

reason: Enrolling 49 autologous transplant lymphoma patients across four US centers may slightly overrun the March 2027 target, though the brief 30-day post-transplant follow-up limits major delays.
rationale: This 49-patient Phase 2 trial comparing ethanol-free carmustine (VI-0609) with BiCNU during BEAM conditioning across four US transplant centers remained recruiting in late October 2026 with registered primary completion on March 31, 2027. Although per-patient follow-up is only 30 days post-AHCT, accruing ~12 transplant candidates per center over two years carries nearly an even chance of slipping past late June 2027 (>90 days late). Given planned study completion in April 2027 at earliest, ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 31, 2027 is unlikely.

reason: Surgical fistula conditioning and saline injection yielded high placebo combined remission (~34-46%) in prior mesenchymal stem cell Phase 3 trials, risking an insufficient treatment delta.
rationale: This 228-patient Chinese Phase 3 trial tests local TH-SC01 stem cell injection versus saline on Week 24 clinical plus central-MRI combined remission in Crohn's perianal fistulas. While darvadstrocel met this endpoint in ADMIRE-CD (50% vs 34%, +15.8%), the larger global ADMIRE-CD II trial failed because surgical conditioning raised placebo remission to ~46% (~49% vs ~46%). With N=114 per arm, achieving p<0.05 requires an observed difference of ~13 percentage points, yielding moderate success odds (~54%). Ongoing recruitment in late October 2026 with a 24-week endpoint makes completion >90 days past December 2026 highly probable.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 ADMIRE-CD trial of allogeneic stem cells for Crohn's perianal fistulas, Week 24 combined remission was 50% vs 34% with placebo.
The Phase 3 ADMIRE-CD II trial of darvadstrocel did not meet its primary endpoint of combined remission at 24 weeks due to a higher-than-expected placebo response rate.

reason: The trial is already marked completed on ClinicalTrials.gov, and Boehringer Ingelheim reliably posts results within one year of completion.
rationale: On the snapshot date of 2026-10-29, this 492-patient Boehringer Ingelheim Phase 2 CKD scheduling trial is already completed with registered primary and study completion dates of 2026-08-14. Retroactive change to a stopped status is extremely rare (<1-2%). Because the one-year statutory results reporting mark (2027-08-14) falls before the 2027-08-31 read date and Boehringer Ingelheim maintains strong ClinicalTrials.gov compliance, results posting is highly likely, while substantive post-completion primary outcome amendments are uncommon.

reason: Orticumab previously missed an FDG-PET arterial inflammation endpoint and relies here on replicating an exploratory CCTA FAI subgroup signal against regression to the mean.
rationale: Orticumab (anti-oxidized ApoB100 IgG1) missed its primary FDG-PET plaque inflammation endpoint in GLACIER but lowered CCTA FAI-Score among high-inflammation participants in a Phase 2a psoriasis trial. FORTIFY enriches for elevated baseline FAI in 240 stable post-MI patients on guideline lipid therapy, giving moderate power if the subgroup effect holds, tempered by CCTA regression to the mean. Because the trial was still recruiting in late October 2026 with a 24-week endpoint, completion will likely slip past May 2027.

assumptions.claim: In an earlier Phase 2 FDG-PET imaging trial (GLACIER), orticumab (MLDL1278A) did not significantly reduce arterial plaque inflammation compared with placebo.
In a randomized Phase 2a trial in psoriasis patients, orticumab reduced coronary inflammation measured by CCTA FAI score in the subgroup with elevated baseline coronary inflammation.

reason: With roughly 41 patients per arm and substantial placebo regression on ESSDAI, the proof-of-concept study is underpowered for moderate treatment effects of selective APRIL blockade.
rationale: Sibeprenlimab potently suppresses APRIL-driven IgG and autoantibody production, as shown in IgA nephropathy, and dual BAFF/APRIL or B-cell-targeting biologics (ianalumab, telitacicept) have lowered ESSDAI in Sjögren's disease. However, selective APRIL inhibition leaves naive/memory B cells intact, placebo ESSDAI typically drops ~3.5-4 points from regression to the mean, and N=83 (~41/arm) requires roughly a 2.4-point delta for p<0.05. Being active, not recruiting in October 2026 fits the March 2027 Week 28 completion.

assumptions.claim: Sibeprenlimab 400 mg or weight-equivalent dosing significantly reduced proteinuria and serum immunoglobulins compared with placebo in the Phase 2 ENVISION trial in IgA nephropathy.
In the Phase 2b Sjögren's trial of ianalumab enrolling patients with ESSDAI of 6 or higher, the placebo arm showed a multi-point reduction from baseline in ESSDAI score.

reason: Although anti-CD79b ADC addition to R-GemOx strongly boosts complete response, overall survival is listed alongside CRR as a primary outcome and could be immature or co-primary.
rationale: SHR-A1912 is Hengrui's anti-CD79b ADC evaluated with R-GemOx versus R-GemOx in 282 R/R DLBCL patients. Class precedent from polatuzumab vedotin plus R-GemOx (POLARGO) and R-GemOx controls (~25-30% CRR in STARGLO) strongly supports a ~20 percentage-point CRR improvement with high statistical power at N=141/arm. The main caveat is whether CRR and OS are dual primaries (split alpha) or co-primaries requiring mature OS at readout. Enrolment is complete, supporting timely 2027 readout and China NDA filing.

assumptions.claim: Adding the anti-CD79b antibody-drug conjugate polatuzumab vedotin to bendamustine-rituximab significantly increased complete response rates in relapsed or refractory DLBCL.
In the Phase 3 STARGLO trial in relapsed or refractory DLBCL, the R-GemOx control arm achieved a complete response rate of approximately 25%.

reason: With enrollment already completed by October 2026 and a 16-week safety follow-up, primary completion should occur near schedule without substantive outcome amendments.
rationale: This 105-participant Phase 2 safety and PoC study of BLU-808 in CIndU and CSU is already active, not recruiting as of 2026-10-29 with a registered completion date of 2026-12-31 and a 16-week primary safety window. Even if final patients entered in autumn 2026, primary completion should fall well before the 90-day late cutoff (2027-03-31). ClinicalTrials.gov results posting typically occurs closer to 12 months post-completion, giving a modest posting probability by 2027-08-31.

reason: Paired Week 60 liver biopsies suffer from histological reader variability and non-responder imputation if participants drop out before repeat biopsy.
rationale: IBI362 (mazdutide) is a potent dual GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist that drives substantial weight loss and direct hepatic defatting via glucagon receptor signaling. In comparable Phase 2 biopsy-proven F2/F3 MASH trials of survodutide (GLP-1/GCGR) and tirzepatide, high-dose arms achieved ~47-62% MASH resolution without fibrosis worsening versus ~10-14% on placebo, yielding >90% power with ~60 patients/arm and two active doses. Study completion in July 2027 suggests full 60-week readouts are likeliest in H2 2027.

assumptions.claim: In a Phase 2 trial in biopsy-confirmed MASH and F1-F3 fibrosis, the dual GLP-1/glucagon receptor agonist survodutide significantly increased MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis versus placebo.
In the Phase 2 SYNERGY-NASH trial, 10% of placebo participants achieved MASH resolution without worsening of fibrosis at Week 52.

reason: Conservative Phase 2 dosing of the engineered chimeric neurotoxin corabotase to minimize dysphagia risk could yield sub-optimal cervical muscle denervation at Week 4.
rationale: Corabotase (IPN10200) is Ipsen's recombinant botulinum neurotoxin chimera engineered for extended duration. Botulinum neurotoxins reliably reduce Week 4 TWSTRS total scores by 11-15 points versus ~4-5 points for placebo (e.g., ASPEN-1 and abobotulinumtoxinA trials). Testing at least two active doses across ~44 patients/arm provides strong power for Week 4 superiority unless safety-constrained doses are too low. Because blinded 36-week duration follow-up runs until November 2027, public topline disclosure before late 2027 is uncertain.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 ASPEN-1 cervical dystonia trial, botulinum neurotoxin significantly improved TWSTRS total score versus placebo, with placebo improving by 4.3 points.

reason: With zibotentan's additive albuminuria reduction on top of dapagliflozin already proven in ZENITH-CKD, operational execution or ERA fluid-retention dropouts pose the main residual risk.
rationale: ZODIAC is a 224-patient Russian regional bridging Phase 2 trial comparing zibotentan/dapagliflozin FDC against dapagliflozin alone over 12 weeks in high-proteinuria CKD (UACR >700 mg/g) following a 28-day dapagliflozin run-in for SGLT2i-naive patients. In ZENITH-CKD, zibotentan plus dapagliflozin reduced Week 12 UACR by 27%-34% versus dapagliflozin alone; with N=112/arm, statistical power exceeds 90% for both UACR and UPCR. AstraZeneca routinely posts results on ClinicalTrials.gov near the 12-month mark after September 2026 completion.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2b ZENITH-CKD trial, zibotentan combined with dapagliflozin reduced Week 12 UACR by 27.0% (0.25 mg) and 33.7% (1.5 mg) compared with dapagliflozin alone.

reason: Sham neurosurgery produces large, durable placebo ON-time gains in Parkinson's trials, and any result reported by mid-2027 despite ongoing 2026 recruitment risks reflecting an early stop.
rationale: Bemdaneprocel moved directly from a 12-patient open-label Phase 1 study into this 102-patient sham-surgery-controlled Phase 3 trial with a 78-week primary endpoint. Historically, double-blind sham-surgery cell and gene therapy trials in Parkinson's disease have struggled against large sham placebo responses and graft variability. Critically, because exPDite-2 was still recruiting in late October 2026 and requires 18 months post-surgery follow-up, true completion is expected in 2028+, making any pre-June-2027 resolution disproportionately likely to be an early stop.

assumptions.claim: The Phase 1 exPDite trial of bemdaneprocel enrolled 12 participants in an open-label design without a sham-surgery control arm.
Double-blind sham-surgery-controlled fetal nigral transplantation trials in Parkinson's disease failed to meet their primary endpoints in the overall trial populations.

reason: Enrollment is already closed as of October 2026 and the longest primary PK assessment is at Week 18, aligning closely with the February 2027 primary completion date.
rationale: CheckMate-1533 is a 76-patient Phase 2 PK study of subcutaneous nivolumab regimens that is already active, not recruiting on 2026-10-29. Because primary PK endpoints run only through Week 18 (Cycle 7 Day 1), the registered primary completion date of 2027-02-05 matches full enrollment completion in autumn 2026, making a >90-day delay unlikely. Bristol-Myers Squibb usually posts results near the 12-month statutory deadline (early 2028) rather than by August 2027.

reason: Pembrolizumab monotherapy already achieves roughly 50% confirmed objective response rates in checkpoint-naive Merkel cell carcinoma, leaving limited headroom for a single-lesion intralesional adjunct to demonstrate statistically significant superiority in 118 patients.
rationale: Pembrolizumab monotherapy yields ~50-56% ORR in first-line advanced Merkel cell carcinoma (KEYNOTE-017, KEYNOTE-913). With only 59 patients per arm, showing two-sided alpha=0.05 superiority requires roughly a 24-26 percentage point ORR improvement, a high hurdle given historical failures of intralesional immunotherapies added to PD-1 blockade in CPI-naive skin cancers (e.g., MASTERKEY-265). Moreover, rare-cancer accrual was still ongoing in late October 2026 with a 24-week assessment window, making primary completion delays beyond March 2027 highly likely.

assumptions.claim: Pembrolizumab monotherapy achieved an objective response rate of 56% in systemic-therapy-naive advanced Merkel cell carcinoma.
Adding intralesional talimogene laherparepvec to pembrolizumab failed to significantly improve outcomes over placebo plus pembrolizumab in checkpoint-naive advanced melanoma.

reason: About 95% of unselected metastatic colorectal cancers are microsatellite-stable tumors where adding PD-1 blockade to chemotherapy plus VEGF inhibition has yielded modest or non-significant progression-free survival gains in prior randomized trials.
rationale: AK112 (ivonescimab) is a PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, but here the control arm already receives bevacizumab plus doublet chemotherapy, which achieves ~10 months median PFS in first-line mCRC. Because the trial enrolls unselected mCRC (~95% MSS/pMMR), efficacy relies on cooperative PD-1/VEGF targeting overcoming MSS immune resistance. Prior trials adding PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors to chemo-bevacizumab (CheckMate 9X8, AtezoTRIBE) showed mixed PFS results (HR 0.70-0.81), supporting moderate success probability.

assumptions.claim: Adding nivolumab to mFOLFOX6 plus bevacizumab did not meet its primary PFS endpoint in unselected first-line metastatic colorectal cancer (HR 0.81).
FOLFOXIRI plus bevacizumab with atezolizumab improved PFS modestly in unselected metastatic colorectal cancer primarily driven by immunogenic subsets.

reason: Cholinergic gastrointestinal adverse events during rapid inpatient titration and high inpatient placebo improvement on YMRS could attenuate the week-3 treatment difference.
rationale: KarXT (xanomeline-trospium) demonstrated robust, rapid acute symptom reduction within 2-3 weeks in inpatient schizophrenia trials (EMERGENT-2, EMERGENT-3), and muscarinic M1/M4 agonism reduces striatal hyperdopaminergia implicated in acute mania. Nearly all approved acute antipsychotics succeed in 3-week inpatient bipolar mania monotherapy trials, where placebo typically improves YMRS by ~10-11 points. Lack of phase 2 mania dose-optimization and cholinergic GI intolerability keep success probability moderate-high rather than certain.

assumptions.claim: KarXT significantly reduced PANSS total scores compared with placebo by week 2 and week 5 in hospitalized adults with acute schizophrenia.
Cholinergic gastrointestinal adverse events such as nausea and vomiting occurred at higher rates with KarXT than placebo in inpatient phase 3 trials.

reason: Broad multinational enrollment across 85 sites in 11 countries increases inter-rater noise and inpatient placebo response on the YMRS, which can dilute week-3 separation.
rationale: BALSAM-2 mirrors BALSAM-1 in testing 3-week inpatient KarXT monotherapy for acute Bipolar-I mania (N=274), supported by KarXT's rapid antipsychotic and anti-agitation activity in EMERGENT-2/3 and mechanistic striatal dopamine modulation. However, BALSAM-2 spans 85 sites across 11 countries, a setting historically associated with slightly larger YMRS placebo responses and rater variance in psychiatry trials. Because it remained recruiting days before its November 2026 target date, a >90-day registry completion shift is likely.

assumptions.claim: KarXT met its primary inpatient efficacy endpoint rapidly in acute schizophrenia trials with treatment separation evident by week 2.

reason: Target-mediated drug disposition and inter-patient myeloma tumor burden variability could widen confidence intervals around subcutaneous daratumumab AUC ratios at early and late sampling windows.
rationale: Phase 3 monoclonal antibody biosimilar pharmacokinetic equivalence trials from experienced sponsors like Celltrion succeed in roughly 90% of cases. With 473 relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma patients already enrolled (active, not recruiting as of October 2026) and primary completion registered for March 2027 based on 24-week follow-up and Weeks 0-1 and 8-10 AUC ratios, sample size provides ample precision against nonlinear CD38 clearance variability and supports timely topline readout and regulatory filing in 2027.

assumptions.claim: Subcutaneous daratumumab (Darzalex Faspro) has well-characterized pharmacokinetics in combination with lenalidomide and dexamethasone in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma.

reason: Because this adaptive 52-site narcolepsy type 2 trial was still recruiting in late October 2026 just ahead of its November 2026 target date and includes up to 15 weeks of follow-up, primary completion will likely slip by more than 90 days.
rationale: This phase 2 adaptive dose-finding study of Takeda's oral orexin-2 receptor agonist TAK-360 in 88 adults with narcolepsy type 2 remained recruiting at snapshot (2026-10-29) despite a registered primary completion date of 2026-11-30 and a 15-week TEAE assessment window. Consequently, primary completion is likely to occur after February 2027. Unlike earlier TAK-994 hepatotoxicity, newer Takeda orexin agonists (oveporexton/TAK-861, TAK-360) have shown clean safety to date, making early safety termination unlikely.

reason: Enrolling all-comer ER-positive/HER2-negative patients without restricting or co-primary gating on ESR1 mutations dilutes oral SERD superiority over fulvestrant.
rationale: Oral SERDs consistently beat fulvestrant in ESR1-mutant pretreated ER+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer, but results in unselected all-comer populations are mixed: EMERALD met overall PFS (HR 0.70) while EMBER-3, AMEERA-3, and acelERA missed statistical significance in overall populations. D-0502 (taragarestrant) benefits here from a large 640-patient sample size in China and a higher share of CDK4/6-inhibitor-naive patients with endocrine-sensitive tumors, yielding near coin-flip odds of meeting IRC PFS.

assumptions.claim: Elacestrant improved progression-free survival over standard endocrine therapy in the overall pretreated ER+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer population with HR 0.70.
Imlunestrant monotherapy significantly improved PFS over standard therapy in ESR1-mutated patients but not in the overall unselected ER+/HER2- population.

reason: Monthly ranibizumab 0.5 mg reliably produces over 10 ETDRS letters of visual gain in DME, posing a tough benchmark for a Wnt-agonist monotherapy that does not directly neutralize VEGF.
rationale: BAROLO completed enrollment (1,054 patients, active not recruiting) on schedule for March 2027 Week-52 primary completion. Ranibizumab 0.5 mg Q4W consistently gains ~10-11 ETDRS letters at 52 weeks in DME. Remigromig (EYE103), a trispecific Wnt/Fz4-LRP5 agonist, showed ~11-letter open-label gains in Phase 1b/2a AMARONE, and 351 patients per arm gives tight precision (~1.6-letter 95% CI half-width) against standard 4- to 4.5-letter non-inferiority margins, though lacking direct VEGF blockade caps anatomical CST superiority odds.

assumptions.claim: Monthly intravitreal ranibizumab 0.5 mg improves ETDRS best-corrected visual acuity by roughly 10 to 12 letters at 1 year in diabetic macular edema.

reason: Spontaneous fluctuation of superficial inflammatory nodules in mild-to-moderate HS without draining tunnels can elevate vehicle HiSCR75 response rates at week 16.
rationale: Ruxolitinib 1.5% cream previously met its primary endpoint in a randomized vehicle-controlled Phase 2 trial in Hurley stage I/II hidradenitis suppurativa without draining tunnels (NCT05635838), demonstrating clear separation on AN count reduction and HiSCR75 at Week 16, alongside oral JAK1 inhibitor efficacy (povorcitinib) in HS. With 573 patients enrolled and primary completion already reached in October 2026, TRuE-HS2 is well-powered for a ~15 percentage point HiSCR75 delta and on track for a near-term readout and sNDA submission.

assumptions.claim: Ruxolitinib cream demonstrated statistically significant reductions in abscess and inflammatory nodule counts versus vehicle at week 16 in Phase 2 mild-to-moderate HS.

reason: With roughly 33 patients per arm, sampling variation in placebo endoscopic response or a high share of anti-TNF-refractory enrollees could keep a clinically meaningful benefit short of statistical significance.
rationale: Brivekimig (SAR442970) is a bispecific nanobody inhibiting both TNF-alpha—a highly validated target in Crohn's disease—and OX40L, and has already shown clinical activity in inflammatory disease (hidradenitis suppurativa Phase 2a). Centrally read placebo SES-CD endoscopic response at Week 16 averages ~10-14%, whereas effective biologics in mixed conventional/advanced-therapy-inadequate CD achieve ~32-40% (e.g., SEQUENCE, VIVID-1, GALAXI). Although 33 patients per arm limits power, two active dose arms provide solid odds of hitting p<0.05.

assumptions.claim: Placebo centrally read SES-CD endoscopic response rates in moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease induction trials typically average around 10% to 15%.

reason: Spontaneous lesion wax-and-wane in mild-to-moderate tunnel-free hidradenitis suppurativa can inflate the vehicle cream HiSCR75 response rate and compress the treatment difference.
rationale: Ruxolitinib 1.5% cream demonstrated clear proof-of-concept in Phase 2 (NCT05635838) in mild-to-moderate HS without draining tunnels, significantly reducing abscess and inflammatory nodule counts and improving HiSCR75 over vehicle at Week 16. Enrolling 580 Hurley I/II tunnel-free patients provides >90% power to detect a ~15 percentage point difference in HiSCR75, while restricting antiseptics and antibiotics helps contain vehicle response. Primary completion passed in October 2026 with enrollment finished, making an early-2027 topline readout and subsequent supplemental NDA filing likely.

assumptions.claim: Phase 2 NCT05635838 evaluated ruxolitinib 1.5% cream twice daily versus vehicle in mild-to-moderate hidradenitis suppurativa for 16 weeks.

reason: Gastrointestinal intolerance, hypoglycemia during insulin titration, or ketosis in type 1 diabetes could elevate treatment discontinuations and attenuate on-treatment glycemic gains.
rationale: Incretin therapies in overweight or obese adults with type 1 diabetes consistently reduce insulin resistance, postprandial glucose excursions, body weight, and HbA1c by 0.5 to 1.0 percentage points, as seen with liraglutide in ADJUNCT ONE/TWO and clinical studies of tirzepatide and semaglutide in T1D. With 465 randomized participants and an HbA1c SD near 0.85%, the trial is overwhelmingly powered for Week 40 HbA1c superiority and CGM time-in-range improvement. Regulatory submission before end-2027 depends on completing the July 2027 long-term safety extension.

assumptions.claim: Adjunctive GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in ADJUNCT ONE significantly reduced HbA1c and body weight compared with placebo in adults with type 1 diabetes.

reason: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate already achieves high 48-week HBV DNA suppression, especially in HBeAg-negative patients, making superiority across both co-primary cohorts difficult with 50 patients per arm.
rationale: ALG-000184 is a potent Class E capsid assembly modulator that produces faster and deeper HBV DNA declines than nucleos(t)ide analogues alone in HBeAg-positive patients with high baseline viremia. However, the record lists two primary Week 48 endpoints (Part 1 HBeAg-positive and Part 2 HBeAg-negative) with ~50 patients per arm per part. While ALG-000184 has a solid chance to beat TDF on <10 IU/mL in high-viral-load HBeAg-positive patients, TDF achieves >70% undetectable HBV DNA by Week 48 in HBeAg-negative patients, making statistical superiority on both co-primaries challenging unless Part 2 tests non-inferiority.

assumptions.claim: Tenofovir disoproxil fumarate monotherapy achieves high rates of HBV DNA suppression at Week 48 in treatment-naive HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B.

reason: Daily topical latanoprost 0.005% produces ~7 mmHg diurnal IOP reduction, leaving minimal room for an intracameral latanoprost implant to prove statistical superiority or tight non-inferiority with 25 patients per arm.
rationale: PA5108 is a biodegradable intracameral ocular implant releasing latanoprost free acid, compared here against daily topical latanoprost 0.005% across 75 patients (~25 per arm). Sustained-release prostaglandin implants (such as bimatoprost and travoprost implants) generally match rather than exceed the 7 to 8 mmHg IOP lowering of daily topical prostaglandin drops. With only 25 patients per arm, a Phase 2 dose-ranging study is severely underpowered either to beat active latanoprost drops on superiority or to establish formal 1.5 mmHg non-inferiority.

assumptions.claim: Topical latanoprost 0.005% once daily typically lowers diurnal intraocular pressure by approximately 6 to 8 mmHg from washed-out baseline in open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension.

reason: Switching treatment-experienced Type 2 SMA patients from ongoing maintenance nusinersen to intrathecal AAV9 gene therapy leaves a modest incremental motor gain over active standard-of-care control in only 50 patients.
rationale: Patients enrolled have Type 2 SMA already treated with nusinersen for >1 year, a maintenance phase where annual HFMSE scores typically plateau (+0 to +1 point). Intrathecal AAV9 SMN gene therapy (as seen with OAV101 in STEER/STRENGTH) provides modest motor gains in sitters, and the open-label design in China may favor the experimental arm on functional motor ratings or employ a non-inferiority margin. However, with status still recruiting in late October 2026 and a 52-week primary endpoint, completion is very likely delayed unless registry updates lagged.

assumptions.claim: Nusinersen significantly improved HFMSE scores over sham control in children with later-onset SMA in the CHERISH trial, before plateauing during long-term maintenance.

reason: IL-1 blockade has historically shown modest efficacy in rheumatoid arthritis, and 30 patients per arm in biologic-experienced patients provides limited power unless CD40 co-blockade drives a large ACR50 jump.
rationale: This Phase 2 platform trial evaluates lutikizumab (anti-IL-1a/1b), ravagalimab (anti-CD40), and their combination versus placebo on background methotrexate in b/tsDMARD-IR rheumatoid arthritis (~30 per arm). Historically, IL-1 inhibition produces modest ACR50 rates in RA compared with TNF or JAK inhibitors, so Substudy 1 (lutikizumab monotherapy) likely yields ~10-12 percentage points over placebo. However, under the round's multiple-arm rule, success in the combination or ravagalimab substudy could still meet the trial's primary objective if adequately powered. Ongoing recruitment in late October 2026 creates moderate delay risk.

assumptions.claim: Placebo plus methotrexate ACR50 response rates at Week 12 in b/tsDMARD-inadequate-responder rheumatoid arthritis trials are typically around 6% to 12%.

reason: Gastrointestinal adverse events or loss to follow-up before Week 52 polysomnography could modestly dilute treatment-regimen estimand effects, though class efficacy in obesity-related OSA is very large.
rationale: HRS9531 is a potent dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist that has produced ~20% weight loss in Chinese clinical trials, closely mirroring tirzepatide. In SURMOUNT-OSA Study 1 (patients with OSA and obesity not using PAP), tirzepatide reduced Week 52 AHI by ~50.7% versus ~4.8% for placebo (treatment difference ~46 percentage points). With 140 randomized patients (70 per arm) and SD ~36%, statistical power for both percent and absolute AHI reduction at Week 52 exceeds 99%. Registry status was still listed as recruiting in October 2026, posing reporting-timeline uncertainty.
