assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-OSA Trial 1, tirzepatide significantly reduced the apnea-hypopnea index at Week 52 compared with placebo in adults with obesity and moderate-to-severe OSA not receiving PAP therapy.

reason: With roughly 35 participants per arm in a mixed advanced-therapy-naive and advanced-therapy-experienced ulcerative colitis population, even an active biologic effect of 15-18 percentage points can miss statistical significance.
rationale: Brivekimig (SAR442970) is a dual anti-TNFalpha/anti-OX40L nanobody tested across two doses versus placebo in 105 patients (~35 per arm) with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis. TNFalpha blockade is well validated in UC (~12-18 percentage point clinical remission delta), and dual OX40L inhibition may enhance T-cell control in advanced-therapy-exposed patients. However, with 35 patients per arm, a 17.5 percentage point remission gain (27.5% vs 10%) sits near the threshold of two-sided p<0.05, yielding moderate power even across two active doses. Enrollment is complete with December 2026 primary completion.

assumptions.claim: Placebo clinical remission rates using modified Mayo criteria at 8 to 16 weeks in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis trials enrolling mixed biologic-naive and biologic-experienced patients typically range from 6% to 15%.

reason: Improved inhalational controller adherence during clinical trial monitoring in bronchodilator-responsive asthma patients frequently produces large placebo FEV1 gains that increase variance and narrow treatment separation.
rationale: PF-07275315 is Pfizer's multispecific cytokine-targeting biologic blocking validated type-2/epithelial asthma pathways (IL-4/IL-13/TSLP). Requiring baseline bronchodilator reversibility (>=12% and >=200 mL) and recent exacerbation history strongly enriches for large Week 12 pre-bronchodilator FEV1 responses (+150 to +220 mL over placebo with dupilumab and tezepelumab). Across 252 participants in a multi-dose design, at least one high dose has good power (~70%) to achieve statistical significance on FEV1 and percent-predicted FEV1. Active recruitment in late October 2026 ahead of a March 2027 completion date introduces moderate timeline risk.

assumptions.claim: Dupilumab and tezepelumab significantly increased pre-bronchodilator FEV1 at Week 12 by roughly 130 to 200 mL over placebo in uncontrolled moderate-to-severe asthma.

reason: A lower-than-expected 24-week exacerbation event rate in the 78-patient placebo group could leave fewer than 55 events per pairwise comparison, reducing power for a ~0.62 hazard ratio.
rationale: XH-S004 is an oral DPP1 (cathepsin C) inhibitor evaluated in 234 Chinese patients with non-CF bronchiectasis and >=2 prior-year exacerbations over 24 weeks, closely replicating WILLOW (brensocatib) and SAVE-BE (HSK31858 in China). Both precedent DPP1 inhibitors significantly prolonged time to first pulmonary exacerbation at 24 weeks with hazard ratios of ~0.50 to 0.62 against placebo 24-week event rates of 42-48%. Testing two active doses (20 mg and 40 mg) with enrollment already complete and January 2027 primary completion gives strong odds of a positive Phase 2 readout.

assumptions.claim: In the 24-week WILLOW Phase 2 trial, brensocatib 10 mg and 25 mg significantly prolonged time to first exacerbation versus placebo (48.3% placebo event rate; hazard ratios 0.58 and 0.62).

reason: Recruiting 30 active Graves' disease patients including an active orbitopathy subset across 24 sites makes a moderate enrollment slip past May 2027 plausible.
rationale: On 2026-10-29 this open-label 2-dose Phase 2 Sanofi trial (N=30, 16-week treatment) is still recruiting with a registered primary completion date of 2027-02-11, leaving less than 15 weeks before the registered date and requiring enrollment completion by mid-January 2027 to avoid exceeding the 90-day late threshold (2027-05-12). Active Graves' orbitopathy criteria (CAS >=3 within 9 months of onset) often slow screening, giving roughly even odds of >90-day delay, while Sanofi rarely terminates small Phase 2 biomarker trials early or posts results within months of completion.

reason: With only 45 enrolled patients, large spontaneous motor recovery variance, and three listed primary outcomes, the trial is severely underpowered unless the true drug effect is unusually large.
rationale: The trial is already marked completed (2026-10-06) with only 45 enrolled participants across 10 Australian sites and three registered primary outcomes (FMMS, TUG, and NIHSS motor change at Week 12). Under ReadoutBench rules all co-primary endpoints must be met unless one was pre-specified as sole primary. Spontaneous 12-week Fugl-Meyer motor recovery from days 2-7 post-stroke averages ~25 points with SD ~20 points, yielding SE ~6 points for N=45; pharmacological stroke recovery trials historically show small effects, and neflamapimod recently missed primary endpoints in other CNS trials.

assumptions.claim: Placebo-treated acute ischemic stroke patients with motor deficits recover roughly 24 points on the Fugl-Meyer motor scale over 90 days.
Oral neflamapimod failed to meet its primary efficacy endpoint in the Phase 2b RewinD-LB CNS trial.

reason: Anti-IL-17A/BAFF blockade could show weaker tissue penetration or dose response than dual IL-17A/F inhibition amidst high placebo variability in hidradenitis suppurativa lesion counts.
rationale: Tibulizumab blocks both IL-17A and BAFF, two validated inflammatory pathways in hidradenitis suppurativa (secukinumab and bimekizumab validate IL-17A blockade, and B-cell infiltrates drive HS tunnels/nodules). Using continuous percent change in AN count at Week 16 across ~82 patients per arm with two active doses gives substantially better statistical power (~70% for a 20-22 percentage-point separation assuming SD ~48%) than dichotomous HiSCR50. Because the trial is active, not recruiting and its September 2026 primary completion date has passed, Zura Bio is very likely to report Period 1 topline results by early 2027.

assumptions.claim: Anti-IL-17A therapy (secukinumab) significantly reduces abscess and inflammatory nodule counts versus placebo at Week 16 in moderate-to-severe hidradenitis suppurativa.

reason: Gastrointestinal intolerability or refusal to pause PAP therapy for repeat polysomnography at Week 52 could increase missing data and dilute treatment-regimen AHI estimates.
rationale: HRS9531 is Hengrui's potent dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist, closely mirroring tirzepatide's weight-loss efficacy (~17-20% over 48-52 weeks). In the identically designed SURMOUNT-OSA Trial 2 in obese OSA patients on PAP therapy, tirzepatide reduced Week 52 AHI by ~23.8 events/h over placebo. Even with N=140 (70/arm) and Chinese BMI >=28 inclusion, an expected ~20.5 events/h difference with SD ~22 events/h (SE ~3.7) provides >99% statistical power. Registry lag in China makes actual completion slightly past March 2027 plausible.

assumptions.claim: In SURMOUNT-OSA Trial 2 among obese adults with moderate-to-severe OSA on PAP therapy, dual GIP/GLP-1 agonism (tirzepatide) reduced Week 52 AHI by 23.8 events per hour versus placebo.

reason: Restricting enrollment to milder macular edema (CST 320 to <400 microns, BCVA up to 78 letters) creates visual acuity ceiling effects and allows greater spontaneous sham improvement.
rationale: KSI-101 combines intravitreal IL-6 and VEGF inhibition against a sham comparator in macular edema secondary to inflammation (MESI). While dual IL-6/VEGF blockade strongly resolves inflammatory fluid, PINNACLE specifically enrolls milder macular edema (CST 320 to <400 microns, baseline BCVA up to 78 letters), capping letter gains and risking sham improvement—a known challenge in MESI Phase 3 trials. With N=300 and SD ~11.5 letters, an expected +6-letter separation yields good power (~68% PoS). Because it is still recruiting on 2026-10-29 with a 24-week endpoint, completion will likely slip past May 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the sham-controlled PEACHTREE Phase 3 trial in macular edema associated with uveitis, the sham arm gained 4.0 ETDRS letters at Week 24.

reason: Only an unexpected off-target safety signal halting the trial could prevent this 3,103-patient PCSK9 inhibitor study from achieving statistical significance on Week 12 LDL-C.
rationale: AZD0780 is AstraZeneca's oral small-molecule PCSK9 inhibitor. In the Phase 2b PURSUIT trial on background statins, AZD0780 30 mg once daily produced a ~50.7% placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction at Week 12 with placebo-like tolerability. With 3,103 participants randomized 1:1 and between-patient SD ~24% (SE <0.9%), statistical power for Week 12 LDL-C reduction and <70 mg/dL goal attainment exceeds 99%. Enrollment is complete (active, not recruiting) with 52-week completion set for 2027-01-11, supporting both on-time readout and 2027 regulatory submission.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2b PURSUIT trial, oral AZD0780 30 mg once daily reduced LDL-C by approximately 50.7% versus placebo at Week 12 on background statin therapy.

reason: An unforeseen idiosyncratic safety issue is the only plausible failure mode given robust PCSK9-mediated LDLR upregulation in heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia.
rationale: PCSK9 inhibition consistently delivers ~45-60% LDL-C reductions in heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (HeFH) because patients retain one functional LDLR allele, matching efficacy in non-FH hypercholesterolaemia (seen across evolocumab, alirocumab, and oral PCSK9 inhibitors). With 473 HeFH patients randomized 2:1 (active, not recruiting, completion 2027-01-04) and SD ~25% (SE ~2.4%), AZD0780's expected ~47.5% placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction at Week 12 provides overwhelming power for both the primary endpoint and LDL-C <70 mg/dL responder rate, directly supporting AstraZeneca's planned 2027 marketing application.

assumptions.claim: Oral AZD0780 30 mg daily reduced Week 12 LDL-C by ~50.7% placebo-adjusted in Phase 2b PURSUIT.
PCSK9 inhibition robustly lowers LDL-C by roughly 50-60% versus placebo in heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia on statin therapy.

reason: Enrolling 100 medically ill cancer or neurodegenerative patients meeting strict psychedelic screening rules leaves substantial risk of recruiting past February 2027.
rationale: On 2026-10-29 this 100-patient Phase 2 psychedelic trial of single-dose RE104 in adjustment disorder secondary to cancer, ALS, MS, PD, or IPF remains recruiting despite a November 2026 registered primary completion date. Although individual follow-up to the Day 7 MADRS primary endpoint is very short, psychedelic trials in seriously medically ill populations face high screen-failure rates from concomitant medication restrictions, cardiovascular/CNS exclusions, and site logistics, making a >90-day enrollment slip past 2027-02-28 slightly more likely than not.

reason: Because enrollment of all 480 toddlers is already complete and the blinded safety period lasts 6 months, primary completion is likely on schedule or only briefly delayed.
rationale: COMFORT Toddlers (N=480) is already active, not recruiting on 2026-10-29 with a registered November 2026 primary completion date for its 26-week double-blind safety period. Having completed enrollment prior to late October 2026, primary completion would only exceed 2027-02-28 if final randomization occurred after late August 2026. Early termination is very unlikely given Viaskin Peanut's established safety in toddlers (EPITOPE), and ClinicalTrials.gov results posting before August 2027 is uncommon while the 18-month open-label extension continues into 2028.

reason: Enrolling 36 Parkinson's patients across 8 academic sites within 6 months of study start under strict weight, non-smoking, and contraception criteria will likely slip past March 2027.
rationale: LoCaMoTE-PD started on 2026-06-30 and remains recruiting on 2026-10-29 with an ambitious 6-month enrollment window to a 2026-12-31 primary completion date across 8 US Parkinson Study Group sites. Multi-center foundation/biotech Phase 2a PK-safety trials in Parkinson's disease requiring narrow body weight (60-110 kg, BMI <30), smoke-free households, stable levodopa, and intensive carboxyhemoglobin sampling routinely require 10-14 months to complete accrual and 44-day follow-up, giving a >60% probability of finishing after 2027-03-31.

reason: Adding CD73 blockade in unselected first-line non-squamous NSCLC without enriching for high CD73 expression is unlikely to yield a large enough hazard ratio improvement over sintilimab plus chemotherapy for N=150 to reach statistical significance.
rationale: Sintilimab plus pemetrexed-platinum is an active control with ~8.9 months median PFS in Chinese untreated non-squamous NSCLC (ORIENT-11). While uliledlimab showed encouraging activity in CD73-high cohorts, this trial enrolls unselected patients (testing CD73 centrally without restricting eligibility). With 150 patients (~98 PFS events), achieving two-sided p<0.05 requires an observed HR near 0.67, whereas unselected anti-CD73 combinations typically yield modest incremental benefit (expected HR ~0.82). Primary completion passed in August 2026, making a 2027 oncology congress readout likely.

assumptions.claim: Sintilimab plus pemetrexed and platinum achieved a median progression-free survival of 8.9 months in untreated non-squamous NSCLC in ORIENT-11.
Adding anti-CD73 antibody oleclumab to PD-L1 blockade improved outcomes modestly in Stage III NSCLC in the Phase 2 COAST study.

reason: Reversible MAO-B inhibition reduced weight in rodent models via astrocytic GABA modulation, but non-incretin central metabolic mechanisms rarely translate into clinically meaningful 12-week human weight loss.
rationale: KDS2010 is an oral reversible MAO-B inhibitor targeting hypothalamic astrocytic GABA signaling. Although preclinical diet-induced obesity models showed fat reduction without appetite suppression, clinical MAO-B inhibitors historically produce minimal human weight loss, and rodent brown/white adipose thermogenic mechanisms translate poorly to humans. With 22 patients on 240 mg versus 11 Stage 3 (or 25 pooled) placebo patients on structured diet and exercise over 12 weeks, detecting superiority requires roughly a 2.5-3.0% placebo-adjusted reduction. Sequential SRC gating across three stages also creates moderate schedule risk.
evidence: Nam et al. KDS2010 preclinical obesity study (2023)

assumptions.claim: KDS2010 reduced body weight in diet-induced obese mice by reversibly inhibiting astrocytic MAO-B and tonic GABA release in the hypothalamus.

reason: Broadening enrollment from genetically defined gain-of-function SCN2A/SCN8A encephalopathies to heterogeneous developmental and epileptic encephalopathies may dilute the strong anticonvulsant effect of persistent sodium current blockade.
rationale: Relutrigine (PRAX-562) selectively inhibits persistent sodium current and demonstrated robust ~46% placebo-adjusted motor seizure reduction in the Phase 2 EMBOLD study in SCN2A/SCN8A DEE. EMERALD enrolls 160 patients (~53 per arm across two active doses and placebo, where either dose succeeding meets the round rule) in broader DEEs. While genetic heterogeneity in general DEE will attenuate effect size compared with gain-of-function sodium channelopathies, selective INa inhibition is broadly active against refractory motor seizures. Being active, not recruiting with December 2026 primary completion, top-line readout in H1 2027 and subsequent NDA filing are highly likely.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 EMBOLD study, relutrigine produced a statistically significant reduction in monthly motor seizure frequency in patients with SCN2A and SCN8A developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.

reason: Only unexpected severe safety findings or extreme gastrointestinal treatment discontinuations could threaten significance, given CagriSema's ~20% weight-loss separation over placebo.
rationale: CagriSema (cagrilintide plus semaglutide) produced >20% mean weight loss (~18-20 percentage points beyond placebo) at 68 weeks in non-diabetic adults with obesity in REDEFINE 1. With 609 non-diabetic participants randomized 2:1 over 80 weeks, statistical power for both primary percent weight loss and >=20% responder rate exceeds 99%. Consistent with GLP-1/amylin class data, women achieve substantially greater relative weight loss than men. Because recruitment is complete and Novo Nordisk tracks timelines reliably, March 2027 completion should yield a Q2 2027 headline announcement.

assumptions.claim: In STEP 1, once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg achieved a mean body weight change of -14.9% versus -2.4% with placebo at Week 68 in adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes.
In REDEFINE 1, once-weekly CagriSema achieved greater than 20% mean weight loss versus approximately 2.3% with placebo at Week 68 in adults with obesity without diabetes.

reason: Upstream TSLP blockade previously failed to achieve robust efficacy in randomized atopic dermatitis trials with tezepelumab, and N=110 leaves limited power for a moderate effect size.
rationale: ATI-045 (bosakitug/BSI-045B) is a high-affinity anti-TSLP monoclonal antibody evaluated here as monotherapy over 24 weeks in 110 moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis patients. While open-label Phase 2a data were encouraging and a 24-week monotherapy design avoids background topical steroid washout noise that hampered tezepelumab in ALLEVIAD, upstream alarmin inhibition (TSLP, IL-33) has consistently proven much weaker than IL-4Ra/IL-13 blockade in controlled AD trials. With ~55 patients per arm, detecting ~15-17% EASI separation is borderline, and binary vIGA success is harder still. Given November 2026 study completion, Aclaris is very likely to report top-line data by March 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2a ALLEVIAD trial, anti-TSLP antibody tezepelumab plus topical corticosteroids did not achieve statistically significant improvement over placebo on Week 12 EASI-50 in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis.

reason: Topical pan-JAK inhibition may struggle to penetrate hyperkeratotic palmoplantar pustular lesions deeply enough to achieve PPPASI-75 in a notoriously treatment-refractory neutrophil-driven dermatosis.
rationale: Delgocitinib cream 20 mg/g is an effective pan-JAK inhibitor on palmar skin in chronic hand eczema (DELTA 1/2), and oral JAK inhibitors show clinical activity in palmoplantar pustulosis (PPP). Low vehicle PPPASI-75 rates (~7-9%) allow ~68 patients per arm to detect a ~14-15 percentage-point gain. However, sterile neutrophilic pustules beneath thick plantar stratum corneum are far more refractory to topical therapy than eczema. Operationally, because the trial remained recruiting in late October 2026 with a 16-week treatment period, primary completion will very likely slip past mid-March 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 DELTA 1 and DELTA 2 trials, twice-daily delgocitinib cream 20 mg/g significantly increased Week 16 treatment success versus vehicle cream in adults with moderate-to-severe chronic hand eczema.
assumptions.source: DELTA 1 and DELTA 2, Bissonnette et al. Lancet 2024

reason: Enrolling 120 healthy donors across just two US sites for 35-day blood storage and dual 51Cr/99mTc radiolabeled red cell infusions faces substantial logistical bottlenecks, making a >90-day completion delay likely.
rationale: This two-site radiolabeled autologous RBC recovery and lifespan trial was still recruiting in late October 2026 against a registered December 15, 2026 primary completion date. Because each participant requires whole blood donation, 35-day storage, 51Cr/99mTc radiolabeling, and post-infusion lifespan sampling, enrolling and completing 120 healthy volunteers before March 15, 2027 is unlikely. Early termination and substantive outcome amendments are rare in standardized FDA RBC radiolabeling validation studies, and results posting by August 2027 is unlikely given probable schedule slippage.

reason: While superiority over enoxaparin is strongly supported by Factor XI class data, co-primary or gated testing against apixaban—a much stronger comparator than enoxaparin—is the primary hurdle.
rationale: Catalytic-domain Factor XI monoclonal antibodies (abelacimab, REGN7508) consistently reduce postoperative venographic VTE after total knee arthroplasty by >50% relative to enoxaparin (~7-8% vs ~18-22%). With ~667 patients per arm, power for superiority over enoxaparin and non-inferiority/superiority against apixaban is high, though any requirement to beat apixaban on superiority represents the main risk. Conversely, confirmed symptomatic DVT alone by Day 12 occurs in <1% of patients (~3-6 events/arm), making statistical significance on that secondary outcome unlikely.

assumptions.claim: In the ANT-005 TKA trial, postoperative Factor XI antibody abelacimab 150 mg reduced total venous thromboembolism incidence to 4% compared with 22% with enoxaparin after total knee arthroplasty.
assumptions.source: ANT-005 TKA, Verhamme et al. NEJM 2021

assumptions.claim: In the FOXTROT trial, high-dose postoperative anti-Factor XIa antibody osocimab was superior to enoxaparin in preventing venous thromboembolism after total knee arthroplasty.

reason: Durable Type VII collagen deposition in the corneal basement membrane from Period 1 KB803 treatment could carry over into Period 2 placebo weeks, blunting the within-patient crossover contrast in N=16.
rationale: KB803 is an ophthalmic formulation of B-VEC, which is FDA-approved for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa skin wounds and directly restores missing COL7A1 anchoring fibrils, with clinical proof of concept in ocular DEB. Pre-selecting symptomatic patients from a 12-week natural history run-in boosts baseline event rates and crossover efficiency. The main risk is carryover of restored Type VII collagen from Period 1 active dosing into Period 2 placebo alongside diary variability in 16 patients. Because the record still showed recruiting in late October 2026 for a 24-week crossover, completion will likely slip past March 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 GEM-3 trial, topical beremagene geperpavec (B-VEC) achieved complete healing in 67% of dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa wounds at 6 months compared with 22% with placebo.

reason: With recruitment finished and registered study completion in October 2026, this small Phase 2a AstraZeneca platform study should conclude cleanly with moderate probability of ClinicalTrials.gov results posting within ten months.
rationale: This small Chinese Phase 2a safety and PK platform trial of AZD6234 and AZD9550 is active, not recruiting, with registered primary and study completion on October 23, 2026. Late termination or substantive primary safety outcome changes after scheduled completion are very unlikely (~4%). AstraZeneca maintains high compliance with the 12-month ClinicalTrials.gov results reporting window, giving roughly a 45% chance that results are posted slightly ahead of the 12-month mark by August 31, 2027.

reason: Botulinum toxin type A injections have repeatedly shown minimal or no superiority over placebo in episodic migraine trials despite efficacy in chronic migraine.
rationale: Xeomin (incobotulinumtoxinA) shares the botulinum toxin type A mechanism of onabotulinumtoxinA, which failed multiple randomized placebo-controlled trials in episodic migraine despite robust efficacy in chronic migraine. Even with enrichment for 6 to 14 baseline monthly migraine days and a large sample (~332 per arm), cranial injection trials elicit a strong ~3.8-day placebo reduction, and the expected true treatment difference is small (~0.5 days), yielding modest probability of statistical significance at Month 6.

assumptions.claim: Previous randomized placebo-controlled trials of botulinum toxin type A in episodic migraine failed to show statistically significant reductions in migraine frequency versus placebo.
Cranial placebo injections produce substantial reductions of roughly 3 to 4 monthly migraine days in episodic migraine prevention trials.

reason: Multi-site cranial placebo injections induce large reductions of 6 or more monthly migraine days in chronic migraine, which can narrow the treatment difference.
rationale: Unlike episodic migraine, chronic migraine is a validated indication for botulinum toxin type A based on the pivotal PREEMPT 1 and PREEMPT 2 trials of onabotulinumtoxinA, which demonstrated approximately 1.8 to 2.0 fewer monthly headache and migraine days versus placebo at Week 24. Xeomin contains the same 150 kDa botulinum neurotoxin type A core, and ~269 patients per arm provides roughly 85-90% power if PREEMPT-like efficacy holds, moderated by dose uncertainty and high injection placebo responses.

assumptions.claim: In pooled PREEMPT 1 and 2 analyses at Week 24, onabotulinumtoxinA reduced monthly headache days by 8.4 versus 6.6 for placebo (difference -1.8 days, p<0.001).
Discontinuation due to adverse events in 24-week botulinum toxin type A chronic migraine trials was approximately 3.8% on active treatment versus 1.2% on placebo.

reason: Because the 192-patient multi-cohort lung cancer study is still recruiting fewer than four months before its February 2027 registered primary completion date, completion will likely slip by more than 90 days.
rationale: On 2026-10-29 the trial remains recruiting across 17 sites in China for 192 patients with NSCLC or SCLC, with primary outcomes including ORR and PFS assessed up to 24 months and a registered primary completion date of 2027-02-20. Enrolling the remaining cohorts and accruing sufficient RECIST follow-up makes a >90-day delay past May 2027 likely. Early termination and ClinicalTrials.gov results posting prior to October 2027 study completion are uncommon for China-only Phase 2 oncology trials.

reason: With enrollment completed and the 24-week primary biomarker period passed, this open-label atacicept dosing study should proceed smoothly through its September 2027 completion without posted results before August 2027.
rationale: This 90-patient Phase 2 dosing regimen study of atacicept in IgA nephropathy is active, not recruiting, and its September 2026 primary completion date for 24-week Gd-IgA1 levels has already passed. Given positive clinical experience with atacicept in IgAN (ORIGIN program), safety-related termination is unlikely, and primary outcome amendments after primary completion are rare. Results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov before 2027-08-31 is unlikely because full study completion is scheduled for September 2027.

reason: If the unspecified clinical response definition relies heavily on cardiopulmonary exercise testing, background beta-blocker blunting of peak heart rate could attenuate the responder difference.
rationale: HRS-1893 is an oral cardiac myosin inhibitor evaluated in 228 Chinese patients with obstructive HCM over 24 weeks. Cardiac myosin inhibitors (mavacamten in EXPLORER-HCM and EXPLORER-CN; aficamten in SEQUOIA-HCM) have consistently produced large, highly significant improvements in LVOT gradients, NYHA class, composite clinical response (~19-35 percentage-point gains over ~17-22% placebo), and KCCQ-CSS (+7 to +9 points). With enrollment finished and study completion in November 2026, timely readout and NMPA NDA filing in 2027 are likely.

assumptions.claim: In EXPLORER-HCM, 37% of mavacamten patients versus 17% of placebo patients met the primary composite clinical response endpoint at Week 30 (difference +19.4%, p=0.0005).
In EXPLORER-HCM, mavacamten improved KCCQ-CSS by 9.1 points more than placebo at Week 30 (p<0.0001) with smaller CPET responses among patients on beta-blockers.

reason: Metabolic modulators and other pharmacotherapies have repeatedly failed to significantly improve KCCQ symptom scores over strong placebo responses in non-obstructive HCM.
rationale: In the 67-patient Phase 2 IMPROVE-HCM trial, ninerafaxstat was well tolerated and modestly improved VE/VCO2 slope, but KCCQ-CSS was not significantly improved in the overall population, showing a signal only in a post-hoc symptomatic subgroup. Non-obstructive HCM has a high failure rate across metabolic and sarcomere drugs (including RESTYLE-HCM and ODYSSEY-HCM), and detecting an effect on KCCQ-CSS (SD ~15) with ~82 patients per arm requires a nearly 5-point true difference over substantial placebo gains. Ongoing recruitment in October 2026 also points to schedule slippage.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 IMPROVE-HCM trial of ninerafaxstat in non-obstructive HCM, KCCQ-CSS change from baseline to Week 12 did not differ significantly from placebo in the overall trial population.

reason: Because dual therapy with dapagliflozin plus metformin already lowers HbA1c by nearly 1%, multiple co-primary comparisons across five arms slightly compress margin for error.
rationale: Adding a DPP-4 inhibitor (prusogliptin) to an SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin) and metformin in type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin has highly predictable additive glycemic efficacy. Prior Phase 3 triple-combination factorial trials (saxagliptin + dapagliflozin + metformin; ertugliflozin + sitagliptin + metformin) consistently demonstrated -0.85% to -1.1% HbA1c change with SGLT2i + metformin and an additional -0.40% to -0.55% reduction from the DPP-4i component (SD ~0.85%). With ~163 patients per arm, statistical power exceeds 90% even across multiple component comparisons.

assumptions.claim: In Rosenstock et al. 2015, triple therapy with saxagliptin, dapagliflozin 10 mg, and metformin reduced Week 24 HbA1c by -1.47% versus -0.88% with dapagliflozin plus metformin (p<0.0001).

reason: With only 20 patients per arm across heterogeneous localized and generalized EBS subtypes, spontaneous blister fluctuation and vehicle gel effects will likely obscure modest topical efficacy.
rationale: TolaSure Gel targets mutant keratin aggregation in epidermolysis bullosa simplex, an unvalidated topical mechanism tested here in just 40 flaring pediatric and adult patients across diverse anatomic sites (plantar feet versus limbs/torso). Prior randomized EBS topical trials (such as diacerein 1% ointment) failed primary endpoints due to natural waxing-and-waning seasonal blistering and substantial vehicle skin-care improvements. Recruiting 40 actively flaring rare-disease patients across two US sites was still ongoing in late October 2026, making a >90-day completion delay past May 2027 likely.

assumptions.claim: The randomized placebo-controlled CAST trial of topical 1% diacerein in epidermolysis bullosa simplex failed to meet its primary blister reduction endpoint amid high placebo response and disease variability.

reason: Still recruiting 72 patients at a single Italian clinic right before its November 2026 registered primary completion date, this 4-month follow-up nail patch trial will likely finish more than 90 days late.
rationale: On 2026-10-29 this single-center 72-patient cosmetic urea hydrogel nail patch study in Italy is still recruiting despite a registered primary completion date of November 2026 and a 4-month per-patient follow-up window (12 weeks treatment plus 4 weeks follow-up). Unless the registry date is left un-updated, completion after February 2027 is likely. Cosmetic device/patch studies rarely terminate for safety or post results on ClinicalTrials.gov promptly.

reason: Achieving the stringent EU/UK SALT <=10 complete hair regrowth threshold by Week 24 with ~69 children per arm carries modest risk if many participants have baseline alopecia totalis or universalis.
rationale: Ritlecitinib is already approved for severe alopecia areata in patients aged >=12 years based on the pivotal ALLEGRO Phase 2b/3 trial, where 50 mg daily achieved 23% SALT <=20 and 13.4% SALT <=10 at Week 24 versus 1.5% on placebo, with adolescents showing comparable or slightly stronger hair regrowth and PGI-C response (~50% vs 9%). Spontaneous regrowth in severe AA is near zero (~2%), giving ~69 children per arm high power on both SALT <=20 and SALT <=10. With completion in January 2027, pediatric sNDA submission in 2027 is likely.

assumptions.claim: In ALLEGRO (NCT03732807), Week 24 SALT <=20 response was 23% with ritlecitinib 50 mg daily versus 1.5% with placebo, and SALT <=10 response was 13.4% versus 1.5%.
Patients with baseline alopecia totalis or universalis had lower Week 24 SALT <=20 response rates than patients with incomplete scalp hair loss in ALLEGRO.

reason: Restylane Perlane achieves very high 6-month MFVDS responder rates, so modest random variation or a tight non-inferiority margin could cause the lower confidence bound to miss.
rationale: HArmonyCa Lidocaine combines cross-linked hyaluronic acid for immediate mid-face lift with calcium hydroxyapatite microspheres for sustained collagen stimulation, and is already approved in multiple markets. Against Restylane Perlane Lidocaine with optional Day 31 touch-up in 252 Chinese participants (2:1 allocation), both dermal fillers reliably achieve ~85-90% 1-point MFVDS responder rates at Month 6. With a standard ~10% non-inferiority margin and ~4.3% standard error on the rate difference, statistical power for non-inferiority is high (~88%), whereas superiority on GAIS responder rate is unlikely.

reason: Allosteric TYK2 inhibition previously failed to induce Week 12 remission in ulcerative colitis (deucravacitinib LATTICE-UC), leaving target efficacy in gut mucosa uncertain.
rationale: D-2570 is InventisBio's oral selective TYK2 JH2 allosteric inhibitor, active in psoriasis Phase 2, now tested in 120 Chinese patients with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis (pooled Parts A and B). While selective IL-23 blockade works well in UC, allosteric TYK2 inhibition failed in the Phase 2 LATTICE-UC trial of deucravacitinib, possibly due to incomplete colonic IL-23 suppression or counterproductive Type I interferon blockade during mucosal healing. Furthermore, splitting 120 patients across placebo and potentially multiple D-2570 doses yields modest statistical power unless higher receptor occupancy achieves a >=15-point remission delta.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 LATTICE-UC trial, the selective TYK2 inhibitor deucravacitinib failed to meet its primary endpoint of clinical remission at Week 12 versus placebo in moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.

reason: With 81 IPF patients mostly on background antifibrotics over just 12 weeks, FVC variability (~190 mL SD) requires a >80 mL effect to achieve two-sided p<0.05.
rationale: BI 765423 is an intravenous anti-IL-11 antibody evaluated in an 81-patient Phase 2a IPF proof-of-concept trial with or without background standard antifibrotics. Over 12 weeks on background therapy, placebo FVC typically declines by only ~40-50 mL while between-patient FVC change SD is ~180-200 mL, giving a standard error near 42 mL. Achieving formal two-sided p<0.05 requires an observed separation exceeding ~83 mL—essentially halting all decline plus reversing lung restriction—in an indication where Phase 2 translation of novel anti-fibrotic mechanisms has historically had high attrition.

assumptions.claim: Boehringer Ingelheim's Phase 2 trial of nerandomilast (BI 1015550) in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis used change from baseline in FVC (mL) at 12 weeks with or without background antifibrotic therapy as its primary endpoint.

reason: Sofosbuvir-velpatasvir achieves ~96-98% cure rates, so slightly higher genotype 3 relapse or open-label loss to follow-up on BEM/RZR could breach a tight non-inferiority margin.
rationale: Bemnifosbuvir-ruzasvir (nucleotide NS5B plus pan-genotypic NS5A inhibitor) achieved ~98% SVR12 in a 275-patient Phase 2 chronic HCV study. In this 880-patient global open-label Phase 3 trial (already active, not recruiting) versus 12-week sofosbuvir-velpatasvir in DAA-naive non-cirrhotic and compensated cirrhotic patients, both regimens should achieve ~95-97% Week 24 HCV RNA < LLOQ (accounting for small ITT missingness). With 440 patients per arm, the 95% CI half-width is ~2.6 percentage points, giving strong power against a typical 5% non-inferiority margin, though virologic failure superiority is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Twelve weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir achieved sustained virologic response rates of 95% to 99% across chronic HCV genotypes 1 through 6 in the Phase 3 ASTRAL-1 and ASTRAL-3 trials.

reason: Because the primary endpoint restricts analysis to baseline LA grade C/D patients within a 523-patient LA A-D trial, a lower-than-planned C/D share or high lansoprazole healing could reduce power.
rationale: Linaprazan glurate is a potassium-competitive acid blocker (P-CAB) prodrug dosed up to 50 mg BID, providing sustained 24-hour intragastric acid suppression unaffected by CYP2C19 polymorphism. In Cinclus Pharma's Phase 2 LEVER study and prior P-CAB trials (such as PHALCON-EE), lansoprazole 30 mg QD heals only ~55-62% of severe LA grade C/D erosive esophagitis by Week 4, whereas potent P-CAB regimens heal ~80-88%. Assuming ~40-50% LA grade C/D enrichment (~70-85 evaluable C/D patients per arm) and two tested linaprazan doses, power to demonstrate Week 4 superiority is high.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 PHALCON-EE trial, the potassium-competitive acid blocker vonoprazan demonstrated substantially higher endoscopic healing rates than lansoprazole 30 mg once daily in participants with LA grade C/D erosive esophagitis.

reason: Two prior Japanese Phase 3 confirmatory trials of KPS-0373 (rovatirelin) missed their 24-week SARA primary endpoints due to modest drug effect (~0.4-0.5 points) and placebo stabilization.
rationale: KPS-0373 (rovatirelin) is an oral TRH analogue developed by Kissei for spinocerebellar degeneration in Japan. Two earlier Phase 3 trials failed to achieve significant 24-week SARA improvements in overall populations, prompting JNDA withdrawal and this 142-patient Confirmatory Study 3, likely enriched for responsive patients based on prior post-hoc subgroup signals (~0.9-point SARA benefit in more severe ataxia). With N=71 per arm and SD ~2.1 SARA points, an observed difference around -0.70 points is needed for p<0.05; slow 24-week natural progression and SARA practice effects keep success uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Two previous Japanese Phase 3 randomized placebo-controlled trials of rovatirelin (KPS-0373) in spinocerebellar degeneration failed to meet their primary endpoint of change in total SARA score at 24 weeks in the overall study populations.

reason: Because 177Lu-DOTATATE efficacy over octreotide LAR in progressive SSTR-positive GEP-NETs is overwhelming, the main risk is immature follow-up or censoring anomalies on the 18-month landmark rate.
rationale: This 184-patient Chinese Phase 3 registrational trial replicates the NETTER-1 paradigm by comparing 177Lu-DOTATATE peptide receptor radionuclide therapy against octreotide LAR in progressive SSTR-positive G1/G2 gastroenteropancreatic NETs after prior somatostatin analogue progression. In NETTER-1 and subsequent GEP-NET PRRT cohorts, 177Lu-DOTATATE reduced progression or death by ~75-80% (HR ~0.21-0.25), lifting 18-to-20-month PFS from ~11-22% on octreotide LAR to ~65-72%. With 92 patients per arm, statistical power exceeds 95%, though ongoing recruitment status in late 2026 suggests likely timeline slippage.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 NETTER-1 trial, 177Lu-DOTATATE significantly prolonged progression-free survival compared with high-dose octreotide LAR in progressive somatostatin-receptor-positive midgut neuroendocrine tumors with a hazard ratio of 0.21.

reason: Potent dual GIP/GLP-1 agonism makes efficacy failure versus placebo nearly impossible, leaving operational execution or unexpected safety-related hold as the only residual risk.
rationale: HRS9531 is Hengrui's dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist, which has already demonstrated robust ~2.0-2.5% HbA1c reductions and substantial weight loss in Phase 2/3 Chinese trials. Adding two doses of HRS9531 versus placebo to stable basal insulin (+/- metformin/SGLT2i) over 40 weeks in 300 T2DM patients (100 per arm) mirrors the SURPASS-5 design with tirzepatide. Expecting a ~1.5-1.8 percentage point placebo-adjusted HbA1c drop against a ~0.13% standard error yields overwhelming (>99%) statistical power on both primary HbA1c change and the <7.0% responder secondary endpoint.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 SURPASS-5 trial, adding the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide to basal insulin significantly reduced HbA1c from baseline at Week 40 by more than 2 percentage points compared with placebo.

reason: With 278 osteoporosis patients (~139 per arm), slightly higher BMD measurement variance or dropouts could push the 90%/95% confidence bounds outside tight biosimilar equivalence margins.
rationale: QL1206 is Qilu Pharmaceutical's proposed denosumab biosimilar (already validated analytically and clinically in oncology bone indications in China), here compared head-to-head against reference Prolia on 12-month percent change in lumbar spine BMD in 278 postmenopausal women with osteoporosis. Phase 3 denosumab biosimilar equivalence trials consistently succeed (>90% rate) because denosumab reliably increases 12-month LS-BMD by ~5-6% with ~3.8% between-patient SD, yielding a standard error near ~0.46% across 139 patients per arm—well within typical +/-1.5% to +/-2.0% equivalence margins.

assumptions.claim: In postmenopausal women with osteoporosis in the FREEDOM trial, denosumab 60 mg every 6 months increased lumbar spine bone mineral density by approximately 5% to 6% at 12 months.

reason: Large 6-week placebo HAM-D-17 improvements across 61 multinational MDD sites and potential attenuation of GABA-A neurosteroid separation by Day 42 pose major failure risks.
rationale: SPT-300 (GlyphAllo) is an oral lymphatic-targeted prodrug of endogenous allopregnanolone (brexanolone), avoiding hepatic first-pass clearance to enable oral neurosteroid GABA-A positive allosteric modulation in MDD. While IV brexanolone is active in postpartum depression and oral zuranolone showed rapid Day 15 HAM-D-17 effects in MDD, neurosteroid drug-placebo differences historically narrow substantially by Day 42 as placebo continues improving (-12 to -14 points) or receptor tolerance/sedation limits dosing. Across 61 US/European sites, high MDD placebo response keeps Day 42 superiority challenging (~34%).

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 WATERFALL trial of the neuroactive steroid zuranolone in major depressive disorder, the HAM-D-17 improvement over placebo was statistically significant at Day 15 (-1.7 points) but narrowed and was not statistically significant at Day 42.

reason: Pharmacotherapies in age-related sarcopenia have consistently struggled to improve composite physical function scores like SPPB over 12 weeks, especially against background exercise and nutrition guidance in a small 20-patient-per-arm trial.
rationale: AMC6156 is an unvalidated early-stage candidate in primary sarcopenia, an indication where multiple anabolic and myostatin-pathway agents failed to show statistically significant gains on physical performance endpoints such as SPPB. Participants receive exercise and nutrition guidance, which typically produces a 0.7 to 1.2 point placebo improvement on SPPB at 12 weeks and compresses treatment differences. With roughly 20 patients per group across three active doses and placebo, the trial requires nearly a 1.0-point treatment advantage for statistical significance, making primary success unlikely.

assumptions.claim: Lifestyle and exercise interventions in older adults with physical frailty and sarcopenia improve SPPB scores over follow-up.
Bimagrumab failed to show significant improvement in SPPB over placebo in older adults with sarcopenia.

reason: Recruiting 87 oncology patients with adjustment disorder across five Australian sites for intensive 8-hour psilocybin-assisted psychotherapy sessions faces substantial screening and scheduling bottlenecks, making completion delays past June 2027 highly likely.
rationale: This Phase 2b trial compares three psilocybin doses in cancer-associated adjustment disorder across five Australian sites with a registered primary completion of March 2027. Psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy trials in oncology require psychiatric clearance, washout of sedating or psychiatric medications, dedicated therapist pairs, and 8-hour in-clinic dosing days. Given recruiting status in late October 2026 and a 10-week primary assessment plus Day 14 dosing, finishing primary follow-up within 90 days of March 2027 is unlikely, whereas early results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 is improbable.

reason: Subcutaneous monoclonal antibody formulations can exhibit slightly altered absorption rates affecting Cmax geometric mean ratios even when total exposure (AUC) matches closely.
rationale: PORTAMENTO evaluates pharmacokinetic bioequivalence (AUC0-12w and Cmax) between a test subcutaneous ocrelizumab formulation and the marketed subcutaneous reference formulation in 193 MS patients (~96 per arm). With inter-subject PK variability of roughly 30-35% for subcutaneous anti-CD20 antibodies, ~96 patients per parallel group provides strong precision (~8% half-width for the 90% CI on geometric mean ratios), comfortably within standard 80-125% bioequivalence bounds unless formulation changes shift Cmax. Because enrollment is complete and registered primary completion passed in September 2026, completion risk is minimal.

assumptions.claim: Subcutaneous ocrelizumab demonstrated pharmacokinetic non-inferiority in B-cell-depleting exposure to intravenous ocrelizumab in MS patients in OCARINA II.

reason: Because enrollment of 50 participants is already complete as of late October 2026 for a 16-week treatment period, this Galderma PK/PD study should wrap up close to its December 2026 primary completion target.
rationale: This 50-patient Galderma exploratory PK/PD study of nemolizumab in chronic pruritus of unknown origin already reached 'active, not recruiting' status prior to late October 2026 across 26 North American sites. With a 16-week treatment window and registered primary completion in December 2026, finishing primary data collection before the 90-day late threshold (end of March 2027) is very likely. Termination or substantive primary PK/PD endpoint amendments after full enrollment are rare, while results posting by August 2027 is modest given standard 12-month reporting timelines.

reason: Once-weekly insulin icodec provides slightly less day-to-day basal flexibility in type 1 diabetes than daily basal analogues, creating a small risk of trailing glargine U100 if hypoglycemia-avoidance titration limits dosing.
rationale: ONWARDS 11 compares once-weekly insulin icodec against daily glargine U100 over 26 weeks in 877 adults with T1D. In ONWARDS 6 (N=582), icodec met HbA1c non-inferiority (0.3%-point margin) versus daily insulin degludec with an estimated treatment difference of +0.05%-points (-0.47% vs -0.51%). Against glargine U100 with ~439 patients per arm, precision is very high (SE ~0.06%), giving ~90% probability of meeting non-inferiority, though statistical superiority on CGM time-in-range is unlikely. Enrollment is complete with January 2027 primary completion, supporting timely Q2 2027 readout and regulatory resubmission.

assumptions.claim: In ONWARDS 6, once-weekly insulin icodec met its primary endpoint of non-inferiority in HbA1c change at week 26 compared with once-daily insulin degludec in adults with type 1 diabetes.
In ONWARDS 6, percentage of time in glucose range 3.9-10.0 mmol/L at weeks 22-26 did not show superiority of insulin icodec over insulin degludec.

reason: With roughly 40 patients per arm across five groups, chance variation or a higher-than-expected placebo remission rate in biologic-naive patients could mask a clinically meaningful anti-TL1A induction effect.
rationale: BCD-261 targets TL1A, one of the strongest validated novel mechanisms in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis: Phase 2 trials of tulisokibart (ARTEMIS-UC) and afimkibart (TUSCANY-2) demonstrated ~18-25 percentage-point clinical remission advantages over placebo at weeks 12-14 with favorable tolerability. Testing four active regimens (~40 patients per group) increases the chance that at least one dose meets superiority on week-14 clinical remission. However, because the trial was still recruiting in late October 2026 with a 14-week induction endpoint, primary completion will likely slip past May 2027.

assumptions.claim: In ARTEMIS-UC, the anti-TL1A antibody tulisokibart achieved a significantly higher week-12 clinical remission rate than placebo in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis.

reason: High-dose oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonists cause substantial gastrointestinal adverse events and occasional transaminase elevations that could elevate treatment discontinuations and attenuate estimand efficacy.
rationale: HDM1002 is an oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist evaluated at 100, 200, and 400 mg daily versus dapagliflozin on background metformin in 800 Chinese T2DM patients (200 per arm). Dapagliflozin typically reduces HbA1c by ~0.8-0.9%-points from an ~8.3% baseline, whereas oral GLP-1RAs achieve ~1.3-1.5% reductions despite ~8-12% GI-related discontinuations at top doses. With 200 patients per group (SE ~0.09%), a ~0.55%-point HbA1c advantage provides high power for superiority on both mean HbA1c change and the <7.0% responder secondary at Week 40.

assumptions.claim: Oral GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy demonstrated superior HbA1c reduction compared with an SGLT2 inhibitor on background metformin in Phase 3 T2DM testing (PIONEER 2).

reason: Enrolling only 30 patients randomized 2:1 (20 experimental vs 10 control) yields fewer than 25 PFS events, making statistical significance unattainable unless the observed hazard ratio is extreme.
rationale: This signal-seeking open-label Phase 2 study randomizes only 30 treatment-naive clear cell RCC patients 2:1 to IBR854 (an investigational cellular immunotherapy) plus pazopanib versus pazopanib monotherapy. First-line pazopanib yields a median PFS of ~8.4-10.5 months (COMPARZ), where modern IO-TKI regimens are standard of care, potentially slowing enrollment. With ~19 expected PFS events under 2:1 allocation, an observed HR below ~0.39 is needed for two-sided p<0.05, so meeting formal PFS superiority (and especially OS) is unlikely.

assumptions.claim: First-line pazopanib monotherapy achieved a median progression-free survival of 8.4 months in advanced renal cell carcinoma in COMPARZ.

reason: Splitting 80 patients with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae across three distinct infection-specific co-primary endpoints leaves each subgroup too small for reliable formal hypothesis testing, especially against ceftazidime-avibactam in best available therapy.
rationale: Meropenem-pralurbactam combines a carbapenem with a beta-lactamase inhibitor against CRE, analogous to meropenem-vaborbactam in TANGO II (N=77), which numerically improved cure rates and reduced nephrotoxicity versus polymyxin/aminoglycoside-heavy BAT. However, this trial lists three syndrome-specific co-primary endpoints (cUTI overall success, HABP/VABP/BSI mortality, and cIAI clinical response) within only 80 total patients, and modern BAT includes ceftazidime-avibactam. Under benchmark rules requiring all co-primaries to meet formal statistical hypotheses, `p_met` is modest even if cUTI cure rates favor experimental therapy by ~14 points.

assumptions.claim: In TANGO II, meropenem-vaborbactam showed higher clinical cure rates and lower nephrotoxicity than best available therapy in carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae infections.

reason: Improved adherence to background nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy under clinical trial monitoring can drive spontaneous HBV DNA suppression in placebo recipients, though capsid assembly modulation remains far more potent.
rationale: GST-HG141 (neracorvir) is an HBV capsid assembly modulator (CpAM) tested as 48-week add-on therapy versus placebo in 526 HBeAg-positive CHB patients with persistent viremia (>50 IU/mL) despite >=1 year of nucleos(t)ide analogues. While CpAMs rarely clear HBsAg, class precedent (vebicorvir, morphothiadin) and GST-HG141 Phase 2 data show potent additive suppression of pgRNA encapsidation and residual serum HBV DNA (<LLOQ in ~75-85% vs ~20-30% on continued NA alone). With 263 patients per arm (detailed text notes enrollment completed), statistical power for Week-48 virologic suppression and subsequent Chinese NDA filing is very high.

assumptions.claim: Adding an HBV core protein inhibitor (vebicorvir) to nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy achieved deeper HBV DNA suppression than nucleos(t)ide analogue plus placebo in chronic hepatitis B.

reason: Empagliflozin has robustly established glycemic efficacy as an add-on to metformin plus a DPP-4 inhibitor, leaving operational execution or incomplete reporting detail as the only plausible ways to miss.
rationale: Empagliflozin is a well-characterized SGLT2 inhibitor whose mechanism is independent of insulin secretion and complementary to metformin and DPP-4 inhibition. Across prior Phase 3 add-on trials to metformin plus linagliptin or sitagliptin, empagliflozin 10-25 mg lowered Week 24 HbA1c by roughly 0.65 to 0.80 percentage points versus placebo with between-patient SD near 0.75%. With ~85 patients per arm, this provides well over 95% statistical power at two-sided alpha 0.05. Being listed as recruiting in late October 2026 against a December 2026 primary completion suggests likely registry delay.

assumptions.claim: Empagliflozin added to metformin plus a DPP-4 inhibitor reduces HbA1c at 24 weeks by approximately 0.65% to 0.80% relative to placebo.
Patients with higher baseline HbA1c (>=8.0%) experience larger absolute HbA1c reductions with SGLT2 inhibitors than those below 8.0%.

reason: Recruiting 24 genetically confirmed non-dystrophic myotonia patients including 12 mexiletine-naive subjects at a single Belgian center for a 25-week crossover design carries substantial enrollment delay risk.
rationale: Non-dystrophic myotonias are ultra-rare channelopathies, and requiring 12 mexiletine-naive patients alongside 12 pre-treated patients with only one listed Belgian site creates a major recruitment bottleneck before the January 2027 primary completion target, especially given two 12-week crossover periods plus washout. Premature termination and substantive primary safety outcome amendments remain unlikely, while ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 2027 is unlikely unless completion happens on schedule.

reason: Because the molecular target and dose regimen of HRS-7249 are undisclosed in the registry, weaker-than-expected triglyceride lowering at 28 weeks is the main efficacy uncertainty.
rationale: HRS-7249 is an injectable lipid-lowering candidate from Hengrui subsidiary Fujian Shengdi evaluated over 28 weeks in 224 hyperlipidemia patients, consistent with a long-acting RNAi or biologic targeting triglyceride metabolism (such as APOC3 or ANGPTL3). Multiple active doses with a 224-patient sample size afford strong power to detect 30-60% triglyceride reductions at at least one dose, and the trial is already active, not recruiting past its September 2026 primary completion date. Public disclosure timing and Chinese Phase 3 registration by late 2027 are moderate.

assumptions.claim: Injectable Phase 2 triglyceride-lowering therapies assessed at 24-28 weeks typically target large (>35%) placebo-adjusted percent reductions in fasting triglycerides.

reason: Preserving lean mass against active semaglutide weight loss and post-semaglutide washout across two separate co-primary outcomes with roughly 40 patients per arm leaves the study severely underpowered.
rationale: On semaglutide, obese adults typically lose 2.5 to 3.0 kg of lean mass over 20 weeks (~520 g per 4 weeks). Although (S)-pindolol (espindolol) preserved lean body mass in the Phase 2 ACT-ONE cancer cachexia trial via partial beta-2 agonism and beta-1 blockade, attenuating caloric-deficit lean loss during GLP-1RA therapy is pharmacologically distinct. Furthermore, the registry lists two primary outcomes (PROACT 1 during semaglutide and PROACT 2 post-semaglutide) across small arms (~40 per group), making simultaneous statistical significance on both outcomes difficult.

assumptions.claim: Semaglutide treatment in adults with obesity induces substantial lean body mass loss alongside fat loss on DEXA.
Espindolol 10 mg twice daily significantly increased lean body mass relative to placebo over 16 weeks in cancer cachexia.

reason: Intensive in-hospital statin and ezetimibe initiation in statin-naive ACS patients compresses the additive difference in percent LDL-C change from baseline, though not nearly enough to threaten significance.
rationale: Inclisiran reliably lowers LDL-C by ~50% relative to placebo on stable background statins (ORION-10, ORION-11, VICTORION-INITIATE). In acute coronary syndrome, newly initiated or intensified background statins reduce LDL-C in the control arm (~26% averaged across prior-statin and statin-naive strata), compressing the additive difference in percent change from pre-intensification baseline to roughly -42 percentage points—with larger differences in the <100 mg/dL stratum (who must already be on statins per eligibility). With 300 patients across 69 sites, power exceeds 99%.

assumptions.claim: Inclisiran reduces LDL-C by approximately 50% compared with placebo when added to maximally tolerated statin therapy.
High-intensity statin therapy initiated in acute coronary syndrome reduces LDL-C substantially in the placebo arm over follow-up.

reason: Unproven clinical target validation for BFB759 in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis combined with substantial placebo EASI responses creates meaningful risk of insufficient efficacy.
rationale: COMPASS 2-AD is already active, not recruiting with 225 patients across 88 sites and a February 2027 primary completion, making readout by mid-2027 fairly likely. In Phase 2 moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis trials, placebo EASI typically improves ~25-30% at Week 16 with high patient-level variability (SD ~35-40%). While testing multiple doses raises the chance at least one dose reaches significance, unvalidated novel mechanisms in atopic dermatitis have historically shown mixed Phase 2 success rates near 40-50%.

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in Phase 2/3 moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis trials commonly show 20% to 35% mean improvement in EASI at Week 16.

reason: Staged dose-selection enrollment pauses, only two listed clinical sites, and RECIST response follow-up in refractory colorectal cancer make registry primary completion slippage beyond March 2027 likely.
rationale: This 60-patient Chinese Phase 2 dose-optimization trial of anti-PD-L1 ADC HLX43 in refractory colorectal cancer remains recruiting in late October 2026 with a December 30, 2026 registered primary completion date, despite a mandatory enrollment pause after the first 15 patients to select two expansion doses and an outcome timeframe up to 24 months. Registry primary completion delay past March 2027 is therefore likely, while ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by Chinese oncology sponsors within months is rare.

reason: Requiring simultaneous statistical significance across four registered primary endpoints spanning both Nasal Polyp Score and Nasal Congestion Score in overall and eosinophilic subsets adds a modest hurdle.
rationale: TQC2731 is a humanized anti-TSLP monoclonal antibody in a 246-patient Chinese Phase 3 CRSwNP trial that has already completed recruitment. TSLP blockade was strongly validated in CRSwNP by tezepelumab in WAYPOINT (NCT04851964), producing large Week 24/52 reductions in both endoscopic Nasal Polyp Score and Nasal Congestion Score across overall and eosinophilic populations, and Chinese Phase 3 biologic trials in CRSwNP (e.g., stapokibart) showed comparably large effects with high power across co-primary overall and ECRSwNP endpoints.

assumptions.claim: Anti-TSLP antibody therapy (tezepelumab) produced large, statistically significant reductions in both Nasal Polyp Score and Nasal Congestion Score versus placebo in Phase 3 CRSwNP.
Type-2 inflammation-predominant ECRSwNP shows larger polyp score reductions with upstream epithelial or type-2 biologics than non-eosinophilic CRSwNP.

reason: Fourteen days of daily placebo vaginal inserts and spontaneous resolution can elevate Day 28 complete symptom-absence rates in the vehicle arm, narrowing the treatment delta.
rationale: Intravaginal boric acid 600 mg daily for 14 days has well-documented clinical and mycological antifungal activity against both Candida albicans and non-albicans species. In contemporary US Phase 3 acute VVC trials using the strict composite VSS=0 clinical cure criterion (such as VANISH-303 and VANISH-306), placebo cure rates are roughly 29-44% while effective antifungals achieve ~50-65%. With ~111 patients per arm and two active regimens (7-day and 14-day), power to exceed placebo by ~20-25 percentage points is strong, and the study is already completed.

assumptions.claim: In US Phase 3 acute VVC trials using composite VSS=0 clinical cure criteria, placebo clinical cure rates typically fall around 29% to 44%.
Boric acid 600 mg vaginal suppositories for 14 days achieve high mycological and clinical cure rates across Candida species including non-albicans VVC.

reason: Achieving statistically significant complete corneal staining clearance across eyes by Day 28 in Sjögren's syndrome dry eye with only 40 patients per arm requires an unrealistically large responder difference.
rationale: Topical recombinant human lubricin (rhPRG4) previously improved ocular symptoms and mean corneal staining in a small 28-day Phase 2 dry eye trial (Lambiase et al. 2017). However, complete resolution of total Oxford corneal staining by Day 28 in autoimmune Sjögren's-related dry eye is a stringent binary threshold, and 40 patients per arm provides adequate power only if active response exceeds vehicle by roughly 20-25 percentage points (e.g., >32% vs 11%), making primary statistical success uncertain.

assumptions.claim: Topical rhPRG4 (150 ug/mL) demonstrated improvements in dry eye symptoms and mean corneal fluorescein staining over 28 days in an earlier randomized Phase 2 trial.

reason: With only 15 crossover patients, achieving statistical significance on both co-primary sign and symptom endpoints in fibrotic ocular GVHD after a short 14-day washout is severely underpowered.
rationale: Recombinant human lubricin (rhPRG4) previously improved corneal fluorescein staining and VAS dry eye symptoms in moderate dry eye disease (NCT02507934), and this trial uses a higher 450 ug/mL concentration in a within-patient crossover design. However, enrollment is only 15 patients in severe, fibrotic ocular GVHD, both co-primary outcomes (Oxford corneal staining and 8-item total VAS symptom score at Day 28) must be met under round rules, and a 14-day vehicle washout risks carryover of surface-bound lubricin into the second period.

assumptions.claim: Topical rhPRG4 (150 ug/mL) significantly improved dry eye symptoms and corneal fluorescein staining compared with sodium hyaluronate in a two-week randomized trial of 39 dry eye patients.

reason: Recruiting 48 idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis patients across 12 Chinese centers with an approximately 1-year safety observation timeframe makes primary completion by December 2026 unlikely.
rationale: This Phase 2a multiple ascending dose safety and PK trial of SV001 in 48 IPF patients across 12 sites in China started in November 2025, remains recruiting as of late October 2026, and specifies an approximately 1-year primary outcome timeframe despite a registered primary completion date of December 31, 2026. Consequently, registry primary completion is very likely to slip more than 90 days past March 2027, while ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by Chinese biotech sponsors in early-phase trials is rare.

reason: Titrated active-control cinacalcet robustly lowers iPTH in compliant double-dummy dialysis trials, leaving little margin if MT1013 underdoses or requires meeting both co-primary responder thresholds.
rationale: MT1013 is an intravenous dual CaSR and osteogenic growth peptide receptor agonist compared against oral cinacalcet in a 424-patient double-dummy Phase 3 trial for dialysis SHPT. In head-to-head calcimimetic trials (e.g., etelcalcetide vs cinacalcet, NCT01896232), cinacalcet achieved >50% iPTH reduction in ~40% of patients and >30% in ~58%, while IV calcimimetic delivery reliably matched or modestly exceeded oral cinacalcet on non-inferiority. With 212 patients per arm, statistical power for non-inferiority across both iPTH thresholds is high, though still-recruiting status in October 2026 implies probable delay.

assumptions.claim: In the active-controlled Phase 3 trial comparing intravenous etelcalcetide with oral cinacalcet in hemodialysis SHPT, 40.2% of cinacalcet patients achieved greater than 50% mean iPTH reduction.

reason: Beating an active pembrolizumab-plus-chemotherapy regimen on pathologic complete response in non-squamous NSCLC with 85 patients per arm requires a large absolute pCR gain to reach formal significance.
rationale: IBI363 is a PD-1/IL-2alpha-bias bispecific antibody combined with pemetrexed-platinum against active standard-of-care pembrolizumab plus pemetrexed-platinum in 170 resectable stage IB-III non-squamous NSCLC patients. In KEYNOTE-671, neoadjuvant pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy yielded an overall pCR rate of ~18% (slightly lower in non-squamous histology, though typically ~18-22% in Chinese neoadjuvant chemo-IO cohorts). With 85 patients per arm, formal superiority at alpha 0.05 requires ~16 percentage points improvement; randomized Phase 2 oncology studies often examine numerical trends rather than powered p<0.05 superiority.

assumptions.claim: In KEYNOTE-671, neoadjuvant pembrolizumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy achieved a pathologic complete response rate of 18.1% in resectable stage II-IIIB NSCLC.

reason: Because cabergoline is pharmacologically far more effective and better tolerated than bromocriptine, failure would almost certainly stem from reporting vagueness or operational issues rather than efficacy.
rationale: This 382-patient double-blind Phase 3 domestic registration study in China compares well-established cabergoline against bromocriptine over 14 weeks in female hyperprolactinemia. In the landmark multicenter randomized double-blind comparator trial (Webster et al. 1994), cabergoline normalized serum prolactin in 83% of women versus 59% with bromocriptine, resumed ovulatory cycles in 72% versus 52%, and cut AE discontinuations from 12% to 3%. With 191 women per arm, power exceeds 99% under either non-inferiority or superiority.

assumptions.claim: In the pivotal randomized double-blind trial in hyperprolactinemic women, cabergoline normalized prolactin in 83% of patients versus 59% treated with bromocriptine.

reason: Intravenous tranexamic acid before and after incision already potently inhibits perioperative fibrinolysis in total knee arthroplasty, leaving a small ceiling for further blood loss reduction.
rationale: BT-114143 (low and high dose) is tested against perioperative IV tranexamic acid (TXA) in 270 unilateral TKA patients (90 per arm) using Day 3 Gross-formula total blood loss. Perioperative pre- and post-incision IV TXA already lowers mean TKA total blood loss to roughly 650-800 mL (SD ~300 mL), leaving limited room for incremental hemostatic benefit without thrombotic risk. Unless the protocol specifies a wide non-inferiority margin rather than superiority, beating active IV TXA in a 90-per-arm Phase 2 dose-ranging study has low probability.

reason: While Week 24 virologic suppression should overwhelmingly beat continued bulevirtide, the second registered primary outcome (24 weeks post-treatment) will remain immature at the Week 24 readout.
rationale: ECLIPSE 2 is fully enrolled (active, not recruiting; PCD Dec 2026) comparing tobevibart + elebsiran against continued bulevirtide 2 mg QD in 150 chronic HDV patients still viremic (>=500 IU/mL) after >=24 weeks of bulevirtide. In Phase 2 SOLSTICE (NCT05461170), tobevibart + elebsiran produced rapid, high rates (~40-65%) of HDV RNA target not detected (TND), whereas patients already failing bulevirtide 2 mg rarely achieve TND over 24 more weeks (~5-8%). Power at Week 24 exceeds 99%; main risk is co-primary scoring if post-treatment TND is co-primary rather than separate/regional.

assumptions.claim: In MYR301, 2 mg daily bulevirtide monotherapy achieved undetectable HDV RNA in only 12% of chronic HDV patients at Week 48.
Tobevibart plus elebsiran achieved high rates of undetectable HDV RNA in Phase 2 SOLSTICE in chronic hepatitis delta.

reason: Topical 1.0% prednisolone acetate clears anterior chamber cells rapidly over 14 days, making non-inferiority challenging for a non-steroidal JAK1/TYK2 inhibitor drop and superiority unlikely.
rationale: This pivotal Phase 3 China trial of 1.0% VVN461 (topical dual JAK1/TYK2 inhibitor) vs 1.0% prednisolone acetate in 154 acute non-infectious anterior uveitis patients (baseline ACC 2+ or 3+) is already active, not recruiting, with a 14-day primary endpoint and December 2026 PCD. Pivotal uveitis trials against 1.0% prednisolone acetate typically test non-inferiority using a ~0.5 SUN-unit margin (where prednisolone lowers ACC by ~1.9 grades at Day 14, SD ~0.85). VVN461 showed anti-inflammatory activity in Phase 2, giving moderate non-inferiority odds (~58%) but low superiority odds on Day 14 complete clearing.

assumptions.claim: In pivotal randomized non-inferiority trials of acute endogenous anterior uveitis, 1.0% prednisolone acetate reduced mean anterior chamber cell grade by roughly 1.8 to 2.0 units by Day 14.

reason: Measuring pre-dose trough office systolic blood pressure tests end-of-dosing-interval persistence, where vasodilatory NO-cGMP effects can wane and office measurement noise is substantial.
rationale: RTN-001 (modified-release NO-cGMP/PDE5 pathway antihypertensive, inferred from strict nitrate, PDE5i, and alpha-blocker exclusions) is evaluated across three assumed active doses versus placebo (70/arm, N=280) after a run-in period in uncontrolled hypertension on 2-5 drugs. Under round rules, any one dose beating placebo on Week 4 pre-dose office SBP suffices. With office SBP SD ~13 mmHg (SE ~2.2 mmHg), an active vasodilator lowering trough SBP by 4.5-5.5 mmHg over placebo has slightly above-even power, aided by testing multiple doses and run-in stabilization.

reason: Although Week 48 undetectable HDV RNA rates should strongly exceed bulevirtide monotherapy, co-listing 24-week post-treatment TND as a primary outcome creates ambiguity at the Week 48 readout.
rationale: ECLIPSE 3 (Phase 2b, N=100, active not recruiting, PCD Nov 2026) randomizes bulevirtide-naive chronic HDV patients to tobevibart + elebsiran versus bulevirtide for Week 48 HDV RNA <LLOQ, target not detected (TND). In MYR301 (NCT03852719), bulevirtide monotherapy achieved undetectable HDV RNA at Week 48 in only 12% (2 mg) to 20% (10 mg) of patients, whereas tobevibart + elebsiran in SOLSTICE achieved ~50-65% TND. With 50 patients per arm, ~55% vs ~15% yields >98% power at Week 48, tempered only by potential co-primary status of 24-week post-treatment durability.

assumptions.claim: In Phase 3 MYR301, undetectable HDV RNA at Week 48 occurred in 12% of the 2-mg bulevirtide group and 20% of the 10-mg bulevirtide group.
Combination tobevibart and elebsiran achieved high rates of HDV RNA target not detected in Phase 2 SOLSTICE.

reason: Splitting 160 participants across four treatment and incubation arms yields roughly 40 patients per arm, though the very large historical effect of 20% ALA blue-light PDT keeps power high.
rationale: 20% aminolevulinic acid HCl (Levulan Kerastick) plus BLU-U blue-light PDT is an established, FDA-approved therapy for facial and scalp actinic keratosis. With up to two PDT sessions over 12 weeks on mild-to-moderate Olsen grade 1-2 lesions, 20% ALA field-directed PDT historically achieves ~60-75% complete patient clearance versus ~12-20% for vehicle-PDT, with higher clearance on the face than the bald scalp. Even at ~40 patients per arm, a ~48-point difference provides >95% statistical power, and having two active incubation arms further raises the chance at least one arm meets superiority.

assumptions.claim: In pivotal Phase 3 trials of 20% ALA HCl solution plus blue-light PDT for face and scalp actinic keratoses with re-treatment of persistent lesions, Week 12 complete clearance was roughly 72% versus 20% with vehicle-PDT.
Complete clearance rates with ALA blue-light or red-light PDT are consistently higher on the face than on the scalp.

reason: Upper-extremity actinic keratoses are thicker and less responsive to topical ALA penetration than facial lesions, yielding lower complete clearance rates if the reformulated vehicle underperforms.
rationale: Original 20% ALA HCl (Levulan Kerastick) plus BLU-U blue-light PDT is already FDA-approved for upper-extremity actinic keratoses based on NCT02137785, where up to two PDT treatments achieved ~31% Week 12 complete clearance versus ~13% with vehicle. Upper-extremity skin clears less readily than facial skin, and clearing all 6-8 baseline lesions is harder than clearing 4-5, so the Sponsor powered this two-arm trial generously at N=260 (130 per arm). At ~37% versus ~13% complete clearance, statistical power exceeds 95%, leaving major formulation bioinequivalence as the only substantive efficacy risk.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 trial of 20% ALA HCl plus blue-light PDT for upper-extremity actinic keratoses, Week 12 complete clearance after up to two sessions was approximately 31% for ALA-PDT versus 13% for vehicle-PDT.

reason: Early treatment discontinuations, relapse, or immunogenicity before Cycle 7 could shrink the steady-state PK evaluable set and widen the 90% confidence interval past equivalence bounds.
rationale: Monoclonal antibody pharmacokinetic equivalence trials conducted by experienced biosimilar manufacturers like Qilu Pharmaceutical succeed at a high rate (~85-90%) because physicochemical and analytical similarity are rigorously confirmed prior to Phase 3 entry. Testing in resected Stage II-IIIA adjuvant NSCLC avoids variable tumor-burden target-mediated clearance seen in metastatic disease, stabilizing Cycle 1 and Cycle 7 AUC variability across 146 randomized patients. Because enrollment was already completed ('active, not recruiting') by late October 2026 and Cycle 7 spans 21 weeks, on-time primary completion around year-end 2026 is highly likely.

assumptions.claim: Standard regulatory pharmacokinetic biosimilarity criteria require the 90% confidence interval for geometric mean AUC ratios between test and reference antibodies to lie within 80% to 125%.
assumptions.source: FDA Scientific Considerations in Demonstrating Biosimilarity to a Reference Product (2015)

reason: With only 48 participants total and high UAS7 spontaneous remission and patient-to-patient variance, a moderate treatment benefit could easily miss two-sided p<0.05.
rationale: CM512 is a long-acting bispecific antibody targeting TSLP and IL-13. In antihistamine-refractory CSU, IL-4/IL-13 blockade with dupilumab reduced UAS7 by ~8.5 points over placebo, whereas TSLP blockade alone with tezepelumab (INCEPTION) produced smaller numerical Week 16 reductions (~3-4 points) without meeting primary significance. Combining TSLP and IL-13 inhibition without blocking IL-4 should yield a moderate UAS7 effect (~ -6 to -7 points) against a strong ~ -11.5-point placebo response. However, with N=48 (likely 16-24 per arm) and SD ~12 points, statistical power at alpha=0.05 is near 45-50%.

assumptions.claim: In LIBERTY-CSU CUPID Study A of H1-antihistamine-refractory CSU patients, placebo mean UAS7 change was roughly -12.0 points and dupilumab improved UAS7 by -8.5 points versus placebo.
assumptions.source: Maurer et al., J Allergy Clin Immunol 2024

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2b INCEPTION study in CSU, anti-TSLP monotherapy tezepelumab did not achieve statistically significant superiority over placebo on Week 16 UAS7 change in biologic-naive patients.

reason: Dual kallikrein 5/7 protease inhibition is an unvalidated epidermal-barrier mechanism in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, where non-Th2 targets have historically shown low efficacy.
rationale: TRIV-509 is a first-in-class monoclonal antibody inhibiting kallikrein proteases KLK5 and KLK7 to restore epidermal barrier integrity and reduce protease-driven itch in atopic dermatitis. While genetically supported by Netherton syndrome biology, inhibiting downstream epidermal desquamation proteases has not yet demonstrated clinical efficacy in established moderate-to-severe AD, where numerous non-Th2/non-JAK pathways (e.g., IL-33, TSLP, IL-1alpha, H4R) failed Phase 2a responder endpoints. With N=95 on a binary Week 16 responder endpoint (likely EASI-75 or vIGA 0/1, placebo ~12-20%), PoS is modest (~28%), and Phase 2b would precede any Phase 3.

assumptions.claim: In global placebo-controlled trials of moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis without background topical corticosteroids, Week 16 placebo responder rates are typically ~10-15% for IGA 0/1 and ~12-20% for EASI-75.
assumptions.source: Simpson et al., N Engl J Med 2016

reason: Topical ciclosporin ophthalmic emulsion already produces substantial 4-week reductions in corneal fluorescein staining in pediatric VKC, leaving narrow headroom for superiority.
rationale: This 120-patient pediatric Phase 2 study compares Laboratoires Thea's T1695 ophthalmic suspension directly against an active standard of care, ciclosporin ophthalmic emulsion, on Day 29 modified Oxford corneal fluorescein staining (0-5 scale) in Bonini grade 3-4 VKC. In VEKTIS, topical ciclosporin rapidly improved corneal staining by ~1.5-1.8 Oxford grades within one month. Demonstrating statistical superiority over an effective active control with 60 patients per arm is challenging unless the protocol pre-specifies a non-inferiority margin or T1695 has corticosteroid-level potency. Private sponsor Thea also discloses Phase 2 readouts slowly.

assumptions.claim: In the pivotal VEKTIS trial of pediatric severe VKC, topical ciclosporin cationic emulsion significantly improved modified Oxford corneal fluorescein staining within 1 month of treatment.

reason: Modern triple or quadruple standard-of-care antiemetic prophylaxis already achieves ~70-80% delayed complete response, making incremental superiority hard to power with 204 patients.
rationale: LY3537021 is Eli Lilly's selective long-acting GIP receptor agonist, backed by strong preclinical evidence that area postrema GIPR activation suppresses cisplatin- and GLP-1-induced emesis. However, participants receive full standard-of-care antiemetic prophylaxis (NK1RA, 5-HT3RA, dexamethasone, +/- olanzapine) during cisplatin >=70 mg/m2 or AC chemotherapy, where delayed-phase CR (24-120h) already reaches ~72-80%. With 204 patients total (likely 2-3 arms, ~68-102 per arm), detecting a realistic +7 to +10 percentage-point incremental gain over SoC carries <45% power, compounded by preclinical-to-human translational risk.

assumptions.claim: Contemporary standard-of-care NK1RA/5-HT3RA/dexamethasone-based prophylaxis in cisplatin or AC highly emetogenic chemotherapy achieves delayed-phase complete response rates of roughly 70% to 80%.
