Results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 is unlikely so soon after completion.

reason: With roughly 80 patients per arm, achieving statistical significance on binary Day-90 mRS 0-1 requires a large ~15 percentage-point improvement over placebo.
rationale: QHRD106 (dosed in IU with porcine allergy and alpha-1 antitrypsin exclusions, consistent with a kallikrein-pathway biologic) is tested across three weekly IV doses in non-thrombolysed NIHSS 6-20 acute ischemic stroke. In Chinese AIS trials of moderate severity, Day-90 placebo mRS 0-1 rates are typically ~40-48%. While three dose arms increase the chance one arm reaches nominal significance, 80 patients per arm underpowers realistic neuroprotective effects of 6-10 percentage points. As a Shenzhen-listed sponsor, Qianhong has moderate likelihood of disclosing topline Phase 2b results in 2027.

assumptions.claim: In Chinese acute ischemic stroke trials enrolling non-thrombolysed patients within 48 hours, control arm 90-day mRS 0-1 rates are roughly 40% to 54% depending on baseline NIHSS.

reason: Zinc citrate toothpastes reliably outperform regular fluoride dentifrice on morning organoleptic malodor, leaving incomplete summary disclosure as the main residual risk.
rationale: This completed 3-week, 80-subject randomized study compares Colgate Max Fresh containing zinc citrate against regular Colgate Cavity Protection fluoride toothpaste on morning organoleptic malodor scores (enrolled between 6.0 and 8.4 on the standard 9-point hedonic scale). Zinc ions directly neutralize volatile sulfur compounds, and Colgate's standardized 3-week China malodor trials consistently demonstrate large, highly significant reductions versus regular fluoride dentifrice with near-zero adverse event dropouts. Publication typically occurs via dental journals or IADR abstracts rather than formal drug-style marketing application announcements.

reason: If bispecific stoichiometry or subcutaneous dosing achieves incomplete IL-4Ralpha receptor occupancy, EASI reductions could fall short in a 24-patient-per-arm comparison.
rationale: IBI3002 is Innovent's anti-IL-4Ralpha/TSLP bispecific antibody tested across multiple dose levels alongside dupilumab and placebo in 120 Chinese adults with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis. Validated IL-4Ralpha blockade produces ~35-45 percentage-point greater Week-16 EASI reductions than placebo (~-70% vs ~-33%), giving high statistical power even with ~24 patients per arm and multiple active doses. Binary vIGA-AD 0/1 has lower power at this sample size. With primary completion registered for late March 2027, public readout is unlikely before Q2-Q4 2027.

assumptions.claim: Biologics targeting IL-4Ralpha in Chinese patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis achieve large, statistically significant Week-16 EASI improvements over placebo.

reason: This Phase 2 safety study of aleniglipron is already marked completed on ClinicalTrials.gov, with results posting likely near the one-year statutory deadline in September 2027.
rationale: The trial completed in September 2026 across 16 US sites with 58 participants, making post-completion termination or substantive primary outcome amendments very unlikely. Under FDAAA 801, standard results submission falls due in September 2027—just after the August 31, 2027 read date—giving a modest probability of early results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov beforehand.

reason: If CMS-D002 achieves submaximal hormonal or target suppression at the 50 mg daily dose, responder rates could miss expectations.
rationale: CMS-D002 is evaluated at 10, 25, and 50 mg daily over 12 weeks in 120 women with uterine fibroid menorrhagia, measuring standard alkaline hematin/menstrual blood loss responder criteria (<80 mL and >=50% reduction) alongside fibroid/uterine volume and amenorrhea—hallmark endpoints of oral GnRH antagonists. In Phase 2/3 fibroid studies, placebo responder rates average ~15-20% while high-dose active regimens achieve 70-85%, offering high power even at 30 patients per arm across three active doses. HKEX-listed CMS regularly reports clinical milestones in corporate filings.

assumptions.claim: Placebo responder rates for menstrual blood loss <80 mL and >=50% reduction from baseline in uterine fibroid trials are typically around 10% to 25%.

reason: Recruiting 20 biopsy-proven primary vitreoretinal lymphoma patients is challenging due to extreme disease rarity, creating a high likelihood of completion delays beyond March 2027.
rationale: Primary vitreoretinal lymphoma is an ultra-rare intraocular malignancy requiring biopsy confirmation, and only one US site was listed as of late October 2026 while still recruiting toward 20 patients. Consequently, primary completion is very likely to slip more than 90 days past December 2026, and results posting on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 is unlikely.

reason: Enrolling 24 csDMARD-IR rheumatoid arthritis patients in China is manageable, though modest recruitment or registry update lag could push completion past March 2027.
rationale: This 24-patient, 8-week Phase 2a safety study in active rheumatoid arthritis started in September 2025 and remained recruiting in October 2026 ahead of a December 2026 registered completion date. Small sample size and short 8-week follow-up make completion by early 2027 plausible, with moderate risk of slipping past March 2027 and minimal chance of ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 2027.

reason: Novel topical ocular analgesics often produce modest incremental pain relief below the ~0.9-point threshold needed for significance in a 43-patient-per-arm PRK trial.
rationale: This completed 130-patient US Phase 2 study tested two doses of topical BL1332 against vehicle for acute 24-hour pain after photorefractive keratectomy. In post-PRK pain models using a 0-10 NRS, vehicle mean 24-hour scores typically average ~4-5 with inter-patient SD ~2.1, requiring roughly a 0.9-point reduction for p<0.05 with ~43 subjects per arm. Having two active doses improves odds, though novel ophthalmic analgesics historically show mixed Phase 2 efficacy. Completion in October 2026 supports potential spring/summer 2027 ophthalmic congress disclosure.

reason: Sepsis-associated ARDS is biologically heterogeneous with high mortality noise, and pharmacologic candidates rarely achieve a >2.2-day gain in 28-day ventilator-free days.
rationale: YD0743 is tested against placebo in 309 ICU patients with sepsis-associated ARDS on 28-day ventilator-free days. Historically, Phase 2/3 pharmacologic trials in sepsis and ARDS fail at high rates (>85%) because bimodal outcomes (death = 0 VFDs vs rapid extubation) create large standard deviations (~10 days), requiring >=2.2 VFDs difference for significance at N=155 per arm. Recruiting 309 acute ICU patients within 48 hours of ARDS diagnosis makes a >90-day delay beyond December 2026 likely.

assumptions.claim: In randomized clinical trials of moderate-to-severe ARDS, 28-day ventilator-free days have a wide standard deviation of roughly 9 to 11 days.

reason: With botulinum neurotoxins showing massive Week 4 treatment effects over near-zero placebo composite response rates, the main risk is an early top-line press release omitting explicit confirmation of all co-primary endpoints.
rationale: Corabotase (IPN10200) is Ipsen's recombinant chimeric BoNT-AB neurotoxin with Phase 2 proof-of-concept in glabellar lines (LANTIC). In Phase 3 glabellar line trials using the FDA composite >=2-grade ILA/SSA endpoint at Week 4, placebo response is ~0-2% while active neurotoxins achieve ~60-76%, giving >99% statistical power with 309 enrolled participants. Enrollment is already complete (active, not recruiting) ahead of the December 2026 Week 4 primary completion date, making an H1 2027 readout highly likely, while BLA filing likely awaits longer-term repeat-dose safety from LAURITE 2.

assumptions.claim: In SAKURA 1 and SAKURA 2, placebo Week 4 composite >=2-grade glabellar line responder rates were 0.0% and 1.0% while daxibotulinumtoxinA achieved 73.6% and 74.0%.

reason: Because enrollment is already complete with primary completion scheduled two weeks after the October 2026 snapshot, the trial should finish on time with results posted closer to the one-year statutory deadline.
rationale: This US Phase 2 PK/safety trial of Regeneron's GLP-1/GIP agonist olatorepatide (N=120) is already active, not recruiting as of late October 2026 with registered primary completion on 2026-11-13 and study completion on 2026-12-18. Given completed enrollment and short remaining follow-up, a >90-day delay or termination is very unlikely. Regeneron reliably meets FDAAA 12-month ClinicalTrials.gov posting timelines (due November 2027), giving a modest probability of early posting before 2027-08-31.

reason: Dosing only 15 minutes before intercourse leaves minimal time for sublingual SERT inhibitor absorption, CNS penetration, and serotonergic delay of ejaculation.
rationale: Selective serotonin transporter inhibitors (such as dapoxetine and clomipramine) reliably prolong geometric mean IELT over placebo in lifelong premature ejaculation, and a 40-patient crossover design provides solid paired power for a >=0.6-minute difference. However, requiring on-demand sublingual dosing just 15 minutes prior to penetration creates substantial PK/PD timing risk if peak central SERT occupancy occurs later. Because the single Australian site was still recruiting two days before its October 2026 target completion, readout will likely slip into 2027, and a Phase 2b study would precede any Phase 3.

assumptions.claim: On-demand SERT inhibition with dapoxetine significantly increased stopwatch-measured intravaginal ejaculatory latency time compared with placebo in men with premature ejaculation.

reason: Efficacy failure at Week 4 is extremely unlikely for a botulinum neurotoxin in glabellar lines, leaving incomplete endpoint specificity in a top-line press release as the primary scoring risk.
rationale: LAURITE 2 is the global Phase 3 double-blind and open-label repeat-dose companion study to LAURITE 1 evaluating Corabotase (IPN10200) in moderate-to-severe glabellar lines. Both North American composite and EU/ROW Week 4 primary endpoints have near-100% power given typical ~65-percentage-point treatment effects over ~1% placebo response. Because Corabotase is engineered for prolonged duration, ILA response through Week 24 also has high likelihood of success. Status is already active, not recruiting with December 2026 primary completion, though full open-label completion in October 2028 delays registry results posting and likely pushes regulatory submission past 2027.

assumptions.claim: In SAKURA 1 and SAKURA 2, placebo Week 4 composite >=2-grade glabellar line responder rates were 0.0% and 1.0% while daxibotulinumtoxinA achieved 73.6% and 74.0%.

reason: High placebo CLASI-A improvement on stable background lupus therapy with 35 patients per arm could narrow separation despite active TYK2 inhibition.
rationale: ICP-488 is InnoCare's selective allosteric TYK2 JH2 inhibitor, clinically active in psoriasis and targeting the Type I interferon/IL-12/IL-23 pathways central to DLE and SCLE. Allosteric TYK2 inhibition was strongly validated in PAISLEY CLE (NCT03920267), where deucravacitinib reduced Week 16 CLASI-A by ~48-50% vs ~17% on placebo in an almost identical biopsy-proven CLE population (CLASI-A >=8). Testing two active doses (N=35 per arm) improves the probability at least one dose meets Week 16 superiority, though enrolling 105 biopsy-proven patients across China may modestly delay the March 2027 primary completion.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 PAISLEY CLE trial (NCT03920267), oral allosteric TYK2 inhibition with deucravacitinib met its primary endpoint of percent change from baseline in CLASI-A at week 16 versus placebo.

reason: Still enrolling by invitation across only two US sites in late October 2026 for a 16-week primary endpoint makes slipping past March 2027 moderately likely, with results posting unlikely before December 2027 study completion.
rationale: Tarsus's Phase 2 KORE safety trial of lotilaner ophthalmic gel in ocular rosacea (N=155) lists only 2 US sites and remains enrolling by invitation on 2026-10-29 despite a 2026-12-31 registered primary completion date and a 16-week primary assessment window. Unless enrollment actually finished shortly before the snapshot without a status update, completing 16-week follow-up after 2027-03-31 (>90 days late) is nearly coin-flip likely. Because full study completion runs to 2027-12-31, ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by 2027-08-31 is very unlikely.

reason: Although rapid-recovery neuromuscular blockers easily beat cisatracurium on spontaneous TOFr >=0.9 recovery time, this small four-subgroup Phase 2 could report descriptive arm-level recovery times without formal pooled superiority testing.
rationale: Cisatracurium continuous infusion requires ~45-60 minutes for spontaneous recovery to TOFr >=0.9 after stopping infusion (longer under inhalational anesthesia than propofol TIVA). HengRui designed this completed 67-patient head-to-head Phase 2 specifically around spontaneous TOFr >=0.9 recovery time, strongly indicating HRS-9190 is a faster-recovering neuromuscular blocker where a 20-30 minute reduction yields high power even at N=34 vs 33. Because the trial completed in July 2026, HengRui has ample time to initiate Phase 3 by December 2027, though Phase 2 public disclosure typically awaits a conference abstract or journal article.

reason: With only 10 participants per arm and a stringent >=90% metagenomic Lactobacillus dominance cutoff, even a substantial biologic effect can easily miss two-sided p<0.05.
rationale: Measuring vaginal metagenomics at Day 16 immediately after a chlorhexidine pre-cleanse and 15 days of intravaginal FB301 during estrogen-supported mock FET favors high short-term Lactobacillus abundance relative to saline/placebo (~10% spontaneous conversion). However, achieving >=90% combined relative abundance by shotgun metagenomics is a strict threshold, and N=10 vs 10 requires roughly a 50-60 percentage-point gap for two-sided statistical significance. Biochemical pregnancy in N=10 per arm is severely underpowered, and a larger Phase 2 clinical pregnancy trial would precede any Phase 3.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2b LACTIN-V trial (NCT02766023), intravaginal live biotherapeutic Lactobacillus crispatus significantly increased vaginal Lactobacillus colonization and reduced bacterial vaginosis recurrence versus placebo.

reason: Oral oleoylethanolamide has an unproven link to gut bacterial histidine-to-imidazole propionate conversion, and healthy non-diabetic adults have low baseline imidazole propionate levels.
rationale: TRPTI (oleoylethanolamide, 300 mg/day) is a dietary lipid supplement acting mainly via intestinal PPAR-alpha/GPR119 signaling, whereas plasma imidazole propionate is generated by specific gut bacterial urocanate reductase activity predominantly elevated in type 2 diabetes. In 90 generally healthy non-diabetic volunteers over 8 weeks, low and skewed baseline imidazole propionate levels create a strong floor effect and low prior probability of significant reduction or HOMA-IR improvement. As a single-site Australian nutraceutical study, pharmaceutical Phase 3 development or drug marketing applications are virtually ruled out.

assumptions.claim: Imidazole propionate is a gut microbiota-produced histidine metabolite elevated in individuals with type 2 diabetes that impairs insulin signaling.

reason: With 61 total participants—potentially split across multiple HRS-1780 dose groups—office blood pressure variability could obscure a clinically meaningful antihypertensive effect.
rationale: HRS-1780 is HengRui/Suncadia's oral non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist tested in primary aldosteronism, a condition directly driven by autonomous aldosterone excess where MR blockade reliably lowers office SBP by ~10-12 mmHg beyond placebo at Week 8. With 61 patients already enrolled (active, not recruiting ahead of November 2026 primary completion), statistical power is ~70-85% depending on whether one or two active dose arms were randomized. Early completion gives HengRui over a year to register a Chinese Phase 3 trial before end of 2027.

reason: Because recruitment of all 102 participants had already finished by late October 2026 for a 20-week treatment period, the trial is very likely to complete on time without stopping or posting early results on ClinicalTrials.gov.
rationale: On 2026-10-29 the trial is already active, not recruiting with 102 T2DM participants across 2 Chinese sites and a 20-week treatment window. Even if the final participant entered in October 2026, 20-week follow-up ends by mid-March 2027, before the 2027-03-31 lateness threshold. Termination and substantive primary outcome amendments are rare in completed-enrollment insulin titration studies, while Hengrui rarely posts China-only Phase 2 results on ClinicalTrials.gov within 6 months of completion.

reason: Because tafolecimab is an approved PCSK9 antibody with overwhelming statistical power for week-12 LDL-C reduction, the main risk to scoring met is a brief corporate update calling the trial positive without explicitly stating the primary endpoint result.
rationale: IBI306 (tafolecimab) is an NMPA-approved anti-PCSK9 monoclonal antibody that reduced LDL-C by ~57-65% versus placebo in prior Phase 3 CREDIT trials. As monotherapy in low-to-moderate risk hypercholesterolemia (N=198, week 12), PCSK9 antibodies reliably yield ~55% placebo-adjusted LDL-C reductions with ~16.5% inter-patient SD, giving >99% statistical power for both the primary endpoint and the <2.6 mmol/L responder secondary. Enrollment is complete and primary completion passed in September 2026, supporting a high likelihood of a Chinese sNDA filing in 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 CREDIT-1 trial in Chinese patients with non-familial hypercholesterolemia, tafolecimab (IBI306) reduced LDL-C by more than 55% relative to placebo at week 12.
In the MENDEL-2 Phase 3 monotherapy trial in hypercholesterolemia, PCSK9 antibody therapy reduced week-12 LDL-C by approximately 55-57% versus placebo.

reason: With enrollment of 438 US participants already completed by late October 2026 and only a 12-week primary follow-up, primary completion should occur on schedule in December 2026 or January 2027.
rationale: Regeneron's ASCEND-QW Phase 2 study of weekly alirocumab is already active, not recruiting as of 2026-10-29 across 34 US sites with a 12-week primary outcome window. Even the latest enrolled participants should finish Week 12 by January 2027, well ahead of the 2027-03-29 lateness cutoff. Regeneron maintains timely ClinicalTrials.gov status updates, rarely amends or terminates completed-enrollment lipid studies, and typically posts results closer to the 12-month FDAAA deadline rather than within 6 months of February 2027 study completion.

reason: Listing nine distinct fMRI, behavioral, and self-report primary outcomes in a single-dose N=24 crossover study creates a high bar under co-primary rules and high likelihood of exploratory biomarker reporting without formal primary significance.
rationale: SYT-510 is a selective endocannabinoid reuptake inhibitor tested as a single acute dose in a 24-patient GAD experimental medicine crossover at one UK site. Nine co-listed primary fMRI and behavioral outcomes make meeting all co-primaries nearly impossible if tested jointly, and even if one fMRI measure is primary in the protocol, single-dose endocannabinoid modulation in N=24 has modest power and private biotechs often issue qualitative biomarker press releases. Even if positive, a multi-week Phase 2b trial rather than Phase 3 would follow.
evidence: Schmidt et al. JNJ-42165279 SAD trial (2021)

assumptions.claim: In a randomized Phase 2b trial in social anxiety disorder, the endocannabinoid degradation inhibitor JNJ-42165279 did not meet its primary efficacy endpoint versus placebo.
assumptions.source: Schmidt et al. JNJ-42165279 SAD trial (2021)

reason: Enrolling 120 symptomatic premenopausal women with bacterial vaginosis under strict contraception, menses-timed dosing, and sexual abstinence rules across just two German sites carries substantial risk of recruitment extending past June 2027.
rationale: As of 2026-10-29 this 4-arm open-label microbiome trial (N=120) is still recruiting across only 2 German sites. Eligibility requires acute symptomatic BV with Nugent score >=7, stable contraception, regular cycles, and sexual abstinence through primary evaluation, which frequently slows enrollment beyond initial projections. Consequently, slipping >90 days past the March 2027 primary completion target is roughly even-money, while ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 2027 is very unlikely.

reason: Initiating an oral RSV replication inhibitor up to 72 hours after symptom onset typically produces modest acceleration of complete clinical sign resolution relative to the ~1.43 hazard ratio needed for significance in 150 children.
rationale: Zelicapavir (EDP-938) lowers RSV viral load in challenge and clinical studies but missed symptom endpoints in the adult RSVP Phase 2b trial, reflecting the narrow therapeutic window once RSV airway inflammation is established within 72 hours of onset. In 150 young children (~120 complete-resolution events by Day 14, placebo median ~8.5 days), two-sided p<0.05 requires an observed HR near 1.43 versus an expected HR around 1.18. If Thai sites miss completing enrollment before the rainy-season RSV wave ends in late 2026, completion will slip into 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2b RSVP study in otherwise healthy adults with acute RSV infection, zelicapavir (EDP-938) failed to meet its primary total symptom score endpoint.
In the Phase 3 AIRFLO trial in infants and young children hospitalized with RSV, oral ziresovir improved clinical bronchiolitis scores more than placebo at 48 hours.

reason: Although TL1A blockade downregulates Th1 and Th17 pathways relevant to psoriatic arthritis, tulisokibart lacks prior clinical proof-of-concept in joint disease and ~35-47 patients per arm requires a ~20-point ACR20 gain.
rationale: Tulisokibart (MK-7240) demonstrated robust efficacy in ulcerative colitis (ARTEMIS-UC) and targets TL1A upstream of IL-17 and TNF, giving solid mechanistic rationale in PsA, though clinical magnitude in peripheral arthritis is unproven. Assuming ~24% placebo Week-16 ACR20 in a mixed bDMARD-naive/IR cohort and ~44% on top-dose tulisokibart across multiple dose arms (N=140 total), power is moderate (~56%). Because status flipped to active, not recruiting by 2026-10-29 with a 16-week endpoint matching 2027-02-17 completion, on-time completion and EULAR/ACR 2027 disclosure are likely.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 ARTEMIS-UC trial in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis, tulisokibart achieved significantly higher week-12 clinical remission than placebo (26% vs 1%).
In the Phase 3 BE OPTIMAL trial in psoriatic arthritis, the week-16 ACR20 response rate in the placebo group was approximately 24%.

reason: Treat-to-target oral HIF-PHI titration reliably achieves hemoglobin non-inferiority versus ESA, leaving vague topline press-release wording without explicit primary endpoint confirmation as the main scoring risk.
rationale: Oral HIF-PHIs titrated to maintain Hb 10.0-12.0 g/dL consistently meet non-inferiority against ESA in NDD-CKD Phase 3 trials (roxadustat, daprodustat, vadadustat). With N=240 and inter-patient Hb SD ~1.05 g/dL, the 95% CI half-width (~0.27 g/dL) easily clears standard -0.75 or -1.0 g/dL margins. However, key secondary resolution requires statistical superiority over active ESA on Hb response, which is unlikely when both arms titrate to the same target. Because the record still lists recruiting on 2026-10-29 for a 27-week endpoint, completion will likely slip past March 2027.
evidence: Chen et al. Roxadustat NDD-CKD China (2019)

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 ASCEND-ND trial in non-dialysis CKD anemia, daprodustat met non-inferiority compared with darbepoetin alfa for mean hemoglobin maintenance.
In the Phase 3 PRO2TECT trials in non-dialysis CKD anemia, vadadustat met its primary hematologic non-inferiority endpoint versus darbepoetin alfa.

reason: Large placebo office systolic blood pressure drops from regression to the mean and improved background adherence frequently compress treatment differences in uncontrolled and resistant hypertension trials.
rationale: The trial's design—3 oral doses versus placebo over 12 weeks in uncontrolled/resistant hypertension on >=2 drugs including a diuretic, excluding eGFR <45 and serum K+ >=5.0 mmol/L—matches an aldosterone synthase inhibitor program akin to baxdrostat and lorundrostat. In Phase 2 resistant/uncontrolled HTN trials (BrigHTN, Target-HTN), top doses lower seated SBP by ~8-11 mmHg beyond placebo (~-8.5 mmHg placebo drop, SD ~14 mmHg), though large placebo responses occasionally dilute effects (HALO). With ~65 patients per arm and three active doses, power is solid (~68%).

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 BrigHTN trial in treatment-resistant hypertension, baxdrostat 2 mg reduced week-12 seated systolic blood pressure by 11.0 mmHg more than placebo.
In the Phase 2 HALO trial in uncontrolled hypertension, a 16.6 mmHg systolic blood pressure drop in the placebo group contributed to baxdrostat missing its primary endpoint.

reason: Because safety and PK measures are co-listed alongside two MRI-PDFF endpoints as primary outcomes in this Phase 2a study, the main risk is descriptive topline reporting that omits formal hypothesis-test statements on all efficacy primaries.
rationale: HU6 is a controlled metabolic accelerator that achieved ~33-36% relative MRI-PDFF liver fat reduction and >70% >=30%-responder rates in just 61 days in its prior MASLD Phase 2a trial. Extending treatment to 26 weeks in MASH (~45 patients per arm across 3 doses plus placebo) provides >99% power for a ~36 percentage-point placebo-adjusted relative MRI-PDFF reduction and the >=30% responder primary. Because the trial is still recruiting on 2026-10-29 with a 26-week primary window, primary completion will likely slip past May 2027, delaying readout to H2 2027.

assumptions.claim: In a 61-day randomized placebo-controlled Phase 2a trial in adults with elevated liver fat and high BMI, HU6 significantly reduced MRI-PDFF liver fat content compared with placebo.

reason: Higher gastrointestinal intolerance or thromboembolic discontinuations in the open-label oral HIF-PHI arm versus established ESA therapy could dilute treatment maintenance and narrow the non-inferiority cushion.
rationale: AND017 is an oral HIF-prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor tested against continued ESA maintenance in 300 Chinese dialysis-dependent CKD patients with baseline Hb 9.0-12.0 g/dL. Across the HIF-PHI class (roxadustat, daprodustat, vadadustat), Phase 3 active-controlled dialysis conversion trials consistently achieve non-inferiority on mean Hb (~10.5-11.0 g/dL) with near-zero between-arm differences and SD near 1.0 g/dL, giving high statistical power under standard -1.0 or -0.75 g/dL margins. Because the trial was still recruiting at snapshot with a single listed Chinese site, public readout by June 2027 is uncertain, and superiority on secondary responder rate is unlikely.
evidence: Chen et al. NEJM 2019 (roxadustat China DD-CKD)

assumptions.claim: Oral HIF-PHI maintenance therapy in Chinese dialysis-dependent CKD patients achieved non-inferior hemoglobin maintenance versus epoetin alfa with mean Hb near 10.5-11.0 g/dL.
In ASCEND-D, daprodustat vs ESA in dialysis patients showed a tiny mean hemoglobin difference within standard non-inferiority margins.

reason: Avian H5 hemagglutination inhibition assays can exhibit lower sensitivity and higher assay variability than microneutralization, risking a miss against strict CBER lower-bound seroprotection thresholds despite robust neutralizing immunity.
rationale: Moderna's mRNA-1018-H5 Phase 3 trial (N=4,050, already active not recruiting with primary completion January 2027) evaluates Day 43 HAI seroprotection (>=1:40) and seroconversion after two doses. H5-naive placebo recipients rarely have baseline/Day 43 HAI >=1:40 (<2%), whereas two-dose mRNA H5 vaccination elicited strong HAI and microneutralization responses in Phase 1/2 (NCT05972174). With >2,000 vaccinees, statistical precision is very high; the main risk is meeting fixed regulatory lower-bound CBER criteria across age strata on the H5 HAI assay rather than superiority over placebo.

assumptions.claim: Healthy adults without prior pandemic H5 vaccination have near-zero baseline seropositivity against avian H5N1 by HAI assay.

reason: More thorough preoperative CT/PET staging or surgeon localization under standard white-light/palpation in academic thoracic centers could lower the fraction of occult or unlocalized lesions below the threshold needed.
rationale: VISUALIZE-2 evaluates abenacianine (VGT-309), a cathepsin-activatable NIR fluorescent imaging agent, in ~115 evaluable lung cancer resection patients using an intrasubject clinically significant event (CSE) primary endpoint. Intraoperative optical imaging Phase 3 trials (such as pafolacianine ELUCIDATE in lung cancer, which met its CSE threshold with >25-50% event rates, and prior VGT-309 Phase 2 VISUALIZE data showing ~40% CSEs) typically test against a modest performance goal (~10-15%). Given the single perioperative infusion and same-day surgical endpoint, efficacy success is likely once recruitment finishes across the 9 sites.

assumptions.claim: Intraoperative NIR fluorescence imaging with pafolacianine in lung cancer surgery (ELUCIDATE) demonstrated clinically significant events well above pre-specified Phase 3 thresholds.

reason: Measuring glycemic superiority at Week 26—fourteen weeks after stopping a 12-week icovamenib course—in only 64 total participants leaves low statistical power against typical HbA1c drift and variability.
rationale: Biomea Fusion's icovamenib (BMF-219), an oral covalent menin inhibitor intended to restore beta-cell mass/function, is dosed 100 mg daily for 12 weeks with primary HbA1c change assessed off-treatment at Week 26 in 64 T2D patients (BMI <=32). While earlier COVALENT-111 cohorts suggested durable glycemic reductions mainly in insulin-deficient T2D subgroups, overall placebo-adjusted HbA1c effects across broader T2D were modest. With ~32 patients per arm and 26-week HbA1c SD near 0.95%, a ~0.48% durable off-drug difference is needed for significance. Enrollment is already complete (active, not recruiting), supporting timely mid-2027 readout.

assumptions.claim: COVALENT-111 evaluated oral icovamenib (BMF-219) short-course dosing with off-treatment glycemic follow-up in adults with type 2 diabetes.

reason: Frequent instillation of ophthalmic vehicle drops produces substantial corneal surface lubrication and regression to the mean on NEI fluorescein staining, often masking modest Phase 2 active drug effects.
rationale: Dompe's Phase 2 trial randomizes 417 US dry eye disease patients (SANDE >=30, Schirmer <10 mm, total NEI CFS >=4) to DFL24498 0.08% ophthalmic solution or vehicle for 12 weeks. Although sample size (~208/arm) provides ~80% power to detect a ~0.65-point difference on the 0-15 NEI CFS scale (SD ~2.4), exploratory Phase 2 DED trials historically face large vehicle healing responses (~1.8-2.2 points) and low single-trial hit rates (~35-40%), with even lower odds of simultaneously achieving formal significance on SANDE symptom scores.

reason: Satisfying both pharmacokinetic Cmax comparability and high molecular CR non-inferiority bounds in 150 APL patients leaves vulnerability to PK Cmax divergence between oral capsules and IV infusion or random early induction dropouts.
rationale: QUATRO-APL compares oral arsenic trioxide (QTX-2101) + ATRA against standard IV ATO + ATRA in 150 newly diagnosed low/intermediate-risk APL patients on co-primary AsIII Cmax PK and post-consolidation molecular CR rate. Chemo-free ATO + ATRA achieves ~97-100% CR/molecular CR, and oral arsenic regimens in APL have matched IV ATO efficacy in prior randomized studies; however, meeting strict Cmax bounds alongside mCR non-inferiority carries moderate technical risk. Furthermore, recruiting 150 rare APL patients starting June 2026 and completing ~7.5 months of induction plus 3 consolidation cycles makes completion by mid-2027 unlikely.

assumptions.claim: ATRA plus IV arsenic trioxide achieved complete remission rates near 97-100% in newly diagnosed low-to-intermediate-risk APL in APL0406.
Oral arsenic plus ATRA demonstrated non-inferior complete remission and molecular remission outcomes compared with IV arsenic trioxide plus ATRA in APL.

reason: Liver-selective THR-beta agonists reliably reduce hepatic steatosis on MRI-PDFF but historically exert minimal systemic body-weight loss, making co-primary incremental weight reduction over active semaglutide in 11 weeks unlikely.
rationale: Eccogene's Phase 2a MIST trial adds oral THR-beta agonist ECC4703 or placebo to background semaglutide from Week 9 to Week 20 in 151 obese adults, registering five primary outcomes spanning body weight (% change and >=5% responders) and substudy MRI-PDFF liver fat. Selective THR-beta agonists (e.g., resmetirom) strongly lower MRI-PDFF liver fat by 35-50% yet are largely weight-neutral in humans. Achieving statistically significant superiority on incremental body-weight loss and >=5% responder rate over ongoing semaglutide weight loss (~5% over 11 weeks) alongside all registered co-primaries has low probability despite likely positive liver-fat effects.

assumptions.claim: In MAESTRO-NASH, selective THR-beta agonism with resmetirom markedly reduced liver fat by MRI-PDFF without producing clinically meaningful body-weight loss versus placebo.

reason: Although hepatic ASO knockdown of plasma AGT is robust, the sequential Part A-to-Part B structure could delay or modify Part B reporting, or acute post-discharge renin-angiotensin shifts could inflate AGT variability.
rationale: KARDINAL-ASH evaluates tonlamarsen (IONIS-AGT-LRx, a GalNAc-conjugated antisense oligonucleotide targeting hepatic angiotensinogen) in recently hospitalized acute severe hypertension patients. Part B's primary efficacy endpoint is a pharmacodynamic biomarker: percent change in plasma AGT at Week 4. Prior Phase 2 trials of IONIS-AGT-LRx consistently demonstrated ~55-70% reductions in plasma AGT versus near-zero placebo change, providing >95% statistical power even in a modest Part B sample. In contrast, Week 4 home SBP (key secondary) faces high post-discharge medication variability. Sequential Part A/B execution across 13 sites makes >90-day registry delay likely.
evidence: Mullick et al. / Bakris et al. IONIS-AGT-LRx Phase 2 2021 (NCT04083222)

assumptions.claim: IONIS-AGT-LRx (tonlamarsen) produced robust >50% reductions in plasma angiotensinogen compared with placebo in Phase 2 hypertension trials.

reason: Novel non-opioid oral analgesic mechanisms frequently exhibit insufficient acute analgesic magnitude or delayed onset after bony third-molar extraction compared with established inflammatory pain pathways.
rationale: Eli Lilly's Phase 2 single-dose dental impaction pain study tests multiple doses of LY4515100 against placebo in 212 participants at a specialized clinical research unit. Bilateral impacted mandibular third-molar extraction offers high assay sensitivity and low placebo noise over 24 hours, and testing multiple doses improves the chance that at least one dose meets superiority. However, unvalidated early-phase non-opioid analgesic candidates historically clear acute dental pain proof-of-concept less than half the time. Lilly rarely press-releases Phase 2 pain trials early unless advancing, relying largely on registry results posting.

reason: Selective peripheral P2X3 antagonism may inadequately block multifactorial visceral hypersensitivity in IBS-D and IBS-M against the large placebo pain reductions typical of Rome IV diary trials.
rationale: GSK's Phase 2b BALANCE trial evaluates camlipixant (a selective P2X3 antagonist proven effective in refractory chronic cough) across multiple doses versus placebo in 420 adults with Rome IV IBS-D or IBS-M on weekly abdominal pain intensity (0-10 NRS) over Weeks 7-12. Although ATP-gated P2X3 signaling contributes to gut nociception in preclinical models, translational success of novel visceral analgesics in mixed IBS cohorts is modest (~30-40%) due to ~1.8-point placebo pain drops and patient heterogeneity. Strict run-in diary criteria typically drive high screen-failure rates, creating substantial risk of >90-day enrollment delay.

assumptions.claim: Camlipixant (BLU-5937) demonstrated favorable tolerability and low adverse-event discontinuation rates near placebo in Phase 2b testing.

reason: With only 18 participants per arm and strict complete symptom resolution (VSS=0) potentially required across multiple visits, statistical power is modest even if topical occidiofungin has meaningful antifungal activity.
rationale: Occidiofungin (OCF001) has fungicidal activity against Candida species, and 7-day intravaginal dosing directly targets localized acute VVC. However, strict clinical cure (VSS=0) immediately post-treatment at Day 8 is demanding because mucosal erythema and irritation often lag mycological clearance, while placebo gel still yields ~20% resolution. With N=36 (18 per arm) at a single site and ambiguity across Day 4, 8, and 25 assessments in the primary outcome, only a large treatment effect (>35 percentage points) reaches significance.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 VANISH 303 trial in acute vulvovaginal candidiasis, complete clinical cure (VSS=0) at the test-of-cure visit occurred in roughly one-quarter of placebo-treated patients versus half of ibrexafungerp-treated patients.

reason: Tirzepatide produces ~15% mean body weight reduction and ~90% 5%-responder rates in Chinese adults with obesity, making statistical superiority extremely difficult unless a pre-specified non-inferiority margin applies.
rationale: HDM1005 is a dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist tested open-label across three weekly doses against tirzepatide in Chinese adults with non-diabetic obesity. In SURMOUNT-CN, tirzepatide achieved ~14-18% weight loss and >85% >=5% responders. Beating tirzepatide on superiority at Week 40 with 93 patients per arm is unlikely; `p_met` mainly reflects the modest chance that HDM1005 high dose modestly outperforms tirzepatide or that the protocol pre-specifies non-inferiority. Comparable efficacy could still prompt Huadong to advance HDM1005 into Phase 3.

assumptions.claim: In the SURMOUNT-CN Phase 3 trial in Chinese adults with obesity or overweight, weekly tirzepatide 10 mg and 15 mg produced mean body weight reductions exceeding 13% at Week 52, with over 85% of tirzepatide-treated participants achieving at least 5% weight loss.

reason: Selective muscarinic M4 positive allosteric modulation lacks proven clinical efficacy in acute schizophrenia following the Phase 2 failures of emraclidine, and 50 patients per arm offers limited power against inpatient placebo improvement.
rationale: NS-136 is an oral muscarinic M4 positive allosteric modulator evaluated at 80 mg and 120 mg QD versus placebo over 5 weeks in acute schizophrenia (N=150). While direct M1/M4 agonism (xanomeline-trospium) succeeded in EMERGENT trials, selective M4 PAM monotherapy (emraclidine) failed both EMPOWER Phase 2 trials to separate from placebo on PANSS total score. Controlled inpatient execution in China may curb placebo drift, leaving a ~30% chance that at least one NS-136 dose achieves significant PANSS improvement.

assumptions.claim: Both EMPOWER-1 and EMPOWER-2 Phase 2 trials of the selective muscarinic M4 positive allosteric modulator emraclidine failed to meet their primary endpoint of statistically significant PANSS total score reduction versus placebo at Week 6 in acute schizophrenia.

reason: Although apraclonidine 0.125% will reliably blanch ocular redness at 15 minutes, meeting both co-primary endpoints requires maintaining statistically significant vasoconstriction 14 hours (840 minutes) after a single drop.
rationale: Apraclonidine 0.125% is a potent alpha-2/weak alpha-1 adrenergic vasoconstrictor; at 15 minutes post-instillation (N=230), large superiority over vehicle (~-0.95 Ora Calibra units) is virtually assured. However, the trial specifies a second primary outcome at 840 minutes (14 hours) post-dose on Day 2, beyond the 8-hour benchmark of brimonidine 0.025% (Lumify). Waning vasoconstriction at 14 hours creates moderate failure risk on the co-primary durability hurdle despite strong sample power.
evidence: McLaurin et al., Eye & Contact Lens (2018)

assumptions.claim: Low-dose brimonidine tartrate 0.025% ophthalmic solution demonstrated statistically significant reductions in investigator-assessed ocular redness versus vehicle from 5 minutes through 8 hours post-instillation on the Ora Calibra scale.
assumptions.source: McLaurin et al., Eye & Contact Lens (2018)

reason: Frequent rescue analgesia use in the placebo group after abdominal surgery can compress SPID24 differences if HSK55718 has modest analgesic potency or short duration.
rationale: This double-blind, placebo- and morphine-controlled Phase 2 trial tests three parenteral doses of HSK55718 in acute post-abdominal surgery pain (NRS >=4, N=200 across five arms). Hospitalized postoperative SPID24 trials have well-established assay sensitivity, low dropout over 24 hours, and three chances across dose levels to beat placebo. The main risk is analgesic ceiling or rescue-medication dilution with N=40 per arm. Haisco historically advances successful acute-care Phase 2 candidates rapidly into Chinese Phase 3 trials.

reason: With only 25 participants per arm and volatile Week 12 placebo response rates (~25-35%) in hidradenitis suppurativa, achieving two-sided p<0.05 requires an unusually large treatment delta exceeding typical biologic benchmarks.
rationale: LAD328 is tested in a 50-patient proof-of-concept HS trial using Week 12 IHS4-55. Even validated HS biologics (adalimumab, secukinumab, bimekizumab) typically separate from placebo by 15-25 percentage points against background topical antiseptics and fluctuating lesion counts (~25-35% placebo response). At N=25 per group, two-sided p<0.05 demands ~30+ percentage points separation, leaving low statistical power unless LAD328 is exceptionally active or evaluated at a relaxed Phase 2 alpha.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 SUNSHINE and SUNRISE trials in moderate-to-severe hidradenitis suppurativa, Week 16 placebo HiSCR50 response rates were approximately 31% to 34%.

reason: Retrospectively identified pharmacogenetic responder subgroups in dry eye disease frequently exhibit regression toward the mean on subjective discomfort endpoints when tested prospectively against an active lubricating vehicle.
rationale: PREDICT-1 prospectively tests topical anti-TNFa fragment licaminlimab on Day 29 ocular discomfort in DED patients carrying the TNFR1 genotype associated with enhanced response in prior Phase 2b studies. Although precision biomarker enrichment strengthens biological plausibility, DED symptom trials remain plagued by large vehicle effects despite artificial-tear run-in, and the primary genotype subset within N=160 may limit power if non-carriers are co-enrolled. Because enrollment is already complete with a 29-day endpoint, Q1 2027 topline disclosure is highly likely.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2b RELIEF trial of topical licaminlimab in dry eye disease, Oculis identified a specific TNFR1 genotype subgroup showing greater symptom improvement versus vehicle than the overall study population.

reason: With only 10 placebo patients and 20 patients in the primary FXS5626 arm, statistical significance requires a dramatic ~40 percentage point reduction in post-steroid-taper treatment failure.
rationale: Using the VISUAL-I / NEPTUNE steroid-taper design in active non-anterior NIU, roughly 70-80% of placebo patients meet multi-component treatment failure criteria between Weeks 6 and 24. Potent oral targeted immunomodulators or biologics can cut failure rates by 35-45 percentage points, which is barely sufficient to reach p<0.05 with 20 versus 10 patients. Because the trial was still recruiting in late October 2026 with a 24-week endpoint and February 2027 target date, substantial completion delay is expected.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 3 VISUAL I trial in active non-infectious intermediate, posterior, or panuveitis, the majority of placebo-treated patients experienced treatment failure following corticosteroid taper.

reason: Complex eligibility criteria requiring vascular perfusion testing, caregiver attendance, and same-day external specialist consensus review make recruitment delays past the five-month window highly likely.
rationale: Enrolling 24 ambulatory patients with Wagner Grade 1 mildly infected diabetic foot ulcers, confirmed vascular perfusion, a participating caregiver, and external specialist consensus review across six US sites rarely completes within five months (August 2026 to January 2027). Small private sponsor Lakewood-Amedex has historically experienced slow trial timelines, and boilerplate errors in the registry text suggest potential future record cleanup or amendments, with low likelihood of ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 2027.

reason: Frequent thrice-daily vehicle lubrication and regression from mandatory Grade 3 baseline staining produce substantial control-arm improvement in Stage 1 neurotrophic keratitis, while Lacripep showed modest staining effects in prior ocular surface studies.
rationale: Lacripep (synthetic lacritin peptide) is tested against TID vehicle over 8 weeks in 54 patients with Stage 1 NK starting at maximum Grade 3 central corneal fluorescein staining despite a 2-week vehicle run-in. Central reading improves precision, but regression from ceiling baseline plus continuous lubrication typically reduces vehicle staining by ~0.9 NEI points, and N=27 per arm requires ~0.5 points incremental reduction. Restoring Cochet-Bonnet corneal sensitivity within 8 weeks is even harder than improving epithelial staining.

assumptions.claim: In pivotal trials of cenegermin in Stage 2 and 3 neurotrophic keratitis, statistically significant improvement in Cochet-Bonnet corneal sensitivity over vehicle at Week 8 was not consistently achieved despite robust epithelial healing.

reason: With only 45 participants and multiple primary endpoints assessed just 30 days after a 15-day intravaginal course, the trial lacks statistical power to show both cytologic regression and hr-HPV clearance over spontaneous resolution.
rationale: This single-site proof-of-concept trial enrolls only 45 women (23 vs 22) and lists both cervical cytology regression to NILM and hr-HPV clearance at Day 50 alongside safety as primary outcomes. Under round rules, all co-primary efficacy endpoints must be statistically significant. Over 50 days, spontaneous ASC-US/LSIL cytologic regression is roughly 25-30% with notable sampling variability, while full viral clearance after 15 days of topical EGCG and quinine sulfate is biologically challenging. Detecting two binary differences at p<0.05 with ~22 patients per arm requires implausibly large treatment effects (>35-40 percentage points).

assumptions.claim: Previous clinical trials of green tea catechin (EGCG/Polyphenon E) ointments or oral capsules in cervical HPV lesions showed variable efficacy over 8 to 16 weeks rather than a 15-day regimen.
Short-term spontaneous regression or cytologic normalization of ASC-US and LSIL in placebo arms of topical cervical dysplasia trials typically ranges from 20% to 35%.

reason: Established pathological scars that have shown no spontaneous regression for 6 months are densely fibrotic and rarely remodel enough within 12 weeks of anti-IL-11 therapy in a 30-patient trial to achieve statistical superiority.
rationale: 9MW3811 is a humanized anti-IL-11 monoclonal antibody targeting profibrotic signaling, evaluated here in a 30-patient single-site Phase 2 safety, PK, and preliminary efficacy trial in China. Enrolled patients have mature pathological scars (mVSS >=9, stable >=6 months), where existing collagen cross-linking resists rapid reversal over 12 weeks without physical debulking. Furthermore, a 30-patient exploratory study (potentially split across dose cohorts) is underpowered for formal statistical testing on mVSS unless the clinical effect is unusually large, and safety/PK readouts may be reported descriptively without formal p-values.

assumptions.claim: 9MW3811 is an anti-IL-11 monoclonal antibody previously evaluated in Phase 1 healthy volunteer safety and pharmacokinetic studies.

reason: While apraclonidine 0.125% reliably blanches conjunctival vessels at 15 minutes, meeting the co-primary endpoint at 600 minutes (10 hours) post-instillation risks waning vasoconstrictor duration at this diluted concentration.
rationale: Apraclonidine is an established ophthalmic alpha-2 (with weak alpha-1) adrenergic agonist with potent conjunctival vasoconstrictor activity. At 15 minutes on Day 1, 0.125% apraclonidine will easily outperform vehicle by roughly 1.0 point on the 0-4 Ora Calibra scale (similar to low-dose brimonidine 0.025% trials). The main hurdle is the co-primary outcome at 600 minutes (10 hours) post-dose; however, apraclonidine has a relatively long ocular half-life (~8 hours) and polar retention on the ocular surface, and 89 subjects per arm provide strong power to detect even a 0.3-unit residual benefit at 10 hours.

assumptions.claim: In Phase 3 ocular redness trials using the 0-4 Ora Calibra scale (such as brimonidine 0.025%), vehicle mean change at 15 minutes is small (around -0.2 to -0.3 units) while selective alpha-2 agonists achieve -1.2 to -1.5 units.

reason: Three ultrasound-guided intra-articular placebo injections generate a large and variable analgesic response in knee osteoarthritis, making superiority on both WOMAC Pain and WOMAC Function at 3 months difficult to achieve.
rationale: Intra-articular biological and cell therapies for primary knee osteoarthritis have a very low Phase 2b/3 success rate (<20%). Administering three ultrasound-guided intra-articular injections (Days 0, 14, 28) induces substantial joint-lavage and contextual placebo analgesia, typically lowering WOMAC Pain by 25-40% (~11-15 points on a 0-50 scale) with high inter-patient standard deviation (~10-12 points). In addition, meeting both WOMAC Pain and WOMAC Function co-primary endpoints at 3 months raises the statistical hurdle, and macrophage reprogramming by allogeneic apoptotic cells (Allocetra) remains unproven in randomized degenerative joint trials.

assumptions.claim: Intra-articular saline placebo injections in randomized knee osteoarthritis trials consistently produce clinically meaningful improvements in WOMAC pain and function scores at 3 months.

reason: Although GalNAc-siRNA knockdown of apoC-III yields large triglyceride reductions, splitting 40 participants across multiple dose cohorts could reduce per-arm sample size if high fasting triglyceride variability occurs.
rationale: RBD5044 is a liver-targeted GalNAc-siRNA against APOC3 dosed subcutaneously on Day 1 and Day 84, closely mirroring plozasiran (ARO-APOC3). Across Phase 2 trials of APOC3 RNAi agents (plozasiran in MUIR and SHASTA-2; olezarsen in Bridge-TIMI 73a), quarterly subcutaneous dosing consistently reduces apoC-III by >70% and fasting triglycerides by 50-65% relative to placebo. Even with 40 total participants split across active doses and placebo, a ~53 percentage-point TG reduction against ~28% SD provides very high statistical power. Conversely, APOC3 inhibition minimally lowers or slightly raises LDL-C, keeping key secondary success low.

assumptions.claim: Quarterly subcutaneous GalNAc-siRNA targeting APOC3 (plozasiran) reduced fasting triglycerides by roughly 50% to 62% placebo-adjusted at week 16 to 24 in patients with moderate hypertriglyceridemia (TG 150-499 mg/dL) in the MUIR trial.
RBD5044 is an APOC3-targeting GalNAc-siRNA previously tested for safety, pharmacokinetics, and lipid lowering in Phase 1 clinical development.

reason: Moisturizing vehicle gel effects and regression to the mean over 4 weeks in mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis can narrow the EASI difference if baseline disease severity is low.
rationale: VC005 is a selective JAK1 inhibitor developed by Jiangsu Vcare (already active orally in inflammatory diseases) formulated here as a topical gel for mild-to-moderate adult atopic dermatitis. Topical JAK inhibitors (such as ruxolitinib cream, delgocitinib ointment, and ivarmacitinib ointment) have a strong track record in Phase 2/3 AD trials, showing rapid anti-inflammatory and antipruritic onset within 2-4 weeks. With 120 participants (even if divided across two concentrations vs vehicle) and a 4-week EASI endpoint, at least one VC005 gel dose has a high probability of statistically beating vehicle.

assumptions.claim: Topical JAK inhibitors such as ruxolitinib cream demonstrated statistically significant reductions in EASI score compared with vehicle by Week 4 in adult mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis.

reason: High week-to-week seizure diary variability, small Part 2 sample size, and CNS/cardiac dose-limiting tolerability constraints of KCNT1 channel blockade make statistical superiority over 12 weeks challenging.
rationale: ABS-1230 directly targets gain-of-function KCNT1 potassium channel mutations driving severe pediatric epilepsies (such as EIMFS), giving clear genetic target validation. However, KCNT1-related epilepsy is ultra-rare and highly treatment-refractory with severe structural/network encephalopathy, high seizure frequency variance, and historical CNS/cardiac safety hurdles for KCNT1 blockers (e.g., quinidine and earlier small-molecule programs). Furthermore, enrolling 61 pediatric/young adult patients across Part 1 and Part 2 at two US sites between May 2026 and January 2027 is operationally unrealistic, making substantial completion delays very likely.

assumptions.claim: Prior pharmacological attempts to inhibit gain-of-function KCNT1 channels in KCNT1-related epilepsy (such as quinidine) were limited by narrow therapeutic windows and variable seizure responses.

reason: If public disclosure occurs only via abbreviated summary without reporting formal statistical tests on both Gingival Index and Plaque Index co-primaries, technical resolution could fail despite strong clinical efficacy.
rationale: Standardized 6-month single-site, single-examiner triple-blind Colgate clinical trials comparing stabilized stannous fluoride dentifrices (SNaP Total formulation) against Colgate Great Regular Flavor (sodium monofluorophosphate without specific antibacterial actives) have an exceptionally high historical success rate (>90%). In subjects with established gingivitis (GI >=1.0) and plaque (PI >=1.5), stannous fluoride consistently delivers 20-30% reductions (~0.25-0.40 Loe-Silness points) over negative-control fluoride paste with very tight examiner variance (SD ~0.12-0.18), giving N=85 near-certain statistical power on both GI and plaque co-primaries. The trial is already active, not recruiting, on track for November 2026 completion.

assumptions.claim: In 6-month randomized double-blind clinical trials, stabilized stannous fluoride toothpastes consistently produce statistically significant ~20-30% reductions in Loe-Silness Gingival Index and Turesky-modified Quigley-Hein Plaque Index compared with regular monofluorophosphate fluoride toothpaste.

reason: Non-adherence to double-dummy oral regimens could slightly dilute treatment differences, although obicetrapib's substantially greater LDL-C lowering over bempedoic acid leaves wide statistical margin.
rationale: Obicetrapib 10 mg (CETP inhibitor) reliably lowers LDL-C by ~32-37% at Day 84 on top of maximally tolerated statins (BROADWAY, BROOKLYN, ROSE2), whereas bempedoic acid 180 mg lowers LDL-C by only ~15-18% on background statins (CLEAR Harmony, CLEAR Wisdom) because ATP citrate lyase inhibition acts in the same hepatic synthesis pathway as statins. With 213 patients per arm and an expected ~17 percentage-point treatment difference (SD ~24%), statistical power exceeds 99% for both primary LDL-C and key secondary non-HDL-C superiority.

assumptions.claim: Bempedoic acid 180 mg added to maximally tolerated statin therapy lowered LDL-C from baseline by approximately 16.5% at Week 12 in CLEAR Harmony.
Obicetrapib 10 mg added to maximally tolerated lipid-lowering therapy lowered LDL-C by more than 30% at 84 days in Phase 2/3 trials including ROSE2 and BROADWAY.

reason: This 18-site GSK 8-week crossover safety study in stable adult asthma uses straightforward inclusion criteria and should complete close to schedule with routine ClinicalTrials.gov results posting.
rationale: GSK is conducting an 18-site, 4-country Phase 3 crossover safety trial enrolling 110 adults with stable asthma across broad background therapies to support switching MDI propellants from HFA-134a to low-global-warming HFA-152a. Broad asthma eligibility and short 8-week follow-up make severe delays (>90 days past February 2027) or early termination unlikely. GSK has high compliance with ClinicalTrials.gov results reporting, giving a solid chance of posting even within six months of completion by August 2027.

reason: As a non-triptan TRPM8 antagonist, elismetrep may yield a modest single-attack treatment effect insufficient to clear both 2-hour pain freedom and MBS freedom co-primary endpoints.
rationale: Large US multicenter Phase 3 acute migraine trial (N=1800 across 113 sites) provides strong statistical power (~90% for a 7-8 percentage point difference) on standard FDA co-primary endpoints of 2-hour pain freedom and MBS freedom. Modern oral acute migraine trials (gepants, ditans) consistently show 16-21% placebo 2-hour pain freedom and 7-13 percentage point active gains. While Phase 3 advancement indicates positive Phase 2 proof-of-concept for TRPM8 inhibition, novel non-CGRP acute migraine mechanisms carry moderate efficacy risk and high placebo response sensitivity.

assumptions.claim: In Phase 3 acute migraine trials of oral non-triptan agents such as rimegepant and ubrogepant, placebo 2-hour pain freedom rates typically range between 11% and 21%.
FDA acute migraine registrational trials require statistically significant superiority on both 2-hour pain freedom and 2-hour freedom from most bothersome symptom.

reason: Patient self-administration via a dry powder inhaler during an acute migraine attack can cause variable pulmonary drug delivery and attenuate 2-hour pain-free rates.
rationale: Dihydroergotamine (DHE) has well-established antimigraine efficacy when systemic therapeutic concentrations are reached rapidly. Earlier orally inhaled pulmonary DHE (MAP0004) achieved roughly 28-36% 2-hour pain freedom versus 10-18% on placebo, whereas intranasal DHE powder (STS101) struggled in Phase 3 due to slower absorption and device-handling variability during attacks. This 108-patient two-period crossover design boosts statistical power substantially over a parallel-group trial of similar size and tests a single primary endpoint (2-hour pain freedom without a co-primary MBS hurdle), supporting a relatively high probability of success if inhalation delivery is reliable.

assumptions.claim: Orally inhaled DHE (MAP0004) demonstrated statistically significant superiority over placebo for 2-hour pain relief and pain freedom in the Phase 3 FREEDOM-301 migraine study.
Intranasal DHE dry powder (STS101) missed statistical significance on 2-hour pain freedom in its Phase 3 ASCEND acute migraine trial despite DHE being a known active drug.

reason: Pfizer's descriptive Phase 3 safety and immunogenicity bridging trial of Abrysvo (RSVpreF) across 13 sites in India has short 1-to-3-month follow-up and should complete quickly with low termination risk.
rationale: This is a standard 540-participant Indian regulatory bridging study evaluating 1-month neutralizing titers and 3-month safety for Pfizer's already approved RSVpreF vaccine (Abrysvo). With 13 sites, simple single-dose outpatient vaccination, and only 3 months of follow-up, operational execution by a major global sponsor is predictable, stoppage risk is very low, and substantive primary endpoint amendments are rare. ClinicalTrials.gov results posting typically occurs around 10-12 months post-completion, giving a moderate chance of posting before August 31, 2027.

reason: Large placebo blood pressure reductions from Hawthorne effects and regression to the mean in uncontrolled hypertension trials can compress treatment differences.
rationale: Exclusion of patients with hypersensitivity to aldosterone synthase inhibitors indicates SAL0140 belongs to the selective aldosterone synthase inhibitor (ASI) class. Selective ASIs such as baxdrostat and lorundrostat have consistently produced 8-11 mmHg placebo-adjusted reductions in seated systolic blood pressure at 8-12 weeks in uncontrolled and resistant hypertension. With 252 patients across three active doses and placebo (~63 per arm, SD ~14 mmHg, standard error of difference ~2.5 mmHg), and only one dose required to beat placebo per benchmark rules, statistical power exceeds 85%.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 BrigHTN trial in treatment-resistant hypertension, the aldosterone synthase inhibitor baxdrostat reduced seated systolic blood pressure by up to 11 mmHg more than placebo at 12 weeks.
Lorundrostat significantly reduced automated office systolic blood pressure compared with placebo in patients with uncontrolled hypertension in Target-HTN.

reason: Oral small-molecule NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors carry class-related hepatotoxicity and tolerability risks that could trigger dose holds, discontinuations, or early termination.
rationale: BGE-102 is an oral NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitor evaluated on a direct downstream pharmacodynamic biomarker, 12-week percent change in hsCRP, in obese adults screened for elevated hsCRP. Inflammasome/IL-1beta/IL-6 pathway inhibitors reliably suppress elevated hsCRP by 35-65% versus ~5-15% placebo drift. With three daily doses (40 participants per arm) and one winning dose sufficient for success, pharmacodynamic efficacy is highly probable unless drug-induced liver injury or adverse events disrupt treatment. Because enrollment was already completed ('active, not recruiting') prior to November 2026 completion, on-time readout by early 2027 is very likely.

assumptions.claim: Direct inhibition of the NLRP3-IL-1beta-IL-6 inflammatory cascade in patients with elevated baseline hsCRP produces median hsCRP reductions of roughly 35% to 60% relative to minimal change on placebo.

reason: Oral tablet formulations of peptide incretin agonists face low and variable gastrointestinal bioavailability that could limit weight loss relative to injectable BGM0504.
rationale: BGM0504 is a potent dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist that demonstrated robust weight reduction in injectable trials; this 20-week, 200-participant Chinese Phase 2 trial tests four oral tablet dose levels versus placebo (40 per arm). Although oral peptide delivery carries absorption variability and GI tolerability challenges, advancing directly into a 200-patient four-dose trial implies Phase 1 achieved clinically active exposures. Even a moderate 5-8% placebo-adjusted weight loss at the top dose yields high power (>90% given ~5.5% SD in 20-week obesity trials), and meeting superiority on any of four doses suffices.

assumptions.claim: In Chinese Phase 2 and Phase 3 obesity trials of incretin agonists, placebo plus lifestyle modification typically yields 1.5% to 2.5% body weight reduction over 20 to 24 weeks.

reason: Botanical extracts rarely demonstrate reproducible superiority over placebo across co-primary subjective fatigue scales amid fluctuating chemotherapy toxicity.
rationale: Nuvastatic (an Orthosiphon stamineus botanical formulation) is tested against placebo in 180 colon cancer patients starting first-line chemotherapy across 6 Indian sites, with two registered primary outcomes (BFI and VAFS/fatigue scale). Supportive-care botanical interventions for cancer-related fatigue historically show high failure rates in double-blind randomized trials due to large placebo responses, noisy subjective scoring across chemotherapy cycles, and modest biological potency, and benchmark rules require both co-primary outcomes to succeed. Moderate sample size and concentrated regional execution partially offset this skepticism, yielding an intermediate-low probability of meeting both primary endpoints.

assumptions.claim: Randomized placebo-controlled trials of cancer-related fatigue interventions using 0-10 fatigue inventories typically observe standard deviations of roughly 2.0 to 2.5 points in change scores.

reason: Severe late-radiotherapy oral mucositis and dysphagia may cause substantial attrition or missing pain assessments on the final day of radiotherapy.
rationale: BupiZenge delivers slow-dissolving topical bupivacaine, an amide local anesthetic with a 2-to-3-hour duration of analgesia, compared open-label against viscous 2% lidocaine, whose mucosal anesthesia typically wanes within 30-45 minutes. Assessing integrated pain reduction over a 3-hour post-dose window strongly favors the longer-acting bupivacaine lozenge, supported by prior positive Phase 2 randomized evidence in head-and-neck radiotherapy mucositis and potential expectation effects in an open-label design. However, enrolling 150 pre-IMRT patients across 11 Nordic/German sites starting July 2026 and following them through 6-7 weeks of radiotherapy makes late completion past March 2027 highly likely.
evidence: Mogensen et al. bupivacaine lozenge Phase 2 (2017)

assumptions.claim: A randomized Phase 2 trial in head and neck cancer patients with oral mucositis showed bupivacaine lozenges significantly reduced oral cavity pain compared with standard pain management.

reason: Unexpected opportunistic infections, laboratory abnormalities, or skin tolerability issues could reduce response rates under non-responder imputation.
rationale: WD-890 is an oral selective TYK2 inhibitor in a 375-patient Chinese Phase 3 plaque psoriasis study with standard Week 16 co-primary endpoints (PGA 0/1 and PASI 75). Oral TYK2 inhibitors (deucravacitinib in POETYK PSO-1/2/3 and next-generation allosteric TYK2 inhibitors) consistently achieve 50-65% PGA 0/1 and 55-75% PASI 75 at Week 16 versus 5-10% on placebo in Chinese and global cohorts. With 375 randomized patients, statistical power for a >35 percentage point separation exceeds 99%, giving very high likelihood of meeting both co-primary endpoints and supporting a Chinese NDA filing in 2027.

assumptions.claim: In the Asian Phase 3 POETYK PSO-3 trial of oral TYK2 inhibitor deucravacitinib in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, Week 16 sPGA 0/1 was 55.6% on active treatment versus 7.4% on placebo.

reason: Interstitial lung disease or hematologic toxicity associated with topoisomerase-I payload HER2 ADCs could trigger early discontinuations and censor BICR progression events.
rationale: GQ1005 is a site-specific anti-HER2 antibody-drug conjugate carrying a topoisomerase-I inhibitor payload, compared head-to-head against T-DM1 in 228 ADC-naive HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer patients across 70 Chinese sites. Next-generation HER2 ADCs (particularly topoisomerase-I ADCs like trastuzumab deruxtecan in DESTINY-Breast03 and ARX788 in ACE-Breast-02) consistently outperform T-DM1, which yields ~6.8-8.2 months median BICR PFS, with hazard ratios of 0.28-0.55. Sizing the Phase 3 trial at 228 patients (~140 PFS events) reflects strong Phase 1/2 activity and high power for PFS, though interim overall survival will likely remain statistically immature.

assumptions.claim: In DESTINY-Breast03, control-arm T-DM1 achieved a median BICR progression-free survival of 6.8 months in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane.

reason: High adherence to background intranasal corticosteroids and antihistamines or variable pollen exposure in adolescents could narrow the treatment difference over two weeks.
rationale: Stapokibart (CM310), an anti-IL-4Ralpha antibody already approved in China for adult seasonal allergic rhinitis based on the Phase 3 PHECDA trial, demonstrated a clear 2-week rTNSS improvement (~1.3 points over background therapy placebo). Disease pathophysiology and IL-4/IL-13 signaling in adolescents aged 12-17 closely mirror adults, and 68 patients per arm provides roughly 90% power for a ~1.25-point difference assuming SD ~2.1. Enrollment across 27 Chinese sites during the autumn 2026 pollen season aligns with December 2026 completion and a likely supplemental filing in 2027.
evidence: PHECDA Phase 3 trial of stapokibart in adult seasonal allergic rhinitis (2024)

assumptions.claim: Stapokibart significantly improved 2-week daily rTNSS versus placebo as add-on therapy in adults with seasonal allergic rhinitis.

reason: Substantial placebo and background medication improvement or waning seasonal pollen counts could attenuate the 2-week rTNSS separation.
rationale: SHR-1819 is Hengrui's anti-IL-4Ralpha monoclonal antibody, targeting the same clinically validated pathway as stapokibart in adult seasonal allergic rhinitis. With 220 patients (110 per arm), statistical power exceeds 90% to detect an expected ~1.3-point reduction in 2-week rTNSS (SD ~2.2). Because the trial was already active, not recruiting in October 2026 during the autumn pollen season with a 4-week follow-up, on-time December 2026 primary completion and a 2027 Chinese regulatory submission are highly likely.
evidence: PHECDA Phase 3 trial of stapokibart in adult seasonal allergic rhinitis (2024)

assumptions.claim: IL-4Ralpha blockade reduces 2-week daily rTNSS by roughly 1.2 to 1.4 points over placebo in seasonal allergic rhinitis.

reason: Topical airway magnesium salt spray lacks strong clinical validation for suppressing refractory chronic cough reflex hypersensitivity against a large placebo response.
rationale: Refractory and unexplained chronic cough trials exhibit substantial placebo reductions in 24-hour objective cough frequency (typically 20-35%) and high inter-patient variability. Even systemic neuromodulators such as P2X3 antagonists achieve modest 15-20% placebo-adjusted reductions requiring large sample sizes. SC0032, a topical magnesium salt oral spray tested in at most 30 randomized patients per arm (fewer if run-in failures count toward the 60 enrollment figure), faces both low mechanistic prior probability and limited statistical power.
evidence: COUGH-1 and COUGH-2 Phase 3 trials of gefapixant in refractory chronic cough (2022)

assumptions.claim: Placebo arms in objective 24-hour cough frequency trials for refractory chronic cough commonly show 20% to 35% reductions from baseline.

reason: Topical 5% ascorbic acid drops four times daily may not maintain high enough intraoperative aqueous humor antioxidant concentrations to meaningfully reduce phacoemulsification endothelial loss.
rationale: Phacoemulsification of hard nuclear cataracts (LOCS III grade 3-5) generates free radicals that cause roughly 10-16% (~300-400 cells/mm2) central endothelial cell loss by week 12. While intracameral or perioperative ascorbic acid has shown endothelial protection in preclinical and small clinical studies, topical 5% eye drops face corneal bioavailability limits during ultrasound delivery, and surgeon-to-surgeon phaco energy adds substantial variance (~300 cells/mm2 SD). With 100 patients per arm, a moderate biological benefit yields a 38% probability of statistical significance.

reason: With roughly 87 patients per arm, higher-than-expected complete response on palonosetron alone could leave a real additive antiemetic benefit short of statistical significance.
rationale: High-risk surgical patients (>=3 Apfel PONV risk factors, >=2-hour general anesthesia) treated with palonosetron monotherapy typically achieve 50-58% complete response over 72 hours. Adding a second complementary antiemetic such as HRS5580 (from Hengrui's perioperative pipeline) in a two-dose Phase 2 trial has solid precedent for lifting 72-hour complete response by 15-20 percentage points, especially on vomiting suppression. Testing two active dose arms increases the probability that at least one dose meets superiority at alpha 0.05.

reason: Facial repigmentation at 24 weeks can lag behind longer treatment durations if baseline vitiligo activity is high or ambient UV exposure is low.
rationale: QY201 is an oral JAK1/TYK2 inhibitor with demonstrated clinical activity in type 1/2 inflammatory skin disease. Oral JAK1 and TYK2 inhibitors (such as povorcitinib and upadacitinib) consistently produce ~30-40% reductions in F-VASI at week 24 in non-segmental vitiligo compared with minimal change on placebo. With three active doses up to 20 mg and ~50 patients per arm, power is strong. Because the record still listed recruiting in late October 2026 with a 24-week endpoint, completion will likely slip past Q1 2027.
evidence: Phase 2b trial of oral povorcitinib in non-segmental vitiligo (2023)
Phase 2 trial of upadacitinib in non-segmental vitiligo (2023)

assumptions.claim: Oral JAK1 inhibitors achieve roughly 30% to 40% mean reductions in F-VASI at week 24 versus single-digit changes on placebo in non-segmental vitiligo.

reason: If the 60 patients are split across multiple unstated dose arms, small per-arm sample sizes could reduce power for the stringent week-12 PASI 100 threshold.
rationale: Choosing PASI 100 at week 12 as primary outcome signals a high-efficacy psoriasis biologic targeting the IL-17 or IL-23 axis. Placebo PASI 100 rates at week 12 in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis are near zero (0-2%), so even with 15-30 patients per arm, a 35-45% PASI 100 response rate achieves high statistical significance. PASI 75 at week 12 has even greater separation. Because the trial was still recruiting in late October 2026 with a 12-week primary endpoint, completion may slip slightly into early 2027.

reason: Thirteen weeks during initial semaglutide titration in patients with type 2 diabetes is short to separate incremental weight loss over active GLP-1 therapy.
rationale: AT673 (Antag's peptide GIPR antagonist) co-administered with semaglutide tests dual GLP-1R agonism plus GIPR antagonism, a mechanism validated for additive weight loss. However, weight loss in type 2 diabetes is blunted compared with non-diabetic obesity, and all arms initiate semaglutide titration simultaneously over just 13 weeks (control ~-4.2%, SD ~3.8%). With 50 patients per arm, an incremental ~1.6% weight reduction gives roughly 52% probability of statistical significance. Active, not recruiting status in October 2026 supports timely Q1/Q2 2027 readout.
evidence: STEP 2 trial of semaglutide in type 2 diabetes and obesity (2021)

reason: Enrollment is already complete at two experienced Canadian vaccine centers, so follow-up through February 2027 should finish on schedule with minimal risk of termination or amendment.
rationale: This 47-participant Phase 2 Hia glycoconjugate vaccine trial at two established Canadian Immunization Research Network centers was already active, not recruiting in October 2026 with registered completion on February 3, 2027. Because enrollment is finished and remaining visits follow a fixed post-vaccination safety schedule, primary completion is unlikely to slip past May 4, 2027 (`p_late` = 0.18). Safety stops and substantive primary outcome amendments in small post-enrollment adult conjugate vaccine trials are rare, while ClinicalTrials.gov results posting by August 2027 is modest (~22%).

reason: Slightly slower neuromuscular onset at the selected bolus dose could lower the rate of excellent or good intubation conditions within 5 minutes relative to rocuronium.
rationale: In Phase 3 elective anesthesia trials, standard-dose rocuronium achieves excellent or good Cooper intubation scores within 5 minutes in ~97-99% of adults. After Phase 2 dose optimization, neuromuscular blocking agents tested in 320 patients (160 per arm) have narrow confidence intervals (~+/-3.5 percentage points) that readily satisfy standard non-inferiority margins (~7.5-10%). Single-day surgical endpoints allow rapid recruitment in China, supporting timely completion and a high likelihood of an NDA filing by Hengrui in 2027.

reason: With only 15 patients per arm and substantial vehicle lubrication responses, the study is severely underpowered to hit both corneal staining and OSDI symptom co-primary endpoints simultaneously.
rationale: Meeting both sign (Modified Oxford staining) and symptom (OSDI) co-primary endpoints at two-sided alpha 0.05 with N=30 total (15 per arm) requires an unusually large effect size (>0.75 Oxford grades and >15 OSDI points over vehicle). Vehicle eye drops produce meaningful symptomatic and staining improvements in chronic oGVHD, and biological heterogeneity post-transplant is high. Enrolling 30 stable chronic oGVHD patients across 5 US sites with a 90-day treatment window also makes delays beyond March 2027 likely.

assumptions.claim: In ocular surface disease trials such as OPUS-2, meeting both corneal staining sign and symptom co-primary endpoints proved difficult even with over 350 patients per arm because of vehicle effects and weak sign-symptom correlation.

reason: Large placebo office blood pressure reductions and requirement to demonstrate consistent efficacy across listed timepoints could attenuate the placebo-adjusted treatment difference.
rationale: SAL0120 is a selective aldosterone synthase inhibitor tested across three doses versus placebo (about 64 per arm) in 256 patients with uncontrolled or resistant hypertension on diuretic-containing regimens. Class benchmarks (baxdrostat, lorundrostat) consistently lower seated office SBP by 8 to 11 mmHg beyond placebo by Weeks 8 to 12. With SD ~13.5 mmHg and 64 patients per group, high-dose SAL0120 has high power to beat placebo, tempered mainly by office-BP placebo drift and potential co-primary reporting across Weeks 4, 8, and 12.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 BrigHTN trial in treatment-resistant hypertension, high-dose aldosterone synthase inhibition lowered seated systolic blood pressure at Week 12 by roughly 11 mmHg more than placebo despite a ~9 mmHg placebo drop.

reason: Gastrointestinal adverse events during 20-week oral dose titration could drive early treatment discontinuations and attenuate intention-to-treat weight loss at the highest dose.
rationale: MWN109 is an incretin-based agonist evaluated across four titrated oral dose groups versus placebo (about 51 per arm) over 20 weeks in Chinese adults with overweight or obesity, and the trial is already completed. Only one of four active doses needs to achieve superiority. With between-patient SD ~5.5%, N=51 per arm detects even a 3.5% weight difference at p<0.01, whereas active oral incretin therapies typically yield 7% to 12% placebo-adjusted loss at 20 weeks. Subsequent initiation of Phase 2 T2DM trial NCT07801820 further signals encouraging clinical activity.
