assumptions.claim: Shanghai Minwei subsequently initiated a 240-patient Phase 2 trial of MWN109 tablets in type 2 diabetes (NCT07801820) in June 2026.
In Phase 2 obesity trials of titrated oral incretin agonists such as orforglipron, placebo weight loss is near 2% while top oral doses exceed 9% reduction by 20 to 26 weeks.

reason: Gastrointestinal intolerability at top titrated subcutaneous doses is the main risk, though multiple dose arms buffer overall primary endpoint success.
rationale: Injectable incretin agonists over 36 weeks in Chinese non-diabetic obesity populations consistently produce large weight reductions (13% to 20%) versus ~2% on placebo. Even with ~31 participants per arm and SD ~6.5%, power exceeds 95% for any placebo-adjusted effect beyond 6%, and three active doses are tested. Crucially, the companion maintenance extension trial NCT07804797 enrolled 71 completers from MWN109-II-WL who achieved at least 5% weight loss at end of treatment, confirming robust weight reduction in this parent study.

assumptions.claim: Extension study NCT07804797 enrolled 71 participants who completed MWN109-II-WL with at least a 5% body weight reduction from baseline.
In Chinese non-diabetic adults with overweight or obesity in SURMOUNT-CN, injectable incretin therapy achieved >13% weight loss versus ~2% with placebo.

reason: High gastrointestinal discontinuation or limited oral bioavailability at tolerated doses could narrow the HbA1c separation from placebo.
rationale: MWN109 tablets are tested across four daily doses against placebo and active-control oral semaglutide 14 mg (~40 patients per arm) over 20 weeks in T2DM inadequately controlled on lifestyle or metformin (baseline HbA1c 7.5% to 11.0%). Prior completion of the 255-patient obesity Phase 2 tablet trial supports oral exposure and dose selection. With HbA1c change SD ~0.9% and N=40 per arm, an expected -1.1% placebo-adjusted HbA1c reduction provides >95% statistical power, and any of the four doses meeting superiority suffices.

assumptions.claim: In PIONEER 1, oral semaglutide 14 mg once daily lowered HbA1c by roughly 1.1 to 1.4 percentage points relative to placebo in early type 2 diabetes.
assumptions.source: PIONEER 1, Aroda et al. Diabetes Care 2019

reason: With enrollment of 71 rollover responders completed and status active, not recruiting past its September 2026 registered completion date, this open-label China extension should finish cleanly without posting results on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027.
rationale: This 71-participant open-label 24-week weight-maintenance extension (QD vs QW MWN109 tablets) is already active, not recruiting, with its September 2026 primary completion date passed. Termination risk is minimal (~2%). Because China-only Phase 2 trials are not subject to US FDAAA 12-month ClinicalTrials.gov results-posting mandates, posting tabular results on ClinicalTrials.gov by August 2027 is unlikely (~4%), and substantive post-completion changes to the straightforward Week 24 percent weight-change primary outcome are rare.

reason: Lubricating vehicle eye drops and regression to the mean from baseline NEI staining >=4 typically produce large control improvements relative to ~30 patients per arm.
rationale: TJO-087 tests two topical doses against vehicle in 90 Korean adults with dry eye disease (~30 per arm) on 12-week change in NEI corneal fluorescein staining (0-15 scale, baseline >=4). In dry eye trials, vehicle drops routinely reduce NEI staining by ~1.5 to 2.2 points via tear supplementation and regression to the mean, while effective anti-inflammatory drops typically add only 0.5 to 1.1 points of benefit with between-patient SD ~2.3. At N=30 per arm (SE ~0.59), the trial has under 40% power for typical DED effect sizes.

assumptions.claim: In dry eye clinical trials such as OPUS-1, vehicle eye drops produce substantial 12-week improvements in corneal fluorescein staining, leaving modest active-versus-vehicle differences that usually require >100 patients per arm.

reason: Three-day Coartem cures ~96-98% of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in children, leaving virtually no room for superiority and high risk of late recrudescence after a single oral dose.
rationale: PLATINUM Cohort C2 randomizes 120 African children (2 to <12 years) to a single oral loose combination of cipargamin (KAE609) + ganaplacide (KLU156) versus 3-day Coartem on Day 29 PCR-corrected ACPR. Coartem achieves ~96-98% PCR-corrected ACPR, making statistical superiority virtually unattainable, while single-dose antimalarial cure in young children with lower immunity and faster clearance carries meaningful Day 29 recrudescence risk even under a benchmark or non-inferiority protocol goal. Cipargamin clears parasites markedly faster than artemisinins, supporting key secondary PCT if formally tested.

assumptions.claim: Standard 3-day artemether-lumefantrine (Coartem) achieves Day 29 PCR-corrected ACPR rates around 95% to 98% in uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria trials.
assumptions.source: KALUMI, Ogutu et al. Lancet Infect Dis 2023

assumptions.claim: Cipargamin (KAE609) clears P. falciparum blood-stage parasites with median clearance times under 12 hours in Phase 2 clinical studies.

reason: Spontaneous resolution of postoperative pain by Day 8 or mild inflammation in micro-incision cataract surgery could narrow sham-controlled responder differences.
rationale: Subconjunctival triamcinolone acetonide (4 mg / 100 uL TRIESENCE) provides a potent sustained corticosteroid depot directly after phacoemulsification cataract surgery against a sham (no-treatment) control across 250 patients (125 per arm). In sham/placebo-controlled cataract surgery trials, sustained ocular corticosteroids raise Day 14 complete anterior chamber cell clearing from ~25% to ~60% and Day 8 pain-free rates from ~50% to ~80%, giving >95% power on both co-primary endpoints. With only 1 site listed in October 2026 out of 16 planned, moderate enrollment slippage past December 2026 is plausible.

assumptions.claim: In placebo-controlled Phase 3 cataract surgery trials of sustained ocular corticosteroids, untreated/placebo eyes achieve Day 14 anterior chamber cell grade 0 in roughly 20% to 30% of subjects versus ~52% to 65% with depot steroid.

reason: Regression to the mean and white-coat blood pressure habituation in office sphygmomanometry could inflate placebo reductions if pharmacodynamic knockdown is suboptimal.
rationale: GW906 (SAL0132) is a long-acting subcutaneous antihypertensive (6-month double-blind period with primary Week 12 msSBP readout, consistent with hepatic angiotensinogen-targeting siRNA) evaluated in 319 patients with essential hypertension (msSBP 140 to <180 mmHg). In KARDIA-1, subcutaneous AGT siRNA reduced Month 3 office SBP by ~9 to 12 mmHg versus placebo with low discontinuation rates. With 319 randomized participants and office SBP SD ~13 mmHg, statistical power for Week 12 superiority exceeds 90%, and Part A's September 2026 primary completion date has already passed.

assumptions.claim: In the Phase 2 KARDIA-1 trial, single-dose subcutaneous angiotensinogen siRNA (zilebesiran) reduced Month 3 office systolic blood pressure by roughly 9 to 12 mmHg compared with placebo.

reason: If the primary hypothesis requires statistical superiority across all three co-primary plaque and gingivitis indices against the active 67% sodium bicarbonate comparator in addition to the negative fluoride control, the narrower margin against bicarbonate could prevent full primary success.
rationale: Stabilized 0.45% stannous fluoride toothpastes consistently produce large, statistically significant 6-month reductions in Lobene Modified Gingivitis Index, gingival bleeding, and Quigley-Hein plaque scores relative to regular sodium fluoride dentifrice (Colgate Cavity Protection) in single-center examiner-blinded trials, with low inter-subject variability (SD ~0.22) giving high power at n=40 per arm. The primary residual risk is whether Colgate's protocol requires beating both Cavity Protection and the active 67% sodium bicarbonate arm across all three co-primary endpoints. Single-site Italian consumer oral-care studies enroll rapidly on schedule, though public result disclosure by June 2027 is relatively uncommon.

reason: Recruiting 24 adult epidermolysis bullosa patients in Taiwan who each have two matched chronic 10-40 cm2 non-joint target lesions and completing up to 16 weeks of participation within five months of study start makes a substantial completion delay highly likely.
rationale: Epidermolysis bullosa is an ultra-rare genetic disorder, and this trial restricts eligibility to adults with confirmed subtypes who simultaneously carry two size-matched (within 20%), chronic (21 days to 9 months), 10-40 cm2 lesions separated by at least 6 cm outside joints, hands, and feet. Because each participant requires 2-4 weeks of screening plus 12 weeks to the Day 85 primary safety assessment, meeting the registered March 2027 primary completion date would require completing enrollment within roughly eight weeks of the October 2026 start at one site, making >90-day delay very likely and ClinicalTrials.gov posting by August 2027 unlikely.

reason: With only 15 participants per arm, substantial inter-patient variability in acute opioid withdrawal trajectories, rescue medication adjustments, and potential multiplicity testing across two dose regimens could leave a real pharmacological effect short of statistical significance.
rationale: Cebranopadol is a potent full agonist at mu-opioid and nociceptin/orphanin FQ peptide (NOP) receptors; 400 mcg twice daily (800 mcg/day) exceeds doses that matched 60 mg/day morphine analgesia in chronic pain trials and should strongly suppress withdrawal in patients dependent on 50-90 MME/day opioids whose physical dependence is pre-confirmed on Day -1 before randomization. However, n=15 per arm introduces sampling variance, and cebranopadol's 4-6 hour Tmax could permit early breakthrough withdrawal or rescue use in higher-MME patients. Inpatient chronic-pain opioid-withdrawal recruitment across two US sites carries moderate delay risk.

assumptions.claim: Cebranopadol at daily doses of 200 to 600 micrograms produced statistically significant analgesia versus placebo comparable to prolonged-release morphine in chronic low back pain.
